chapters.title: Chapter 701
paragraphs: “My hunting dog. I took great care training him.”
The Southern Heaven Demon Emress’s voice rang out softly. At the same time, the Masked Man took a step forward.
Step.
His stride never faltered as he emerged from the settling cloud of dust.
As the Masked Man’s form gradually came into focus, I muttered like a groan.
“...Fuck. What the hell is that?”
I wasn’t looking for an answer. I already knew.
Regeneration.
That one word explained the bizarre sight unfolding before my eyes.
Crack. Slither.
Shattered bones joined together. Flesh and blood filled the wounds.
Darkness writhed like a living snake across the Masked Man’s body, healing his injuries and pouring new strength into him wherever it passed.
—The power of defying heaven...
Defying heaven.
What I was seeing seemed to run against the will of heaven and the natural order itself.
As the guardian spirit’s lament reached me, the Masked Man finished healing and bent his strangely twisted elbow.
Crunch.
He broke the elbow that had already fused back together, then aligned it and healed it again.
The pain must have been tremendous, yet he didn’t so much as twitch an eyebrow. At last, I understood what had felt wrong about him during our fight.
That bastard can’t feel pain.
Even someone with a dulled sense of pain would feel something.
But the Masked Man hadn’t groaned or screamed once. Not when a dagger lodged in his chest or his elbow was crushed. Not even when the terrible heat of the Flame Divine Palm had struck him.
What the hell did they do to him?
Had he gone somewhere for a painkilling shot?
As I stared at the emotionless eyes visible above his mask and swallowed a low groan, someone’s small, snow-white foot stepped onto the damp earth.
Scuff.
From the sky to the ground. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress landed lightly and smiled.
“You look like you’ve seen a ghost. Then again, I suppose you weren’t all that surprised? You saw it once in Henan.”
Grrr.
With a low growl, the guardian spirit raised its enormous, bloodstained body on weary limbs.
Its breathing was much rougher than it had been at the start. If it fought her now, it would lose. No question.
I stepped in front of the guardian spirit and opened my mouth.
“Yeah. The Blood Lord. That crazy bastard was the same.”
“What a shame. If you hadn’t met the Blood Lord, I could’ve seen you scared out of your wits.”
“If I scared that easily, I’d have died ages ago.”
“Maybe it’s because you’re young. You can’t help the bluffing.”
A bluff.
What the Blood Lord had done during the Shaolin Bloodshed had certainly surprised me. It hadn’t scared me out of my wits.
I’d seen and been through too much in the modern world where I was born and raised.
“Think whatever you want.”
Something in my calm reply made the Southern Heaven Demon Empress draw her brows together. She looked me up and down through narrowed eyes, then licked her red lips.

“I can’t tell if you’re simply brave or if you have something no one else knows about... But there’s something strange about you. I’m beginning to see why the Lord of Heaven takes an interest in you.”
“An interest?”
I began circulating my internal energy, slowly enough that she wouldn’t notice.

She was more than enough of a monster to deal with alone. Now I had a drugged-up bastard who might as well have had a painkilling shot to worry about too. I needed to buy time and heal as much of my Internal Injury as I could.
“The Great Snow Fiend, that old man, spouted the same nonsense.”
“Oh? Do you still think it’s nonsense?”
She smiled and took a step toward me. I tightened my grip on my spear.
“I wish it were.”
“Why?”
“Because I don’t want some deranged old man’s attention, Lord of Heaven or not. Same goes for the crazy bitch standing in front of me.”
Whoosh—pfft!
Pain stung my cheek, and heat spread across it. I’d dodged the Finger Qi by a hair.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress sighed in relief.
“Phew. I nearly killed you. Good dodge. You’re better than I thought.”
Praise from an enemy, at a time like this.
It pissed me off. It also told me two things.
First, even if that monster went all out, I could handle her attacks if I kept the damage as slight as I had just now.
Second, she had more to lose than gain by killing me.
Blood ran down my cheek. Instead of wiping it away, I tightened my grip on the spear.
“The Lord of Heaven must be more interested in me than I thought. Even a crazy bitch like you is worried about killing me.”
“I think I’m starting to understand why you only watched me in Hubei Province.”
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress was staggeringly powerful. Of everyone I’d ever encountered, very few could stand against her.
At least on the level of the Ten Kings. Maybe higher.
I could feel the sheer force of her power just standing here.
Apart from Jeok Cheongang, who was an exception even among the Ten Kings, she had to be one of the ten strongest people alive.
And yet she did nothing. She had dozens—hundreds—of chances to make a move in Hubei Province.
The question had stayed with me ever since I learned who she was.
Why had she left me alive?
Was I not worth killing? Was it all just a game to her?
I didn’t know the full story, but I was certain neither answer was right. I was Fire King Jeok Cheongang’s only Disciple and a successor of the Fire Gate Clan.

If she got me into her hands, she could lure in Jeok Cheongang, who would become a major obstacle to Dark Heaven’s future movements, and kill him. Even if that attempt came to nothing, she could still obtain the Fire Gate Clan’s supreme arts.
There were plenty of ways to make a man talk.
Torture. Torture. And endless torture.
But she hadn’t killed me when I was completely taken in by her. She hadn’t abducted me either.
She had merely watched me right before my eyes, then vanished without a trace. Like an observer sent on someone else’s orders.
My dry lips parted.
“Why is the Lord of Heaven so interested in me? Why go this far when there are people far more worth his attention?”
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s lips had pressed shut at some point. My question did nothing to open them.
After a brief silence, she gave only a short answer.
“What could an insignificant creature like you know of that omnipotent, exalted one’s will?”
Insignificant.
I studied her tense face, the way her gaze had dropped and how she pressed her teeth lightly against her lip.
A thought flashed through my mind. I spoke it aloud.
“You don’t know, do you?”
I saw her eyes waver. A derisive laugh slipped out of me.
“Fucking idiot.”
“...What?”
“I said you’re a fucking idiot. You worthless fucking idiot of an old hag.”
That was enough to light the Southern Heaven Demon Emress’s fuse.
Rooooar!
A storm of qi swept out in every direction. Layer upon layer of pitch-black darkness wrapped around her.
Beside me, the guardian spirit steadied its ragged breathing and sent me a thought.
—If you were going to provoke her, couldn’t you have stalled a little longer?
I regretted it a little myself. But there was no other way.
We had to finish this before the humans and beasts still in the Inner Palace completed their mutation. Which of us fell and which remained standing came after that.
I sent a Sound Transmission to the guardian spirit. It was still grumbling, though it was hardly in fighting shape itself.
—Are you really a guardian spirit? Stop acting like you’re about to keel over and fight with everything you’ve got.
—How dare you insult me. Three hundred years ago, I would never have endured such humiliation from a mere human.
—Sure. That crazy bitch wouldn’t have been born yet, either.
—...Damn it.
Cursing in a manner hardly befitting a guardian spirit, it bristled from head to tail. Its gaze flicked over the two figures approaching us from front and back.
—This has become more difficult.
—Wow. I had absolutely no idea. Good thing you’re a guardian spirit. Thanks for telling me.
—We’ll take one each. The human male or the human female. Choose.
—Then I’ll take the male.
Does this bastard have no conscience?
That seemed to be what its pale blue eyes were asking me. Even in this godforsaken mess, I let out a short laugh and started walking.
Toward the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Step.
Maybe it was nerves, but my footstep sounded unusually loud. Her eyes had turned blood red, and a chill ran through me.
“You mean to fight me? You?”
Her voice was cold and eerie. I let out a deep sigh before answering.
“That hurts. We insignificant creatures ought to look out for each other. Don’t you think?”
“Choose. Kill me and get your ass kicked by the Lord of Heaven, or die nicely right here.”
Hack—ptoo.
I spat out a mouthful of phlegm mixed with stale blood and raised my spearhead.
When I spoke again, my voice sounded unfamiliar. Cold.
“For the record... I’ll fight until I die.”
Fwoosh—boom!
Flamefire Path.
A single line of flame shot forward, consuming the air in its path.
And at the end of that path stood a monster wrapped in deep darkness.
Whoooosh—boom!
Bang!
An immense shockwave shook the world.
The ground split beneath Jin Taekyung’s descending spearhead, and searing heat burst from the fissure.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress dodged the strike by a hair and thrust out her hand.
Kraaaaaash!
A palm strike carrying unprecedented qi collided with the spearhead slicing through space like a ray of light.
Qi collided with qi. The difference in strength was unmistakable.
Boom!
Compressed air exploded, and one figure was hurled backward.
Delight shone in the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s eyes.
That wretch is nothing.
Jin Taekyung’s martial power had clearly advanced at an unbelievable pace. He had changed so much that she found herself wondering whether he was truly the same boy she had met in Hubei.
Perhaps the greatest obstacle to their grand plan was no longer the Beast Miao King, but Jin Taekyung.
But...
I’ve grown stronger still.
She could feel power unlike anything she had known boiling through her body.
The denser the demonic qi flowing from the rift grew, the stronger she became.
Even now.
Pop!
One step.
She vanished like a ghost and reappeared in midair.
As she plunged toward him like a meteor, Jin Taekyung opened his eyes wide. He was still buried deep in the ground.
Crunch.
Solid earth crumbled like mud beneath her strike. Jin Taekyung escaped it by a hair and flicked his sleeve.
A dagger flew at her from somewhere, as though he had conjured it from thin air. She avoided it easily and thrust out her hand with lightning speed.
Slash!
Her fingers only grazed him.
But curled like hooks, they tore through his martial uniform and cut into his thigh.
Blood spurted. Jin Taekyung staggered.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress beamed as she brought the edge of her hand down toward him.
Shu-whaack!

chapters.title: Chapter 702
paragraphs: Shwaaak!
A straightened hand-blade sliced through the air and came crashing down.

Slender and snow-white, it looked as though it had never been dipped in water. But Jin Taekyung knew how much blood had flowed from that hand. He knew what darkness lurked behind the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s dazzling smile.
Monster.
Those two words surfaced in his mind once more.
As the blood-red Force fell like a meteor toward the crown of his head, his legs, frozen as though nailed to the ground, moved at last.
Shhk!
The earth split like tofu. Jin Taekyung slipped past the Force by a hair and drove his spear forward like lightning.
Shwaaak!

The spearhead flew toward a single point with terrifying speed, power, and precision. Even a fistfighter who had spent a lifetime honing his techniques and reached the Supreme Peak realm would not have dared meet that strike head-on.
But the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was different.
No. Today, at least, she had the power to do exactly that.
Krrrkkk!
Empty-Hand Seizes the Blade.

She caught the spearhead between her palms as though bringing her hands together in prayer. Hellfire flickered around the blade as it trembled between them. Enough power was concentrated in those snow-white hands to keep them from being reduced to ash.
The corners of her unlined mouth lifted.
“With only this much...”
The instant her voice, filled with mockery, emerged—
Plop. Plip.
Drops of blood fell. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress noticed them and fell silent.
The pain reached her half a beat later. Jin Taekyung gave her a sheepish smile.
“Oh, I forgot to mention. This is Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.”
“What were you saying?”
Her delicate brow furrowed. Jin Taekyung let go of the spear shaft and thrust out both arms.
Palm Force?
She was wrong.
Shhk! Shhk!
Two daggers shot toward her throat and chest. They were already too close to dodge, so she released the spearhead and snapped her sleeves.
Whoooosh!
Wind burst from the billowing fabric and sent the daggers flying. At that instant, Jin Taekyung’s foot caught the end of White Flame’s slowly tilting shaft.
No—he kicked it.
...What?
He kicked it? The divine weapon that would have helped him most in this fight?
A flash of light hurtled toward her face.
Shwaaack! Slash!
It happened in an instant. The attack was so unexpected that avoiding it completely was all but impossible. She turned her head on instinct, felt pain flare in her earlobe, and stared.
“How dare you!”
If it had only been her earring, she would not have been so furious. She had liked it, but she could always find another.
Her earlobe had been torn. Worse, her hair had been cut. Half of the thick, glossy hair she had always taken such pride in was gone.
“Die!”
Kraaaaaash!
The unprecedented energy that had faltered for a moment surged through her slender body. The pressure seemed capable of crushing a massive boulder in an instant.

But the Southern Heaven Demon Empress did not know that the young—almost absurdly young—enemy before her had once climbed a cliff with iron balls weighing well over a thousand geun strapped to his body.
Crack. Crrrunch!
The earth sank beneath the pressure crushing everything within a radius of over ten jang, while the limbs of the humans and beasts struggling in the area twisted and snapped.
—Krrk, krrrk!
“Aaaaaagh!”
Amid the blood and dying screams, Jin Taekyung endured the pressure and stamped his foot.
Boom!
A line of flame rose from his toe as he shot forward. At the same time, a spear he had somehow taken hold of swept fiercely from his fingertips and split the air like lightning.
Shwaaaargh! Boom!
The impact sent out a shockwave that shook the world. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress had caught the side of the spearhead with perfect precision. Power surged through her hand.
Crack!
The Scorching Yang Qi surrounding the spearhead, along with the steel that a skilled blacksmith had folded and tempered more than a hundred times, crumbled like tofu.
A smile full of killing intent touched her lips.
Foolish boy.
Jin Taekyung had made the mistake of giving up his peerless divine weapon of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron. Now she would make him pay for wounding her beautiful body—and for cutting her precious hair.
I meant to bring him back as unharmed as possible. That won’t do anymore.
At first, after hearing that the exalted Lord of Heaven had taken an interest in Jin Taekyung, she had intended to act as the Lord’s faithful servant and capture the young man to offer him up.
Now she had changed her mind.

He was no longer a feisty cat in her eyes, but a proud beast. Young though he was, he had teeth and claws as sharp as a great tiger’s. If she was careless, he might leave even worse wounds on her beautiful body.
Jin Taekyung rushed toward her, reflected in her blood-red eyes.
You should be prepared to lose a limb or two. I’ll reattach them later anyway.
She snapped both sleeves.
Papapapap!

The shattered spearhead broke into dozens, then hundreds, of fragments that filled the air. Each one carried Force. Jin Taekyung drove his clenched fist into the wave of hidden weapons without hesitation.
Kraaaaaash!
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
A fire dragon burst from his callused fist and swallowed the fragments. Heated red-hot, they melted into liquid iron and spattered across the ground.
Hissssssss.
But beneath the molten iron raining down like a shower, what awaited Jin Taekyung as he shot through the air was the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s slender, jade-like hand.
Whoosh!
Five fingers came at him, sweeping the air aside. They hooked like a rake toward his right arm.
Jin Taekyung twisted as though he had expected it all along.
He was not trying to save the arm she would otherwise tear away. He was putting his own neck in her path.
But at the same time, it was also a lethal move that struck at an opening the opponent had never expected.
This lunatic...!
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress screamed inwardly.

The Lord of Heaven had taken an interest in Jin Taekyung. He absolutely could not die. She had wanted to take him alive as a show of loyalty; the Lord had not even given her a specific order. If Jin Taekyung died by her hand, she might have to face the Lord’s fury alone.
No!

She hurriedly dragged back her surging internal energy. The muscles and flow of qi-blood throughout her body, already committed to the strike, twisted against the sudden reversal. A wave of backflow swept through her.
Urk!
“Kwaaaagh!”
Blood shot up from deep within her and sprayed between her lips. At the last moment, she managed to turn her hand. The Force at her fingertips missed Jin Taekyung’s throat.
Shhk! Spit!
The blade-sharp wind sliced his skin.
Jin Taekyung did not waver. He had never had any reason to.
This is the moment I’ve been waiting for.
His mind had gone cold. He had already made his calculations.

By his reckoning, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was at least on the level of the Ten Kings. She might even rival the Three Saints. Her martial arts could be no better than the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s—perhaps worse—but her overwhelming internal energy more than made up for any gap.
And when facing a master of this level, there was only one possible method.
One opening.
He had wagered his life to create it. He would not get another chance.
And now...
I’ll wager my life again.
Inventory Open. Summon.
Along with the commands ringing through his mind, he thrust out his hand like a flash of lightning.
Shhk!
A slender wrist, impossible to believe belonged to such a powerful monster, was cleanly severed.
“Aaaaaaaagh!”
Her scream was louder and more agonized than any Jin Taekyung had heard from the creatures of the Nanman Beast Palace writhing under the demonic qi. No, it was the worst scream he had ever heard.
In a way, that was only natural. People were born to forget, and the powerful, accustomed to causing pain, tended to forget their own.
Even so, she was the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
“Jin Taekyung—!”
Shhk!

She lunged with a shriek that seemed to tear through the air. Jin Taekyung met her blood-red gaze, now clouded with darkness, and knew instinctively that this time he could neither dodge nor block her attack completely.
The immense Internal Injury had thrown off her stance. The internal energy she had forced up while vomiting blood was wildly unstable. That made her all the more dangerous.
No. The real danger was the killing intent pouring from her.
“How dare you! How dare someone like you!”
His luck had only worked once.
Consumed by pain and fury, forgetting even her loyalty to her master, the monster thrust out a palm packed with power.
The world slowed. Darkness and blood-red Force churned together in the palm strike as it rushed toward him, erasing the space in its path.
Kraaaaaash!
The force was overwhelming, as though the sea and a great mountain had risen to engulf him.
Fear that made every hair on his body stand on end seized Jin Taekyung.
But he knew that if he took even one step back, everything would be over.
He had to go forward, even if it cost him his life.
Come.
He did not know what he was calling to. His foot came down on the blood-soaked earth.
Crush.
The ground sank beneath a step weighted with internal energy as heavy as his life, then burst with heat.
Boom!

“Die!”
At that instant—
Inventory Open. Summon.
Jin Taekyung’s hand, spread wide as though ready to unleash a palm strike, closed. A cold spear shaft filled his empty palm, and its spearhead erased the distance between them.
Shwaaaargh! Shhk!
The spearhead tore past the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s neck by a hair. Faint delight lit her eyes.
I read him. Perfectly.
His technique was astonishing, and dangerous. But amid the chaos of the fight, she had predicted it.
Or so she believed—until, just as she was about to take off his head, a cold draft touched her back.
Shhk.
A faint hiss reached her ear. She spun on instinct, but something icy and razor-sharp raked across her side.
Shhk!
Blood burst out like a fountain. She felt muscle and veins sever, her qi-blood tangling inside her.
Th-this is...
Backflow.
A second backflow had struck before she could even settle the Internal Injury she had suffered earlier—and it was more fatal than any wound she had received until now.
This was what he was after... from the start.
The realization flashed through her whitening vision. She swallowed the blood rising in her throat and turned.
At last, she saw it.
Goooooong.
Blue-white flames whirled at the tip of a transparent spearhead that had answered its master’s call.
Beneath Jin Taekyung’s deeply shadowed eyes, his lips moved silently, forming two words.
One Annihilation.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s eyes flew wide.
—Human!
An urgent thought suddenly rang out. With it, a vast vortex unlike anything anyone in Nanman had ever seen erupted.
Kraaaaaash!

sentences.text: Shwaaak!
A straightened hand-blade sliced through the air and came crashing down.
Slender and snow-white, it looked as though it had never been dipped in water.
But Jin Taekyung knew how much blood had flowed from that hand.
He knew what darkness lurked behind the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s dazzling smile.
Monster.
Those two words surfaced in his mind once more.
As the blood-red Force fell like a meteor toward the crown of his head, his legs, frozen as though nailed to the ground, moved at last.
Shhk!
The earth split like tofu.
Jin Taekyung slipped past the Force by a hair and drove his spear forward like lightning.
Shwaaak!
The spearhead flew toward a single point with terrifying speed, power, and precision.
Even a fistfighter who had spent a lifetime honing his techniques and reached the Supreme Peak realm would not have dared meet that strike head-on.
But the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was different.
No.
Today, at least, she had the power to do exactly that.
Krrrkkk!
Empty-Hand Seizes the Blade.
She caught the spearhead between her palms as though bringing her hands together in prayer.
Hellfire flickered around the blade as it trembled between them.
Enough power was concentrated in those snow-white hands to keep them from being reduced to ash.
The corners of her unlined mouth lifted.
“With only this much...”
The instant her voice, filled with mockery, emerged—
Plop.
Plip.
Drops of blood fell.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress noticed them and fell silent.
The pain reached her half a beat later.
Jin Taekyung gave her a sheepish smile.
“Oh, I forgot to mention.
This is Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.”
“What were you saying?”
Her delicate brow furrowed.
Jin Taekyung let go of the spear shaft and thrust out both arms.
Palm Force?
She was wrong.
Shhk!
Shhk!
Two daggers shot toward her throat and chest.
They were already too close to dodge, so she released the spearhead and snapped her sleeves.
Whoooosh!
Wind burst from the billowing fabric and sent the daggers flying.
At that instant, Jin Taekyung’s foot caught the end of White Flame’s slowly tilting shaft.
No—he kicked it.
...What?
He kicked it?
The divine weapon that would have helped him most in this fight?
A flash of light hurtled toward her face.
Shwaaack!
Slash!
It happened in an instant.
The attack was so unexpected that avoiding it completely was all but impossible.
She turned her head on instinct, felt pain flare in her earlobe, and stared.
“How dare you!”
If it had only been her earring, she would not have been so furious.
She had liked it, but she could always find another.
Her earlobe had been torn.
Worse, her hair had been cut.
Half of the thick, glossy hair she had always taken such pride in was gone.
“Die!”
Kraaaaaash!
The unprecedented energy that had faltered for a moment surged through her slender body.
The pressure seemed capable of crushing a massive boulder in an instant.

But the Southern Heaven Demon Empress did not know that the young—almost absurdly young—enemy before her had once climbed a cliff with iron balls weighing well over a thousand geun strapped to his body.
Crack.
Crrrunch!
The earth sank beneath the pressure crushing everything within a radius of over ten jang, while the limbs of the humans and beasts struggling in the area twisted and snapped.
—Krrk, krrrk!
“Aaaaaagh!”
Amid the blood and dying screams, Jin Taekyung endured the pressure and stamped his foot.
Boom!
A line of flame rose from his toe as he shot forward.
At the same time, a spear he had somehow taken hold of swept fiercely from his fingertips and split the air like lightning.
Shwaaaargh!
Boom!
The impact sent out a shockwave that shook the world.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress had caught the side of the spearhead with perfect precision.
Power surged through her hand.
Crack!
The Scorching Yang Qi surrounding the spearhead, along with the steel that a skilled blacksmith had folded and tempered more than a hundred times, crumbled like tofu.
A smile full of killing intent touched her lips.
Foolish boy.
Jin Taekyung had made the mistake of giving up his peerless divine weapon of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
Now she would make him pay for wounding her beautiful body—and for cutting her precious hair.
I meant to bring him back as unharmed as possible.
That won’t do anymore.
At first, after hearing that the exalted Lord of Heaven had taken an interest in Jin Taekyung, she had intended to act as the Lord’s faithful servant and capture the young man to offer him up.
Now she had changed her mind.
He was no longer a feisty cat in her eyes, but a proud beast.
Young though he was, he had teeth and claws as sharp as a great tiger’s.
If she was careless, he might leave even worse wounds on her beautiful body.
Jin Taekyung rushed toward her, reflected in her blood-red eyes.
You should be prepared to lose a limb or two.
I’ll reattach them later anyway.
She snapped both sleeves.
Papapapap!
The shattered spearhead broke into dozens, then hundreds, of fragments that filled the air.
Each one carried Force.
Jin Taekyung drove his clenched fist into the wave of hidden weapons without hesitation.
Kraaaaaash!
The Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
A fire dragon burst from his callused fist and swallowed the fragments.
Heated red-hot, they melted into liquid iron and spattered across the ground.
Hissssssss.
But beneath the molten iron raining down like a shower, what awaited Jin Taekyung as he shot through the air was the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s slender, jade-like hand.
Whoosh!
Five fingers came at him, sweeping the air aside.
They hooked like a rake toward his right arm.
Jin Taekyung twisted as though he had expected it all along.
He was not trying to save the arm she would otherwise tear away.
He was putting his own neck in her path.
But at the same time, it was also a lethal move that struck at an opening the opponent had never expected.
This lunatic...!
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress screamed inwardly.
The Lord of Heaven had taken an interest in Jin Taekyung.
He absolutely could not die.
She had wanted to take him alive as a show of loyalty; the Lord had not even given her a specific order.
If Jin Taekyung died by her hand, she might have to face the Lord’s fury alone.
No!
She hurriedly dragged back her surging internal energy.
The muscles and flow of qi-blood throughout her body, already committed to the strike, twisted against the sudden reversal.
A wave of backflow swept through her.
Urk!
“Kwaaaagh!”
Blood shot up from deep within her and sprayed between her lips.
At the last moment, she managed to turn her hand.
The Force at her fingertips missed Jin Taekyung’s throat.
Shhk!
Spit!
The blade-sharp wind sliced his skin.
Jin Taekyung did not waver.
He had never had any reason to.
This is the moment I’ve been waiting for.

He had already made his calculations.

Her martial arts could be no better than the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s—perhaps worse—but her overwhelming internal energy more than made up for any gap.

One opening.
He had wagered his life to create it.
He would not get another chance.

I’ll wager my life again.

Summon.

Shhk!

chapters.title: Chapter 703
paragraphs: Kwoooooong...!
I couldn’t breathe.
The roar still hadn’t faded. Its endless reverberations sounded impossibly distant.
And yet the System notifications rang clearly in my ears.

System Beep! Beep-beep! Status Effect: Severe Internal Injury has been applied! Status Effect: Severe Exhaustion has been applied! Status Effect: Severe Muscle Tear has been applied! Status Effect: ...
The notifications—or rather, the warning sounds—kept coming, itemizing just how bad my condition was.
If the System were a doctor, it would probably look at me with a grave expression and say:
Patient, I hate to tell you this, but... you’re really fucked this time. Why the hell do you keep using One Annihilation? Is dying young on your bucket list?
How considerate.
Just imagining it should have made me feel like shit. Strangely, it didn’t change my mood much. The reason was simple: reality was even shittier than anything I could imagine.
“Cough.”
Splatter. Drip, drip.
Blood burst from my mouth and scattered across the ground. I’d felt a few chunks in it, too. Pieces of my organs, no doubt. One Annihilation really gave you your money’s worth—
Fuck. It’s not a convenience-store lunchbox.
Damn it.

My vision blurred. Senses that had been sharp enough to rival a divine weapon moments ago were now as dull as an ax abandoned in a ruined cabin. White Flame, which I’d always swung around like a pinwheel, had become the heaviest thing in the world.
But one thing still worked well enough: I could feel the pain in my forearm.
Crunch. Crunch.
I stared at it through my blurred vision.
It kept chewing my flesh with teeth that jutted out like an animal’s, swallowing the blood. Its eyes held nothing but greed and madness.
It was hard to believe it had once been human, like me.
“Good?”
Crunch.
“Yeah. Guess it is.”
I didn’t know why I was talking to it when I knew it couldn’t understand me anymore. Or why I was letting the bastard livestream an eating show with my wrist.
Maybe I selfishly wanted someone else to do what had to be done. Or maybe I still felt a last shred of pity for something that had once been human.
Shwaaak! Slash!
Crunch...
Something sliced through the air, and the teeth that had been chewing so fiercely went slack.
I was staring at the young man, frozen with his red eyes wide, when a silver mane caked in blood and dust swept across my vision.
—Human. You don’t look all right.
The guardian spirit. The moment I recognized it, my legs gave out. I caught hold of its mane and answered weakly.
“Don’t people usually ask if someone’s all right first?”
—I’m not human. You clearly weren’t all right, so there was no need to ask.
“I like that about you. What about that pitch-black bastard?”
—I killed him. For the fourth time.
“What?”
—He kept getting back up. Each time, he recovered faster and grew stronger. This time may be no different.
The rift. More precisely, the demonic qi flowing from it.

And as the Masked Man grew stronger under its influence, the guardian spirit must have been growing weaker. Just like the sacred stone in its mouth, which could no longer give off the great radiance it had before.
The guardian spirit shares its power with the sacred stone.
Only now did I notice the deep wounds all over its body, its heaving shoulders and ragged breaths.
It must have caught me looking. It turned its massive body to hide the wounds.
“I’m sorry.”
The guardian spirit studied me with its blue-white eyes, then shook its head.
—You did all you could.
“At the end...”
—I know. If those things hadn’t interfered, you would have succeeded.
I looked around weakly. Torn corpses lay everywhere.
They were the mutants that had finished transforming first and rushed me at the guardian spirit’s warning, just as I was about to unleash One Annihilation.
I didn’t see them coming.
No. I hadn’t had the chance to watch for them. I’d been too hard-pressed even to look around, and the mutants had charged straight at me.
And died.
What awaited roughly one hundred of them was the immense vortex created by One Annihilation.
But in that brief instant, split into smaller and smaller fractions of time, the mutants had instinctively stopped me and fulfilled their mission.
They’d bitten my forearm and turned my attack aside, blocked my view, and thrown themselves in front of a force they couldn’t stop.
And that was how one person survived.
“Southern Heaven Demon Empress.”
My voice came out almost as a groan. A figure standing amid the hazy dust took a step forward.
Scuff.
Everything in that section of the palace had been erased by the aftermath of One Annihilation. From its very center emerged the only monster to survive, her red eyes glowing.
Red. Everything was red.
The sky. The ground. Everything between them.
At the same time, things that should never have been visible came into view.
Ah.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress stared blankly at her hand.

The smooth, snow-white hand she had gained by taking several jiazi worth of internal energy and countless measures of vital essence was gone. In its place was a hand covered in fine wrinkles and age spots, as dry and thin as the branch of a dying tree.
“Ah. Aah...”
Tears welled in her eyes, red with burst blood vessels.
This couldn’t be happening. It couldn’t.
She had been more beautiful than anyone in the world. She was supposed to be beautiful.
But the great art she had cultivated for nearly a century had been broken, and her old, ugly appearance had returned like a curse.
Trembling with shock and rage, she realized that the aging she had kept at bay was not the only curse to come upon her.
It hurts.
Only when sudden agony made her look down at herself did she understand.
Flesh had been torn from her side as though an invisible beast had bitten it away. One arm was gone entirely. And half her face had melted in the tremendous heat.
Her eyes flew wide. It was impossible. It should never have happened.
The wound in her side could heal. A skilled enough practitioner could even reattach her arm without leaving a scar.
But not her face. Unless she followed the same path as the Blood Lord she so despised, those terrible burns would leave their mark.
“No. This... this can’t...”
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress stopped short. Someone had appeared in her blood-red eyes, now wet with tears.
Jin Taekyung.
She could see him. And feel him.
After the dazzling flash that had erased everything, he was left with no strength, little more than an empty shell. That insignificant creature had stolen her youth and beauty.
A single thought seized her.
Kill him.
At that moment, her mind, muddled by countless emotions, turned cold.
The monster who had lived for an age wrapped herself in darkness and moved forward without hesitation.
Scuff. Scuff.
Crack.
With every step, the energy pouring from her body crushed everything around her.
She had lost her youth, but she still had the strength to kill him. The bleeding from her side and arm had stopped, and her battered insides were slowly settling.
If the sudden return of age was a curse, then the demonic qi pouring from the rift, growing denser by the moment, was a blessing.
It would let her tear apart Jin Taekyung, who could barely stand, and the reeking old beast in front of him.
—Stop.
Ssssss.
Light spread from the guardian spirit as its thought rang out. The thousand mutants packed around it crouched low, but the Southern Heaven Demon Empress kept walking.
Bang!
A palm strike shot forward without the slightest hesitation. Darkness mixed with blood-red Force pressed down on the sacred stone’s light and engulfed Jin Taekyung.
Boom!
The ground burst apart with a deafening crash. In that instant, the guardian spirit bit Jin Taekyung by the nape and darted away like lightning, releasing a low growl.
—The sacred stone...
It left the thought unfinished, but the truth was cruelly clear.
Rumble...
A faint trembling came from inside its mouth. Like an old man facing a young man in his prime, the sacred stone was losing strength even now.
So was the White Tiger that had guarded it for so many years.
Even the spiritual energy left by the imugi wasn’t enough?
The guardian spirit hadn’t expected that energy to restore all its former strength. The Water God Dragon’s earlier mutation had left it with little energy to give.
The demonic qi is too strong. Strong enough to suppress even the sacred stone’s power.
The demonic qi had already spread beyond the Inner Palace and was encroaching on the Outer Palace.

The guardian spirit had brought the beasts of the Sacred Land with it. But if they, too, fell under the demonic qi’s influence while the sacred stone weakened, the situation would spiral out of control.
No. It was already as bad as it could get.
Nearly a thousand mutants, wholly under the demonic qi’s influence, surrounded them without leaving a gap. And the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had survived to come after them.
At this rate...
The guardian spirit’s expression darkened. Then Jin Taekyung spoke, his voice weak.
“Go.”
—What?
“You’ve worked hard. You’ve been through enough.”
Jin Taekyung met its wide blue-white eyes and struggled to his feet, using White Flame as a cane.
“That’s enough. Get out and save the people. Get them as far away from this goddamn place as you can, as fast as you can.”
—How can you say that now...?

“I guarantee it. No matter how fast you are, I won’t last long if you take me with you. I’ll probably start whining for you to put me down in less than half a shichen. I’ll die if I don’t circulate my qi.”
The words were playful, but the judgment behind them wasn’t. The guardian spirit fell silent.
Jin Taekyung grinned.
“So go. Before it’s too late.”
He turned to face the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. His eyes looked ready to go dark at any moment; hers burned blood-red with fury.
“All right. I’ll come quietly, so let’s stop this. Lord of Heaven or some dogshit lord, let’s go see him.”
Instead of answering, she raised her hand.
Swish, spit!
Finger Qi shot toward him like a beam of light and tore the back of his neck. Jin Taekyung shrugged as if it were nothing.
“If you’re angry, just say so. I’ve lost enough blood already. What if I die on the way?”
“That would be troublesome,” she said coldly.
“Now we’re finally talking—”
“You mustn’t die that easily. I’m going to tear you apart slowly with my own hands.”
“...I guess we’re not exactly communicating. What are you planning to do about the fallout?”
“It’ll be fine. The Lord of Heaven will be pleased if I bring him the divine artifact. The White Tiger’s pelt will be a bonus.”
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress smiled brightly and opened her hand.
Kwoooong—!
A tremendous rumble swept across the Nanman Beast Palace.

In its place was a hand covered in fine wrinkles and age spots, as dry and thin as the branch of a dying tree.
“Ah.
Aah...”
Tears welled in her eyes, red with burst blood vessels.
This couldn’t be happening.
It couldn’t.
She had been more beautiful than anyone in the world.
She was supposed to be beautiful.
But the great art she had cultivated for nearly a century had been broken, and her old, ugly appearance had returned like a curse.
Trembling with shock and rage, she realized that the aging she had kept at bay was not the only curse to come upon her.
It hurts.
Only when sudden agony made her look down at herself did she understand.
Flesh had been torn from her side as though an invisible beast had bitten it away.
One arm was gone entirely.
And half her face had melted in the tremendous heat.
Her eyes flew wide.
It was impossible.
It should never have happened.
The wound in her side could heal.
A skilled enough practitioner could even reattach her arm without leaving a scar.
But not her face.
Unless she followed the same path as the Blood Lord she so despised, those terrible burns would leave their mark.
“No.
This... this can’t...”
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress stopped short.
Someone had appeared in her blood-red eyes, now wet with tears.
Jin Taekyung.
She could see him.
And feel him.
After the dazzling flash that had erased everything, he was left with no strength, little more than an empty shell.
That insignificant creature had stolen her youth and beauty.
A single thought seized her.
Kill him.
At that moment, her mind, muddled by countless emotions, turned cold.
The monster who had lived for an age wrapped herself in darkness and moved forward without hesitation.
Scuff.
Scuff.
Crack.
With every step, the energy pouring from her body crushed everything around her.
She had lost her youth, but she still had the strength to kill him.
The bleeding from her side and arm had stopped, and her battered insides were slowly settling.
If the sudden return of age was a curse, then the demonic qi pouring from the rift, growing denser by the moment, was a blessing.
It would let her tear apart Jin Taekyung, who could barely stand, and the reeking old beast in front of him.
—Stop.
Ssssss.
Light spread from the guardian spirit as its thought rang out.
The thousand mutants packed around it crouched low, but the Southern Heaven Demon Empress kept walking.
Bang!
A palm strike shot forward without the slightest hesitation.
Darkness mixed with blood-red Force pressed down on the sacred stone’s light and engulfed Jin Taekyung.
Boom!
The ground burst apart with a deafening crash.
In that instant, the guardian spirit bit Jin Taekyung by the nape and darted away like lightning, releasing a low growl.
—The sacred stone...
It left the thought unfinished, but the truth was cruelly clear.
Rumble...
A faint trembling came from inside its mouth.
Like an old man facing a young man in his prime, the sacred stone was losing strength even now.
So was the White Tiger that had guarded it for so many years.
Even the spiritual energy left by the imugi wasn’t enough?
The guardian spirit hadn’t expected that energy to restore all its former strength.
The Water God Dragon’s earlier mutation had left it with little energy to give.
The demonic qi is too strong.
Strong enough to suppress even the sacred stone’s power.
The demonic qi had already spread beyond the Inner Palace and was encroaching on the Outer Palace.
The guardian spirit had brought the beasts of the Sacred Land with it.
But if they, too, fell under the demonic qi’s influence while the sacred stone weakened, the situation would spiral out of control.
No.
It was already as bad as it could get.
Nearly a thousand mutants, wholly under the demonic qi’s influence, surrounded them without leaving a gap.
And the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had survived to come after them.
At this rate...
The guardian spirit’s expression darkened.
Then Jin Taekyung spoke, his voice weak.
“Go.”
—What?
“You’ve worked hard.
You’ve been through enough.”
Jin Taekyung met its wide blue-white eyes and struggled to his feet, using White Flame as a cane.
“That’s enough.
Get out and save the people.
Get them as far away from this goddamn place as you can, as fast as you can.”
—How can you say that now...?
“I guarantee it.
No matter how fast you are, I won’t last long if you take me with you.
I’ll probably start whining for you to put me down in less than half a shichen.
I’ll die if I don’t circulate my qi.”
The words were playful, but the judgment behind them wasn’t.
The guardian spirit fell silent.
Jin Taekyung grinned.
“So go.
Before it’s too late.”
He turned to face the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
His eyes looked ready to go dark at any moment; hers burned blood-red with fury.
“All right.
I’ll come quietly, so let’s stop this.
Lord of Heaven or some dogshit lord, let’s go see him.”
Instead of answering, she raised her hand.
Swish, spit!
Finger Qi shot toward him like a beam of light and tore the back of his neck.
Jin Taekyung shrugged as if it were nothing.
“If you’re angry, just say so.
I’ve lost enough blood already.
What if I die on the way?”
“That would be troublesome,” she said coldly.
“Now we’re finally talking—”
“You mustn’t die that easily.
I’m going to tear you apart slowly with my own hands.”
“...I guess we’re not exactly communicating.
What are you planning to do about the fallout?”
“It’ll be fine.
The Lord of Heaven will be pleased if I bring him the divine artifact.
The White Tiger’s pelt will be a bonus.”
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress smiled brightly and opened her hand.
Kwoooong—!
A tremendous rumble swept across the Nanman Beast Palace.

chapters.title: Chapter 704
paragraphs: The Southern Heaven Demon Empress was certain.
Give her the time it took to drink a cup of tea, and she could end this tiresome battle. That was all the time the brat she wanted to tear apart and his beast had left to live.
But as she raised her hand to strike, that certainty cracked.
Kwoooong—!

A vast rumble rose from somewhere. At the same time, the air rippled and the wind stopped. Sensing the powerful wave of qi coming from beyond the thick darkness, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress clenched her teeth.
This is...!
A master. One strong enough to resist the demonic qi’s influence.

The thought and her response came in the same instant. Realizing something had gone wrong, she released the internal energy gathered in her remaining hand and shouted—not toward the approaching master, but toward the person she had to kill before it was too late.
“Kill him!”
Kwooooooosh!
A vast palm force tinged with murky light tore through the air. It was not the only thing hurtling toward Jin Taekyung.
Nearly a thousand humans and beasts—mutants made more vicious and powerful by the demonic qi—lunged together with a chorus of shrieks.
Pap-pap. Shhhhhk!
—Krrk, kraaaah!

Teeth harder and sharper than steel glinted in the darkness. The mutants charged with strength and speed far beyond what their bodies had once possessed, while the palm force streaked above their heads like a meteor.
All of it bore down on the two figures standing in the dark beneath a faint glow.
No. It was meant to tear apart the one human who had dealt the Southern Heaven Demon Empress an insult she could never wash away.
Jin Taekyung watched it come. The corner of his weary mouth twisted.
“Too bad. You’re already too late.”
Only a shichen ago, those words had come from her lips. Now they came back to her, thick with mockery.
Boom! Fwoosh!
The darkness on either side burst apart as though the demonic qi itself had exploded. Green Force, the color of forest and leaves, surged through the opening and smashed everything in its path.
No—it tore into them and devoured them.
Like a wild beast.
Krrrunch!

The earth shook. Compressed air burst outward, sweeping away the wind laced with bitter demonic qi. The green Force ripped the limbs from the mutants rushing in on every side, then opened its jaws toward the immense palm force.
Kwaaang! Rumble!
Light mingled where the attacks collided. After a deafening roar that made it seem as though the sky itself had split apart, a terrifying shock wave shook the surrounding space.
Beyond it, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress stared wide-eyed at her palm force as it faded away helplessly.
They canceled each other out?
Who was she?

One of the Lord of Heaven’s most loyal servants. A master he trusted enough to place Southern Heaven in her hands. In her own eyes, she was among the greatest and most exalted beings beneath heaven and earth.
Jin Taekyung had cost her a considerable amount of strength, but she could still tear an ordinary Supreme Peak master apart in moments.
And yet their attacks had canceled each other out.
She did not want to believe it. But she was not stupid enough to deny what had happened before her eyes, nor did it take long to guess who had arrived.
It has to be him.
Fist Force of that magnitude. The massive figure taking shape through the settling dust.
Her voice came out cold.
“...Yayul Cheok. The Beast Miao King.”
Boom!
She swept her sleeve aside. The wind from it cleared the dust, revealing a giant of a man whose half-gray beard hung like an old tiger’s mane.
Behind his towering frame, a young man leaned against the massive body of the White Tiger.
“You’re late. Very late.”
Jin Taekyung’s voice was faint. The Beast Miao King answered calmly.
“I’m sorry. I came too late.”
“I almost died out here.”
“That won’t happen.”
He thrust out a hand as fast as lightning.
Bang.

The sound was like a drum bursting. Jin Taekyung’s body jerked, and the guardian spirit hurriedly caught him as he started to collapse. It bared its teeth on instinct, but Jin shook his head and opened his mouth.
“Urk. Ueeecch!”
Shwaaaaaak!
Dark red blood poured from him, soaking the guardian spirit’s broad back. Feeling the hot, dead blood run through its fur like vomit, it muttered.
“What a wonderful feeling.”
“Don’t look at me like that, large human. I am—”
The guardian spirit was about to continue addressing the wide-eyed Beast Miao King when Jin Taekyung pushed himself upright. Having spat out the dead blood, he sounded much more alive.
“Not exactly the best time for introductions, but say hello. This is Whitey. I just adopted him.”
“Adopted? How dare you!”
“Oh. So Whitey’s fine?”
“You bastard!”
Jin grinned as the guardian spirit bristled, forgetting the danger around them. Then the Beast Miao King suddenly swept both hands outward.
Boom!
Green Fist Force struck a murky palm force in midair. At the same instant, the transparent spearhead that had hung limp moved.
Slash!
A dozen or so mutants trying to exploit the opening were cut apart before they could scream.
Another group rushed at Jin’s back as he briefly staggered. They saw the enormous forepaw waiting for them.
Whoosh! Crunch!
Blood spurted like a fountain. Severed limbs tumbled across the ground.
The guardian spirit let out a low growl. Jin stood back-to-back with it, raised White Flame, and pointed its spearhead in one direction.
“And the fucking bitch who interrupted while someone else was talking... You know her, right?”
The Beast Miao King nodded. An ugly old woman was reflected in his dark eyes.
“Yes. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress.”
His voice seemed to boil with anger that could not be hidden.
Countless mutants still surrounded them. The demonic qi had taken their original forms from them, but they were the tribespeople of this land—the people he had cherished more than anyone.
No. Had cherished was wrong. He still did.
The ache that had started in his chest the moment he saw them was proof enough.
I hoped I wouldn’t be too late.

He had run until he could hardly breathe, wringing every last measure of strength from himself to get here. Then he had seen the Nanman Beast Palace in the distance, engulfed in darkness and flame, and known.
He was already too late.
To reach this place, he had passed more than mountains and plains, rivers and valleys.
He had seen a hellscape.

It brought back fragments of the Great Faction War, that horror from decades ago, and cut his heart to pieces. The bodies of tribespeople who had failed to escape lay crushed beneath fallen buildings. Streets that had rung with music and laughter not long ago belonged to surging darkness and fire.
And now the one most responsible for that hellscape stood before him.
“I swear this as the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace.”
Fire blazed in his reddened eyes. There was no trace of the man who loved a drink and good company, who laughed heartily when he had had his fill.

Decades ago, he had led ten thousand warriors north against the Demonic Cult’s Hundred Thousand Demonic Disciples and earned his place among the Ten Kings. Now that giant spoke in a voice cold as steel.
“I will tear your limbs apart piece by piece.”
Jin poked his head out from behind the Beast Miao King’s broad back.
“Thought I’d save you some trouble. I’ve already cut off one of her arms.”
He was still pale, but color was returning to his face. The hand around his spear no longer trembled. He drew a deep breath and stepped forward.
Scuff.
Just one step.
The mutants crowding every side flinched, but none dared charge. Their reason had been paralyzed, yet the mutation had sharpened their instincts. They sensed the change in the air.
They sensed, too, that the master who should have ordered them forward had fallen silent.
Their instincts were right. For the second time since coming to Nanman, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress felt threatened.
This isn’t good...
Ordinarily, she would have snorted at the thought. The Beast Miao King might be one of the Ten Kings, but he could not have closed the gap between them.
Now things were different.

Jin Taekyung’s One Strike had been powerful enough to freeze her with fear for an instant. It had cost her an arm and much of her strength. With her in this condition, the Beast Miao King was a threat.
Jin had recovered a little strength with his help, and the guardian spirit still held considerable qi. The mutants were no match for either of them.
But they were not the only reason her unease kept growing.
Why? Why haven’t they appeared?

Like the Western Heaven Demon Lord, who had died in Sichuan a few months ago, she commanded a sizable force: roughly five hundred subordinates. Perhaps not enough to be called an army, but they were handpicked fighters, hidden from Nanman’s people and held ready for precisely such a situation.
Yet—
They still haven’t come.
More than half a shichen had passed since the rift opened. Only the Masked Man had appeared on time.
By now, over half her force should have crossed through the Moving Formation engraved on the mirror she had given Baeksang. The rest should have sealed the Outer Palace gates from outside.
Even if something went wrong with the Moving Formation, they should have shown up somehow by now.
She pressed her lips together. Then the ground beneath her feet began to tremble.
Creak. Creak-creak.
A faint smile touched her face. Her subordinates had finally arrived.

She had selected every one of those five hundred fighters herself. They practiced demonic martial arts, and the demonic qi would make them stronger still. No matter how many beasts remained in the Outer Palace, they could not block their way.
“Tear my limbs off? You?”
She let out a short laugh. Seeing Jin Taekyung’s and the Beast Miao King’s faces stiffen, she could not help laughing again.
“I’ll admit it. You fought better than I expected. No—no one could have imagined it would come to this.”
She kept the rest to herself.
But now it’s over.
As though nothing had happened, she began to walk lightly forward. The taut air seemed to ease. Then the Beast Miao King spoke.
“Someone did.”
“What?”
“Someone foresaw this. He walked a path he couldn’t turn back from and tormented himself with guilt, but he never gave up hope. Not until the very end.”
She blinked, unable to make sense of it.
The Beast Miao King spun like lightning and drove out a fist.
Kwoooooosh!
Green Force punched through the darkness, carving a path.
Along it came the reinforcements who would decide the battle’s outcome.
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
A company clad in white garments and armor emerged. The man at their head bowed to the Beast Miao King.
“Wang Ho, Commander of the Baekcheon Unit... pays his respects to the Palace Lord.”

chapters.title: Chapter 705
paragraphs: “Wang Ho, Commander of the Baekcheon Unit, pays his respects to the Palace Lord.”
The moment the Southern Heaven Demon Empress heard those words, she thought the world had stopped.
Time slowed. Everything around her surged forward like a wave and filled her vision.
Clothing and armor as white as snow, instead of the pitch-black martial uniforms that were practically Dark Heaven’s symbol.
Three hundred warriors whose dress and features marked them unmistakably as Bai people. Beasts beside them, growling low.
And then...
Flap.
A flag stirred in a breeze from somewhere. Three characters had been scrawled across it in a bold, soaring hand.
Baekcheon Unit.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s pupils trembled.

She couldn’t understand why those characters beneath the endless dark sky unsettled her so deeply. Why a piece of old silk, yellowed by the years and fluttering in the wind, should make her uneasy at all.
Or why a memory she had once dismissed was returning now.
Demon Empress. Baeksang is secretly training warriors and beasts. They’re all Bai people, and after a thorough investigation, we found that most of them...
Are orphans who lost their parents in the Great Faction War or the plague. They disappeared after the great fire several years ago.
Y-you knew?
For a long time. He’s set up a refuge somewhere called Wenshan, hasn’t he?
Th-then, may this lowly servant dare ask the Demon Empress just one thing?
You want to know why I’m watching when I know what he’s doing.
Forgive my impertinence, but yes. Even now, a considerable portion of the vast supplies flowing to Baeksang is being used to train warriors. If he should ever harbor different intentions...
So what? It’s amusing.
Pardon?
Think about it. What could possibly change just because he feeds elixirs to orphans who have nowhere to go and teaches them a few forms of martial arts?
Th-that...

Scrap iron is scrap iron, however many times you hammer it. You’ll never make a divine weapon that way. But I rather enjoy watching Baeksang struggle over his scrap iron, dreaming of what it might become. And imagining the look on his face when hope turns to despair.
Besides, Baeksang will never turn against me. Even if he does, that will only give me something else to enjoy.
That conversation had taken place more than a dozen years ago.
The spy, who had become a Great Chieftain at a young age, had struck his forehead against the floor until it bled, then left. In time, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress forgot about him.
No—she erased him from her mind.
What happened in a remote mountain valley where no one set foot gradually ceased to interest her, too.
It was too insignificant to keep watching.
It was only natural. She held Baeksang’s leash, and even if he cut it himself and charged at her, she possessed more than enough power to crush him to death in an instant.
Such arrogance, such ease, belonged only to those with overwhelming strength.
Only now did the Southern Heaven Demon Empress realize that Baeksang, the hunting dog she had believed incapable of betraying her, had torn off his leash.
Her own arrogance had brought them here.
“...Baekcheon. The Baekcheon Unit.”
She spoke the words like a groan.
While she dreamed of the dark sky to come, someone else had looked toward a sky strewn with white clouds.
No. He had carried that sky in his heart.

Even as he followed another’s orders like a hunting dog forced into a leash he had never wanted, he must have written those characters with guilt and anger at knowing his path was wrong and being unable to leave it.
On that yellowed, worn silk that had once been dazzlingly white, he must have drawn the sky he had wanted to see.
And the wish he could not fulfill with his own hands had been passed on to one person.
“Leave. I have already cleared the East Gate. The guards at the underground prison will be more lax than usual, so the Han Chinese should be able to escape this place without much difficulty.”
At the low voice echoing through the air, Jin Taekyung looked between the Baekcheon Unit and the Beast Miao King, his eyes wide. A groan escaped him.
“No way.”
It was as though scattered pieces were slowly falling into place.
His eyes bloodshot and fixed on the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, the Beast Miao King continued reciting what someone had told him a few days earlier.
“Go straight to Wenshan, northeast of here. Show this to the people on its highest peak.”
Whoosh. Clatter.
Something flew from the Beast Miao King’s hand, arced through the air, and landed at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s feet.
It was half of a jade identification token. The only proof of authority that could move the Baekcheon Unit.
“I’ve gone down a path I can’t turn back from. I can’t stop of my own will, and even if I did, it wouldn’t be enough to stop the grand scheme.”
The Beast Miao King’s voice trembled.
He could almost see his sworn brother’s face in that dimly lit room. Baeksang had cut through his own wrist—a wrist as precious to a swordsman as his life.
And he could hear Baeksang’s last words.

That was all. The sworn elder brother had left, and the sworn younger brother had remained.

Three days later, the Baekcheon Unit knelt before the token in the Beast Miao King’s hand. They remembered the charge given to them by the man who had become their father and teacher after they lost their homes and families.
If someone other than me brings you this token one day... he is the lord you must serve.
And so the three hundred warriors who had lain hidden in a remote mountain valley for decades descended with the Beast Miao King.
Rumors of warriors racing across the wilderness spread quietly, but swiftly.
The Palace Lord has returned!
Our Dai people will join the Palace Lord! Protect this land from the traitors who colluded with Dark Heaven, usurped the Palace Lord’s position, and betrayed Nanman!
Mobilize every warrior. Send out messengers, now!
As many as ten thousand warriors headed for the Nanman Beast Palace, leaving behind a vacuum of equal size.
The tribal chieftains who had rebelled against Baeksang and left the Nanman Beast Palace led their warriors to join their true Palace Lord.
You...
We’ll follow you to the death, Palace Lord.
One day passed. Then another.
By then, they had become a vast army. They were racing toward the Nanman Beast Palace when they encountered an unexpected enemy.
Or so they thought.
The force numbered roughly three thousand. Then the Bai man at its head stepped forward alone and knelt.
We surrender.
The Beast Miao King asked why. The Bai man answered with a dazed look.
The being who guards the divine artifact opened our eyes—all of us. It showed us which path was right and which choice we had to make.
The Beast King Stone was a legend. A miracle.
And that day, the Bai man—no, the Captain of the Guards—was not the only one who witnessed the wondrous sight on Ailao Mountain.
That Han Chinese bastard... No. Great Hero Jin Taekyung told us to find you at once, Palace Lord. He said everything would be lost if we were any later.
Once the three thousand warriors who had surrounded Ailao Mountain joined them, nothing could stop them. Not rugged mountains, deep swamps, or jungles thick with undergrowth.
Nor could the group that had realized something was wrong and hurried toward the Nanman Beast Palace.
“I had to rush to the Inner Palace and didn’t see it through to the end. How did the battle turn out?”

The Beast Miao King asked without taking his eyes off the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. Wang Ho, Commander of the Baekcheon Unit, wiped blood from his cheek. The heat of battle still burned in his eyes.
“Two hundred casualties on our side.”
“And theirs?”
“Annihilated. We killed or captured every last one.”
Jin Taekyung, who had watched it all unfold, gave a short laugh. He didn’t know every detail, but he had a good idea how things had gone.
“Old hag. You’re fucked, huh?”
Crunch.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress clenched her teeth before she could stop herself. The metallic tang of blood filled her mouth.
Dead. All of them.
Five hundred elite fighters, wiped out.
The thousands who had arrived with the Beast Miao King had crushed her last move—the one that could have turned this dangerous situation around in an instant.
No. This can’t be happening...!
Fury boiled up inside her. Worse than the fury was the unease, the cold creeping through her chest.
The two characters filling the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s mind now were death.
...Die? I’m going to die? Me?
She couldn’t believe it.

She had lived for more than a hundred and thirty years. Since her youth, she had stopped at nothing to become beautiful and stay young. She had cast aside every human scruple countless times, building formidable martial prowess along the way.
She had never imagined that, if her life ended, it would end at someone else’s hands.
Now that absurd possibility was becoming real. Drawing closer before her eyes.
With killing intent as sharp as the point of an awl.
Thoom.
Hundreds of feet stepped forward at once, their combined impact spreading as a tremendous echo.
Grrrr.
The beasts carrying warriors on their backs growled low.
Light flowed from the largest White Tiger at their center, enveloping them all and shielding them from the darkness.
Fwoooosh.
Faint but unmistakable light. The mutants sensed the power of the sacred stone that had shared this land’s fate for ages, and instinctively backed away.
Or perhaps they sensed something else, too.
They could not win against these people. Their bodies had grown fiercer and stronger, but it would make no difference. Not even if the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, who led them, joined the fight.
—Krrk.
—Kk.
Their cries sounded almost like groans. Nearly a thousand monsters stood there, as hideous as the sounds they made.
The Baekcheon Unit did not waver. They leveled weapons still wet with their previous enemies’ blood at the mutants.
Shing.
Hundreds of spears and blades flashed in the dim light.
Decades ago, someone had called these warriors scrap iron and treated them as a diversion. She had been wrong.
No. Perhaps she had been right back then.
But the scrap iron had been hammered, cooled, and heated again and again until it became something new.
Hard steel. Then keen blades capable of cutting even steel.
And only one man in all the world could wield the blade called the Baekcheon Unit.
“Give the order, Palace Lord. No...”
A middle-aged man whose black hair had turned half gray with the passage of time—the Commander of the Baekcheon Unit, Wang Ho—spoke in a weighty voice.
“My lord.”
His gaze turned, and every member of the Baekcheon Unit looked the same way.
The giant standing before them like an iron tower—the Beast Miao King, Yayul Cheok—opened his mouth.
“I’m going forward. Follow me.”
“As you command.”
That was all.
In the next instant, they moved as one. Like a wave rolling in from the open sea. Like an arrow loosed from its bow. Like a bolt of lightning.
At their head, an enormous White Tiger shot forward beside the Beast Miao King.
—Kraaaaaaang!
Krrrunch!
Its roar shook heaven and earth. Its forepaw swept through everything in its way, tearing and crushing.
Gripping the guardian spirit’s mane, white enough to match his own pallor, Jin Taekyung muttered,
“No, fuck. I’m exhausted enough to die, so why am I—”
His dismay at the sudden acceleration—and his suspicion that the guardian spirit might be a Korean-made tiger—vanished the next moment.
To be precise, they had no choice but to vanish.
Gooooong.
The air froze. At the center of a whirlwind rising as it drew in the surrounding darkness, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress lifted her head.
Jin yanked the guardian spirit’s mane backward at lightning speed.
His ace in the hole: reverse gear.
The guardian spirit understood his intention perfectly and launched itself.
Forward.
Whoosh!
—Hold on tight, human!
No, fuck.
