chapters.title: Chapter 706
paragraphs: A thought occurred to me.
Can’t I sit this one out now?
The greater good. A spirit of self-sacrifice. Laying down your life for others. All that stuff.
All good things. Heartwarming, if a little embarrassing to say out loud. But...
Haven’t I done enough of that already?

I had come all the way to this cursed continent-sized greenbelt for the greater good, and I had fought while wearing my spirit of self-sacrifice over my entire body—so thoroughly that it might as well have been tattooed onto me.
Actually, considering how many battles I’d fought in Nanman, just saying I’d fought didn’t do it justice.
I’d fought a fucking lot.
In forests. In fields. In swamps and jungles.
I’d driven my spear into spiders the size of houses. I’d answered the Nanman warriors who kept coming for glory with fire and fists.
If only it had ended there.
At the Poisonblood Grounds, I’d faced two Supreme Peak masters at once. Before I’d even recovered from that, I’d had to fight the monster known as the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
And then there was One Annihilation.
One Annihilation. Killing everything in a single strike—that was what the name meant. Lately, though, I’d begun to wonder if everything included me.
What the fuck was I pouring into that one blow? My internal energy or my lifespan?

Still, things had not turned out too badly. Just when I had been wondering whether that was the day I would see the ending of my life, the Beast Miao King and the Baekcheon Unit had appeared. With the Beast Miao King’s help, I had partially recovered from my Internal Injury, and I had also learned that allies were already swarming outside the Inner Palace.
With the battle finally turning in our favor, I could breathe a little easier.
Until one insane tiger suddenly hit the gas.
Whoosh!
No, fuck. Did this bastard live on Frosted Flakes?
I’d noticed it when we first met on Ailao Mountain: the guardian spirit was faster than the three hundred warriors of the Baekcheon Unit. Faster even than the Beast Miao King.
Across the vast Inner Palace, now reduced to ruins, a thousand mutants stood in our way like an iron wall.
The guardian spirit’s silver body shot toward the Southern Heaven Demon Empress beyond them. Its thought rang through my head.
—Hold on tight, human!
Is he trying to kill me...?
At that instant, a massive, murky light erupted above the mutants’ heads.
Kraaaaaaash!
—Duck.
Along with the brief thought, the guardian spirit tilted its body. Its powerful forepaw struck the ground, and its enormous body changed direction at an angle.
Whoosh!
Those instincts, those movements—spiritual creature hardly covered it. Divine beast seemed closer.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s palm strike, packed with tremendous internal energy, missed its target and slammed into the ground.
Boom! Rumble, rumble!
Dust billowed up. Countless fragments came hurtling through it toward us, and I brought White Flame’s spearhead down.
Whoosh!
The spearhead whistled through the air. Debris flung up by the impact crumbled to powder and scattered.
Then—
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
Hundreds of figures riding enormous beasts burst through the darkness and pale dust.
They charged in a triangular wedge, carrying tremendous weight and momentum. At its tip, a half-gray-haired middle-aged man drove out a fist.
The Beast Miao King.
Fwoom! Boom!
No furious shout. No command.
In place of his voice, green Fist Force erupted, crushing dozens of mutants in an instant and opening a gap. Three hundred charging spears drove into it like sharp awls.
Kra-crack!
Blood burst forth. Severed limbs flew high into the air.
One thousand against three hundred. Humans and beasts against monsters.
Slice! Slice!
Whoosh! Stab-stab-stab!
“Guh!”
—Kraaaaaaang!
Screams and the sounds of blades cutting flesh rang out on every side.
The Baekcheon Unit’s charge crushed hundreds of mutants, but a fierce close-quarters battle awaited them. The Beast Miao King shot past it toward the true enemy waiting for him.
“Southern Heaven Demon Empress!”
His body surged forward like a streak of light alongside his roar. A moment later, the aftermath of their collision, carrying a distant flash of light, shook the foundations of the earth.
Boom! Rumble!
Figures and sharpened weapons clashed in a blur. Above them, the darkness slowly gave way before the green Force.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress is already exhausted. The Beast Miao King has the advantage.
But the close-quarters battle wasn’t going nearly as well.

The beasts, made bigger and stronger by mutation, were a match for First Rate masters. The warriors had retained all the martial arts they’d known as humans, and now they moved faster than ever as they went after the Baekcheon Unit.
Like this one.
Whoosh! Slice!
A mutant’s head flew up with a sharp cutting sound.
The Baekcheon warrior who had failed to notice it behind him stared at me, eyes wide.
“No matter how busy you are, you’ve got to watch your back.”
“Thank you. But who are you...?”
The Beast Miao King or the Baekcheon Unit. After a moment’s hesitation between the two, I answered.
“An ally. I’ll take the lead. Follow me.”
I didn’t have much choice.

The Baekcheon Unit could stand against such overwhelming numbers because every single one of its members had reached at least the realm of a Supreme First Rate master. The mutants, whose bodies had been completely consumed by demonic qi, were powerful.
With the Beast Miao King gone from their midst, the guardian spirit and I had to lead the charge.
“...Shit. Now that I think about it, why am I—”
—Is it my imagination, or are you fighting just fine while you complain?
“Be honest. You’ve got a grudge against me, don’t you?”
Crack!

Maybe demonic qi drove the mutant’s ferocity. Maybe it was loyalty to the commander it wanted to protect. Either way, it charged out of the dust and filled my vision—until the guardian spirit crushed it in a single blow.
—A grudge?
“Don’t play dumb, you bastard. You accelerated like your life depended on it because I set fire to Ailao Mountain.”
Kra-crack!
A single sweep of its forepaw tore the heads off four or five mutants. The guardian spirit clicked its tongue—despite being a tiger.
—Ridiculous.
“Are you sure?”
—No.
“Then is this revenge for the Thousand-Year Spider that lived upstairs?”
—What nonsense is that?
“I’ve thought it over, and it’s suspicious as hell. You know what they say. Our friendly neighborhood Thousand-Year Spider... up!”
Stab!
With that shout, I thrust White Flame straight through the head of a tiger that had leaped at us, casting a shadow over the guardian spirit.
Grrrk...
Its cry died away. With the dead tiger still impaled on my spear, I swung it hard.
Fwoom! Crack!
The carcass, weighing well over several hundred geun, flew into other mutants and crushed them.
“If you weren’t holding a grudge, you wouldn’t throw a patient who needs bed rest into a mess like this. That’s my conclusion.”
Whoosh! Slice!
I swept my spear sideways in one fluid motion. Five heads flew along its path.
The headless corpses collapsed at the same speed they had charged. The guardian spirit stared blankly at the sight and muttered,
—I think your idea of a patient differs from mine.
“Are you insane? Can’t you see what shape I’m in?”
—I can. That is why I said it.
“You just don’t understand. My bones ache when I breathe.”
Stab!
—You seem perfectly capable of stabbing everything around you. That hardly makes a convincing argument.
“Damn it. I’m only doing this to stay alive...”
—Do you know something?
“What?”
—For a human, you are remarkably bad at lying.
“What’s that supposed to—”
I didn’t have time to finish.
Crack! Whoosh!
A silver mane wet with blood scattered through the air. The guardian spirit leaped upward after bursting a mutant’s head, then swung its forepaw as it descended.
Its hooklike claws carried blade-sharp wind and an energy that could only be called Force.
Boom! Rumble!
One strike.
Amid the thunderous sound and the vibrations, dozens of mutants were sent flying as bloody pulp, and even more mutants rushed forward to fill the empty space.
Whoosh!
—Kweeeek!
Their movements were swift and fierce, at odds with their grotesque cries. Streams of Sword Energy poured from some of their weapons—proof they had once been renowned warriors even in Nanman.
But—
—Kraaaaaaang!
The guardian spirit existed solely to protect the sacred stone. At the roar of that enormous White Tiger, unlike any anyone had ever seen, the mutants froze.
As though we’d planned it, I brought White Flame down at an angle.
Cut them. All at once.
The three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi were gone. So were the blue-white flames that had once burned around the transparent spearhead.

All I had left now was a body as heavy as waterlogged cotton, along with a small amount of internal energy—so little that I wondered whether it could fill even one handful—and the only divine weapon I could still trust: White Flame.
That was all. Yet I couldn’t explain—
Slice!
Why I kept cutting without pause.
Stab!
And stabbing.
Crack!
And swinging my spear at the mutants.
Why I forced my aching legs to hold on so I wouldn’t fall from the guardian spirit’s back.
No. Perhaps I dimly understood.
Even the meaning behind what the guardian spirit had said to me moments earlier.
“...Damn it.”
The curse escaped me before I could stop it. The guardian spirit laughed softly.
—I told you. You are bad at lying.
—If staying alive were all you wanted, you would never have come here. Yet exhausted as you are, you will not stop fighting.
“Enough. Shut up.”
—Why? Do you pity those who were human like you before they became monsters? Or do you want to kill the vile human who turned them into monsters?
Its thought whispered inside my head. My breath caught, and something hot rose in my chest.
But the hand I thrust forward was still driving my spear toward another mutant’s throat.
Thrust!
The transparent spearhead cut through flesh and bone. Darkness slowly receded from eyes that had been black from edge to edge.
Death took its place.
Thud.
The body collapsed. I stared at the nameless warrior’s grotesquely twisted face and murmured, “Did he feel pain?”
—Yes. Probably.
Crack!
The guardian spirit swung its massive forepaw, killing the mutant leopard that had charged at me and sending it flying like a cannonball, then continued, calm as ever.
—But after that brief pain, a great, warm rest would have been waiting for him. Simply being alive must be agony for them now.
—They do not resent you. So stop blaming yourself, human.
Damn it.
I knew. I’d done my best. I’d risked my life again and again to stop this disaster and come all the way here.
But doing my best didn’t always bring the best result.
I should have stopped it.
In the end, I had failed to stop it. I had saved many people, but I had also failed to save many others.
Ultimately, the only thing I could do was end their lives with everything I had.
Just like now.
Fwoooooosh!
I swung with all my strength. The spearhead tore through the wind and split the air, and my whole body screamed from the toll One Annihilation had taken.
Pain so fierce my vision went white.
But I gritted my teeth and endured it. I sent a single spear packed with terrifying strength and speed toward the people who had once been human like me.
Kra-crack!
The spearhead carved an enormous arc. In its wake, a raging gale filled with dark red blood.
Severed heads and limbs rose into the air. Countless deaths followed. Countless moments of rest.
Ding. Ding. Ding.

The first time I had wanted to cover my ears at the clear ringing of the chimes announcing EXP gained. The first time the sight of my enemies collapsing while spraying blood had felt so unbearably sorrowful.
But I didn’t stop.
Slice. Slice. Slice!
I cut. Cut again. And kept cutting.
Until nothing stood in my way. Until my spearhead passed through empty air.
Fwoom!
The world tilted.
No—the body that could not withstand the force carried by the spearhead tilted.
As I began to roll off the guardian spirit’s back, a rough hand caught me.
“It’s over. Please stop.”
Wang Ho, Commander of the Baekcheon Unit.
Shock rang in his voice. Breathing hard, I looked around.
The Baekcheon Unit had lost more than half its number. Countless bodies lay in pools of blood all around us.
But...
No.
He was wrong.
This fight—today’s disaster—wasn’t over.
Not until one particular person was dead for good.
“Let’s go.”
—...Human.
“We have to finish it.”
At my voice, which slipped through cracked lips, the guardian spirit seemed about to answer. Instead, it pushed its heavy body forward.
Whoosh!
Wind swept over me.
At the end of the road we were traveling, one person was struggling to live despite vomiting blood.
No.
There was a monster.

sentences.text: A thought occurred to me.
Can’t I sit this one out now?
The greater good.
A spirit of self-sacrifice.
Laying down your life for others.
All that stuff.
All good things.
Heartwarming, if a little embarrassing to say out loud.
But...
Haven’t I done enough of that already?

I had come all the way to this cursed continent-sized greenbelt for the greater good, and I had fought while wearing my spirit of self-sacrifice over my entire body—so thoroughly that it might as well have been tattooed onto me.
Actually, considering how many battles I’d fought in Nanman, just saying I’d fought didn’t do it justice.
I’d fought a fucking lot.
In forests.
In fields.
In swamps and jungles.
I’d driven my spear into spiders the size of houses.
I’d answered the Nanman warriors who kept coming for glory with fire and fists.
If only it had ended there.
At the Poisonblood Grounds, I’d faced two Supreme Peak masters at once.
Before I’d even recovered from that, I’d had to fight the monster known as the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
And then there was One Annihilation.
One Annihilation.
Killing everything in a single strike—that was what the name meant.
Lately, though, I’d begun to wonder if everything included me.
What the fuck was I pouring into that one blow?
My internal energy or my lifespan?
Still, things had not turned out too badly.
Just when I had been wondering whether that was the day I would see the ending of my life, the Beast Miao King and the Baekcheon Unit had appeared.
With the Beast Miao King’s help, I had partially recovered from my Internal Injury, and I had also learned that allies were already swarming outside the Inner Palace.
With the battle finally turning in our favor, I could breathe a little easier.
Until one insane tiger suddenly hit the gas.
Whoosh!
No, fuck.
Did this bastard live on Frosted Flakes?
I’d noticed it when we first met on Ailao Mountain: the guardian spirit was faster than the three hundred warriors of the Baekcheon Unit.
Faster even than the Beast Miao King.
Across the vast Inner Palace, now reduced to ruins, a thousand mutants stood in our way like an iron wall.
The guardian spirit’s silver body shot toward the Southern Heaven Demon Empress beyond them.
Its thought rang through my head.
—Hold on tight, human!
Is he trying to kill me...?
At that instant, a massive, murky light erupted above the mutants’ heads.
Kraaaaaaash!
—Duck.
Along with the brief thought, the guardian spirit tilted its body.
Its powerful forepaw struck the ground, and its enormous body changed direction at an angle.
Whoosh!
Those instincts, those movements—spiritual creature hardly covered it.
Divine beast seemed closer.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s palm strike, packed with tremendous internal energy, missed its target and slammed into the ground.
Boom!
Rumble, rumble!
Dust billowed up.
Countless fragments came hurtling through it toward us, and I brought White Flame’s spearhead down.
Whoosh!
The spearhead whistled through the air.
Debris flung up by the impact crumbled to powder and scattered.
Then—
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
Hundreds of figures riding enormous beasts burst through the darkness and pale dust.
They charged in a triangular wedge, carrying tremendous weight and momentum.
At its tip, a half-gray-haired middle-aged man drove out a fist.
The Beast Miao King.
Fwoom!
Boom!
No furious shout.
No command.
In place of his voice, green Fist Force erupted, crushing dozens of mutants in an instant and opening a gap.
Three hundred charging spears drove into it like sharp awls.
Kra-crack!
Blood burst forth.
Severed limbs flew high into the air.
One thousand against three hundred.
Humans and beasts against monsters.
Slice!
Slice!
Whoosh!
Stab-stab-stab!
“Guh!”
—Kraaaaaaang!
Screams and the sounds of blades cutting flesh rang out on every side.
The Baekcheon Unit’s charge crushed hundreds of mutants, but a fierce close-quarters battle awaited them.
The Beast Miao King shot past it toward the true enemy waiting for him.
“Southern Heaven Demon Empress!”
His body surged forward like a streak of light alongside his roar.
A moment later, the aftermath of their collision, carrying a distant flash of light, shook the foundations of the earth.
Boom!
Rumble!
Figures and sharpened weapons clashed in a blur.
Above them, the darkness slowly gave way before the green Force.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress is already exhausted.
The Beast Miao King has the advantage.
But the close-quarters battle wasn’t going nearly as well.
The beasts, made bigger and stronger by mutation, were a match for First Rate masters.
The warriors had retained all the martial arts they’d known as humans, and now they moved faster than ever as they went after the Baekcheon Unit.
Like this one.
Whoosh!
Slice!
A mutant’s head flew up with a sharp cutting sound.
The Baekcheon warrior who had failed to notice it behind him stared at me, eyes wide.
“No matter how busy you are, you’ve got to watch your back.”
“Thank you.
But who are you...?”
The Beast Miao King or the Baekcheon Unit.
After a moment’s hesitation between the two, I answered.
“An ally.
I’ll take the lead.
Follow me.”
I didn’t have much choice.
The Baekcheon Unit could stand against such overwhelming numbers because every single one of its members had reached at least the realm of a Supreme First Rate master.
The mutants, whose bodies had been completely consumed by demonic qi, were powerful.
With the Beast Miao King gone from their midst, the guardian spirit and I had to lead the charge.
“...Shit.
Now that I think about it, why am I—”
—Is it my imagination, or are you fighting just fine while you complain?
“Be honest.
You’ve got a grudge against me, don’t you?”
Crack!
Maybe demonic qi drove the mutant’s ferocity.
Maybe it was loyalty to the commander it wanted to protect.
Either way, it charged out of the dust and filled my vision—until the guardian spirit crushed it in a single blow.
—A grudge?
“Don’t play dumb, you bastard.
You accelerated like your life depended on it because I set fire to Ailao Mountain.”
Kra-crack!
A single sweep of its forepaw tore the heads off four or five mutants.
The guardian spirit clicked its tongue—despite being a tiger.
—Ridiculous.
“Are you sure?”
—No.
“Then is this revenge for the Thousand-Year Spider that lived upstairs?”
—What nonsense is that?
“I’ve thought it over, and it’s suspicious as hell.
You know what they say.
Our friendly neighborhood Thousand-Year Spider... up!”
Stab!
With that shout, I thrust White Flame straight through the head of a tiger that had leaped at us, casting a shadow over the guardian spirit.
Grrrk...
Its cry died away.
With the dead tiger still impaled on my spear, I swung it hard.
Fwoom!
Crack!
The carcass, weighing well over several hundred geun, flew into other mutants and crushed them.
“If you weren’t holding a grudge, you wouldn’t throw a patient who needs bed rest into a mess like this.
That’s my conclusion.”
Whoosh!
Slice!
I swept my spear sideways in one fluid motion.
Five heads flew along its path.
The headless corpses collapsed at the same speed they had charged.
The guardian spirit stared blankly at the sight and muttered,
—I think your idea of a patient differs from mine.
“Are you insane?
Can’t you see what shape I’m in?”
—I can.
That is why I said it.
“You just don’t understand.
My bones ache when I breathe.”
Stab!
—You seem perfectly capable of stabbing everything around you.
That hardly makes a convincing argument.
“Damn it.
I’m only doing this to stay alive...”
—Do you know something?
“What?”
—For a human, you are remarkably bad at lying.
“What’s that supposed to—”
I didn’t have time to finish.
Crack!
Whoosh!
A silver mane wet with blood scattered through the air.
The guardian spirit leaped upward after bursting a mutant’s head, then swung its forepaw as it descended.
Its hooklike claws carried blade-sharp wind and an energy that could only be called Force.
Boom!
Rumble!
One strike.
Amid the thunderous sound and the vibrations, dozens of mutants were sent flying as bloody pulp, and even more mutants rushed forward to fill the empty space.
Whoosh!
—Kweeeek!
Their movements were swift and fierce, at odds with their grotesque cries.
Streams of Sword Energy poured from some of their weapons—proof they had once been renowned warriors even in Nanman.
But—
—Kraaaaaaang!
The guardian spirit existed solely to protect the sacred stone.
At the roar of that enormous White Tiger, unlike any anyone had ever seen, the mutants froze.
As though we’d planned it, I brought White Flame down at an angle.
Cut them.
All at once.
The three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi were gone.
So were the blue-white flames that had once burned around the transparent spearhead.

That was all.
Yet I couldn’t explain—
Slice!
Why I kept cutting without pause.
Stab!
And stabbing.
Crack!
And swinging my spear at the mutants.
Why I forced my aching legs to hold on so I wouldn’t fall from the guardian spirit’s back.
No.
Perhaps I dimly understood.
Even the meaning behind what the guardian spirit had said to me moments earlier.
“...Damn it.”
The curse escaped me before I could stop it.
The guardian spirit laughed softly.

You are bad at lying.

Yet exhausted as you are, you will not stop fighting.

Shut up.”

chapters.title: Chapter 707
paragraphs: The Southern Heaven Demon Empress could not understand.
How had the grand plan she’d been so sure was perfect fallen apart? And why had she been reduced to the humiliation of fighting a mere member of the Ten Kings on equal terms?
But she had no time to dwell on it.
Whoosh!
A fierce rush of air drowned out the wind.
A massive figure surged forward, erasing the space around it. Green Fist Force erupted from the Beast Miao King’s fist, illuminating the world.
Kraaaaaaash!
Not long ago—just two shichen ago—the Southern Heaven Demon Empress would have snorted and knocked that Fist Force aside.
The Beast Miao King was one of the Ten Kings. He might even have been underestimated because he was from Nanman. But he was still unmistakably a step below her.
He had been.
Until someone’s strike took one of her arms and tore away part of her side.
Jin Taekyung.
Merely thinking the name filled her with rage.
Gritting her teeth, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress stepped forward and vanished. The Beast Miao King realized his attack had missed and reacted at once.
Whoosh!
He stood over eight cheok tall, yet he moved like the wind. His tiger eyes, streaming with flame, were already fixed on the Southern Heaven Demon Empress as she rushed toward his side.
Shwaaak!
His hand, as large as a tiger’s forepaw, raked across the air.
Slice!
Blade-sharp wind cut the hem of her robe. In the same instant, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress leaped in close and drove a palm toward him with all her strength.
Whoosh!
The blow should have crushed flesh and burst bones and organs.
Instead, her small, blood-drenched hand met the Beast Miao King’s palm—several times larger than her own.
Boom!
The world shook. Murky internal energy, as though laced with deadly poison, flowed through the point where their palms met and churned the Beast Miao King’s insides.
He swallowed the blood rising in his throat and grinned.
“So this is all you’ve got?”
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s eyes widened.
It was unbelievable. That the Beast Miao King could smile even in a situation like this.
And that her full-strength palm strike had become so pathetically weak.
Blood slipped between her clenched teeth. Then her figure blurred.
Whoosh-whoosh-whoosh—boom!
Compressed air burst outward with each sharp report.
In an instant, her hands and feet struck all over the Beast Miao King’s body like flashes of lightning, jolting his massive frame.
But that was all.
Long years of training in the external arts had made his body as tough as steel. Her blows should long since have left him vomiting blood on his knees, yet they no longer carried their former weight.
No. They were growing weaker.
The demonic qi from the rift was strengthening her, but it could not undo the terrible injuries Jin Taekyung had inflicted. Nor could it steady the mental strength those injuries had shaken.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress realized it before anyone else.
...Tired? Me?
Everything had a limit. At some point, she had forgotten hers. How could she not have? For so many years, no one had pushed her far enough to feel it.
Until now.
Whoosh—crack!
The relentless rush of her attacks stopped. Pain shot through her hand.
Crack.
Bones shifted in the small fist that should have smashed into his chest and burst his heart. The Beast Miao King had caught it in his enormous palm.
He bared his bloodstained teeth.
“I told you. I’d tear off your limbs and kill you.”
His cold voice cut into her ears. Blood vessels burst in her eyes as she stared at him.
She instinctively reached out with her other hand to seize the Beast Miao King by the throat. But then she saw the green Fist Force filling her vision and realized—
Ah.
Someone else had already taken that arm.
Boom!
The world turned upside down. Flung away like a cannonball, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress felt her vision dim.
In the slowed-down world, light and darkness flashed endlessly before her eyes. The sky and the earth traded places, twisting together.
Then came an impact that threatened to grind her entire body to powder.
Kraaaaaaang!
She tore through the mound of Inner Palace ruins and crashed deep into its center, vomiting blood.
“Kweh-heeeeeck!”
Splash!
Dark. Red.
Dark-red blood mixed with pieces of internal organs sprayed across the countless large and small fragments scattered in every direction.
She felt her body trembling along with the horrible pain.
This... This can’t be happening. It can’t.
As that single thought filled her mind, something came into her blurred view.
Thud. Thud.
The rubble shifted. Someone staggered upright beneath it.
Hope glimmered in her unsteady eyes.
That was it. Hope.
“M-Me. Hurry, take me...”
Her voice was barely more than a breath. She reached out a trembling hand toward the figure slowly rising on two legs bent at unnatural angles.
Toward her loyal subordinate, his torn-open neck hanging limp as he awaited a recovery that defied even the words supernatural powers.
“Hurry. Take me as far away from here as you can...”
At this moment, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was more desperate than anyone else in the world.
Her grand plan had achieved only half its aim. Death, which she had never once imagined for herself, loomed before her.
She had to escape. She wanted to live, even if fleeing was the only way. As long as she survived, she could plan what came next.
She could return and carry on her grand plan—her revenge—somewhere else.
But her last hope died as a shadow fell over the Masked Man’s head.
Whoosh. Crack!
It was not the Beast Miao King, Jin Taekyung, or anyone else.
It was simply a massive boulder.
It had probably been dislodged by the force of the impact.

Somewhere in the ruins piled up like a mountain—perhaps even the foundation stone of the Nanman Beast Palace—a massive stone weighing a thousand geun crashed down over the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s final hope.
The Masked Man, who had lost his reason long ago and now did nothing but obey his master’s commands, was crushed beneath the boulder. His limbs twitched.
She stared blankly at him. Then footsteps like thunder reached her ears.
Thud. Thud.
A footfall approached over blood-soaked ground, treading on sand and rubble.
No. Footsteps.
No strange cries or clashing weapons accompanied those unusually loud steps.
Ah.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress raised her head and finally understood.
The fierce battle for the fate of this land—for Nanman—was over.
And along with it, the fate she had carried forward for so many years was also nearing its end.
At the head of the approaching group was the person who had created this entire situation.
Thud.
A blood-soaked beast’s forepaw stepped over the rubble.
The enormous White Tiger stopped three jang away. On its back sat a man whose face she never wanted to see again, not even in a dream.
“Feels like I haven’t seen you in a while... You’ve gotten a lot prettier.”
Whoosh! Thud!
The Finger Qi she fired on instinct grazed Jin Taekyung’s shoulder and pierced the rubble behind him.
He casually rubbed the blood flowing from the cut, then licked his palm, wet with blood.
“Thanks. I was thirsty anyway. Is this what they mean by a grandmother’s love?”
Blood welled up between her clenched teeth.
She gathered every scrap of strength and tried to rise. A dozen or so assault spears flew over Jin Taekyung’s head.
Whiiiiiiish—boom!
She knocked aside the Baekcheon Unit’s spears with a single sweep of her hand, then glared at him, the blood vessels in her eyes bursting.
“How dare you!”
Fwoooooosh!
Her voice, charged with internal energy, shook the air around them. She had lost an arm and suffered severe Internal Injury, but the demonic qi flowing from the rift still lent her power.
But...
Not enough.
Even so, she could not overturn the current situation.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress understood that better than anyone. She knew the desperate reality that had befallen her.
When she saw the Beast Miao King beside Jin Taekyung, she was certain.
I’m going to die.
With her body in ruins, there was nothing she could do. Even if she somehow escaped, thousands of Nanman warriors waited outside.
Certain death.
The words closed around her with a weight she had never imagined. Every thought vanished; the turmoil in her mind fell still.
Then a low hiss of air broke the silence.
Whoosh!
The Beast Miao King. The guardian spirit. Jin Taekyung.
As though they had planned it, all three surged forward like a single gust of wind. They would give her no opening, not even a moment for final words.
They had only one resolve: to cut off the breath of the Fiend known as the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Kraaaaaaaash!
Green Fist Force bore down on the air. Bloodstained teeth tore through the wind. A transparent spearhead, carrying one last handful of internal energy, burned with blue-white hellfire.
She saw it all.
A faint light entered the empty eyes of the old woman who had lost the beauty once called the greatest in the world, as she watched death rush toward her.
Lord of Heaven.
The noblest, most exalted being in the world.
Long ago, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had loved him from the moment she first saw him. She had prostrated herself at his feet and sworn her loyalty.
She would offer her insignificant life for him.
Even if her youth and beauty faded someday, she had promised to remain by his side forever, even if only from a distance.
She had not known then that the day she would give her life would come so soon. Or that a day would come when she could no longer remain near the Lord of Heaven she revered.
But...
Please remember that this lowly woman stood beside you.
If the Lord of Heaven remembered her as a servant who had loved him more than anyone, that would be enough.
If he did, she could gladly burn through the life she had left with a smile.
Just as she was doing at this very moment.
Crack.
In the slowed world, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress heard the rift—a sound only she could hear.
Innate qi.
The purest, most powerful force she had carried since birth awakened. An immense energy surged through her body and gathered in her hand.
Gooooooooong.
Space twisted as though invisible hands were tearing it apart. At the shock on the three faces before her, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress smiled.
No. She tried to.
Thud!
Until a sword thrust out from the heap of ruins behind her and buried itself in her back, emerging from the deep, dark gap between the fallen stones.

I’d tear off your limbs and kill you.”
His cold voice cut into her ears.
Blood vessels burst in her eyes as she stared at him.
She instinctively reached out with her other hand to seize the Beast Miao King by the throat.
But then she saw the green Fist Force filling her vision and realized—
Ah.
Someone else had already taken that arm.
Boom!
The world turned upside down.
Flung away like a cannonball, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress felt her vision dim.
In the slowed-down world, light and darkness flashed endlessly before her eyes.
The sky and the earth traded places, twisting together.
Then came an impact that threatened to grind her entire body to powder.
Kraaaaaaang!
She tore through the mound of Inner Palace ruins and crashed deep into its center, vomiting blood.
“Kweh-heeeeeck!”
Splash!
Dark.
Red.
Dark-red blood mixed with pieces of internal organs sprayed across the countless large and small fragments scattered in every direction.
She felt her body trembling along with the horrible pain.
This...
This can’t be happening.
It can’t.
As that single thought filled her mind, something came into her blurred view.
Thud.
Thud.
The rubble shifted.
Someone staggered upright beneath it.
Hope glimmered in her unsteady eyes.
That was it.
Hope.
“M-Me.
Hurry, take me...”
Her voice was barely more than a breath.
She reached out a trembling hand toward the figure slowly rising on two legs bent at unnatural angles.
Toward her loyal subordinate, his torn-open neck hanging limp as he awaited a recovery that defied even the words supernatural powers.
“Hurry.
Take me as far away from here as you can...”
At this moment, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was more desperate than anyone else in the world.
Her grand plan had achieved only half its aim.
Death, which she had never once imagined for herself, loomed before her.
She had to escape.
She wanted to live, even if fleeing was the only way.
As long as she survived, she could plan what came next.
She could return and carry on her grand plan—her revenge—somewhere else.
But her last hope died as a shadow fell over the Masked Man’s head.
Whoosh.
Crack!
It was not the Beast Miao King, Jin Taekyung, or anyone else.
It was simply a massive boulder.
It had probably been dislodged by the force of the impact.

Somewhere in the ruins piled up like a mountain—perhaps even the foundation stone of the Nanman Beast Palace—a massive stone weighing a thousand geun crashed down over the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s final hope.
The Masked Man, who had lost his reason long ago and now did nothing but obey his master’s commands, was crushed beneath the boulder.
His limbs twitched.
She stared blankly at him.
Then footsteps like thunder reached her ears.
Thud.
Thud.
A footfall approached over blood-soaked ground, treading on sand and rubble.
No.
Footsteps.
No strange cries or clashing weapons accompanied those unusually loud steps.
Ah.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress raised her head and finally understood.
The fierce battle for the fate of this land—for Nanman—was over.
And along with it, the fate she had carried forward for so many years was also nearing its end.
At the head of the approaching group was the person who had created this entire situation.
Thud.
A blood-soaked beast’s forepaw stepped over the rubble.
The enormous White Tiger stopped three jang away.
On its back sat a man whose face she never wanted to see again, not even in a dream.
“Feels like I haven’t seen you in a while...
You’ve gotten a lot prettier.”
Whoosh!
Thud!
The Finger Qi she fired on instinct grazed Jin Taekyung’s shoulder and pierced the rubble behind him.
He casually rubbed the blood flowing from the cut, then licked his palm, wet with blood.
“Thanks.
I was thirsty anyway.
Is this what they mean by a grandmother’s love?”
Blood welled up between her clenched teeth.
She gathered every scrap of strength and tried to rise.
A dozen or so assault spears flew over Jin Taekyung’s head.
Whiiiiiiish—boom!
She knocked aside the Baekcheon Unit’s spears with a single sweep of her hand, then glared at him, the blood vessels in her eyes bursting.
“How dare you!”
Fwoooooosh!
Her voice, charged with internal energy, shook the air around them.
She had lost an arm and suffered severe Internal Injury, but the demonic qi flowing from the rift still lent her power.
But...
Not enough.
Even so, she could not overturn the current situation.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress understood that better than anyone.
She knew the desperate reality that had befallen her.
When she saw the Beast Miao King beside Jin Taekyung, she was certain.
I’m going to die.
With her body in ruins, there was nothing she could do.
Even if she somehow escaped, thousands of Nanman warriors waited outside.
Certain death.
The words closed around her with a weight she had never imagined.
Every thought vanished; the turmoil in her mind fell still.
Then a low hiss of air broke the silence.
Whoosh!
The Beast Miao King.
The guardian spirit.
Jin Taekyung.
As though they had planned it, all three surged forward like a single gust of wind.
They would give her no opening, not even a moment for final words.
They had only one resolve: to cut off the breath of the Fiend known as the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Kraaaaaaaash!
Green Fist Force bore down on the air.
Bloodstained teeth tore through the wind.
A transparent spearhead, carrying one last handful of internal energy, burned with blue-white hellfire.
She saw it all.
A faint light entered the empty eyes of the old woman who had lost the beauty once called the greatest in the world, as she watched death rush toward her.
Lord of Heaven.
The noblest, most exalted being in the world.
Long ago, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had loved him from the moment she first saw him.
She had prostrated herself at his feet and sworn her loyalty.
She would offer her insignificant life for him.
Even if her youth and beauty faded someday, she had promised to remain by his side forever, even if only from a distance.
She had not known then that the day she would give her life would come so soon.
Or that a day would come when she could no longer remain near the Lord of Heaven she revered.
But...
Please remember that this lowly woman stood beside you.
If the Lord of Heaven remembered her as a servant who had loved him more than anyone, that would be enough.
If he did, she could gladly burn through the life she had left with a smile.
Just as she was doing at this very moment.
Crack.
In the slowed world, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress heard the rift—a sound only she could hear.
Innate qi.
The purest, most powerful force she had carried since birth awakened.
An immense energy surged through her body and gathered in her hand.
Gooooooooong.
Space twisted as though invisible hands were tearing it apart.
At the shock on the three faces before her, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress smiled.
No.
She tried to.
Thud!
Until a sword thrust out from the heap of ruins behind her and buried itself in her back, emerging from the deep, dark gap between the fallen stones.

chapters.title: Chapter 708
paragraphs: Thrust!
The unmistakable sound of a blade piercing flesh reached the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s ears, and the world around her stopped.
All she could feel was the cold blade driven deep into her back.
Why? Who? How?
Questions crowded her mind through the distant pain.
Instinct moved her before reason could. She spun at lightning speed and thrust out a palm.
Whoosh!
Innate qi. A portion of the immense internal energy gathered in her hand struck the collapsed ruins.
Kraaaaaaash!
Thousands upon thousands of geun of rubble exploded outward with a tremendous roar.
Among the flying fragments was the answer to her questions.
“Kugh!”
A figure was flung helplessly away by the blast.
One sleeve of his blood- and dust-stained white robe hung empty. Blood gushed from the wound in his chest, an injury beyond recovery.
But his cold, steady gaze remained fixed on the Southern Heaven Demon Empress until the very end.
His eyes, filled with rage and regret beyond measure, seemed to tell her he had waited a very long time for this moment.
“Baeksang...!”
His name burst from her lips like a scream. At the same instant, she felt wind rushing at her from behind, and her eyes widened.
Shwaaaaaak!
Baeksang’s unexpected strike had cost her no more than a moment.
But that single blink had given someone else an advantage—and dealt her a terrible blow.
Crack.
Swallowing the thick blood in her mouth, she wrenched the sword from her back and turned at lightning speed.
Three figures swept toward her like a gale.
The Beast Miao King. The guardian spirit. Jin Taekyung.
At the sight of them, the qi and blood Baeksang’s strike had thrown into turmoil convulsed inside her.
She felt the flame of mutual destruction, kindled with her own life as fuel, flicker like a candle in the wind.
Pain surged through her again. Her vision blurred.
She could not stop. She must not stop.
Kill.
Clinging to that single thought, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress gritted her teeth and extended her hand.
Toward the three figures already upon her. Toward the enemies who dared obstruct the great work the exalted Lord of Heaven sought to accomplish.
Gooooooooong.
In the slowed world, immense energy flowed through her blood-soaked hand and into the blade. The sword, now in its new master’s grasp, swept down at an angle.
Shwaaaaaak!
Through the warping space, she saw three pairs of eyes slowly widen. Green Force surged up like an iron wall to shield them all.
But...
It’s over.
With that thought, unheard by anyone else, a blinding flash swallowed everything.
Fwoooooosh!
No one in that land had ever seen an explosion like it.
Fwoom! Ruuuuumble!
Yohi and Muyaho saw it as they evacuated the survivors alongside countless wild beasts.
The thousands of warriors surrounding the darkened Inner Palace saw it, their blood-soaked weapons held ready.
So did the tribespeople running toward the hills beyond the Outer Palace, gasping for breath.
One word came to them all.
A cataclysm.
Nothing else could describe it. The blinding flash and violent tremors reached far beyond the Inner Palace. Everyone who felt their force froze.
No—they trembled with a fear that seemed to bind their very souls.
The groans rising from every direction all turned toward one place: the Nanman Beast Palace they had left behind.
Boom. Rumble.
It was collapsing.
The pavilions and homes their ancestors had spent long years building with blood and sweat—the place where they had been born and raised—were on the verge of collapsing before their eyes.
What more was there to say?
Thousands upon thousands stared at the Nanman Beast Palace, trying to take in one last sight of their beloved home before it was lost to them forever.
But soon, their despair gave way to hope.
Ruuuuumble...

The tremors gradually subsided. The ground stopped collapsing before it could swallow the Nanman Beast Palace whole. The houses and pavilions that had swayed on the brink of falling remained standing, though they leaned.
An unimaginable disaster. Then a miracle.
The people who witnessed it were overcome with relief and joy. But the person who had unleashed that disaster with nothing more than a human body shook with pain and rage.
“T-This can’t... Kueeegh!”
Drip. Drip.
Dark-red blood spilled down from the corner of her mouth.
Everything within a radius of fifty jang had been shattered and hurled away. Standing in the empty space left behind, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress looked around with blood-red eyes.
One strike. One sure chance.
She had not cared if it killed her. There was no returning alive now, and even if she lived, she would have to spend the rest of her days in this old, hideous body.
And yet she had survived.
She should have been blown apart and killed in the explosion, after swallowing everything in its path. Instead, she had survived. The humiliation burned.
“Baeksang! You bastard. How dare you!”
Rumble!
A wave of qi burst from her with the roar, shaking the space around her.
Baeksang’s unexpected strike. That single thrust of his sword, made with what must have been the last of his strength, had changed everything.
The turmoil it caused within her had kept her from pouring all her innate qi into the attack. She had escaped death in the explosion because of it.
So had they.
“Cough.”
Thud.
Several dozen jang away, a graying giant dropped to one knee and vomited blood mixed with pieces of his organs.
Countless fragments studded his body. Behind his broad back, she saw the enormous White Tiger and a young man lying drenched in blood.
“Yayul Cheok, you bastard...!”
Blood and phlegm rattled in her throat. The Beast Miao King’s actions in the final instant flashed through her mind.
He had stepped in front of Jin Taekyung without the slightest hesitation.
Why?
She could not understand why Yayul Cheok, who had earned a place among the Ten Kings in the distant Central Plains, would make that choice.
And that stinking beast had done the same.
Risk their only lives? For a mere brat?
The question brought her one certainty.
Jin Taekyung. I have to kill him, whatever it takes.

The Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, a man little different from the king of a nation, and the White Tiger that bore a divine artifact had risked their lives for him. That made him the one person here with the most dangerous potential.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress still had innate qi she had not spent.
The last strength bought by burning her life.
Lord of Heaven. Please forgive this disloyal servant for daring to defy your will.
Step.
She took a heavy step, and a sharp sound of splitting air rang out.
Shk! Crack!
A spear that had flown from somewhere trembled in her grasp. She crushed its steel spearhead in her bare hand, her eyes glowing blood-red.
“Do you all want to die?”
A middle-aged man stood where her cold words were directed, his armor torn almost to shreds.
And he was not alone.
Drip. Thud.
Across the devastated ground, more than a hundred warriors staggered to their feet and gathered behind him, gripping swords and spears.
Though they had been farther from the center of the blast, every one of them bore wounds. They stood in her way to fulfill the mission entrusted to them.
Splash.
The middle-aged man lifted something from a pool of blood and bound it tightly around his forehead. His gaze remained steady on the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Three characters were written on the old silk, still legible beneath the blood.
Baekcheon Unit.
That was his answer to her question. It was Wang Ho’s answer as Commander of the Baekcheon Unit, and the resolve of every surviving member.
The next moment—
Screeeeeech! Boom!
The Fiend known as the Southern Heaven Demon Empress charged at them.
A flash of light. An explosion.
Those were the last things I remembered. I’d thought that when I opened my eyes again, everything would be over.
I’d be alive. Or I’d be dead.
A battle could only end one of those two ways.
But when I opened my eyes after a brief spell of darkness, I realized I’d been only half right.
I was alive. The battle wasn’t over.
Kraaaaaack!
“Gaaaaah!”
“Stop her—!”
Slice!
“Noooo!”
My senses returned, and I saw blood spraying into the sky. Severed limbs flew after it. Someone’s body, crushed into a bloody pulp by overwhelming force, hurtled away.
Whoom! Boom!
Drip.
Blood splashed across my face from only a few steps away.
I stared blankly at a warrior lying dead with a hole through the center of his chest. Then a weak voice reached me.
No. It was someone’s thought.
—Human.
Only then did I realize what was supporting my back, and whose warmth I felt.
The thick smell of blood filled my nose. I turned my head and lost my words.
A massive body trembled now and then in a deep pool of blood.
The silver fur I’d once thought almost mystical was soaked through. Pale blue eyes blinked at me with visible effort.
—You’ve slept a long time.
“...What is this?”
—I have no regrets. Neither does he.
At the moment that distant flash had filled my vision, there had been green Force and a silver mane blocking my eyes.
No way.
As usual, my worst suspicion was right.
I turned and saw a broad back. The man kneeling there, so drenched in blood he scarcely looked human, was the Beast Miao King, Yayul Cheok.
He was unconscious. Fragments of the sword were embedded all over his body. He must have taken them while shielding someone else.
“This is insane. Why the hell...?”
—Go.
“What?”
—Leave. Hurry. There’s no time.
The guardian spirit turned its head with difficulty and spat something out.
Fwoooooosh.
The sacred stone, now no larger than a child’s fist, gave off a faint light.
I understood what it meant and gritted my teeth.
“Don’t give me that bullshit.”
—If they fall too, you are next. But if you run, you can survive.
Kraaaaaack!
“Gaaaaaaaah!”

The ground shook, and another scream followed. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress entered my field of vision, her veins standing out across her entire body as she burned through the last of her life and tore apart more than a hundred members of the Baekcheon Unit.
A chill swept over me at the sight of that overwhelming power. As I froze in place, the guardian spirit whispered with all its strength.
—Go. Now!
I knew it was right. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress didn’t have much time left. If I ran alone, I could survive.
But...
I’d regret it for the rest of my life.
I muttered dazedly and grabbed the sacred stone.
Then I rose and ran.
Not toward the Outer Palace.
Toward the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.

chapters.title: Chapter 709
paragraphs: Screeeeeech!
Jin Taekyung wavered slightly as he shot forward at breakneck speed.
His limbs, usually as light as down, hung heavy and ached. Every step felt incomparably heavier than before.

One Annihilation had taken a terrible toll. Without the Beast Miao King’s help, Jin would not have been able to stand, much less run. And even if he had somehow stayed on his feet, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s devastating attack would have killed him.
And yet... he had survived.

The Beast Miao King and the guardian spirit had risked their lives to save him when he had the least strength left to spare. Now the Baekcheon Unit was carrying on their resolve, staking their lives at this very moment.
Charging into the darkness. Toward a Fiend they had no power to stop.
Crack!
One strike.
The Fiend’s blood-soaked hand crushed bone and flesh, then punched through a chest.
An unnamed life went out. Someone else stepped forward to fill the gap.
Why?
Jin Taekyung did not know them. They did not know him.
Yet every one of them was willing to throw away their life. They filled the places left by comrades dying one after another and charged toward a death they could not stop.
The sight of the Baekcheon Unit overlapped with that of someone who had forced a smile in a dark cave.
Go on ahead, Taekyung.
Jin had survived because he ran. Because he had survived, he had regretted it countless times. If he could return to that moment, he would say—
“I’m not going. Never.”
At the words forced through his clenched teeth, Wang Ho, Commander of the Baekcheon Unit, turned his head.
Drenched in blood that might not have been his own, Wang Ho stared at the figure rapidly closing in.
Jin Taekyung should not be here.
The Beast Miao King, Wang Ho, and the hundred warriors of the Baekcheon Unit had risked their lives to buy him this precious time. Surely his one task was to survive, whatever it took.
Instead, he had come running straight back into danger.
“What the hell is going on...!”
As Wang Ho cried out and moved to block Jin Taekyung, a hand planted firmly on his shoulder. A low voice sounded beside his ear.
“Let’s get out of this alive together.”
“Fuck. I said let’s survive together!”
Wang Ho went rigid.
He could find no words for that cry—not let’s die together, but let’s survive together—or for Jin’s eyes, burning like fire and wet with tears.
He could not stop the young man from leaving him behind and running toward death.
And then he understood why the Beast Miao King, his lord, who had nearly a hundred thousand tribespeople to lead, had made his choice.
Was this why? Was it because of this very sight that you wanted to protect that young man more than your own safety?
If Jin had returned so they could die together, it would have been nothing more than foolhardy courage.
But Jin Taekyung had come back to fight beside them. To save as many people as they could—even one more—and for all of them to survive.
Tsstsst!
The Sword Energy that had seemed about to gutter out blazed stronger. Wang Ho raised his blade, sheathed in blue qi, and charged.
He shouted to his subordinates, fewer than half of whom remained.
“Kill that Fiend!”
It was a small difference in resolve, and an enormous one.
Hold her back? Or kill her?
Until now, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress had been someone they could not kill with the strength they had. No—they had believed they could not kill her and accepted their deaths.
Not anymore.
Now they were fighting to kill the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. Fighting to survive.
At the center of it all was the young man who had made them see the difference.
“Southern Heaven Demon Empress!”
Jin Taekyung roared in fury. A faint flame sprang from his toes.
Boom!
A small explosion cratered the ground, cracks spreading through it like a spiderweb. The recoil hurled him forward even faster.
Ahead of him stood the Fiend, steeped in blood and darkness.
Slice! Shraaaaaak!
A hand blade wreathed in murky darkness split someone in two.
Beyond the blood spraying in every direction, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress saw Jin Taekyung tearing through space as he charged toward her—and smiled delightedly.
Foolish child. Your recklessness has given me one last chance.

Until a moment ago, she had been furious. The innate qi bought with her life was dwindling by the moment, and the hundred Baekcheon Unit warriors blocking her path had worn away her remaining strength even as they died.
But now she could smile. Her most important prey had come searching for the place where he would die, foolishly walking there on his own two feet.
“Now, you small fry... get out of my way.”
Roooooar!
Murky palm Force swept through the warriors blocking her path. They flew in every direction, coughing blood.
A sound split the air across the space they left behind.
Screeeeeech! Boom!
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress knocked away an iron spear that shot toward her like a flash of light with her bare hand, then swung down with her hand blade.
Whoooosh!
Space split, and a blade-sharp wind tore through it.
But Jin Taekyung was nowhere to be seen.
Above!
As she realized it, her figure blurred. A transparent spearhead slashed down from overhead and cut through her afterimage.
Slice!
No—not only her afterimage.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress felt a drop of blood roll down her forehead. Her expression tightened slightly.
Fast.
In a way, it was only natural. A martial artist who had reached the Supreme Peak was more than worthy of being called superhuman.
But martial insight alone did not make them superhuman. They also possessed vast reserves of internal energy, which heightened the physical abilities they had honed over years of training.
Then how...?
Jin Taekyung had used up most of his internal energy. How could he still move with such speed and strength?
Shk-shk-shk-shk!
The spear tip trembled. Dozens of spear shadows spread out and rained down on her entire body.
Their speed and force far exceeded anything she had expected. But she did not retreat.
“How dare you, you little brat...!”
Her voice seethed as her one remaining hand shot through the air. Her palm strike, stained with the blood of countless warriors, swallowed the spear shadows bearing down on her.
Roooooar!
No matter how many falsehoods there were, in the end, only one truth would emerge.
The shadows vanished in the palm Force. Her hand, shrouded in murky darkness, closed around the transparent spearhead.
Slice!
Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, said to be harder and sharper than anything under heaven, tore through her Force and cut into her flesh.
Pain struck. The Southern Heaven Demon Empress smiled anyway.
I’ve got it.
At that moment—
Shwaaaaaaak!
Her qi flowed along the spearhead and swept through Jin Taekyung’s insides.
Boom!
His body jerked. The injuries within him, briefly calmed by the Beast Miao King’s help, were thrown into turmoil again.
Jin swallowed the blood rising in his throat and tightened his grip on the spear shaft.
Crack!
The White Flame’s spearhead twisted in her grasp and drove farther forward. Her hand was shredded in an instant. Her eyes widened at the pain.
Before she could finish, a sharp sound cut through the air.
Shiiiiing!
A sword flew through the wind. Its owner, wrapped in blue Sword Energy, was none other than Wang Ho, Commander of the Baekcheon Unit.
Slice!
She twisted away, but too late. Her Body-Protecting Qi, far weaker than before, could not stop the Sword Energy. Pain shot through her slashed flank, and she kicked upward.
Screeeeeech—crack!
Her foot struck Wang Ho’s abdomen like a whip. He flew more than ten jang, hurtling away like a cannonball.
Boom!
Dust billowed from the impact.
But Wang Ho was not the only one charging her.
Pat-pat-pat!
Figures rushed in from front and back, left and right, surrounding the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.

Fewer than twenty warriors of the Baekcheon Unit remained. They gathered the last of their strength and charged—to end this fight, to drive their spears and blades into the Fiend even if it cost them their lives.
Shk-shk-shk-shk!
At that moment, when the fierce sounds of weapons tearing through the air mingled with the wind—
Kraaaaaash!
Energy burst outward like a storm, sweeping away everything coming at her from every side.
And from between the lips of the person standing tall at its center, blood that could no longer be held back began to flow.
Cough.
Through dimming vision, she looked with trembling eyes at the young man kneeling before her.
His gaze was faint, as though its light might go out at any moment. But his hands did not shake. They gripped the spear shaft and held it thrust forward, its transparent head driven into her chest.
She coughed up dark-red blood and gasped for air.
She had needed to stop him. She had thought she could.
She had failed.
How? How could he still move?
Just before she unleashed her palm Force at the warriors, she had sent internal energy into Jin Taekyung again—to ensure that this time he would never rise, that his breath would stop for good.
But he had not fallen. He had not died.
Even though his heart meridian had undoubtedly been torn to shreds, he had driven the spear he had held until the very end into the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s chest.
“Jin Tae...kyung.”
Her broken voice had barely left her lips when—
Slide. Thud.
Jin Taekyung’s blood-soaked hands slipped from the shaft. His head fell back, and his eyes grew hazy.
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress felt it then. She could hear it, too: death approaching Jin Taekyung, slowly but surely.
And his voice, impossibly bright for a man so close to death.
“Finally got you, you... fucking bitch.”
Every hair on her body seemed to stand on end.
It was fear. Terror of a human being whose resolve would not waver, no matter what happened.
...Afraid? I’m afraid? Me? Of that bastard?
Impossible. She could not fear anyone but the Lord of Heaven—least of all a mere brat on the brink of death.
I have to kill him. I have to stop his breath with my own hand.
She raised her hand slowly, the thought repeating in a daze.
She would likely die too. But unless she killed Jin Taekyung herself, she felt she would never rest in peace, even in death.
Die.
You monster.
With those words she did not have the chance to spit out, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress swung down her hand blade with the last of her strength.
Shk!
And at the moment the murky darkness was about to bore into the crown of Jin Taekyung’s head—
Screeeeeech! Crack!
A streak of light flew in from somewhere and swallowed her only remaining arm.
A cold voice reached her as she froze.
“Just whose body do you think you’re laying a hand on, you fucking bitch?”
