chapters.title: Chapter 710
paragraphs: He could feel it. Death was right before his eyes.
His blurred vision could barely make out shapes. His once-sharp senses seemed ready to leave his body.
In the darkness of his fading consciousness, Jin Taekyung thought:
No doubt about it.
This is a dream. Or maybe I’m hearing things because I’m about to die.
How else could he explain the voice behind him?
“Just whose body do you think you’re laying a hand on, you fucking bitch?”
And yet... it sounded so much like him.

That sharp voice, almost shrill with irritation. Those foul-mouthed curses. Both brought one person to mind. Taekyung knew that person could not possibly be here, and he scolded himself for even thinking it. Still, he couldn’t help hoping.
I really must be dying.
The hollow thought echoed through his mind.
“So... how long are you going to sit there in a daze?”
Jin Taekyung’s eyelids, which had been slowly closing, stopped abruptly.
The shock jolted him awake, and his distant senses rushed back.
No way.
No. It can’t be.
It was impossible. He was supposed to be somewhere far away in the Central Plains.
But someone had once said that hope could break a person—and raise them up again. Taekyung clung to that invisible thread and opened his eyes.
“Ah. Aah...”
He saw the Southern Heaven Demon Empress staggering, both arms gone.
And a single Zen staff planted at an angle beside her as she stood gripped by shock and confusion.
Clatter.
The rings hanging from it rattled loudly. The staff glowed red, and Taekyung could feel the Scorching Yang Qi flowing from it. A faint smile touched his lips.
“You... could’ve come a little sooner.”
He spoke so softly that anyone else would have needed to stand right beside him to hear.
But the owner of the staff was different. He could have heard Taekyung from hundreds of jang away—hundreds of li, even.
Not with his ears.
With his heart. With the heart he held for his one and only Disciple.
“I’m allowed to be a little late. No need to give me grief, you brat.”
His gruff answer betrayed none of what he felt. Blood Monk—no, Fire King Jeok Cheongang—took a step forward.
Thud.
And the next moment—
Whoosh!
In the blackout that followed the end of the performance, a flame rose, larger and fiercer than anything else on the stage.
Kraaaaaash!
Flame Divine Palm.
A wave of fire surged through the darkness, devouring it with terrible heat. It rushed on without slowing, with only one purpose: to burn the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Ah.
She watched it approach with empty eyes.
No groan or scream escaped her. Her feet might as well have been nailed to the ground, and the pain where her arms had been felt strangely distant.
I have to dodge. Somehow, I have to dodge...
Her body would not obey the cry in her head.

Perhaps it had all ended the moment she lost her one remaining arm. The Zen staff had flown so fast it could have been mistaken for a flash of light, carrying enough heat to turn more than her arm to ash.
Her innate qi.
It had stripped away the last handful of strength she had saved to bring one person’s life to an end. Indifferently. Mercilessly.
Watching herself stand there without the strength to take even one step, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress finally understood.
It’s over.
Her life had been long indeed. She no longer knew exactly where it had begun, but here, today, it would end.
If she had one regret, it was that she had failed to stop Jin Taekyung’s breath with her own hand.
But... that’s all right.
She did not know why Fire King Jeok Cheongang had come here, or what trick of fate had brought him.
But just as she would die here, Jin Taekyung could not escape death either. Not even the Great Firmament Immortal could change that.
The certainty comforted her as she accepted the flames.
Lord of Heaven.
The invocation sounded softly within her heart.
Her thoughts had been long, but only an instant had passed. The flames shot over Taekyung’s kneeling head and opened their maw toward her.
Whoooosh!
As the light-flames poured down, melting the darkness, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress closed her eyes.
No—she tried to.
She would have succeeded if, just as everything turned white, someone had not thrown himself onto her body, which no longer had the strength to move a finger.
Whump!
In that split instant, she saw him clearly.
Jin Taekyung’s face was deathly pale. In a world moving impossibly slowly, his lips parted.
And then—
Crack!
Sharp pain shot through her throat, and her vision went dark.
The realization struck like a flash of light. It was an inescapable fact.
If the Southern Heaven Demon Empress dies now, I die too.
The main reason I’d survived fights against people stronger than me was the recovery I got when I leveled up.

Even with outstanding Muscles and Bones and all the stats I’d raised, I couldn’t survive certain death. Not with my acupoints wrecked and my duodenum on leave from its post like a soldier who’d wandered outside his assigned area.
If someone else killed the Southern Heaven Demon Empress now, I was fucked.
That left me one choice.
Tank it.
Fuck.
I swallowed the curse and squeezed out every last bit of strength to throw myself forward.
No—it would be more accurate to say that I barely managed to raise my body and throw myself over the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Whump!
Her eyes, closing in resignation, snapped wide open. Shock and confusion swirled in them, asking the question she could not voice.
Why?
I had no reason to answer, and no time.
If I’d had the strength, I would have picked up White Flame from where it had fallen a few steps away. Or pulled another weapon from my Inventory and driven it into her heart.
But damn it, I could barely hold on to consciousness. This was the best attack I had left.
Crack!
Wrinkled skin mottled with age spots tore away. The taste of blood filled my mouth and wet my parched lips.
Of all the attacks I’d made in all the battles I’d fought, this was the most primitive. And I had never needed one to work more badly.
I tore a mouthful from the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s throat.
Then I felt tremendous heat at my back and heard someone scream.
Whoosh! Boom!
A massive impact slammed into me. A roar swallowed the rest of the cry, and terrible heat swept out in every direction. I felt weightless for an instant before it hurled me away.
Ah.
Who was it who said that the worst pain a person could feel was being burned?
They were right.
Pain too awful to scream through seized my entire body. My vision went white. I couldn’t see an inch in front of me as I hurtled through the air.
Screeeeeech—boom!
The rushing wind seemed to go on forever. Then something rough and hard struck my whole body.
No. My body had shot through the rubble like a beam of light and buried itself there.
Cough.
With a cough, what little blood I had left trickled from the corner of my mouth.

My eardrums had burst, yet I heard a swarm of bees buzzing in my ears. Through my blurred vision, I could make out the Southern Heaven Demon Empress sprawled on the ground and someone’s figure wavering like a heat haze.
“No!”
At that scream—
Ding.
A clear bell rang in my ear, and warmth enveloped me.
Screeeeeech!
Jeok Cheongang raced forward with all his strength, his heart full of despair.
No. No, this can’t happen.
Every step felt heavy.
His heart, aged by more than a century, pounded harder than it ever had. His eyes trembled, fixed on the person rapidly drawing closer.
Jin Taekyung.
The second Disciple he had taken in his lifetime, and the only one he had left.
The one ember that had appeared in the life of a man who had wished only for death and shown him a reason to keep living.
But why? Why the hell would he do that?
He felt as though he might cough up blood.
What he had unleashed at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was the Flame Divine Palm, driven to a staggering twelve-tenths of its normal limit.
And Jin Taekyung had suddenly blocked that horrifying heat, powerful enough to melt steel.
You crazy bastard. You stupid bastard!
Jeok Cheongang did not know why. The reason did not matter. The curses he could not bring himself to shout were meant for himself.
His one and only Disciple had always had a reason for his choices. He had always been right.
It was the grief and guilt of knowing his own hasty judgment had cost Taekyung his life that tore Jeok Cheongang’s heart apart.
“No!”
The old master’s desperate cry rang out as he finally stopped before his Disciple.
“Taekyung! You bastard!”
There was no answer.
Taekyung lay with his eyes closed, his breathing so faint it could stop at any moment. Jeok Cheongang’s heart sank.
Ah.
His vision swam.
Taekyung’s armor was shattered beyond recognition. His limbs lay twisted at unnatural angles. Beneath the heat of the Flame Divine Palm, flesh had melted and bone had broken.
Perhaps the armor had saved him. Somehow, he was still breathing.
But only just. He had mere moments left.
Even if Jeok Cheongang poured all his internal energy into him, it would not change that. It would only prolong the pain.
Tap.
His hand stopped in midair, trembling as he reached for Taekyung’s wrist to take his pulse.
...Dying? He’s dying? That boy?
Unable to watch Taekyung die before his eyes, Jeok Cheongang squeezed his eyes shut.
He had seen countless deaths. Some he had witnessed from afar. Others he had caused with his own hands.
But... Jin Taekyung’s death was different.
The boy had barely passed twenty. Unlike Jeok Cheongang, he had so many years left to live, so much happiness still to enjoy.
“What... what could be so urgent that you have to leave already? Why!”
Jeok Cheongang cried out as though the words were tearing blood from him.
He held Jin Taekyung’s hand, which had been half melted by his own martial arts. Holding that hand, still bearing the marks of those horrific injuries, he wept his heart out...
Huh?
Something felt strange beneath his fingers. He opened his eyes.
Through his tears, he saw Taekyung’s hand.
The back of it was pale and smooth as a newborn baby’s. Its veins stood out in thick ridges.
That was strange. A moment ago, the flesh had been melted together. He was almost sure he had seen bone.
What the hell?
There were only two possibilities. Either those damned infirmities of old age had returned, or...
Gulp.
Jeok Cheongang swallowed and slowly raised his head.
A pair of eyes was watching him with interest.
They stared at each other. Jeok Cheongang froze.
Facing him, Jin Taekyung wiggled his fingers sheepishly.
“Um, could you let go of my hand first? Then we can talk.”

sentences.text: He could feel it.
Death was right before his eyes.
His blurred vision could barely make out shapes.
His once-sharp senses seemed ready to leave his body.
In the darkness of his fading consciousness, Jin Taekyung thought:
No doubt about it.
This is a dream.
Or maybe I’m hearing things because I’m about to die.
How else could he explain the voice behind him?
“Just whose body do you think you’re laying a hand on, you fucking bitch?”
And yet... it sounded so much like him.
That sharp voice, almost shrill with irritation.
Those foul-mouthed curses.
Both brought one person to mind.
Taekyung knew that person could not possibly be here, and he scolded himself for even thinking it.
Still, he couldn’t help hoping.
I really must be dying.
The hollow thought echoed through his mind.
“So... how long are you going to sit there in a daze?”
Jin Taekyung’s eyelids, which had been slowly closing, stopped abruptly.
The shock jolted him awake, and his distant senses rushed back.
No way.
No.
It can’t be.
It was impossible.
He was supposed to be somewhere far away in the Central Plains.
But someone had once said that hope could break a person—and raise them up again.
Taekyung clung to that invisible thread and opened his eyes.
“Ah.
Aah...”
He saw the Southern Heaven Demon Empress staggering, both arms gone.
And a single Zen staff planted at an angle beside her as she stood gripped by shock and confusion.
Clatter.
The rings hanging from it rattled loudly.
The staff glowed red, and Taekyung could feel the Scorching Yang Qi flowing from it.
A faint smile touched his lips.
“You... could’ve come a little sooner.”
He spoke so softly that anyone else would have needed to stand right beside him to hear.
But the owner of the staff was different.
He could have heard Taekyung from hundreds of jang away—hundreds of li, even.
Not with his ears.
With his heart.
With the heart he held for his one and only Disciple.
“I’m allowed to be a little late.
No need to give me grief, you brat.”
His gruff answer betrayed none of what he felt.
Blood Monk—no, Fire King Jeok Cheongang—took a step forward.
Thud.
And the next moment—
Whoosh!
In the blackout that followed the end of the performance, a flame rose, larger and fiercer than anything else on the stage.
Kraaaaaash!
Flame Divine Palm.
A wave of fire surged through the darkness, devouring it with terrible heat.
It rushed on without slowing, with only one purpose: to burn the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Ah.
She watched it approach with empty eyes.
No groan or scream escaped her.
Her feet might as well have been nailed to the ground, and the pain where her arms had been felt strangely distant.
I have to dodge.
Somehow, I have to dodge...
Her body would not obey the cry in her head.
Perhaps it had all ended the moment she lost her one remaining arm.
The Zen staff had flown so fast it could have been mistaken for a flash of light, carrying enough heat to turn more than her arm to ash.
Her innate qi.
It had stripped away the last handful of strength she had saved to bring one person’s life to an end.
Indifferently.
Mercilessly.
Watching herself stand there without the strength to take even one step, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress finally understood.
It’s over.
Her life had been long indeed.
She no longer knew exactly where it had begun, but here, today, it would end.
If she had one regret, it was that she had failed to stop Jin Taekyung’s breath with her own hand.
But... that’s all right.
She did not know why Fire King Jeok Cheongang had come here, or what trick of fate had brought him.
But just as she would die here, Jin Taekyung could not escape death either.
Not even the Great Firmament Immortal could change that.
The certainty comforted her as she accepted the flames.
Lord of Heaven.
The invocation sounded softly within her heart.
Her thoughts had been long, but only an instant had passed.
The flames shot over Taekyung’s kneeling head and opened their maw toward her.
Whoooosh!
As the light-flames poured down, melting the darkness, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress closed her eyes.
No—she tried to.
She would have succeeded if, just as everything turned white, someone had not thrown himself onto her body, which no longer had the strength to move a finger.
Whump!
In that split instant, she saw him clearly.
Jin Taekyung’s face was deathly pale.
In a world moving impossibly slowly, his lips parted.
And then—
Crack!
Sharp pain shot through her throat, and her vision went dark.
The realization struck like a flash of light.
It was an inescapable fact.
If the Southern Heaven Demon Empress dies now, I die too.
The main reason I’d survived fights against people stronger than me was the recovery I got when I leveled up.
Even with outstanding Muscles and Bones and all the stats I’d raised, I couldn’t survive certain death.
Not with my acupoints wrecked and my duodenum on leave from its post like a soldier who’d wandered outside his assigned area.
If someone else killed the Southern Heaven Demon Empress now, I was fucked.
That left me one choice.
Tank it.
Fuck.
I swallowed the curse and squeezed out every last bit of strength to throw myself forward.
No—it would be more accurate to say that I barely managed to raise my body and throw myself over the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Whump!
Her eyes, closing in resignation, snapped wide open.
Shock and confusion swirled in them, asking the question she could not voice.
Why?
I had no reason to answer, and no time.
If I’d had the strength, I would have picked up White Flame from where it had fallen a few steps away.
Or pulled another weapon from my Inventory and driven it into her heart.
But damn it, I could barely hold on to consciousness.
This was the best attack I had left.
Crack!
Wrinkled skin mottled with age spots tore away.
The taste of blood filled my mouth and wet my parched lips.
Of all the attacks I’d made in all the battles I’d fought, this was the most primitive.
And I had never needed one to work more badly.
I tore a mouthful from the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s throat.
Then I felt tremendous heat at my back and heard someone scream.
Whoosh!
Boom!
A massive impact slammed into me.
A roar swallowed the rest of the cry, and terrible heat swept out in every direction.
I felt weightless for an instant before it hurled me away.
Ah.
Who was it who said that the worst pain a person could feel was being burned?
They were right.
Pain too awful to scream through seized my entire body.
My vision went white.
I couldn’t see an inch in front of me as I hurtled through the air.
Screeeeeech—boom!
The rushing wind seemed to go on forever.
Then something rough and hard struck my whole body.
No.
My body had shot through the rubble like a beam of light and buried itself there.
Cough.
With a cough, what little blood I had left trickled from the corner of my mouth.
My eardrums had burst, yet I heard a swarm of bees buzzing in my ears.
Through my blurred vision, I could make out the Southern Heaven Demon Empress sprawled on the ground and someone’s figure wavering like a heat haze.
“No!”
At that scream—
Ding.
A clear bell rang in my ear, and warmth enveloped me.
Screeeeeech!
Jeok Cheongang raced forward with all his strength, his heart full of despair.
No.
No, this can’t happen.
Every step felt heavy.
His heart, aged by more than a century, pounded harder than it ever had.
His eyes trembled, fixed on the person rapidly drawing closer.
Jin Taekyung.
The second Disciple he had taken in his lifetime, and the only one he had left.
The one ember that had appeared in the life of a man who had wished only for death and shown him a reason to keep living.
But why?
Why the hell would he do that?
He felt as though he might cough up blood.
What he had unleashed at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress was the Flame Divine Palm, driven to a staggering twelve-tenths of its normal limit.
And Jin Taekyung had suddenly blocked that horrifying heat, powerful enough to melt steel.
You crazy bastard.
You stupid bastard!
Jeok Cheongang did not know why.
The reason did not matter.
The curses he could not bring himself to shout were meant for himself.
His one and only Disciple had always had a reason for his choices.
He had always been right.
It was the grief and guilt of knowing his own hasty judgment had cost Taekyung his life that tore Jeok Cheongang’s heart apart.
“No!”
The old master’s desperate cry rang out as he finally stopped before his Disciple.
“Taekyung!
You bastard!”
There was no answer.
Taekyung lay with his eyes closed, his breathing so faint it could stop at any moment.
Jeok Cheongang’s heart sank.
Ah.
His vision swam.
Taekyung’s armor was shattered beyond recognition.
His limbs lay twisted at unnatural angles.
Beneath the heat of the Flame Divine Palm, flesh had melted and bone had broken.
Perhaps the armor had saved him.
Somehow, he was still breathing.
But only just.
He had mere moments left.
Even if Jeok Cheongang poured all his internal energy into him, it would not change that.
It would only prolong the pain.
Tap.
His hand stopped in midair, trembling as he reached for Taekyung’s wrist to take his pulse.
...Dying?
He’s dying?
That boy?
Unable to watch Taekyung die before his eyes, Jeok Cheongang squeezed his eyes shut.
He had seen countless deaths.
Some he had witnessed from afar.
Others he had caused with his own hands.
But...
Jin Taekyung’s death was different.
The boy had barely passed twenty.
Unlike Jeok Cheongang, he had so many years left to live, so much happiness still to enjoy.
“What... what could be so urgent that you have to leave already?
Why!”
Jeok Cheongang cried out as though the words were tearing blood from him.
He held Jin Taekyung’s hand, which had been half melted by his own martial arts.
Holding that hand, still bearing the marks of those horrific injuries, he wept his heart out...
Huh?
Something felt strange beneath his fingers.
He opened his eyes.
Through his tears, he saw Taekyung’s hand.
The back of it was pale and smooth as a newborn baby’s.
Its veins stood out in thick ridges.
That was strange.
A moment ago, the flesh had been melted together.
He was almost sure he had seen bone.
What the hell?
There were only two possibilities.
Either those damned infirmities of old age had returned, or...
Gulp.
Jeok Cheongang swallowed and slowly raised his head.
A pair of eyes was watching him with interest.
They stared at each other.
Jeok Cheongang froze.
Facing him, Jin Taekyung wiggled his fingers sheepishly.
“Um, could you let go of my hand first?
Then we can talk.”

chapters.title: Chapter 711
paragraphs: Sometimes, a certain kind of silence can take the place of countless emotions and words.
Like right now.
“Um, could you let go of my hand first? Then we can talk.”
Jeok Cheongang did not let go. He did not answer, either. He only stared, his gaze roaming over my face and the rest of me as if he were in a daze.
What the hell? Is this all a dream?
That was what his eyes seemed to say, and I understood completely.
How else could he react?
The guy who had been dying right in front of him was suddenly alive and whole.

Even that prophet from the neighborhood over had wounds on his palms after rising from the dead three days after being nailed to a cross. Five level-ups had left me with the unblemished skin of a baby.
And Jeok Cheongang had watched it happen.
Smack!
A sharp sound rang out.
Jeok Cheongang had slapped himself across the face with all his strength. He blinked at me, then spoke with a grave expression.
“Let me ask you one thing. Am I dreaming?”
I answered carefully. “No.”
“No matter how I think about it, this feels like a dream.”
“Then slap yourself again.”
Smack!
No hesitation, as usual.
He must have hit himself pretty damn hard. Jeok Cheongang spat out a thick mouthful of blood, then took a deep breath.
“...Damn it. Not a dream. Then is this an illusion cast by a Mystic Gate Formation?”
“Uh, I don’t think so. If I were an illusion, whose hand would the Old Master be holding right now?”

“A Dark Heaven sorcerer wearing your likeness. Or the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, if she isn’t dead after all. Whoever it is, they’ll be preparing a One Strike while I’m distracted by the illusion.”
“Quite an imagination you’ve got. Are you going senile?”
“The way you speak certainly sounds like you. Hah. This is driving me mad.”
“It’s driving me mad too.”
I meant it. I had kept the System hidden all this time, and now I had been caught with no way to explain it away.
I sighed and looked at Jeok Cheongang, who still seemed stunned. No matter how many times I looked, I could not get used to his roughly shaved head and worn monk’s robe.
“Anyway, what’s with that getup?”
“Can’t you tell? It’s a disguise. I look enough like a monk, don’t I?”
“You look like a monk who broke his vows, set fire to a temple, and ran away.”
“...You little bastard. Do you think I wanted to dress up as some fake monk? I had to stay out of Dark Heaven’s sight. My hair stood out too much, so I shaved it off.”
Fair enough. No matter how vast the world was, red hair was rare. He would stand out wherever he went, and word would spread.
But that did not explain everything.
The Blood Monk I had heard about was a terrifying fiend who had single-handedly drenched Guangxi in blood.
“So, to avoid Dark Heaven, you disguised yourself as a monk and beat hundreds of innocent Murim practitioners to death?”
“What those bastards were doing was—what?”
Jeok Cheongang’s brow furrowed as he tried to continue.
“Innocent Murim practitioners? What nonsense is that?”
“I did draw attention in Guangxi, though I never meant to. Some unorthodox faction scum were taking advantage of the chaos to get up to all sorts of vile things, so I dealt with them.”
“Unorthodox faction? Did you just say unorthodox faction?”
“Yes. They were committing atrocities and making them look like Dark Heaven’s work. I went after them and smashed about six of their sects. The rest of the small fry scattered.”
I listened with my mouth open. At last, the pieces fell into place.
That Murim practitioner who fled Guangxi.
The man who had supposedly caught an endemic disease and died as soon as he entered Nanman had actually been unorthodox faction small fry fleeing Jeok Cheongang’s fiery fists.
Crayfish side with crabs, and people know how to read the room.

Nanman already shunned outsiders. There was no way those people could admit that they were bad guys, and in the process, the unorthodox practitioners killed by Jeok Cheongang had been transformed into righteous heroes who loved justice and peace.
A story like that could take hold because Nanman was so isolated from the outside world.
How the fuck did that happen?
I stared at Jeok Cheongang. Then another thought struck me, and I spoke up quickly.
“Then on your way here, did you happen to—”
“I don’t know who you’re asking about, but I met them all. The river bandits diving around in the Yangtze. The Nanman people who greeted me with spears and swords. Even your subordinates.”
“Oh.”
“The Escort King’s granddaughter told me you were in danger the moment she saw me. That Hyuk fellow grabbed my trouser leg and sobbed so hard I nearly broke his wrist.”
I could picture them from his words alone—how desperate they must have been.
And I could picture Jeok Cheongang racing here the moment he heard I was in danger, without a question or a moment’s hesitation.
“But why are we talking about them? I’m the one owed an explanation.”
He made a show of scowling. I found myself laughing.
“...You’re laughing?”
The disbelief on his face only made me smile wider.
“Of course I am. We’re both alive, and we’ve found each other again.”
“I’m sorry. And thank you. I know you have a lot of questions. I’ll explain everything later. I promise.”
Jeok Cheongang looked as though he had plenty to say, but when he answered, his voice was subdued.
“You damn brat.”
There was so much in those three words. For a moment, it almost sounded as though he were thanking me for staying alive. Between us, that was enough.
“Stop smiling. I’ll get attached.”
“For someone who supposedly isn’t attached, you were crying pretty bitterly. Of course, I’m not talking about you, Old Master.”
“...Shut that mouth of yours.”
He must have remembered what he had been doing a moment ago. Still huffing, he took my hand and pulled me to my feet.
Pat, pat.
The dust and stone grit covering my entire body fell away. The pain had been gone for a long time, but my vision blurred for a moment.
Hmm.
I held back a groan. Five level-ups had healed my body, and it moved exactly as I wanted. My mind was another matter. Battle after battle without a moment’s rest had left me exhausted.
Ah, I want to sleep.
I wanted to collapse where I stood. To sleep until my body and mind felt refreshed, then wake to a clear sky and spend the day slowly shaking off the drowsiness.
But... not yet.
Dark clouds still filled the sky. All around us, people lay groaning, some lightly wounded, others gravely hurt.
If we left them there, they would fall asleep and never wake again.
Jeok Cheongang finally looked around. His expression darkened.
“...I should have been faster.”
It was pointless regret and needless self-reproach. If Jeok Cheongang hadn’t come, all of us—including me—might have been buried here.
“Let’s hurry. Before it gets any later.”
I nodded and chose the quickest, most accurate way to find the survivors.
Activate Skill: Qi Sense.
Ding.

Along with the clear ringing of a bell announcing that the System had activated, a blue circle spread outward from me and enclosed a set area. At the same time, Level display windows rose here and there, and my chest tightened.
Too few.
I could see only about thirty Level display windows.
That meant the Nanman warriors, once nearly a thousand strong, and the three hundred members of the Baekcheon Unit had fallen here.
There was one small mercy: those still breathing did not seem to be in critical condition.
By the end, even the Southern Heaven Demon Empress must have been conserving every scrap of strength.
The thought weighed on me as I rushed to the nearest fallen man.
Wang Ho, Commander of the Baekcheon Unit.
I grasped the wrist of the man who had charged at the Southern Heaven Demon Empress until the final moment, then sent internal energy through his back and along his spine with my other hand.
Ssshhhhhh.
“C-cough.”
Wang Ho spat out a mouthful of dark blood. Color began to return to his pale face.
He had been struck particularly hard because he had fought the fiercest battle among the Baekcheon Unit, but this should let us breathe a little easier.
Others were plainly in far worse shape.
Hhh... hhh...
A thin breath escaped through the nose of a giant who had collapsed on his knees. Jeok Cheongang recognized him and let out a low groan.
“...He took a hell of a hit. He wasn’t wounded this badly even during the Great Faction War.”
The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s One Strike, launched at the cost of her own life, had been that devastating.

Countless sword fragments and pieces of debris were lodged deep throughout his body. The Beast Miao King had also suffered massive internal injuries while protecting me, leaving him unconscious. The sight of him was awful.
“Old Master, do you think—”
Jeok Cheongang heard the worry in my voice and shook his head before I could finish.
“The Beast Miao King is as tough as iron, so don’t worry. If this old man does his best, he should be able to survive. But...”
His words trailed off. The certainty in his voice faded as he looked toward the enormous White Tiger lying a few steps away.
“I don’t know about that beast. It seems extraordinary, even for an animal, but must it be saved?”
Yes. No matter what it takes.
Before I could say it aloud, a quiet thought reached us.
—If that is how it ends, then that too is my fate.
—You have lived a long time, old human. Your face is different from the one I saw in the imugi’s memories, but what you are has not changed.
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened. The guardian spirit turned its gaze from him to me.
—Come closer.
I bit my lip and went to it. I sat beside its head and stroked the back of its neck, soaked with blood. A low growl escaped it.
—How insolent. How dare you lay a hand on this body?
What could I say?
As I silently stroked only its neck, the guardian spirit sent another thought to me.
—Though I cannot say I dislike it. There was an impudent human much like you, long ago.
I thought I knew who it meant.
The first Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace. The only human the guardian spirit had ever opened its heart to in all its long life.
—Strange, isn’t it? Everything about you is different, yet you remind me of him. He returned to the earth hundreds of years ago.
—Perhaps that is why I saved you without thinking. Why I entrusted the sacred stone to a mere human.
The White Tiger’s enormous body heaved beneath my hand. Breathing raggedly, the guardian spirit lifted its blue-white eyes to mine.
At that moment, I understood instinctively.
Why it needed the sacred stone. What it meant to do with it.
The rift.
The guardian spirit was trying to close that dense darkness—the rift—all by itself.
Just as an imugi had done several months ago.

The Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s One Strike, launched at the cost of her own life, had been that devastating.
Countless sword fragments and pieces of debris were lodged deep throughout his body.
The Beast Miao King had also suffered massive internal injuries while protecting me, leaving him unconscious.
The sight of him was awful.
“Old Master, do you think—”
Jeok Cheongang heard the worry in my voice and shook his head before I could finish.
“The Beast Miao King is as tough as iron, so don’t worry.
If this old man does his best, he should be able to survive.
But...”
His words trailed off.
The certainty in his voice faded as he looked toward the enormous White Tiger lying a few steps away.
“I don’t know about that beast.
It seems extraordinary, even for an animal, but must it be saved?”
Yes.
No matter what it takes.
Before I could say it aloud, a quiet thought reached us.
—If that is how it ends, then that too is my fate.
—You have lived a long time, old human.
Your face is different from the one I saw in the imugi’s memories, but what you are has not changed.
Jeok Cheongang’s eyes widened.
The guardian spirit turned its gaze from him to me.
—Come closer.
I bit my lip and went to it.
I sat beside its head and stroked the back of its neck, soaked with blood.
A low growl escaped it.
—How insolent.
How dare you lay a hand on this body?
What could I say?
As I silently stroked only its neck, the guardian spirit sent another thought to me.
—Though I cannot say I dislike it.
There was an impudent human much like you, long ago.
I thought I knew who it meant.
The first Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace.
The only human the guardian spirit had ever opened its heart to in all its long life.
—Strange, isn’t it?
Everything about you is different, yet you remind me of him.
He returned to the earth hundreds of years ago.
—Perhaps that is why I saved you without thinking.
Why I entrusted the sacred stone to a mere human.
The White Tiger’s enormous body heaved beneath my hand.
Breathing raggedly, the guardian spirit lifted its blue-white eyes to mine.
At that moment, I understood instinctively.
Why it needed the sacred stone.
What it meant to do with it.
The rift.
The guardian spirit was trying to close that dense darkness—the rift—all by itself.
Just as an imugi had done several months ago.

chapters.title: Chapter 712
paragraphs: I hoped I was wrong.
I wanted the thought that had just occurred to me—my suspicion—to be completely unfounded.
But the guardian spirit’s thoughts reached me the next moment, and I knew it was true.
—Someone has to do it. Perhaps this is the fate I was given.
Just as I had understood what the guardian spirit intended, it had understood me.
My face was reflected in its clear blue-white eyes. They seemed to see through everything.
—Until that darkness... that thing you call a rift is gone, this will not end. No, it will be the beginning of another catastrophe.
I couldn’t deny it. After a desperate struggle, we had defeated the Southern Heaven Demon Empress and her subordinates. But the rift they had opened remained, consuming the space around it.
Even now.
Ssshhhhhh.
The darkness had already passed beyond the Inner Palace and was advancing toward the Outer Palace.
The demonic qi within it would corrupt living things, transform them into beings that had lost their reason, and bring about another disaster.
Basically, an army of monsters.
The rift reminded me of a Gate, but I had no way of knowing how far its power would reach.
If the demonic qi flowing from it could swallow Nanman—or more—then the darkness would keep spreading.
Beyond Nanman, until it consumed all under heaven.
—Human. You have likely guessed that only the sacred stone’s power can withstand that darkness. Someone must enter the center of the rift with the stone and endure it.
I knew that, too. Only a few months ago, the Water God Dragon had sacrificed itself to seal the rift.
And I knew the price it had paid.
“What if you become something different from what you’ve been until now?”
I couldn’t bring myself to say a mutant. The guardian spirit gave me a faint smile.
—Kill me. Without the slightest hesitation.
—With your strength and that old human’s, it shouldn’t be too difficult, even if I become a corrupted being.
I stared at the guardian spirit, then forced myself to speak. I had been holding on to this thought since the moment I understood its intentions. After turning it over for so long, I finally asked.
“What if I seal the rift myself?”
The answer came from someone else.
“Don’t be ridiculous!”
It was Jeok Cheongang’s shout. He had been tending to the Beast Miao King’s Internal Injury.
“Out of the question. Say whatever you like. This old man will not allow it.”
“But, Old Master—”
“I don’t want to hear it. I don’t care how much you’ve accomplished. We have no idea what might happen in there. How could I let you go?”
“I’ll come back safe and sound without so much as a hair out of place. I promise.”
“Without so much as a hair out of place?”
“Yes.”
I nodded. Jeok Cheongang watched me in silence, then spoke.
“If that’s what you want, fine.”
“Then—”
“You stay here. This old man will go.”
“If you can return without a scratch, then it would be even more certain if I went instead. Am I wrong?”
That hit the heart of it. I had no answer.
The guardian spirit’s thoughts rang out.
—Old human. If the darkness changes that young human into something else, what will you do?
“I’ll kill the boy. So he can find peace.”
Jeok Cheongang answered without hesitation. His voice dropped.
“And then this old man will choose death as well.”
—Young human. What would you do if it were the other way around?
I said nothing. The guardian spirit understood my silence and smiled.
—Yes. That is why I must go.

—The humans of this land have already shed enough blood. There is no reason for you and that old human to sacrifice yourselves in my place. You still have many fates ahead of you, while I have already passed through many fates.
The guardian spirit raised its blue-white eyes to Jeok Cheongang.
—Even if the situation becomes irreversible, do not hesitate to kill me.
Jeok Cheongang gave a small nod.
“I’ll give it everything I have.”
—Thank you.
Grrr. The guardian spirit drew a labored breath and opened its mouth toward me.
—Jin Taekyung. It is time.
What more could I say?
I slipped a hand inside my robes and murmured inwardly.
Inventory open. Summon.
The next moment, something giving off a faint, warm light rested on my palm. I held it out to the guardian spirit.
Jeok Cheongang felt its mysterious energy and murmured, almost groaning.
“Could that be...?”
—This sacred stone, which you humans call the Beast King Stone, was the one mission I had left. The reason I existed. And now we will be together until the end.
Ssshhhh.
The sacred stone rose slowly into the air and was drawn into the guardian spirit’s mouth.
Warmth spread outward with its faint radiance.
At the same time, the guardian spirit’s ragged breathing steadied. Strength began to return to its fallen body.
Rustle. Thud.
At last, the enormous White Tiger rose and set a blood-soaked forepaw on the ground.
Thud. Thud.
One step. Then another.
Each step was heavier than ever, yet nothing could stop it.
Not even the darkness, now incomparably denser and stickier than at first, could stop them.
Kraaaash!
Pools of blood lay everywhere, with countless corpses scattered among them. The darkness surged over them like a wave, only to strike the light surrounding the guardian spirit and fall back.
If the darkness flowing from the rift corrupted everything, then the light contained within the sacred stone possessed the power of purification.
—Kraaaaang!
A fierce roar shook heaven and earth. Its silver mane, stained red, whipped violently in the wind.
Before I knew it, the guardian spirit had become a gust of wind and was racing forward.
Shweeeek!
I watched its back as it shot through the darkness.
I watched that faint but unmistakable streak of light cross countless corpses and piles of rubble.
I watched it race across the vast expanse until it reached the cliff swallowed by pitch-black darkness.
And then I realized something.
At the very end, the guardian spirit had called me by name for the first time.
The guardian spirit was out of breath. Its blood-drenched body felt heavy, and the darkness all around constricted it from head to toe.
Imugi. Did you feel this way, too?
With that unheard question, the guardian spirit took a step with all its strength into the gaping fissure in the cliff.
It had to keep going, however hard it was.
It had not known before. Now it did.
This had been its one mission from the beginning. The guardian spirit was meant to protect not the sacred stone, but everything in this land.
Crunch.
Its paw sank deep into the ground beneath the weight of its next step. The closer it came to the center of the rift, the harder the darkness and demonic qi pressed down on its body.
As its consciousness dimmed, memories of the distant past flashed before its blue-white eyes.
Come to think of it, I was always alone.
It had no father, mother, or siblings.
No. At first, it had not even known such things existed.
To one small, pure-white White Tiger, this space it had seen from the moment it first opened its eyes was the world itself. And it had a friend who had always been there with it.
A friend it could neither play with nor speak to, but who had never left its side.
Tap.
Something touched its soft white forepaw, which was like a ball of cotton.
It was a stone so clear that crystal would have been a better name for it. As always, it was warm and comforting.
Grrr.
The young White Tiger let out a contented growl and soon fell asleep, breathing softly.
And at the feet of the sleeping White Tiger, on a hill drenched in warm light that was neither sunlight nor moonlight, a green sprout suddenly pushed its head above the ground.
Rustle. Tap.
The sprout, no larger than a fingernail, began to straighten its bent stem. Colorful buds appeared, and branches grew.
Before long, a giant tree stood where the sprout had been, its roots sunk deep into the earth. Leaves hung from its countless branches, casting a broad, cool shade.
Ssshhhh.
A wind blew from somewhere, stirring the tree’s full crown.
A leaf that had clung stubbornly to its branch finally broke free and fell into the shade.
At the soft tap of its landing, the creature napping beneath the tree opened its eyes.
—Grrr.
It rose with a low growl.
It was a White Tiger.
Far too enormous and powerful to be called a cub—or even an ordinary tiger—it looked around with blue-white eyes.
No one knew exactly how much time had passed.
Only that it had been a long time. The place where it had been born and raised was always peaceful, and it was always day.
But things had changed.
Change as certain as the sprout growing into a giant tree, or the small, soft White Tiger cub becoming a huge and powerful being.
Yes. Him.
It had first met him three hundred years ago. He was a tribal chieftain who led humans and possessed a mysterious power that drew beasts to him. For someone built like a bear, he smiled an awful lot.
That power was probably why the beasts of the Sacred Land had accepted him without the guardian spirit’s permission.
“Oh. I’ve never seen a White Tiger this big before. What’s your name?”

At first, the guardian spirit had been surprised that a human had entered the Sacred Land without its permission. Then the human bastard had stroked the back of its neck without a trace of fear, leaving it dumbfounded.
So it asked him a question.
“And what is your name?”
It could still picture the insolent human bastard’s face. He had gaped at the guardian spirit, then answered in a dazed voice.
“Yayul Cheon...”
“I do not know how you entered this place, but if I see you here again, I will tear you limb from limb and kill you. Do you understand?”
The next day, the guardian spirit realized something.
That young human bastard named Yayul Cheon had less fear than any living creature it had ever seen.
“I believe I told you not to let yourself be seen.”
“That’s why I hid.”
“...Are you joking with me right now?”
“You found me by smell. You didn’t see me. I’m lying facedown in the grass.”
“No, is that supposed to be an answer? ...Wait. What is that smell?”
“Grilled meat. I brought some in case you were hungry. Want some?”
“Meat? Did you hunt the beasts?”
The guardian spirit could not say how they had grown close. Like getting soaked in a light rain without noticing, they came to know each other little by little. The years passed quickly.
Ten years. Twenty years. And then, the day they last faced each other.
“It’s been a long time.”
Yayul Cheon had not visited for several years. He was no longer a young man.
His once-black hair was half gray, and his eyes were worn with fatigue.
“I need your help. Only with your power and the sacred stone’s can we win this war and restore peace to Nanman.”
The guardian spirit knew what kind of war he was fighting. It knew how evil their enemies were.
But it refused.
The sacred stone—and the guardian spirit itself—were merely observers. That was what it believed then.
At least, it had believed it then.
And regret always came too late.
If I had helped you then, would the fate of this land have changed?
The guardian spirit’s blue-white eyes cleared as it came back from its memories.
Turbulent darkness churned before it, writhing strangely and spewing demonic qi as though it would swallow everything.
Ssssss!
Within the warped space, the guardian spirit struggled through one final step and stared into the center of the rift.
Then it hurled its faintly glowing body forward with all the strength it had left.
—Kraaaaang!
A single roar rang out, and an enormous wave of force burst outward.

chapters.title: Chapter 713
paragraphs: The wait was short.
I had gathered the survivors in one place, and with Jeok Cheongang’s help, the Beast Miao King had just managed to open his eyes.
Crack. Crack-crack.
The change began.
I felt it. So did Jeok Cheongang. Even the Baekcheon Unit warriors, still far from recovered, and the Beast Miao King, who had only just regained consciousness, felt the tremor.
Whoooosh.
Space twisted. The darkness that had writhed as though it were alive went still, and the wind began to flow in one direction.
Toward the gap in the cliff, its enormous jaws open like some primordial beast, beyond the thick darkness that had swallowed the guardian spirit.
At the same time, I could clearly see and hear it.
—Kraaaaang!
A roar echoed outward, and a single streak of light grew brighter within the darkness.
This is...
I stared at it in disbelief. So did everyone else.
The injured survivors forgot even to groan. The Beast Miao King, barely conscious, reached toward the distant light with a dazed look on his face.
It carried qi warmer than sunlight and as clear as water.
Silence fell, as though the world had stopped. Then Jeok Cheongang’s low voice reached my ears.
“It’s coming.”
With those words, time began to move again.
Rumble. Boom!
An enormous explosion.
Everything drew together, then burst outward at once. A deafening roar filled my ears as an invisible shock wave swept toward us, broad as a road.
I heard Jeok Cheongang shout through the gale.
“Watch out—!”
Kuwaaaang!
The wind—no, the storm—swallowed his voice.
A distant flash of darkness and light mixed together, blocking my vision, while the enormous shock wave battered and flung away everything within its range.
But—
Now.
I brought White Flame down in a diagonal slash.
Hellfire surged along its transparent spearhead and burned through the wind. The flames found their way into the invisible grain of the shock wave and struck it.
No. They canceled it out.
Kuwaaaang! Crack!
The earth shook with a deafening roar. The impact was powerful enough to push back both of my firmly rooted legs.
Jeok Cheongang had stepped forward to protect the survivors too. He flicked both sleeves.
Fwoosh. Boom!
The Blazing Flame Divine Palm, brought to perfection.

Unlike mine, his two fully formed fire dragons rampaged through the air, tearing into the storm. Flames rose across a radius of dozens of jang, consuming the wind and reducing to ash the countless fragments of debris hurled at us like hidden weapons.
Ssszzzzzt!
Smoke and steam filled every direction. In a world dyed entirely pale white, I exhaled the breath I had been holding and reached out.
Boom!
Compressed air burst outward, driving the smoke and steam away.
And beyond the vision that slowly cleared, the darkness was dispersing, while a collapse that had only just begun awaited us all.
Rumble. Rumble-rumble!
The cliff was coming down. All two hundred jang of it.
Jagged rocks, great and small, poured from above and filled the sky. It was a terrifying sight, but sunlight had begun to break through above them.
That could mean only one thing.
The rift... closed.
It was over.
The long, fierce battle had finally ended. We had stopped a catastrophe that might have claimed hundreds of thousands of lives. Perhaps millions.
Why was the emptiness greater than the joy?
Perhaps because I knew better than anyone that something remained unfinished.
Ding.

System The rift has closed. Demonic qi is disappearing. The power of the sacred stone is purifying qi corrupted by demonic qi. A sudden Quest, Sacrifice and Rest, has been generated. You cannot refuse this Quest.
As the System notification reached my ears, I suddenly reached out.
The darkness that had writhed painfully in the air like a living creature scattered between my fingers.
The sunlight shining through the slowly dispersing storm clouds was warm. Floating above it was a translucent holographic window displaying only a few short lines.
System Quest Sacrifice and Rest Now grant him rest. Grade: None Restriction: None Objective: Defeat Mutated Guardian Spirit (Incomplete) Reward: ??? Failure: ???
This was a first.
Never had a Quest description been so short. Nor had its restriction, which usually bore the three characters of my name, been open to anyone at all.
Perhaps even the System knew what he had sacrificed.
A being worthy of the name divine beast had given himself up and become a corrupted guardian spirit.
Step.
I walked through the darkness as it broke apart and blew away with the ash. Jeok Cheongang followed quietly. Among the countless rocks still crashing down, I sensed someone’s presence.
I saw it.
System Lv. 155 Mutated Guardian Spirit
The fur that had shone silver even in darkness was black now. So were the blue-white eyes that had once been as clear as the pond in the Sacred Land.
Fangs twice their former length gleamed at us.
—Grrrrr.
A low, savage growl. Then he moved like a flash of light.
Whoosh!
His form blurred, and the ten-odd jang between us vanished. His blood-soaked forepaw struck the ground, launching his enormous body into the air.
Pop.
A shadow fell over our heads. Jeok Cheongang and I struck with all our strength, remembering what the guardian spirit had asked of us before he left.
Kill me. Without the slightest hesitation.
We kept our promise.
Whoosh. Slash!
It was somewhere deep and cold. No light reached it. Not even the faintest warmth.
He lay curled up there, sensing death approaching—or perhaps it had already come.
Then he felt warmth and opened his eyes.
No. It was not warmth. It was heat.
Through his blurred vision, he made out a familiar face.
“Jin Tae... kyung.”
His voice came out cracked.
The young man watching Baeksang open his eyes answered evenly.
“Yes.”
That one word told Baeksang it was all over. Or perhaps it was the sunlight falling over Jin Taekyung’s shoulder.
So this is how it ended.
Baeksang looked up at the blue sky, clear of storm clouds.
How strange. He had lost everything he had wanted, yet he felt no despair. Only emptiness.
“What happened to the Southern Heaven Demon Empress?”
“She’s dead.”
“The rift must have disappeared as well.”
There was a hesitation in Jin Taekyung’s voice. He turned his head, his gaze resting briefly on the enormous tiger lying nearby.
But Baeksang saw the countless bodies of beasts and humans scattered all around them.
“Let me ask you one thing,” Jin Taekyung said, his voice low. “Did you know from the beginning that it would come to this?”
Baeksang stared at the bodies with empty eyes.
“Yes. I knew.”
Jin Taekyung clenched his teeth and glared at Baeksang. Baeksang did not avoid the gaze, where flames seemed to pour down in streams.
“To be precise, I learned a few months ago, when a letter arrived from the Central Plains.”
It had come from Henan. Along with an invitation to join the soon-to-be-established Murim Alliance, it contained a detailed account of the events in Hubei.
“That was when I understood why Dark Heaven had reached into Nanman, in the Outer Lands, instead of the Central Plains. I understood what the Southern Heaven Demon Empress meant by her grand plan.”
“And knowing that, you still...”
“Followed orders. I was already a monster, not a man.”
People said ten years could change the mountains and rivers. Sometimes an earthquake brought a mountain down, or a flood forced a river into a new course.

Baeksang had spent more than forty years amid earthquakes and floods of his own, losing his heart little by little. He had lost his only child, and he wanted revenge on the people of the Central Plains who had caused that loss.
But there was more to it.
“After the Great Faction War, I hated the Demonic Path more than anyone. If the Central Plains saw me as a turncoat they could never forgive, then those bastards were enemies I had to kill.”
Jin Taekyung gave a hollow laugh.

Dark Heaven and the Demonic Cult were branches of the same tree, growing from one root. If Baeksang hated the Demonic Path, how could he have joined forces with the Dark Heaven that had killed his child?

Yet he had joined hands with the Southern Heaven Demon Empress and brought about this catastrophe. He had let Dark Heaven open the rift. Knowing how many would die, he had still ordered a general mobilization and brought nearly ten thousand warriors and beasts into the Inner Palace.
To offer them up as living sacrifices.
“You stupid fuck. How can you even say—”
For some reason, Jin Taekyung’s words suddenly trailed off.
Baeksang moved his bloodstained lips.
“Yes. There was something more important to me than hatred. More important than anything.”
At that moment, someone’s face flashed through Jin Taekyung’s mind. He understood why the eyes above that mask had seemed so familiar.
“...Baekhwi.”
It was not Jin Taekyung who had spoken.

Baeksang raised his unfocused eyes toward a figure approaching from the distance. A huge man stumbled closer. Despite Jeok Cheongang’s attempts to stop him, the Beast Miao King came to stand before Baeksang.
“That child,” he asked, the words almost a groan. “Was he alive?”
Baeksang nodded weakly.
That was answer enough. The Beast Miao King knew what the child meant to Baeksang. He knew what his sworn younger brother would do for his only child.
It made him grieve—and it made him furious.
“Why? Why didn’t you tell me? Why?”
“I didn’t want the Palace Lord... I didn’t want you to die, hyung.”
“And Hwi... that child. I would have lost him all over again.”

The day he first faced the darkness, he had rejected the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s offer outright. Then she told him that the child he believed the Great Snow Fiend had killed was alive.

He had believed her. No—he had been forced to push down his distrust. It was the only way he could see his child again.

That was why he had created the Baekcheon Unit.
Not for himself, but for someone else—for the hope that he would stop this catastrophe.

A child might kill a parent, but no parent could kill their child.
Baeksang was a father. Even if he went back to that moment dozens of times—hundreds—he would make the same choice.
Cough.

A memory passed through them: the saddest and happiest day of his life.
Yes. That day.

Baeksang had wept on the day he lost his beloved wife and gained the child he would come to love more than anyone. He had sat across from his only sworn elder brother and drunk fruit wine as though it were his last day alive.
Just as he had decades later, on the day the Southern Heaven Demon Empress came to him.
“I have one last request.”
Baeksang gave a faint smile.
“Please kill me, hyung.”

Crack.
Crack-crack.
The change began.
I felt it.

Even the Baekcheon Unit warriors, still far from recovered, and the Beast Miao King, who had only just regained consciousness, felt the tremor.
Whoooosh.
Space twisted.

Toward the gap in the cliff, its enormous jaws open like some primordial beast, beyond the thick darkness that had swallowed the guardian spirit.
At the same time, I could clearly see and hear it.
—Kraaaaang!
A roar echoed outward, and a single streak of light grew brighter within the darkness.
This is...
I stared at it in disbelief.
So did everyone else.
The injured survivors forgot even to groan.
The Beast Miao King, barely conscious, reached toward the distant light with a dazed look on his face.
It carried qi warmer than sunlight and as clear as water.
Silence fell, as though the world had stopped.
Then Jeok Cheongang’s low voice reached my ears.
“It’s coming.”
With those words, time began to move again.
Rumble.
Boom!
An enormous explosion.
Everything drew together, then burst outward at once.
A deafening roar filled my ears as an invisible shock wave swept toward us, broad as a road.
I heard Jeok Cheongang shout through the gale.
“Watch out—!”
Kuwaaaang!
The wind—no, the storm—swallowed his voice.
A distant flash of darkness and light mixed together, blocking my vision, while the enormous shock wave battered and flung away everything within its range.
But—
Now.
I brought White Flame down in a diagonal slash.
Hellfire surged along its transparent spearhead and burned through the wind.
The flames found their way into the invisible grain of the shock wave and struck it.
No.
They canceled it out.
Kuwaaaang!
Crack!
The earth shook with a deafening roar.
The impact was powerful enough to push back both of my firmly rooted legs.
Jeok Cheongang had stepped forward to protect the survivors too.
He flicked both sleeves.
Fwoosh.
Boom!
The Blazing Flame Divine Palm, brought to perfection.
Unlike mine, his two fully formed fire dragons rampaged through the air, tearing into the storm.
Flames rose across a radius of dozens of jang, consuming the wind and reducing to ash the countless fragments of debris hurled at us like hidden weapons.
Ssszzzzzt!
Smoke and steam filled every direction.
In a world dyed entirely pale white, I exhaled the breath I had been holding and reached out.
Boom!
Compressed air burst outward, driving the smoke and steam away.
And beyond the vision that slowly cleared, the darkness was dispersing, while a collapse that had only just begun awaited us all.
Rumble.
Rumble-rumble!
The cliff was coming down.
All two hundred jang of it.
Jagged rocks, great and small, poured from above and filled the sky.
It was a terrifying sight, but sunlight had begun to break through above them.
That could mean only one thing.
The rift... closed.
It was over.
The long, fierce battle had finally ended.
We had stopped a catastrophe that might have claimed hundreds of thousands of lives.
Perhaps millions.
Why was the emptiness greater than the joy?
Perhaps because I knew better than anyone that something remained unfinished.
Ding.
System The rift has closed.
Demonic qi is disappearing.
The power of the sacred stone is purifying qi corrupted by demonic qi.
A sudden Quest, Sacrifice and Rest, has been generated.
You cannot refuse this Quest.
As the System notification reached my ears, I suddenly reached out.
The darkness that had writhed painfully in the air like a living creature scattered between my fingers.
The sunlight shining through the slowly dispersing storm clouds was warm.
Floating above it was a translucent holographic window displaying only a few short lines.
System Quest Sacrifice and Rest Now grant him rest.
Grade: None Restriction: None Objective: Defeat Mutated Guardian Spirit (Incomplete) Reward: ???
Failure: ???
This was a first.
Never had a Quest description been so short.
Nor had its restriction, which usually bore the three characters of my name, been open to anyone at all.
Perhaps even the System knew what he had sacrificed.
A being worthy of the name divine beast had given himself up and become a corrupted guardian spirit.
Step.
I walked through the darkness as it broke apart and blew away with the ash.
Jeok Cheongang followed quietly.
Among the countless rocks still crashing down, I sensed someone’s presence.
I saw it.
System Lv.
155 Mutated Guardian Spirit
The fur that had shone silver even in darkness was black now.
So were the blue-white eyes that had once been as clear as the pond in the Sacred Land.
Fangs twice their former length gleamed at us.
—Grrrrr.
A low, savage growl.
Then he moved like a flash of light.
Whoosh!
His form blurred, and the ten-odd jang between us vanished.

Pop.

Kill me.

chapters.title: Chapter 714
paragraphs: “Please kill me, hyung.”
The moment he heard those words, the Beast Miao King closed his eyes without realizing it.
His chest ached. He could barely breathe. The request his only sworn younger brother had made after so many years cut deep, like a sharp blade.
Hyung. He called me hyung.
He had wanted to hear that word for so long. Now he wanted to cover his ears.
He would rather be a fool who had seen and heard none of this. Even an incompetent Palace Lord, if it meant he could escape this moment.
If only he could.
“This brings back old memories.”
The Beast Miao King opened his eyes at the quiet voice. Baeksang’s face, wearing a faint smile, was reflected in his eyes.
“We were young back then. I wanted to become Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace someday, and I was desperate to beat you.”
“...Yes. You were.”
They had been little more than boys.
Baeksang had seen the Beast Miao King, several years his senior, as a rival. To the Beast Miao King, Baeksang had simply been adorable. Born an only child, he had never had a sibling.
“But I never caught up to you. Whenever I thought I was getting close, you were already far ahead again.”
“That was because you were younger than me. If we had been the same age...”
“It wouldn’t have changed anything. We were born with different potential.”
But Baeksang had not given up. Every day, he challenged the Beast Miao King to a duel. Every day, he lost. And the next day, he came back as though nothing had happened.
“Then one day, I realized that idiot who stood two heads taller than me wasn’t so bad after all.”
Baeksang could still picture the big boy pulling him to his feet and brushing the dust from his clothes after a fall.
And the shadow of someone quietly leaving medicinal herbs outside his quarters whenever he was sick.
“So I challenged you to one last duel.”
The result was no different that day.
Baeksang fought harder than he ever had—and lost.
If that had been the end of it, the day would have been like any other. But this time, he did not push away the hand that helped him up. He did not stalk back to his quarters, huffing in anger.
Instead, he produced two bottles of fruit wine he had stolen from somewhere and muttered as though to himself.
“I’ve got wine, but no one to drink it with. Come along if you want.”
At the Beast Miao King’s quiet voice, Baeksang’s eyes widened for a moment. Then he coughed up blood and laughed.
“Cough. You still remember that?”
“How could I forget? You’re the only twelve-year-old brat I’ve ever known who’d say something so cheeky.”
“Then you must remember how I emptied both bottles myself.”
“Both bottles?”
The Beast Miao King could not help laughing. Moisture had gathered at the corners of his crescent-shaped eyes.
“Well, I vividly remember the little brat who collapsed before he had even finished a single cup. I also remember what you said while looking at me with those unfocused eyes.”
Baeksang nodded weakly, his unfocused gaze reaching back into the past.
“I said I’d be content to become Great Chieftain, so you should become a great Palace Lord. I couldn’t have said that to you sober. That’s why I drank.”
“And what you said after that? Did you need to be drunk for that too?”
“Of course not.”
Baeksang continued in a quiet voice.
“You were... simply my hyung. Perhaps you had been since the day we met.”

The two boys had tasted alcohol for the first time, then collapsed and fallen asleep. When they opened their eyes the next morning in an old shrine, they had become sworn brothers closer than anyone else.
In the mountains. In the fields. By rivers and in marshes.
They were together on the battlefield too.
Until a terrible fate tore them apart.
“Hyung.”
“The day we became sworn brothers, you made me a vow. You said you’d become a better Palace Lord than anyone. That you’d put Nanman above all else and fight for the people of this land.”
“Enough. Stop.”
The Beast Miao King already knew why Baeksang had brought up these memories. He knew what Baeksang meant to say.
“Do I truly have to... kill you with my own hands?”
Baeksang gave a small nod.
“Far too much blood has already been spilled. Everything happened because of my misguided choices.”

The traitor who had betrayed Nanman and its countless tribespeople had to be executed. That was a duty the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace had to carry out himself—the only way to keep the vow he had made in the old shrine.
“You vowed to become a better Palace Lord than anyone.”
With effort, Baeksang raised a hand and pointed behind the Beast Miao King, who stood as rigid as a statue.
His trembling finger indicated the countless tribespeople and warriors making their way over the rubble into the Inner Palace.
“Everyone is watching. You and me. All of us.”
It was true.

The people constantly pouring into the Inner Palace had learned that the catastrophe was over and cheered. Then they were horrified by the sight that unfolded before their eyes. Finally, they fell silent at the sight of their returning Palace Lord and the traitor collapsed before him.
No. Not silent.
Furious.
“I can feel their anger. It’s aimed at me.”
This was the moment Baeksang had feared most—and wanted more than anything.
If this moment had come, someone had stopped him. Dark Heaven and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s grand plan had failed.
That was why he could laugh aloud. Why he could haul his dying body upright, wring out the last of his strength, and shout.
“Remember this!”
His eyes were dim, as though their light might go out at any moment. But his voice rang through the Inner Palace, clear enough for everyone to hear.
“Though the grand plan has failed, the day will surely come when Dark Heaven’s sky devours Nanman!”
The cry carried over heaps of rubble and corpses to reach every ear.
Blood burst between Baeksang’s teeth with each syllable. Strength drained from his body. Still, he did not stop. He could not.
He was the traitor who had betrayed them all and brought about this catastrophe.
A man guilty of an unforgivable crime had to die a criminal, without sympathy or an explanation for what he had done.
That was... the last thing Baeksang could do.
“That day, which will come before long...!”
He swallowed the blood rising in his throat, clenched his teeth, and shouted on.
“Those contemptible Han Chinese bastards of the Central Plains, and you utterly primitive people of Nanman, will all kneel and submit at the feet of the great Lord of Heaven!”
Baeksang’s bloodstained lips spread into a bright smile.
At that moment, no one was a more loyal servant of the Lord of Heaven, a more faithful dog of Dark Heaven.
And his sworn elder brother had only one choice.
Crack!
A fist shot through the air, crushing flesh and shattering bone.
The single punch buried deep in Baeksang’s chest carried green Force, like the broad fields where they had rolled around together as children.
Thank you, hyung.
You became a truly great Palace Lord, just as you promised.
Along with a murmur no one could hear, Baeksang stared at the face of one person visible beyond his fading field of vision.
But why...?
Why are you crying?
The great Palace Lord who had executed a traitor and stopped a catastrophe was weeping bitterly, like a child who had lost something precious.
Then he shouted, almost howling.
“I have executed Baeksang, the traitor who joined forces with Dark Heaven!”
The people’s cheers reached Baeksang faintly. His head fell back, and he looked up at the sky.
Clear and blue.
The world was no longer dark.
Isn’t that right, Hwi?
He thought of the son who had lost his reason and driven a sword into his father’s chest, and of the child already waiting for him in another world, smiling brightly.
Baeksang smiled in peace.
Thud.
His strength left him, and his body collapsed.
The world remained bright. The people went on cheering.
And in place of his sworn elder brother, who was not even allowed to wail, someone closed Baeksang’s eyes.
“...Fuck. What the hell are you smiling about? It’s not like you did anything right.”
Jin Taekyung muttered to himself, then suddenly looked down at the old thing clenched in his hand.
He didn’t know. Baeksang deserved to die. He was a bad man who had done terrible things. So why did Jin feel so damn awful? Why had he brought this?
Damn it.
Along with the curses that never left his mouth, Jin Taekyung covered Baeksang’s face with the object in his hand.
Baekcheon.
The old silk, bearing someone’s years and hopes, fluttered in a cool breeze from somewhere.
Through the endless cheers came voices, faint as echoes.
“Captain!”
“Pavilion Master—no, Young Master Jin!”
“Taishan is here! Taishan is sorry he’s late!”
“Hey, you bastard! Are you alive?”
Am I hearing things?
Jin Taekyung turned. He stared blankly at the familiar faces drawing closer, then finally let out a quiet laugh.
And collapsed.
I had a very long dream.
A terrible nightmare.
Even in my sleep, I was fighting for my life. In the modern world, I fought monsters. In Murim, I fought Dark Heaven.
Then, after I defeated the Southern Heaven Demon Empress in a brutal fight—just as I had in real life—some masked bastard appeared and said:
“You defeated the Western Heaven Demon Lord and even the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. Not bad.”
I was wondering what hole this bastard had crawled out of when he went on.
“But the Western Heaven Demon Lord and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress were merely the weakest of our Eight Great Heavenly Kings.”
“I am the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who commands the east. Directly beneath me in rank is the East-West Heaven Demon Empress, who commands the east and west.”
No, fuck this. Four directions were plenty. What the hell is an East-West Heaven Demon Empress?
He’d taken the bit so far I had nothing to say.
At this rate, I feared that even if I returned to the modern world, I might find the Dongducheon Demon Lord or the Incheon Demon Empress waiting for me.
But what else could I do? I didn’t know I was dreaming, so I fought like hell.
With every step I took toward him, people I had killed—or failed to save—appeared and blocked my path.
“Just a little more. Just a little farther...”
“If you’d moved faster, we could have lived.”
“We could have gone home to our families.”
“Why do you get to live when we had to die?”
“Why? Why? Why?”
I had no answer. I stopped moving, and they sank their teeth into my torso.
Slowly. Relentlessly.
I could only stand there, frozen like a statue, because I recognized a face among the mutants.
“I cared for you more than anyone, but in the end, you couldn’t save me.”
A face that couldn’t be among them. That mustn’t be.
Jeok Cheongang.
He came toward me with both arms gone and a gaping hole in the middle of his chest. Then he sank his teeth into the back of my neck.
As he greedily swallowed flesh and blood, he whispered in my ear.
“But when is this infuriating bastard supposed to wake up?”
And at that moment, my eyes flew open.
A strong, unfamiliar smell hung in the air. Above me was a ceiling I didn’t recognize.
I blinked blankly, slowly becoming aware of reality. Then a familiar voice pierced my ears.
“Come clean now, and I’ll let you off with a little singeing. You’re a quack, aren’t you?”
“N-no, sir.”
“The child hasn’t woken up for seven days and nights. Does that make any sense? Go get the Beast Miao King.”
“Gasp. Th-that’s...”
“I said bring Yayul Cheok here!”
I turned toward the booming voice. Jeok Cheongang had a physician by the collar and was shaking him violently.
