Baeksang could still picture the big boy pulling him to his feet and brushing the dust from his clothes after a fall.
And the shadow of someone quietly leaving medicinal herbs outside his quarters whenever he was sick.
“So I challenged you to one last duel.”
The result was no different that day.
Baeksang fought harder than he ever had—and lost.
If that had been the end of it, the day would have been like any other.
But this time, he did not push away the hand that helped him up.
He did not stalk back to his quarters, huffing in anger.
Instead, he produced two bottles of fruit wine he had stolen from somewhere and muttered as though to himself.
“I’ve got wine, but no one to drink it with.
Come along if you want.”
At the Beast Miao King’s quiet voice, Baeksang’s eyes widened for a moment.
Then he coughed up blood and laughed.
“Cough.
You still remember that?”
“How could I forget?
You’re the only twelve-year-old brat I’ve ever known who’d say something so cheeky.”
“Then you must remember how I emptied both bottles myself.”
“Both bottles?”
The Beast Miao King could not help laughing.
Moisture had gathered at the corners of his crescent-shaped eyes.
“Well, I vividly remember the little brat who collapsed before he had even finished a single cup.
I also remember what you said while looking at me with those unfocused eyes.”
Baeksang nodded weakly, his unfocused gaze reaching back into the past.
“I said I’d be content to become Great Chieftain, so you should become a great Palace Lord.
I couldn’t have said that to you sober.
That’s why I drank.”
“And what you said after that?
Did you need to be drunk for that too?”
“Of course not.”
Baeksang continued in a quiet voice.
“You were... simply my hyung.
Perhaps you had been since the day we met.”
The two boys had tasted alcohol for the first time, then collapsed and fallen asleep.
When they opened their eyes the next morning in an old shrine, they had become sworn brothers closer than anyone else.
In the mountains.
In the fields.
By rivers and in marshes.
They were together on the battlefield too.
Until a terrible fate tore them apart.
“Hyung.”
“The day we became sworn brothers, you made me a vow.
You said you’d become a better Palace Lord than anyone.
That you’d put Nanman above all else and fight for the people of this land.”
“Enough.
Stop.”
The Beast Miao King already knew why Baeksang had brought up these memories.
He knew what Baeksang meant to say.
“Do I truly have to... kill you with my own hands?”
Baeksang gave a small nod.
“Far too much blood has already been spilled.
Everything happened because of my misguided choices.”
The traitor who had betrayed Nanman and its countless tribespeople had to be executed.
That was a duty the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace had to carry out himself—the only way to keep the vow he had made in the old shrine.
“You vowed to become a better Palace Lord than anyone.”
With effort, Baeksang raised a hand and pointed behind the Beast Miao King, who stood as rigid as a statue.
His trembling finger indicated the countless tribespeople and warriors making their way over the rubble into the Inner Palace.
“Everyone is watching.
You and me.
All of us.”
It was true.
The people constantly pouring into the Inner Palace had learned that the catastrophe was over and cheered.
Then they were horrified by the sight that unfolded before their eyes.
Finally, they fell silent at the sight of their returning Palace Lord and the traitor collapsed before him.
No.
Not silent.
Furious.
“I can feel their anger.
It’s aimed at me.”
This was the moment Baeksang had feared most—and wanted more than anything.
If this moment had come, someone had stopped him.
Dark Heaven and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s grand plan had failed.
That was why he could laugh aloud.
Why he could haul his dying body upright, wring out the last of his strength, and shout.
“Remember this!”
His eyes were dim, as though their light might go out at any moment.
But his voice rang through the Inner Palace, clear enough for everyone to hear.
“Though the grand plan has failed, the day will surely come when Dark Heaven’s sky devours Nanman!”
The cry carried over heaps of rubble and corpses to reach every ear.
Blood burst between Baeksang’s teeth with each syllable.
Strength drained from his body.
Still, he did not stop.
He could not.
He was the traitor who had betrayed them all and brought about this catastrophe.
A man guilty of an unforgivable crime had to die a criminal, without sympathy or an explanation for what he had done.
That was... the last thing Baeksang could do.
“That day, which will come before long...!”
He swallowed the blood rising in his throat, clenched his teeth, and shouted on.
“Those contemptible Han Chinese bastards of the Central Plains, and you utterly primitive people of Nanman, will all kneel and submit at the feet of the great Lord of Heaven!”
Baeksang’s bloodstained lips spread into a bright smile.
At that moment, no one was a more loyal servant of the Lord of Heaven, a more faithful dog of Dark Heaven.
And his sworn elder brother had only one choice.
Crack!
A fist shot through the air, crushing flesh and shattering bone.
The single punch buried deep in Baeksang’s chest carried green Force, like the broad fields where they had rolled around together as children.
Thank you, hyung.
You became a truly great Palace Lord, just as you promised.
Along with a murmur no one could hear, Baeksang stared at the face of one person visible beyond his fading field of vision.
But why...?
Why are you crying?
The great Palace Lord who had executed a traitor and stopped a catastrophe was weeping bitterly, like a child who had lost something precious.
Then he shouted, almost howling.
“I have executed Baeksang, the traitor who joined forces with Dark Heaven!”
The people’s cheers reached Baeksang faintly.
His head fell back, and he looked up at the sky.
Clear and blue.
The world was no longer dark.
Isn’t that right, Hwi?
He thought of the son who had lost his reason and driven a sword into his father’s chest, and of the child already waiting for him in another world, smiling brightly.
Baeksang smiled in peace.
Thud.
His strength left him, and his body collapsed.
The world remained bright.
The people went on cheering.
And in place of his sworn elder brother, who was not even allowed to wail, someone closed Baeksang’s eyes.
“...Fuck.
What the hell are you smiling about?
It’s not like you did anything right.”
Jin Taekyung muttered to himself, then suddenly looked down at the old thing clenched in his hand.
He didn’t know.
Baeksang deserved to die.
He was a bad man who had done terrible things.
So why did Jin feel so damn awful?
Why had he brought this?
Damn it.
Along with the curses that never left his mouth, Jin Taekyung covered Baeksang’s face with the object in his hand.
Baekcheon.
The old silk, bearing someone’s years and hopes, fluttered in a cool breeze from somewhere.
Through the endless cheers came voices, faint as echoes.
“Captain!”
“Pavilion Master—no, Young Master Jin!”
“Taishan is here!
Taishan is sorry he’s late!”
“Hey, you bastard!
Are you alive?”
Am I hearing things?
Jin Taekyung turned.
He stared blankly at the familiar faces drawing closer, then finally let out a quiet laugh.
And collapsed.
I had a very long dream.
A terrible nightmare.
Even in my sleep, I was fighting for my life.
In the modern world, I fought monsters.
In Murim, I fought Dark Heaven.
Then, after I defeated the Southern Heaven Demon Empress in a brutal fight—just as I had in real life—some masked bastard appeared and said:
“You defeated the Western Heaven Demon Lord and even the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
Not bad.”
I was wondering what hole this bastard had crawled out of when he went on.
“But the Western Heaven Demon Lord and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress were merely the weakest of our Eight Great Heavenly Kings.”
“I am the Eastern Heaven Demon Lord, who commands the east.
Directly beneath me in rank is the East-West Heaven Demon Empress, who commands the east and west.”
No, fuck this.
Four directions were plenty.
What the hell is an East-West Heaven Demon Empress?
He’d taken the bit so far I had nothing to say.
At this rate, I feared that even if I returned to the modern world, I might find the Dongducheon Demon Lord or the Incheon Demon Empress waiting for me.
But what else could I do?
I didn’t know I was dreaming, so I fought like hell.
With every step I took toward him, people I had killed—or failed to save—appeared and blocked my path.
“Just a little more.
Just a little farther...”
“If you’d moved faster, we could have lived.”
“We could have gone home to our families.”
“Why do you get to live when we had to die?”
“Why?
Why?
Why?”
I had no answer.
I stopped moving, and they sank their teeth into my torso.
Slowly.
Relentlessly.
I could only stand there, frozen like a statue, because I recognized a face among the mutants.
“I cared for you more than anyone, but in the end, you couldn’t save me.”
A face that couldn’t be among them.
That mustn’t be.
Jeok Cheongang.
He came toward me with both arms gone and a gaping hole in the middle of his chest.
Then he sank his teeth into the back of my neck.
As he greedily swallowed flesh and blood, he whispered in my ear.
“But when is this infuriating bastard supposed to wake up?”
And at that moment, my eyes flew open.
A strong, unfamiliar smell hung in the air.
Above me was a ceiling I didn’t recognize.
I blinked blankly, slowly becoming aware of reality.
Then a familiar voice pierced my ears.
“Come clean now, and I’ll let you off with a little singeing.
You’re a quack, aren’t you?”
“N-no, sir.”
“The child hasn’t woken up for seven days and nights.
Does that make any sense?
Go get the Beast Miao King.”
“Gasp.
Th-that’s...”
“I said bring Yayul Cheok here!”
I turned toward the booming voice.
Jeok Cheongang had a physician by the collar and was shaking him violently.

chapters.title: Chapter 715
paragraphs: The room smelled of medicinal herbs. A middle-aged man stood trembling with a long acupuncture needle in his hand while Jeok Cheongang held him by the collar.
I can see where this is going. Oh, I can see it.
I had only just woken up, but the situation was easy enough to grasp. The man, who looked like a physician, spotted me blinking over Jeok Cheongang’s shoulder and shouted.
“Ah! Ahhh! He’s awake! He’s awake!”
Even my mother wouldn’t have been that happy to see me wake up.
I guarantee it. That wasn’t the joy of a physician whose patient had recovered. It was the relief of a victim spotting the police while facing a serial killer.
Jeok Cheongang let go of the physician’s collar without a fuss and turned to look at me.
He said nothing, even after the physician hurried out. For a long while, he just looked at me.
Then he spoke.
“You took your time waking up.”
At his gruff tone, I shrugged.
I couldn’t exactly tell him I’d had a fucking nightmare in which Old Master tore into my neck with his teeth.
Did you sleep well?
More or less.
“How do you feel?”
“Light. My head’s clear, too.”
That was no exaggeration. My body felt as light as a feather, and the long sleep had cleared the fatigue from my head. I felt sharper than ever.
They said I was unconscious for seven days and nights, didn’t they?
I must have been more exhausted than I realized.
Not to brag, but it was rare for a master who had reached the Supreme Peak realm like me to remain unconscious for an entire week.
Then, without meaning to, I blurted out, “That’s a relief.”
“What is?”
“That this isn’t a dream.”
“It really is a relief.”
I looked around, overcome with emotion.
Sunlight slipped through the half-open window, and birdsong tickled my ears. Far off, I could sense people passing by and talking quietly among themselves.
I’m alive.
It was ironic.
I was breathing. I could feel the world around me. Yet I still found it hard to believe I was alive.
At the same time, a hollow emptiness took hold of me.

For an instant, the darkness that had wrapped around the Inner Palace seemed to pass over the sunlight settling on the window. So did the sight of countless corpses collapsed with their faces buried in pools of blood.
So... none of it was a dream.
The joy and relief of surviving faded, leaving guilt and bitterness in their place.
I stared blankly at the window until a low voice reached me.
“In the end, some survive, and some die.”
Tap.
A hand came to rest on my shoulder. I felt its warmth as Jeok Cheongang gazed into the distance and continued.
“That is the natural order no one can defy. That is Murim.”
“Be grateful you survived, and mourn those who died. For now, that is enough.”
Jeok Cheongang walked to the window and threw it open. Sunlight poured in, bathing him in its glow. I watched him in silence.
Thoughts flashed through my mind, and I opened my mouth.
“Old Master.”
At my call, Jeok Cheongang smiled warmly and shook his head.
“Enough. You needn’t say anything now.”
“Ah, that’s not what I meant.”
“Enough, I said. There’s much I want to ask you, but first you need time to gather your thoughts—”
“No, it’s just... you’re dazzling me.”
“Hm?”
I cautiously pointed at his head. Gleaming in the sunlight, his bald scalp was using Solar Fist as a passive Skill.
“Either close the window or move your head a little.”
“By the way, did you use Force? You shaved it really clean. I get that it’s a disguise, but you should’ve left some hair. What if it doesn’t grow back?”
The warm smile vanished from Jeok Cheongang’s face.
In an instant, the kindly old man next door became the Blood Monk. He gave me a cold stare.
“You goddamn—”
“I was only asking. Why are you swearing at a patient who just woke up?”
“Would you like to go back to sleep? I could put you out for another three months and fifteen days.”
Crack.
Bones shifted in his tightly clenched fist. Sensing I’d made a terrible mistake, I spoke quickly.
“I’ve slept plenty already.”
“This old man thinks you’d like some more.”
“I’m really fine. The work here is almost done, so we should hurry back to the Central Plains—”
“That’s fine. By the time you wake up, we’ll be in Henan at the very least.”
I swallowed hard.
“That sounds... really bad.”
“Why? The journey will only bore you.”
“It won’t be boring at all. I like admiring natural scenery.”
“How about returning to nature for good?”
“...You’re joking, right?”
“Does it sound like a joke?”
“No.”
“That part was a joke. Waking up in Henan wasn’t.”
Whoosh.
Flames curled around Jeok Cheongang’s fist. I instinctively looked around, but of course there was no fire extinguisher.
I’m fucked. Shit.
Resigned to my fate, I made a polite request.
“Please go easy on me.”
“If you take it without a fuss, I can do that. Which would you prefer, Flame Divine Palm or Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist?”
“...Would either of those not hurt if you used them gently?”
“Would you rather I hit you hard?”
“...Is there anything besides Flame Divine Palm and Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist?”
“There is.”
“Oh? What?”
“Dance of the Fire God and Demon.”
I asked with complete sincerity.
“Have you actually gone senile?”
Whack!
My vision flashed white.
I writhed with my mouth hanging open, pain shooting through my forehead. Jeok Cheongang’s impossibly gruff voice reached me.
“I thought it was about time you woke up, so I came by for the first time in a while. And here you are, perfectly fine. Stop spouting nonsense and get your strength back. I’m leaving.”
Click.
I opened my eyes just as the door shut firmly behind him. Rubbing my forehead with tears in my eyes, I looked at the space he’d left behind and muttered, “You could’ve stayed a little longer...”
Before my faint voice had faded, a tremor swept through the pavilion.
Boom. Boom. Rumble!
Amazingly, those were someone’s footsteps. Alongside the vibrations of what sounded like a charging elephant, I sensed several others approaching with uncanny lightness.
They were headed toward the firmly closed door Jeok Cheongang had just passed through.
“Hey, wait—!”
But my desperate shout never reached the end.
Crash!
The wooden door burst apart, sending dust billowing into the air.
As I stood there blankly frozen in the quarters that had become a ruin in an instant, I saw several familiar faces through the dust cloud and let out a helpless laugh.
Yeah. Well, this isn’t so bad either.
“How’s everyone been?”
As if on cue, several figures leaped toward me at once.
No—one enormous figure soared nearly to the ceiling and came down on all of us, myself included.
Whoooosh!
“Taishan missed the Pavilion Master!”
I hadn’t counted on you.
Bang!
Hearing the crash behind him, Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh.
“Well, what a commotion.”
It had to be that huge fellow—Taishan, or was it Geosan?

The physician who had left the quarters first must already have spread the news. The members of the Fire Dragon Pavilion had rushed over faster than anyone else, barely sparing Jeok Cheongang a glance as they headed toward the pavilion. That had happened only moments ago.
The youngsters want to be together. This old man should give them space.
Granted, there was another old man among them. But Jeok Cheongang had passed ninety-nine long ago. To him, anyone under eighty was in the prime of youth.
It was his firm belief that anyone eighty or younger could chew Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron.
...Perhaps that’s going a bit far.
After muttering inwardly, Jeok Cheongang began to walk slowly.
He looked up at the sky, which had cleared as though nothing had happened, and watched the Nanman people begin gathering in groups of three or five after hearing the news of Jin Taekyung.
The cool breeze brushed against him, and a thought came to him.
No—a question for someone who wasn’t there to hear it.
Do you really believe that?
After seven days and nights, Jin Taekyung had woken and said he was glad this wasn’t a dream. Truly glad.
But his voice, his eyes, everything Jeok Cheongang had seen told a different story.
He blames himself for surviving. For failing to save them.
No one knew what became of the dead. Jeok Cheongang had, however, seen countless people survive hell. He knew how they went on living with regret and guilt.
The Great Faction War.
He had lived through that seeming eternity of blood and death himself.
But overcoming it makes you stronger.
That was why he had said as little as he could. He had pretended not to notice Jin Taekyung groaning and thrashing in pain while unconscious, then made himself ask:
Did you sleep well?
More or less.
It must have been a terrible nightmare. Jin Taekyung had lied through his teeth without batting an eye.
Cheeky brat.
Jeok Cheongang wasn’t angry. He was proud to see Jin Taekyung doing his best to endure it, though it saddened him, too.
That was all.
So why did something in his chest still ache? Why did Jin Taekyung’s figure keep wavering before his eyes even as he looked at the world around him?
Damn it. I really am getting old.
Strangely, he didn’t much mind.
He had witnessed that mysterious recovery with his own eyes, but it was Jin Taekyung—not anything else—who filled his heart.
Well, this isn’t so bad either.
With a faint smile, Jeok Cheongang headed somewhere quiet. Sunlight filtered through the leaves onto his bare scalp.
“Captain.”
“What?”
“Captain.”
“Ah, what?”
“Captaiiin!”
“Stop calling me, you bastard. I’m not dead yet.”
Despite my shouting, Hyuk Mujin’s voice still trembled with tears. He gripped my sleeve in both hands and looked up at me with wet eyes.
“Then when are you going to pass away?”
“...Are you insane? You sound like you’re praying for me to die.”
“You were unconscious for seven whole days and nights. I really thought you were going to die.”
Taishan, who was on his hands and knees mopping the floor at my express command, promptly nodded.
“That’s right. Taishan thought the Pavilion Master would never wake up and looked forward to it.”
I was just beginning to feel touched when I noticed that something was wrong and blinked.
“Looked forward to it? Why?”
Namho, who had claimed the only chair on account of his age, muttered, “Why ask? The son of a bitch was looking forward to the funeral feast.”
“No! Taishan worried so much about the Pavilion Master that he drooled whenever he thought of him!”
That bastard really had been looking forward to it.
Sama Pyo, who was practically Taishan’s mother, met my eyes and lowered his head weakly.
“Pretend you didn’t hear that. Even with ten mouths, I’d have nothing to say.”
“Ten mouths? If Taishan had ten mouths—!”
“You’d eat ten times as much. Please, can someone muzzle him?”
Just as Assemblyman Namho of the Nanman Party formally introduced the Taishan Muzzle Bill, something whistled through the air.
Whoosh—crash!
The table—the one piece of furniture in the ruined quarters that had more or less kept its shape—splintered in a single blow.
Then came a cold voice.
“What... are you all doing in front of a patient?”
Everyone fell silent at Ju Hwaran’s question. She had just smashed a table in front of that same patient.

No—a question for someone who wasn’t there to hear it.
Do you really believe that?
After seven days and nights, Jin Taekyung had woken and said he was glad this wasn’t a dream.
Truly glad.
But his voice, his eyes, everything Jeok Cheongang had seen told a different story.
He blames himself for surviving.
For failing to save them.
No one knew what became of the dead.
Jeok Cheongang had, however, seen countless people survive hell.
He knew how they went on living with regret and guilt.
The Great Faction War.
He had lived through that seeming eternity of blood and death himself.
But overcoming it makes you stronger.
That was why he had said as little as he could.
He had pretended not to notice Jin Taekyung groaning and thrashing in pain while unconscious, then made himself ask:
Did you sleep well?
More or less.
It must have been a terrible nightmare.
Jin Taekyung had lied through his teeth without batting an eye.
Cheeky brat.
Jeok Cheongang wasn’t angry.
He was proud to see Jin Taekyung doing his best to endure it, though it saddened him, too.
That was all.
So why did something in his chest still ache?
Why did Jin Taekyung’s figure keep wavering before his eyes even as he looked at the world around him?
Damn it.
I really am getting old.
Strangely, he didn’t much mind.
He had witnessed that mysterious recovery with his own eyes, but it was Jin Taekyung—not anything else—who filled his heart.
Well, this isn’t so bad either.
With a faint smile, Jeok Cheongang headed somewhere quiet.
Sunlight filtered through the leaves onto his bare scalp.
“Captain.”
“What?”
“Captain.”
“Ah, what?”
“Captaiiin!”
“Stop calling me, you bastard.
I’m not dead yet.”
Despite my shouting, Hyuk Mujin’s voice still trembled with tears.
He gripped my sleeve in both hands and looked up at me with wet eyes.
“Then when are you going to pass away?”
“...Are you insane?
You sound like you’re praying for me to die.”
“You were unconscious for seven whole days and nights.
I really thought you were going to die.”
Taishan, who was on his hands and knees mopping the floor at my express command, promptly nodded.
“That’s right.
Taishan thought the Pavilion Master would never wake up and looked forward to it.”
I was just beginning to feel touched when I noticed that something was wrong and blinked.
“Looked forward to it?
Why?”
Namho, who had claimed the only chair on account of his age, muttered, “Why ask?
The son of a bitch was looking forward to the funeral feast.”
“No!
Taishan worried so much about the Pavilion Master that he drooled whenever he thought of him!”
That bastard really had been looking forward to it.
Sama Pyo, who was practically Taishan’s mother, met my eyes and lowered his head weakly.
“Pretend you didn’t hear that.
Even with ten mouths, I’d have nothing to say.”
“Ten mouths?
If Taishan had ten mouths—!”
“You’d eat ten times as much.
Please, can someone muzzle him?”
Just as Assemblyman Namho of the Nanman Party formally introduced the Taishan Muzzle Bill, something whistled through the air.
Whoosh—crash!
The table—the one piece of furniture in the ruined quarters that had more or less kept its shape—splintered in a single blow.
Then came a cold voice.
“What... are you all doing in front of a patient?”
Everyone fell silent at Ju Hwaran’s question.
She had just smashed a table in front of that same patient.

chapters.title: Chapter 716
paragraphs: They say it’s scarier when someone who’s usually quiet gets angry.
Ju Hwaran was proving the point.
Clatter.

Wooden splinters rained from the hand of the Yongbong Escort Bureau’s precious jewel. She was the human air purifier who had kept this jalapeño pepper party—reeking of old men and getting downright spicy—bearable.
Her usually gentle eyes and voice had turned sharp as thorns.
“Young Hero Taishan.”
Taishan, her first target, flinched.
“Do you have any idea how much the Pavilion Master—how much Young Master Jin has gone through for us? How could you say something like that?”
“Ta-Taishan was wrong.”
“I know you have an enormous appetite, but if you say anything ominous like that again, I really will muzzle you, just as Elder Namho suggested.”
At Ju Hwaran’s stern warning, Sama Pyo narrowed his brows and opened his mouth.
“Young Lady Ju, Taishan isn’t a beast.”
“Then should I muzzle you instead of Taishan?”
“Well?”
Sama Pyo considered this for a moment, then answered with a solemn expression.
“Come to think of it, an occasional muzzle might help him manage his diet.”
“Be more careful from now on. I know you meant no harm, but that was too much.”
“...Understood. I’ll have a word with him.”
With his proposed muzzle bill narrowly defeated, Namho muttered mournfully, “I’d hoped to see that bastard muzzled before I died...”
But he couldn’t escape Ju Hwaran’s attention either.
“Elder Namho.”
“H-huh?”
“You’re an elder. You should act like one. Swearing like that in front of a patient who hasn’t even recovered isn’t a good look.”
“What? A patient?”
Namho eyed my face, positively glowing after all those level-ups and days of rest. He looked unconvinced.
“Never mind that. Where would you find a worse foulmouth than Jin Taekyung? Why are you coming after me all of a sudden—”
Tap.
I saw it clearly. Just as Namho was about to continue his protest, Hyuk Mujin discreetly jabbed him in the ribs with an elbow.
Translated into modern terms, that little gesture said:
Don’t kill the mood. Just say “for real, lol.”
Namho had decades of spy work behind him. His eyes darted around before he bowed his head in resignation.
“Understood. I’ll be careful.”
“Good. Next, Young Hero Hyuk—what are you doing?”
“I’m massaging the Captain’s shoulders to help him recover from all his hard work.”
Right. They didn’t call him Hyukroach for nothing.
Ju Hwaran smiled approvingly at the sight of Mujin deftly massaging me, then turned to the last person in the room.
“Captain Song.”
A tremor ran through Song Ilseom’s pupils. He had remained silent from beginning to end.
“I haven’t said anything.”
“I know. Keep it that way.”
“...Understood.”
With her final target dealt with, Ju Hwaran looked at me.
The moment our eyes met, my mouth opened on reflex.
“I’m sorry. I apologize. I was wrong.”
“What?”
“Yes?”
“What are you apologizing for?”
“Oh. Nothing. I just...”
I felt like I had to. Survival instinct, maybe.
I shot a look at Hyuk Mujin, who was now diligently massaging my legs.
What happened? Why is Young Lady Ju like this?
He answered with a look of his own.
She was worried sick about you, Captain. Just let it go.
Even so. The air feels different. The air.
If you can’t read the room, at least keep your mou—
“What are you two doing?” Ju Hwaran asked suddenly.
Mujin’s hands flew twice as fast.
“What do you mean? I’m massaging the Captain’s legs. Oh, these muscles are really knotted up. Should I press harder?”
Something felt wrong. I cautiously caught his arm.
“That’s enough. Stop.”
“Huh? Why?”
“No, it’s... fine now.”
“Our Captain is doing it again. You like it because it feels good, don’t you?”
“No. I said it’s fine. You must be tired too, so stop.”
“Don’t be shy. I, Hyuk Mujin, can do anything for my Captain as his right-hand man. You saw that, didn’t you, Young Lady Ju? That’s how well our Captain takes care of his people.”
As Mujin turned to Ju Hwaran and laughed heartily, I sent him a Sound Transmission in despair.
—That wasn’t my leg just now...
—So get your hand off me right now, you bastard. Before I break your wrist.
After a brief silence, Mujin slowly withdrew his hand.
I wanted desperately to smack the back of his head as he stared at me with a gaze filled with a mixture of awe and fear, but I barely managed to hold myself back in front of everyone else.
Then again, maybe...
No. That’s going too far.
I let the thought go and looked around at each of their faces.
Only a few days ago, I’d thought I might never see them again. Our situation had been that bad. Everything ahead of us had been lost in fog.
But now that we were all gathered together like this, alive, I was overcome with emotion all over again.
The fact that not one of them had died filled me with joy.
“I’m glad. Really.”
At my single sentence, which broke the brief silence, everyone’s eyes widened. Then they smiled faintly.
That was enough.
We’d grown close enough to understand what the others felt.
It took a while to hear the whole story.
We’d lived through the same stretch of time, but in different places, facing different things. Their story also covered the seven days and nights I’d spent unconscious.
“I really thought we were going to die. You weren’t there, Captain, and we were tied up. Then that Blood Monk we’d only heard stories about stepped right off the swift ship. I mean... wow.”
“If we hadn’t recognized Great Hero Jeok, there would have been a fight. The Nanman warriors with us were itching for one.”
“I thought it was all over. We were supposed to be bringing reinforcements to save you, and instead a fiend called the Blood Monk appeared.”
They gave me more detail than Jeok Cheongang had.

The Nanman warriors hadn’t believed the Blood Monk’s identity at first. Then the bandits from the Water Dragon Stronghold—all of them sporting bruises around their eyes—stepped forward to confirm that he was the Fire King. The fight ended before it began.
Jeok Cheongang rushed to the Nanman Beast Palace with all his strength. By the time the Fire Dragon Pavilion members and Nanman scouts arrived a step behind him, everything was over.
“When we saw you collapse, Captain, I really thought you’d died. You were covered in blood, and there was nothing around you but blood and corpses...”
I was about to interrupt Mujin. If the state of my perfectly healthy body came up, how could anyone not be suspicious?
But before I could speak, Ju Hwaran went on.
“Great Hero Jeok reassured everyone. He said you’d only collapsed from exhaustion.”
I asked, feeling uneasy.
“...What exactly did the Old Master—no, my master—say?”
“Hmm. I’m not sure. Everyone was in such a panic. But I remember him saying you hadn’t been seriously injured because he’d arrived in time. Palace Lord Yayul agreed.”
Namho nodded and chimed in.

“It was heavenly luck. Heavenly luck. No matter how powerful that bastard is, how could he have survived that hellscape? Two of the Ten Kings had stepped in. Even the Southern Heaven Demon Empress wouldn’t have been able to do anything.”
That wasn’t quite what had happened.
I nodded anyway.
This was unmistakable protection. Jeok Cheongang and the Beast Miao King had taken action to conceal my secret and keep people from becoming suspicious.
The Baekcheon Unit survivors will keep quiet too. Their loyalty is to the Beast Miao King.
The dead couldn’t talk. Most of the fighting that day had taken place in the Inner Palace, and most of the people there had died.
As long as the survivors said nothing, the secret would hold.
Even though I’ve grown close to them, I can’t tell them.
In the modern world, people called things they couldn’t explain Magic or miracles.
Here in Murim, they would use another word.
Demon.
Supernatural powers beyond anyone’s understanding were bound to inspire fear. I wanted as few people as possible to know about the System—about this ability of mine.
Though what was done was done.

I had no idea what consequences my unavoidable choice that day would bring. Still, I was glad the person who’d seen it up close was Jeok Cheongang. I knew what kind of man the Beast Miao King was, too, and that put me at ease.
“Captain?”
“Huh?”
“What are you thinking about so hard?”
I must have been lost in thought for a while. Mujin was watching me suspiciously, so I waved a hand.
“Nothing. My mind wandered for a second. Go on.”
“Oh, right. Where was I?”
“...Did you hit your head?”
“No. Maybe it’s from someone smacking me in the back of it so often.”
He glanced at me, leaving no doubt who he meant.
“I think I told you we gathered the dead and cremated them. You know all the chieftains who sided with Baeksang and then ran away were thrown into the underground prison, right?”
“More or less.”
“Oh, and I heard Great Chieftain Yohi asked to be punished herself.”
“Yohi did?”
“Yes. Great Hero Yayul seemed willing to forgive her, but she voluntarily entered the underground prison.”
I hadn’t expected Yohi to go that far. In a way, though, it made sense.
She’d repented too late, but she had joined Baeksang for wealth and power. Nearly dying must have taught her something.
She chose it herself. She must have thought it was the right thing to do.
I listened as they went on.

More Nanman people than ever were staying at the Nanman Beast Palace, working to restore the ruined Inner Palace and repair the considerable damage to the Outer Palace. Young Palace Lord Yayul Mok was so busy he barely had a moment to breathe.
“We sent word to him, but I don’t know if he can come right away,” Mujin said. “Lately, we can barely catch a glimpse of him.”
“I can imagine. The Beast Miao King must be just as busy.”
“Great Hero Yayul... You probably won’t see him either—not just us, but anyone else.”
“What?”
“He disappeared two days ago. I hear the leadership is already in an uproar.”

chapters.title: Chapter 717
paragraphs: Seven days and nights could feel long or short, depending on the person.
But for the Nanman Beast Palace, it was nowhere near enough time to repair all the damage.

The demonic qi that had poured from the rift was gone, but its aftermath remained. Countless people had died. Some had lost their families and homes. Others must have been afraid the disaster could return at any moment.
And the Beast Miao King disappeared in the middle of all that?
I frowned, thought it over, then asked, “Tell me exactly what you know.”

Hyuk Mujin scratched the back of his head. “Uh, sorry, but it isn’t much. Like I said, the Nanman leadership is in an uproar. They even discussed casting a net over heaven and earth to find Great Hero Yayul.”
I could hardly blame them. The Palace Lord, the one person they needed to rally around in a crisis, had vanished.
They were probably worried Dark Heaven had made another move, too.
An assassination. Or a kidnapping.

Maybe I was getting ahead of myself, but neither was impossible. The Beast Miao King had been badly injured in his fight with the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. His martial prowess was extraordinary, and Jeok Cheongang had reached him in time to help, but he couldn’t have recovered in just a few days.
“So what did the search turn up?”
Mujin tilted his head. “What search?”
“...Did you actually hurt your head? You’ve forgotten what you said a moment ago?”
“Oh. The net over heaven and earth.” He slapped his forehead. “I only said they discussed it.”
“Huh?”
“They called it off.”
Called it off? Over something this serious?
I blinked, then asked, “Did Dark Heaven take over the Nanman Beast Palace while I was asleep?”
“The leadership? I don’t think so.”
“Then they’re searching in secret so they won’t alarm the tribespeople?”
“I don’t think so either.”
“Then why the hell aren’t they looking for their Palace Lord?”
“Why are you asking me? He isn’t my Palace Lord.”
Whack!
Mujin finally earned himself another point toward his back-of-the-head mileage. He crumpled with a silent scream.
Namho clicked his tongue at the sight of him writhing on the floor, then turned to me.
“Ordinarily, the leadership would have done something. Cast a net over heaven and earth, sent warriors to search in secret—anything.”
I lowered my fist. “But they did nothing?”
“They had no choice. Someone stopped them.”
“Someone?”
“What choice did they have? This wasn’t some nobody who’d crawled in off the street. The great Fire King himself told them to drop everything.”

“He reportedly told them that if the Palace Lord didn’t appear by midnight two days later, he would step in personally, so they should shut their mouths and focus on calming the people. The Young Palace Lord agonized over it, but in the end, he listened to the Fire King. The other chieftains had no choice either.”
Jeok Cheongang—and Yayul Mok, too?
My surprise didn’t last long. I thought for a moment, then nodded.
“Midnight two days later. That’s tonight, isn’t it?”
“That’s right.”
“I see.”
“I see? That’s all?”
“What else is there to say? If Ol—no, if Master said to drop it, then we should drop it.”
Namho stared at me, then smacked his lips. “That’s quite a bond of trust between master and disciple.”
“His personality is terrible, but he has his reasons for doing things.”
“Would that bond hold if I told him what you said about his personality?”
“...Things would get heated. Do you want to see me wake up in Henan?”
“Why even ask? Of course—”
His answer had come without a moment’s hesitation. Then he glanced toward someone and continued in a mournful voice.
“Of course I’ll keep it a secret. Naturally.”
What was that? Had Ju Hwaran just given him an axe-eyed glare?
But her eyes were curved into a smile when I looked. I must have imagined it. I probably wasn’t fully awake yet.
Smack.
I patted my cheeks and stretched. My stiff bones cracked, and I felt lighter than ever.
I’m in perfect shape.
Between leveling up and resting for seven days and nights, my body couldn’t have been better. The nightmare had left me in a foul mood, but that would pass.
Someone else is probably feeling the same way.
I put on a sleepy face for the others.
“Ah, I’m tired after talking so much for the first time in a while. Could you all give me a moment alone?”
Being a patient had its advantages. People accepted whatever I said without question.
Once they were gone, I slipped out of the pavilion through the window.
It was only a guess.
If he isn’t there, no big deal. If he is, then great.
But the moment I entered a remote patch of grass that no one ever visited, my guess became certainty.
“Oh, there you are.”
Rustle.
The grass stirred faintly at my greeting. At the same instant, a streak of light shot toward me.
Whoosh—crack!
The dagger flew straight toward the space between my brows. I caught it without even looking, and the blade began to glow red, unable to withstand the heat of the Scorching Yang Qi in my hand.
Drip. Hissss.
Molten metal fell to the ground. Only then did I remember I was still wearing my mask. I threw both hands up.
“It’s me. Jin Taekyung.”
A moment later, faint sounds of air splitting came from above. Several figures landed among the thick grass.
One, two, three... seven.
Exactly as many as I’d sensed. And I knew who they were.
“The Seven Miao Tigers, right?”
Step.
“Please forgive our rudeness.”
The man in front stepped forward and removed his mask, revealing a good-natured face I recognized from the underground prison.

sentences.text: Seven days and nights could feel long or short, depending on the person.
But for the Nanman Beast Palace, it was nowhere near enough time to repair all the damage.
The demonic qi that had poured from the rift was gone, but its aftermath remained.
Countless people had died.
Some had lost their families and homes.
Others must have been afraid the disaster could return at any moment.
And the Beast Miao King disappeared in the middle of all that?
I frowned, thought it over, then asked, “Tell me exactly what you know.”
Hyuk Mujin scratched the back of his head.
“Uh, sorry, but it isn’t much.
Like I said, the Nanman leadership is in an uproar.
They even discussed casting a net over heaven and earth to find Great Hero Yayul.”
I could hardly blame them.
The Palace Lord, the one person they needed to rally around in a crisis, had vanished.
They were probably worried Dark Heaven had made another move, too.
An assassination.
Or a kidnapping.
Maybe I was getting ahead of myself, but neither was impossible.
The Beast Miao King had been badly injured in his fight with the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
His martial prowess was extraordinary, and Jeok Cheongang had reached him in time to help, but he couldn’t have recovered in just a few days.
“So what did the search turn up?”
Mujin tilted his head.
“What search?”
“...Did you actually hurt your head?
You’ve forgotten what you said a moment ago?”
“Oh.
The net over heaven and earth.” He slapped his forehead.
“I only said they discussed it.”
“Huh?”
“They called it off.”
Called it off?
Over something this serious?
I blinked, then asked, “Did Dark Heaven take over the Nanman Beast Palace while I was asleep?”
“The leadership?
I don’t think so.”
“Then they’re searching in secret so they won’t alarm the tribespeople?”
“I don’t think so either.”
“Then why the hell aren’t they looking for their Palace Lord?”
“Why are you asking me?
He isn’t my Palace Lord.”
Whack!
Mujin finally earned himself another point toward his back-of-the-head mileage.
He crumpled with a silent scream.
Namho clicked his tongue at the sight of him writhing on the floor, then turned to me.
“Ordinarily, the leadership would have done something.
Cast a net over heaven and earth, sent warriors to search in secret—anything.”
I lowered my fist.
“But they did nothing?”
“They had no choice.
Someone stopped them.”
“Someone?”
“What choice did they have?
This wasn’t some nobody who’d crawled in off the street.
The great Fire King himself told them to drop everything.”
“He reportedly told them that if the Palace Lord didn’t appear by midnight two days later, he would step in personally, so they should shut their mouths and focus on calming the people.
The Young Palace Lord agonized over it, but in the end, he listened to the Fire King.
The other chieftains had no choice either.”
Jeok Cheongang—and Yayul Mok, too?
My surprise didn’t last long.
I thought for a moment, then nodded.
“Midnight two days later.
That’s tonight, isn’t it?”
“That’s right.”
“I see.”
“I see?
That’s all?”
“What else is there to say?
If Ol—no, if Master said to drop it, then we should drop it.”
Namho stared at me, then smacked his lips.
“That’s quite a bond of trust between master and disciple.”
“His personality is terrible, but he has his reasons for doing things.”
“Would that bond hold if I told him what you said about his personality?”
“...Things would get heated.
Do you want to see me wake up in Henan?”
“Why even ask?
Of course—”
His answer had come without a moment’s hesitation.
Then he glanced toward someone and continued in a mournful voice.
“Of course I’ll keep it a secret.
Naturally.”
What was that?
Had Ju Hwaran just given him an axe-eyed glare?
But her eyes were curved into a smile when I looked.
I must have imagined it.
I probably wasn’t fully awake yet.
Smack.
I patted my cheeks and stretched.
My stiff bones cracked, and I felt lighter than ever.
I’m in perfect shape.
Between leveling up and resting for seven days and nights, my body couldn’t have been better.
The nightmare had left me in a foul mood, but that would pass.
Someone else is probably feeling the same way.
I put on a sleepy face for the others.
“Ah, I’m tired after talking so much for the first time in a while.
Could you all give me a moment alone?”
Being a patient had its advantages.

It was only a guess.

chapters.title: Chapter 718
paragraphs: “Despite all those deaths, the person I grieved for most was Baeksang.”
The Beast Miao King’s low voice reached me. I stayed silent for a moment before asking, “Is that why you left? Because you thought it was wrong to feel that way?”
“To become the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace means putting this land and its tribespeople before anything else. But I became trapped by my personal feelings.”
I could see his enormous back, like a thousand-year-old megalith. Yet the back of the giant who had supported Nanman for so many years looked pitifully small at that moment, like a child’s.
“Do you know what I was thinking when I faced Baeksang for the last time?”
I could guess, but I said nothing. The person who knew Baeksang best—and who had suffered most because of him—was right in front of me.
“I wanted to save him somehow.”
“Even in that horrific scene, I wanted to save that bastard Baeksang, who had betrayed everyone in this land, myself included, and help him run far away.”

They weren’t related by blood, but they were sworn brothers, as close as family. The Beast Miao King must have wanted to save Baeksang however he could. He must have wanted to absolve the man who had served as Dark Heaven’s hunting dog while the child he’d believed dead was held hostage.
But Baeksang himself had refused.
“He probably knew, too. That I was hesitating. That must be why he made that choice.”

The Beast Miao King’s murmur faded into the silence. The emotion in his voice was grief over being forced to end the life of his sworn younger brother—the man he had cherished more than his own life—with his own hands. It was also self-reproach for abandoning his duty as Palace Lord because of his personal feelings.
“One diseased tree caused the forest to die. Yet the forest keeper is now pacing in front of the diseased tree that has already fallen. Could you call such a person a forest keeper?”
I had been listening quietly to the Beast Miao King’s story. Then I broke the long silence.
“Great Hero Yayul, I’m asking you this in all seriousness...”
My voice trailed off. Even now, I wasn’t sure I should say it. But I had to get that devastated forest keeper back on his feet, even if it meant crossing the line a little. Or a lot.
“Are you fucking stupid?”
I could sense his agitation even from behind. I’d already started, though, so I pressed on.
“What, is the Palace Lord some kind of god of heaven and earth? Don’t you have human emotions?”

“Let’s be honest. Someone who spent their entire life with you, someone like family, just died. Who in this world could be fine after that? Are you supposed to be sadder just because other people died, too?”
The Beast Miao King took a moment to answer my barrage of blunt questions.
“Jin Taekyung, you as well?”
I nodded.
“Of course I would. What’s so special about a bastard like me?”
“People around me can praise me as a chivalrous hero or a Great Hero, but I’m still a person in the end. Why would a Palace Lord be any different?”
I answered without hesitation. His broad back shifted.
Rustle.
He slowly turned his head. For the first time since I’d entered the old shrine, I saw his face. He looked utterly haggard.
“They were also Nanman people I had to protect.”
“And you protected them. Even after being branded a traitor, you came back despite the danger. It was thanks to you that countless others could be saved.”
I continued quietly.
“The diseased trees have fallen, but the forest hasn’t died. It needs its forest keeper more than ever.”
Many people had been sacrificed in this incident. But ironically, Nanman would grow even stronger.
Because Baeksang had not been the only diseased tree in the vast forest called Nanman.
The other chieftains. No—the traitors.
Baeksang had joined forces with Dark Heaven for his child. They had followed him for nothing but their own safety and power.

Those were the trees that should have been cut down long ago, trees sick with greed. More than twenty chieftains had shaken their branches, and countless leaves had fallen into bloody water. But the forest had survived.
Under the single banner of the Nanman Beast Palace, its people would come together and flourish. And only one person could raise that banner before all of Nanman.
“Let’s go back. Then that father and son can rest easier too.”
I was speaking to the Beast Miao King, but my eyes were elsewhere. He followed my gaze.
“You knew?”
“I noticed them as soon as I came in. Everything else in here is covered in dust. Those aren’t.”
I walked forward. Between the faded murals and dozens of stone statues I couldn’t identify stood two memorial tablets that hadn’t been there on my last visit.
Neither bore a name. I knew who they were for.
Baeksang. Baekhwi.
I said their names silently—the names even the person who had made the tablets by hand couldn’t bring himself to carve. Then I lowered myself and bowed.
Once. Then again.
When I turned after the second bow, the Beast Miao King was staring at me, his face stiff.
“Why are you looking at me like that?”
“...I didn’t expect it.”
“What, did you think I’d knock the tablets over?”
“You might have. Especially Baeksang’s, after what he did.”
Damn it. Fair enough.
After everything that had happened, I could have split Baeksang’s tablet in half and spat on it and called it self-defense.
But...
“I just wanted to do this. That’s all.”
What was this filthy, bitter feeling?
I looked back at the tablets and thought I might finally have a name for it. Perhaps it was sympathy. Perhaps empathy.
It’s too late. I’ve gone down a road I can’t turn back from, and I won’t stop.
For an instant, I seemed to hear Baeksang’s voice again, as I had in the dark underground prison. I looked at the blank tablet and asked a question he would never hear.
If I’d been you, what road would I have taken?
No answer came. Not from the tablet, and not from anywhere deep inside me.
If there really is such a thing as an afterlife, I hope that bastard—someone I could tear to pieces without feeling satisfied—gets to live an ordinary life unlike this one.
I hope he can spend a peaceful life without losing anyone or sacrificing anyone, together with the child he missed so terribly.
Damn it. How many people died because of him?
I knew every villain had a story. That wasn’t what made this feel so rotten.
It was the thought that I might have walked the same road as Baeksang. I could imagine how desperately he’d struggled against the circumstances he’d been given.
In the end, this was all I could say.
“...Don’t commit any sins over there, you goddamn bastard.”
As I muttered the words, reddish light slipped through a gap in the shrine door and fell across the two tablets. As though that were their answer.
Then, the next moment, a deep voice pierced my ears.
“The sun’s already setting.”
Creeeak.
The old floorboards screamed. At last, the giant unfolded his crossed legs and rose from his seat, staring at me with calm eyes.
“If we head straight to the Inner Palace, we should still make it back in time for dinner.”
“Come. We should return before it gets any later.”
I looked at him, let out a quiet laugh, and nodded.
Nanman’s forest keeper had returned.
Two days passed.

When the Palace Lord, who had disappeared without a word, returned, the leadership—which had been thrown into confusion—quickly regained its stability. After taking a short rest at everyone’s urging, the Beast Miao King summoned me the following day.
Or rather, he summoned Jeok Cheongang and me.
Jeok Cheongang arrived at the meeting room hastily thrown together over seven days and nights. The moment he saw the Beast Miao King sitting there, he said,
“Look how you’ve grown, our little Miao King. Sitting in the seat of honor and everything.”
“...Oh. My apologies. Force of habit.”
“No, I understand. So you’ll understand this old man’s habit of using the Flame Divine Palm on anyone who forgets his manners.”
Whoosh!
The Beast Miao King had experienced that habit during the Great Faction War. Bandages and all, he swiftly vacated the seat of honor and gestured toward it.
“Please sit, Old Master Jeok.”
“Oh, it’s fine. You’re injured. No need to go that far.”
“Enough. Sit down. I don’t care for some wet-behind-the-ears brat summoning me, but I’ll let you say your piece.”
The Beast Miao King seemed confused by the gangster-like way of speaking he hadn’t heard in a long time, so I opened my mouth politely.
“Just tell him what you need to. That means he’s listening.”
“...Then, Old Master Jeok, may this junior speak?”
“He really hates being asked questions in return. You’re still not fully recovered, so if you don’t want to suffer something nasty, speak right away.”
“...Understood.”
Unlike the Jeok Cheongang in his memories, the one sitting before him looked much younger. The Beast Miao King glanced at him before carefully opening his mouth.
“I asked you to join us, Old Master Jeok, because I wished to consult you about a grave matter.”
“A grave matter?”
“Yes.”
“I hear the cleanup has been going well. Have you found a trail leading to Dark Heaven?”
“I wish we had, but no. In a way, this problem is even more troublesome...”
“Enough preamble. Get to the point before I shorten your life.”
This man really hasn’t changed.
The Beast Miao King looked at Jeok Cheongang with exactly that thought in his eyes, then took something from inside his robes and placed it on the table.
Thud.
It was something wrapped in thick cloth. But everyone in the room, myself included, could sense the ominous energy seeping out from within.
As the air suddenly grew heavy, Jeok Cheongang muttered as though groaning.
“...Demonic qi?”
The Beast Miao King nodded grimly.
“Yes. Extremely pure and powerful demonic qi. I couldn’t entrust it to anyone else in Nanman, so I’ve kept it with me.”
Their voices seemed to recede, as distant as echoes.
I thought I knew where that demonic qi had come from and what lay beneath the cloth. From the deep darkness, the guardian spirit’s final roar rang in my ears once more.
“It’s the sacred stone. The one the guardian spirit carried.”
“As you guessed. Though it is no longer a sacred stone.”
Rustle.
The Beast Miao King answered in a troubled voice and peeled back the cloth. Instead of warm, dazzling radiance, a stone filled with murky darkness was revealed.
It had absorbed all the demonic qi flowing from the rift. Now, it was something that ought to be called a demonic stone, and the Beast Miao King’s gaze sank deeply as he looked at it.
“I’m suppressing its demonic qi for now, but we can’t leave it like this forever. That’s why I asked you and Old Master Jeok here—to decide what to do with it.”
At that moment—
Ding.
A clear chime rang out, utterly at odds with the murky darkness before me, and a holographic window appeared in midair.
System Quest: Corrupted Divine Artifact Will you accept? Y / N

Baeksang.
Baekhwi.
I said their names silently—the names even the person who had made the tablets by hand couldn’t bring himself to carve.
Then I lowered myself and bowed.
Once.
Then again.
When I turned after the second bow, the Beast Miao King was staring at me, his face stiff.
“Why are you looking at me like that?”
“...I didn’t expect it.”
“What, did you think I’d knock the tablets over?”
“You might have.
Especially Baeksang’s, after what he did.”
Damn it.
Fair enough.
After everything that had happened, I could have split Baeksang’s tablet in half and spat on it and called it self-defense.
But...
“I just wanted to do this.
That’s all.”
What was this filthy, bitter feeling?
I looked back at the tablets and thought I might finally have a name for it.
Perhaps it was sympathy.
Perhaps empathy.
It’s too late.
I’ve gone down a road I can’t turn back from, and I won’t stop.
For an instant, I seemed to hear Baeksang’s voice again, as I had in the dark underground prison.
I looked at the blank tablet and asked a question he would never hear.
If I’d been you, what road would I have taken?
No answer came.
Not from the tablet, and not from anywhere deep inside me.
If there really is such a thing as an afterlife, I hope that bastard—someone I could tear to pieces without feeling satisfied—gets to live an ordinary life unlike this one.
I hope he can spend a peaceful life without losing anyone or sacrificing anyone, together with the child he missed so terribly.
Damn it.
How many people died because of him?
I knew every villain had a story.
That wasn’t what made this feel so rotten.
It was the thought that I might have walked the same road as Baeksang.
I could imagine how desperately he’d struggled against the circumstances he’d been given.
In the end, this was all I could say.
“...Don’t commit any sins over there, you goddamn bastard.”
As I muttered the words, reddish light slipped through a gap in the shrine door and fell across the two tablets.
As though that were their answer.
Then, the next moment, a deep voice pierced my ears.
“The sun’s already setting.”
Creeeak.
The old floorboards screamed.
At last, the giant unfolded his crossed legs and rose from his seat, staring at me with calm eyes.
“If we head straight to the Inner Palace, we should still make it back in time for dinner.”
“Come.
We should return before it gets any later.”
I looked at him, let out a quiet laugh, and nodded.
Nanman’s forest keeper had returned.
Two days passed.
When the Palace Lord, who had disappeared without a word, returned, the leadership—which had been thrown into confusion—quickly regained its stability.
After taking a short rest at everyone’s urging, the Beast Miao King summoned me the following day.
Or rather, he summoned Jeok Cheongang and me.
Jeok Cheongang arrived at the meeting room hastily thrown together over seven days and nights.
The moment he saw the Beast Miao King sitting there, he said,
“Look how you’ve grown, our little Miao King.
Sitting in the seat of honor and everything.”
My apologies.
Force of habit.”
“No, I understand.
So you’ll understand this old man’s habit of using the Flame Divine Palm on anyone who forgets his manners.”
Whoosh!
The Beast Miao King had experienced that habit during the Great Faction War.
Bandages and all, he swiftly vacated the seat of honor and gestured toward it.
“Please sit, Old Master Jeok.”
“Oh, it’s fine.
You’re injured.
No need to go that far.”
“Enough.
Sit down.
I don’t care for some wet-behind-the-ears brat summoning me, but I’ll let you say your piece.”
The Beast Miao King seemed confused by the gangster-like way of speaking he hadn’t heard in a long time, so I opened my mouth politely.
“Just tell him what you need to.
That means he’s listening.”
“...Then, Old Master Jeok, may this junior speak?”
“He really hates being asked questions in return.
You’re still not fully recovered, so if you don’t want to suffer something nasty, speak right away.”
“...Understood.”
Unlike the Jeok Cheongang in his memories, the one sitting before him looked much younger.
The Beast Miao King glanced at him before carefully opening his mouth.
“I asked you to join us, Old Master Jeok, because I wished to consult you about a grave matter.”
“A grave matter?”
“Yes.”
“I hear the cleanup has been going well.
Have you found a trail leading to Dark Heaven?”
“I wish we had, but no.
In a way, this problem is even more troublesome...”
“Enough preamble.
Get to the point before I shorten your life.”
This man really hasn’t changed.
The Beast Miao King looked at Jeok Cheongang with exactly that thought in his eyes, then took something from inside his robes and placed it on the table.
Thud.
It was something wrapped in thick cloth.
But everyone in the room, myself included, could sense the ominous energy seeping out from within.
As the air suddenly grew heavy, Jeok Cheongang muttered as though groaning.
“...Demonic qi?”
The Beast Miao King nodded grimly.
“Yes.
Extremely pure and powerful demonic qi.
I couldn’t entrust it to anyone else in Nanman, so I’ve kept it with me.”
Their voices seemed to recede, as distant as echoes.
I thought I knew where that demonic qi had come from and what lay beneath the cloth.
From the deep darkness, the guardian spirit’s final roar rang in my ears once more.
“It’s the sacred stone.
The one the guardian spirit carried.”
“As you guessed.
Though it is no longer a sacred stone.”
Rustle.
The Beast Miao King answered in a troubled voice and peeled back the cloth.
Instead of warm, dazzling radiance, a stone filled with murky darkness was revealed.
It had absorbed all the demonic qi flowing from the rift.
Now, it was something that ought to be called a demonic stone, and the Beast Miao King’s gaze sank deeply as he looked at it.
“I’m suppressing its demonic qi for now, but we can’t leave it like this forever.
That’s why I asked you and Old Master Jeok here—to decide what to do with it.”
At that moment—
Ding.
A clear chime rang out, utterly at odds with the murky darkness before me, and a holographic window appeared in midair.
System Quest: Corrupted Divine Artifact Will you accept?
Y / N

chapters.title: Chapter 719
paragraphs: System Quest: Corrupted Divine Artifact Will you accept? Y / N
That wasn’t the only holographic window to appear before me. I quickly scanned the information for the new Quest.

System Quest Corrupted Divine Artifact The sacred stone that once protected this land has lost its original form. Consumed by demonic qi, it is a spark that could ignite another calamity. You must dispose of this Corrupted Divine Artifact by any means. Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Dispose of Corrupted Divine Artifact (Incomplete) Reward: Varies according to how the mission is carried out Failure: Increase in the Corrupted Divine Artifact’s demonic qi
After reading the Quest information window to the end, I muttered quietly to myself.
Accept.
System You have accepted the Quest Corrupted Divine Artifact!
Unlike some of the Quests I’d been more or less forced into, this one gave me a choice. But as far as I was concerned, refusing wasn’t an option.
I can’t keep suppressing the demonic qi forever.

The sacred stone—no, the Corrupted Divine Artifact—was a bomb that could go off at any moment. We were lucky the Beast Miao King had been keeping it. An ordinary Peak master couldn’t have withstood the demonic qi inside it.
Like the Quest says, we have to deal with it somehow.
How many people had we lost closing the rift? For the sake of the guardian spirit that had thrown itself into it at the very end, I couldn’t let that bomb go off.
I wasn’t the only one who thought so.
“Demonic qi of this magnitude... This won’t do.”
Jeok Cheongang muttered with a frown, then gestured toward the Beast Miao King and me.
“Stand aside. This old man will handle it.”
As if he had guessed what Jeok Cheongang meant, the Beast Miao King’s eyes widened.
“Old Master Jeok, surely you don’t mean...”
“Exactly what you think. If it might cause trouble, we pull it out by the roots.”
“But this... won’t be easy to destroy.”
Jeok Cheongang’s answer was short.
“For you, maybe.”
“I can do it.”
That was some fucking macho-man talk.
One sentence had silenced even the Beast Miao King, the beastliest man in Nanman. Jeok Cheongang slowly reached out.
Whoosh.
Scorching Yang Qi gathered around his hand, giving off such terrible heat that the haze rising on every side made the air seem to warp.
But—
“Old Master.”
The words slipped out after a moment’s thought. Jeok Cheongang stopped just as he was about to strike.
“What?”
“I don’t think you should do that.”
“Why?”
“I gave it some thought, and I have a feeling things could get ugly if we mess with it carelessly.”
“What?”
His eyes widened at my serious tone.
“You mean you actually thought?”
Jeok Cheongang looked at my thoroughly deflated expression, cleared his throat, and opened his mouth.
“If we leave it like this, it will become a source of trouble sooner or later. We need to deal with it as quickly as possible.”
“I know.”
“Then why stop me? Don’t you trust this old man?”
“Oh, come on. Why would you say that? If I can’t trust you, Old Master, who can I trust?”
That was my answer. In truth, about half of me did have doubts.
Not because I distrusted Jeok Cheongang. I was worried about what might happen.
What if he doesn’t destroy it completely?
The Corrupted Divine Artifact was like the teacup in front of me. While the cup stayed intact, the tea stayed inside. Break the cup, and it would spill everywhere.
If we lose control of the demonic qi, we’ll have another goddamn disaster on our hands.
One mad tiger, however wildly it rampaged, could be beaten down. Demonic qi spreading through the area was another matter. If that happened, we’d be lucky if it was merely troublesome.
I had to stop Jeok Cheongang. No matter how much I trusted him, I couldn’t stake other people’s lives on this gamble.
Even if the chance is one in a thousand—or one in ten thousand—not now.
Too much blood had been spilled already.

People had died fighting to the bitter end. Others had lost their minds, become monsters, and died that way. Even people who had never held a sword had died in considerable numbers trying to escape that hellscape.
If the guardian spirit hadn’t sacrificed itself to close the rift, the casualties would have multiplied like a snowball by now...
Wait.
The guardian spirit?
A sudden sense of déjà vu came over me. Those words kept circling in my mind.
The memories from the day I first met it until now brushed past my eyes and ears one after another, racing toward a single thread of enlightenment.
And then—
“Ah.”
The sound escaped before I knew it.
Jeok Cheongang and the Beast Miao King stared at me as if wondering what the hell was wrong with me. Jeok Cheongang spoke first.
“Yeah, why the fuck are you suddenly throwing a fit all by yourself again? Let this old man in on it.”
“Have you perhaps thought of some brilliant strategy?”
Maybe. I didn’t know whether it deserved to be called a plan. Not yet. But if I was right, it was worth trying.
At least we won’t lose anything by trying.
I looked from the still-open Quest window to the two men waiting for an answer, then shrugged.
“Why don’t you both come get some air with me?”
Thud-thud-thud-thud!
Our little group raced through the wind. With only three tigers and three people, group might have been too grand a word.
Then again, it depended on who those people were. The two riding on either side of me made all the difference.
“I wondered how fast a beast could be, but this isn’t bad. Comfortable saddle, too.”
Jeok Cheongang inspected the tiger running beneath him with interest. The Beast Miao King, riding to my left, answered at once.
“He’s one of the bravest and fastest tigers in the Nanman Beast Palace. He’s descended from the one that fought alongside me in the Great Faction War.”
“Oh-ho. That huge one crouching in front of the barracks? I remember him. I thought he looked familiar.”
Yeah. Who needed an Azure Dragon on the left and a White Tiger on the right?

I had the Fire King on my left and the Miao King on my right. My chest swelled at the thought of that insane lineup. If the Southern Heaven Demon Empress came back to life, these two could take her apart.
The feeling of security was more comforting than a bowl of gukbap could have been. The quiet conversation between the two men reached my ears.
“The more I look at him, the more I like him. Good stamina, quick feet. Looks clever, too.”
The Beast Miao King smiled with pride.
“I raised him with particular care. He was such a picky eater as a cub that I had quite a time of it. Whenever that happened, I even fed him milk myself.”
“What? You fed him?”
“...It’s a figure of speech. Not what you’re thinking, Old Master Jeok.”
Jeok Cheongang studied the Beast Miao King’s massive pecs before nodding.
“If you say so.”
“No, when you say it like that, it sounds as though—”
“Never mind. I’ll take this one with me.”
The smile vanished from the Beast Miao King’s face.
“Pardon?”
“Why are you asking again? Were you planning to make him run his legs off all the way back to the Central Plains?”
“O-of course not. But I raised the one you’re riding like a son in my old age...”
“Give him to me.”
“But—”
“Go on.”
“If you don’t want to, I’ll take that one instead. He looks like a spiritual creature.”
The Beast Miao King looked at the tiger Jeok Cheongang had pointed out and shook his head in alarm.
“Gasp. Anyone but him. I only borrowed him for a while in the first place.”
“What if this old man were to take him?”
“I-I didn’t raise him myself. And how could I, as a father, give away someone my son thinks of as a brother?”
“The sky’s clear today. Your tongue’s awfully long.”
After a moment’s silence, the Beast Miao King answered glumly.
“...Understood. You may have the one you’re riding.”
“Well, if you insist. I’ll accept your generosity.”
So much for my chest swelling with pride.
Was this really the senile Fire King I knew? The Fire King truly was a legend...
As I tried to steady my suddenly shrunken chest, the creature carrying me let out a low growl.
Grrr.
He glanced back at me. He seemed to know he’d narrowly escaped the clutches of the Fire King, that dog trader. I felt sorry for him and gently stroked his trembling white fur.
“It’s okay, buddy. You survived.”
Whine.

Muyaho let out a forlorn little cry, like a puppy that had lost its mother, and slowed down. He must have realized that showing off in front of Jeok Cheongang would only make it more likely he’d be dragged all the way to the Central Plains.
Fortunately, Jeok Cheongang’s attention had already shifted.
“What’s that...?”
His voice trailed off. Ahead of us stood a bare mountain, almost completely burned.
No, even that sorry-looking mountain had a name: Ailao Mountain. Everyone who lived in this land knew it.
Just as I was about to explain that to him, Jeok Cheongang’s eyes flew open and he shouted,
“What shameless son of a bitch burned down these precious mountains, trees, and grass?”
For an instant, the Beast Miao King and I exchanged a heated glance. Then I answered with all the outrage I could muster.
“Dark Heaven.”
Some truths are beautiful when left unknown.
Once Jeok Cheongang realized the sorry-looking mountain was our destination, he frowned.
“Did we come all this way to plant trees?”
“...I’m asking because I genuinely want to know. Just how crazy do you think I am?”
What a ridiculous question.

Today wasn’t Arbor Day, and even if it had been, I wouldn’t have planted any trees. I had come with these two to Ailao Mountain, which had been reduced to a bare mountain, for a purpose that had been decided from the beginning.
“This way.”
The Beast Miao King soon realized where I was going.
“The Poisonblood Grounds. Or should I call it the Sacred Land now?”
It would have been stranger if he hadn’t known. Yohi must have told him roughly what had happened, even if she’d left out the details.
I shook my head.
“They’re different. The Poisonblood Grounds are the Poisonblood Grounds. The Sacred Land is the Sacred Land.”
The two places were separate. The Poisonblood Grounds were a land of death made by human hands. The Sacred Land was Nanman’s heart—a land of life.
Life itself.
I set the Corrupted Divine Artifact on the ground. Demonic qi drifted from it like mist, and Muyaho growled softly.
But though darkness had consumed it, its essence had not changed.
Whoosh...
The ground pulsed like a beating heart. A veil lifted from another world that had been hidden for countless ages.
Then I saw it: a space filled with warm radiance, and at its center, a small pond shining more brilliantly than anything else.
“Ah.”
“That’s...”
Jeok Cheongang’s and the Beast Miao King’s exclamations faded without either man finishing his thought.
But I knew what they had felt. And I knew what I had to do.
Purification.
Today, a new sacred stone would be born.
