chapters.title: Chapter 720
paragraphs: Whew.
A cool breeze brushed past me. I took a small, deep breath and looked around.
The Sacred Land.
Could there be another place where those two words fit so perfectly?
But where I stood was only its body.
Even this Sacred Land has a heart of its own.
A place filled with the energy of life and Purification. The place that had brought my dying body back to life.
I walked slowly toward the distant pond.
There was no sun, yet the light falling from above was warm. Flowers and grass bloomed lushly in every direction.

Jeok Cheongang and the Beast Miao King stared at the bizarre space with stunned expressions. Their lips moved as though they were about to say something, but before long, they firmly shut their mouths and followed behind me.
Their patience didn’t last long.
Splash.
I waded straight into the pond. Cold water soon rose to my waist, and Jeok Cheongang cried out in alarm.
“Th-that bastard...!”
Apparently he thought I meant to kill myself.
He looked ready to grab me by the collar and drag me out. Instead of explaining, I bit my pinky.
Crunch.
A faint sting. The skin split, and blood flowed.
But after giving the wide-eyed Jeok Cheongang a crooked grin, I plunged my hand into the clear water without hesitation.
One. Two. Three...
I counted slowly in my head before pulling it out. In barely thirty seconds, my pinky had healed completely.
Jeok Cheongang, who had looked ready to jump in after me, and the Beast Miao King, who had been trying to stop him, muttered in disbelief.
“What in the world...”
“...Everything Yohi said was true. All of it.”
There was a reason people came up with the saying that seeing once was better than hearing a hundred times. I could talk until my mouth went dry, but showing them was faster.
It was a kind of performance.
It worked. And I’d confirmed something for myself, too.
The pond still works.
I’d been a little worried. Like a Golem collapsing when its core was destroyed, the Sacred Land might have vanished once demonic qi consumed the sacred stone.
But that concern vanished as cleanly as the wound on my pinky, replaced by a suspicion bordering on certainty.
This is it. The answer.
The System had never lied to me. It presented the facts as they were; finding a new path in its maddeningly plain text was up to me.
Just like now.
The Quest information said “by any means.” I’m sure of it.
That was right. From the beginning, the mission I had been given was to dispose of the Corrupted Divine Artifact, not to destroy it.
I’d caught on rather late, but my memories of the guardian spirit had led me back to this place. To the pond that had healed me when I was near death and cleansed the impurities from my body.
Healing and Purification.
I didn’t know where its mysterious power came from. I only knew I had no better option.
I walked toward the center of the pond.
Swish.
Gentle ripples spread outward from me. The pond wasn’t very deep, and on its surface—clear enough to see through—I could see the face of a man stiff with tension wavering in the water.
Gulp.
I swallowed and looked at my clenched fist. I felt the hard surface of the Corrupted Divine Artifact—and the powerful demonic qi pulsing up between my fingers.
...If this backfires, we’re in for a real shitshow.
I wasn’t joking. That much demonic qi could ruin not just the pond, but the entire Sacred Land.

Then this place would become the real, true Poisonblood Grounds, and the guardian spirit—who had only just finished filing his move-in registration in the afterlife—would show up in my dreams every night and hiss at me.
But still...
What else am I supposed to do? There’s no other option.
Fuck it. I don’t know.
I squeezed my eyes shut and plunged the Corrupted Sacred Stone into the water.
Splash! Fwoooosh!
The calm surface broke. Spray shot up and soaked me from head to toe.
And then...everything went quiet.
What the hell? Why was it so quiet?
I hesitated through a moment that felt like an eternity, then opened my eyes.
A little. Just a little.
And at the moment I cautiously peered through narrowed eyes—
Blub blub.
Bubbles rose to the surface.
Whoooooosh.
From the center of the pond, water mixed with murky darkness began to whirl into a vortex.
Which meant...
Fuck. I’m standing right on it.
The realization had barely struck when an enormous pillar of water surged up beneath my feet.
Kwaaaaaaah!
I had no time to react. Water and darkness filled everything around me.
Caught in the chaos that had rushed upon me without warning, I thrashed about with all my strength. No, I tried to. I would have, if I hadn’t realized the truth a moment later.
I could see it. Feel it.
Water and darkness spun fiercely around me. But so did fresh air and wind—things I couldn’t have felt underwater.
Air? Wind?
I blinked and looked around.
I wasn’t floating beneath the surface. The water that had risen to my chest was gone. Solid ground lay beneath my feet, while water and darkness swirled endlessly on every side.
It...wrapped around me?

There was no doubt. Instead of sweeping across my entire body, the enormous pillar of water had enclosed me. Beyond the darkness and waves blocking me in on every side, impossible and unbelievable scenes flashed past my eyes.
Fwoooosh!
This is...
I understood at once. What I was seeing wasn’t a hallucination caused by extreme confusion or anything of the sort. It was simply the history of some place contained within this pond.
Or perhaps the memories of the divine artifact that had shared this land’s fate since its birth.
“...The sacred stone.”
I muttered the words like a groan and gazed with stunned eyes at the column of water walling me in on every side.
Time flowed through its ceaseless waves.
A sprout pushed up from barren ground and grew into a towering tree. Grass and flowers spread, and animals appeared one by one.
So fast.

The scenes reflected in the water changed in less than an instant. Day and night traded places dozens of times in the blink of an eye. On one day, thunder and lightning filled the world. On another, a mountain collapsed and erased a river.
Hundreds of years. Perhaps thousands.
Through it all, the sacred stone remained where it was. And others stayed beside it.
Horses. Monkeys. Leopards. Bears...
They differed in species and appearance, but I could hardly call them mere beasts.
Countless among them shone like stars in the night sky before fading away, and eventually, a snow-white White Tiger began guarding the sacred stone.
The guardian spirit.
Then darkness came. A darkness dreadful enough to make me shudder. Sticky, wicked qi surged through the waves.
After all those years, the memories had reached that day.
But the final guardian spirit charged forward, its white mane streaming behind it. With a roar, it bit and clawed at the darkness.
Until demonic qi seeped into the wounds across its body. Until the moment its blue-white eyes turned black.
And then every memory contained within the sacred stone ended as well.
No. Perhaps this was a new beginning.
Swish.
The water rippled again. The darkness vanished, and a face appeared in the pillar surrounding me.
The figure of a young man with his eyes squeezed shut as he immersed something in his hand deep into the pond was unmistakably familiar.
The sacred stone’s newest memory began with me.
And that could mean only one thing.
Ding.
A clear chime rang in my ears. The darkness writhing in the pillar of water faded without a trace.
As I stared blankly at the sight, a translucent holographic window appeared before me.

System The Pond of Life purifies all evil and impure energy. - The demonic qi that had seeped into the Corrupted Divine Artifact has completely disappeared! Mission: Dispose of the Corrupted Divine Artifact (Complete) - You have successfully completed the Quest, Corrupted Divine Artifact! - You have obtained a vast amount of EXP and Fame as a Quest completion Reward! - Level Up! - Level Up! - You have accomplished an unbelievable achievement! ... ... ...
Ding. Ding. Ding.
System notifications rang without pause, and holographic windows filled the air. But all of it felt distant. Through the slowly dispersing pillar of water, a single object shone.
Swish.
As if entranced, I reached out. The water parted before my hand.
It was smaller and lighter than a child’s fist, yet impossibly warm. The moment my fingertips touched it—
Fwoooooosh!
Dazzling light swelled. At the same time, the column of water walling me in on every side shot into the sky and burst apart like an explosion.
Fwoooooosh!
The power of life spread endlessly beyond the hidden Sacred Land, toward some faraway place.
With the new sacred stone in my hand, I tipped my head back and looked up. Another clear chime rang out among the falling droplets.
Ding.

System The energy held within the Pond of Life becomes rain and seeps into every part of this land. - The earth will grow more fertile, the plants will stay green, and the wounded will be healed. - The Pond of Life has lost all its energy and dried up. But do not worry. Time has the power to change many things. - The sacred stone will remain in this land, as it always has. Together with a new guardian spirit.
A new guardian spirit?
Before I could grasp what that meant, I heard footsteps.
Thud.
A large forepaw came down on the dry ground where the pond had been.
Snow-white fur fluttered in a breeze that had come from somewhere, and the blue-white eyes, now clearer and more distinct, looked exactly like those of someone from my memories.
“...So it’s you.”
Grrrr.
Muyaho—no, the new guardian spirit—approached and rubbed its head against me.
Without saying a word, I stroked the back of its neck. Jeok Cheongang, who had watched the entire scene with a dazed expression, barely managed to part his lips.
“...Can’t this old man take him with me?”
The Beast Miao King’s face went stern.
“Would that be possible?”
Neither of them noticed the green leaf that had just poked up beneath the rain falling around them.
Nor did they know that the rain would soak all of Nanman for three days.

chapters.title: Chapter 721
paragraphs: Even now, nearly ten days after that day, restoration work was still underway at the Nanman Beast Palace.
The Inner Palace, its very heart, had been completely devastated. The Outer Palace had also suffered considerable damage in the aftermath of the battle.

Fortunately, by mobilizing all the warriors and beasts, they had managed to clear away most of the rubble in a short time. But considering all the houses and pavilions that still had to be built for the tribespeople who had suddenly lost their homes, the road ahead seemed endless.
“Right, we lift together on three. One, two.”
“Hngh!”
Grrrrind!
They combined their strength to lift a huge boulder, then hoisted thick timber onto bruised shoulders.
Despite the unending hard labor, no one complained. This was work for everyone’s sake.

The Nanman Beast Palace was a symbol to all who lived in this land, a home of the heart passed down from their ancestors. It no longer mattered which tribe the people beside them belonged to, what they wore or ate, or which local god they worshiped.
Everyone here had come for one purpose: to rebuild the Nanman Beast Palace.
That was why one middle-aged man had walked three hundred li to get here, too.
Whack!
The ax blade bounced off the thick timber, sending a sharp pain through his palm. He groaned before he could stop himself, and a young man came over.
“That’s not how you swing it. Let me see your hand.”
The middle-aged man held it out without thinking. He had inherited his family’s business and spent his life as a merchant. Now his palms were covered in blisters and blood.
“Ouch. That must hurt. You haven’t done much of this before, have you?”
“N-no, I haven’t.”
“You can’t do it with strength alone. Put your weight behind the ax and follow the grain. One clean whack. Want me to show you?”
The middle-aged man stared blankly at the young man speaking to him so affably.
Something about him felt unfamiliar. Not simply because they had never met. It was his appearance, and the halting way he spoke, almost like a child.
Then a thought struck him.
“Could you be...?”
“Han Chinese? Yes.”
“Ah, then you’re the one I’ve only heard about through rumors...”
“That’s right. I’m the one.”
“Oh! Ohhh!”
The young man gave him a warm smile.
“My name is Hyuk Mujin.”
“The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Tae... Wait. Mujin who?”

“Hyuk Mujin. The famous Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung’s right-hand man! The pillar of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan! The proud Vice Pavilion Master of the Murim Alliance’s Fire Dragon Pavilion!”
What the hell was wrong with this guy?
Hyuk...what?
Did Han Chinese people have names like that?
The middle-aged man stared at Hyuk Mujin with an uncertain expression, but just as he was about to pick up his ax again—
Tap. Tap-tap.
Raindrops suddenly began to fall.
At the same time, sighs escaped from the people working nearby. There was a mountain of work left to do, and rain would naturally slow them down.
“Damn it. Now it’s raining out of a clear sky.”
“What can we do? We’ll just have to think of it as a passing shower.”
“Come on! Let’s keep at it a little longer!”
The middle-aged man glanced up. There wasn’t a cloud in sight. Even for Nanman’s unpredictable climate, this was unusual.
Still, a little shower won’t hurt.
Perhaps it was because he was already soaked in sweat, but the sudden rain didn’t feel entirely unpleasant. The drops struck his palms and seemed to wash his wounds clean.
That feels good.
He closed his eyes without realizing it.
A hand clamped around his wrist.
Startled, he opened his eyes.
“What...is this?”
Hyuk Mujin’s face had gone rigid. He was staring at the middle-aged man’s palm.
Slowly.
The wounds were disappearing. No—healing.
The blisters that had filled both palms, the skin crushed and torn by swinging the ax...
The rain washed away the abundant blood, revealing new muscle and flesh beneath—paler and firmer than before.
They looked up at the sky at the same instant, eyes wide.
Boom. Boom. Booooom!
Through the sunlit rain came the sound of drums, announcing someone’s return.
A miracle.
Those two words explained everything. There was no other way to describe it.
Tap. Ssshhhh.
Rain had begun to fall. Warm rain that soaked buildings and earth, coaxed flowers and sprouts into bloom, and fell on the heads of every living thing.
It washed away their wounds and fatigue.
“My wound! It’s healed!”
“My body feels so light!”
“W-what in the world...?”
Grrr?
The people stood dazed until a lion’s roar rang out from somewhere.
“By order of the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, everyone outside!”
The shout, charged with powerful internal energy, reached every corner of the Outer Palace. Drawn by the command, people came out to find a massive White Tiger and three men standing before them.
Jeok Cheongang. The Beast Miao King. And Jin Taekyung.
“I’ve called them all out, just as you asked,” Jeok Cheongang whispered. “Now what?”
“Wouldn’t it be enough to tell them to come outside and get rained on? They’ll understand once they experience it themselves.”
At the Beast Miao King and Jeok Cheongang’s whispers, Jin Taekyung shook his head without hesitation.
Unlike those two martial artists to the bone, he had been born and raised in the modern world. He knew what marketing could do.
“We can’t just let them get wet and call it a day. We have to dress this up and sell it first.”
“Dress it up? Sell it?”
“What in the world are you talking about?”
“It’s complicated. Think of it as a bit of political maneuvering.”
Martial artists could reach the end of their lives without learning a thing about politics. Anyone born in twenty-first-century Korea knew better.
It was a ruthless world. Being bad at a game was enough to make people wish you dead.
Jin Taekyung, who had been called an orphan dozens of times in games he had logged into just for fun, knew the importance of politics better than anyone.
Make the guy who did well look like he failed, and the guy who failed look like he did well. And...
Make the guy who did well look even better. That was politics. Modern marketing.
He wasn’t about to waste this opportunity.
It’d be a shame if everyone just went, “Wow, a miracle!” and left it at that.
He muttered inwardly, then took a deep breath. He shouted toward the people, filling his voice with internal energy.
“Listen, everyone! This holy rain was bestowed by the Earth Mother Goddess!”
The Earth Mother Goddess?
People blinked at the unfamiliar name. Beside him, the Beast Miao King frowned.
“What’s that?”
“A god.”
“We don’t have a god like that here.”
“We do now.”
What the hell is wrong with this bastard?
While the Beast Miao King stood speechless, Jin Taekyung went on.
“The Earth Mother Goddess is the mother of this land, and she is the One God!”
The One God.
The crowd gaped.
Nanman was home to thirty-two tribes and more than a hundred local gods—far more gods than tribes. And Jin Taekyung was telling them there was only one?
Nanman might have suffered a disaster and the Nanman Beast Palace might have gone to shit, but the faith they had held all their lives remained.
“What nonsense!”
“I’ve never even heard of an Earth Mother Goddess!”
“I know you have worked hard for Nanman, but how dare you utter such blasphemy! The Wood God I worship is the One God!”
“Don’t bring the Wood God into this! The Fire God is the true god!”
“You little bastard!”
Yet Jin Taekyung looked pleased as he watched the believers grabbing one another by the collars and fighting.
Idiots.
Nanman’s religious landscape was as chaotic as the era of the Five Barbarians and Sixteen Kingdoms. That would make things easier. Unlike them, he had evidence to back his claim.
“You fools! Can you stand in this holy rain and still not feel the Earth Mother Goddess’s grace?”
His stern reprimand rang across the courtyard, and the noise vanished as if it had been washed away.
One tribesman, his fist drawn back for an uppercut, looked at the sky in confusion.
Ssshhhhhh.
Rain fell from a cloudless sky. It healed the sick and brought new shoots out of the earth. The sight gave him pause.
“B-but the Wood God...”
“So what did your Wood God do ten days ago? Even when I was setting fire to the mountain, it didn’t do much.”
“W-well...”
Jin Taekyung cut him off with another shout.
“Everyone gathered here must have seen it! The dazzling radiance of that day! The warmth!”
“The miracle then and the miracle today were both blessings from the Earth Mother Goddess, who took pity on you!”
Uncertainty flickered across the people’s faces.
They had seen and felt it all. And the rain falling on them now was another miracle.
“The Earth Mother Goddess...”
Even the name sounded warm and familiar. Saying it brought a mother’s embrace to mind.
And she was the One God, too. The one and only One God.
“Th-then what are the other gods we’ve worshiped until now?”
Jin Taekyung answered without a moment’s hesitation.
“You can’t compare the great Earth Mother Goddess to a bunch of lesser gods.”
“L-lesser gods...!”
“The Earth Mother Goddess bestowed this miracle and gave me a divine message: ‘Useless gods. The kind that aren’t worth knowing.’ She told me to protect you from them.”
“Oh! Ohhh!”
“A miracle, and a divine message too!”
Excitement swept through the crowd. They were all shouting together now.
Jin Taekyung seized the moment and threw both hands into the air.
“Shout together! Earth Mother Goddess!”
“Earth Mother Goddess! Earth Mother Goddess!”
“Louder!”
“Earth Mother Goddess! Earth Mother Goddess!”
“Repeat after me. Mother Goddess Heaven! Unbeliever Hell!”
“Mother Goddess Heaven! Unbeliever Hell!”
“Those in Nanman who believe in the Earth Mother Goddess will be saved even after death, while those who do not believe will fall into a pit of fire when they die!”
“Woooooah! O Mother Goddess!”
“Save us! Save this land!”
The tribespeople had become the Earth Mother Goddess’s sons and daughters before the Beast Miao King’s eyes. He stared at Jin Taekyung, stunned.
What the hell are you doing, you lunatic?
He wanted to stop him. He had to stop him.

He didn’t know what political maneuvering or dressing things up had to do with this, but the look in everyone’s eyes had already gone frighteningly wild. They screamed to the Earth Mother Goddess as though their throats might tear, their voices shaking heaven and earth.
“Mother Goddess Heaven! Unbeliever Hell!”
“Where’s that guy who said he believed in the Wood God?”
“There! That’s him! Throw him in the fire!”
“Gasp! No! I-I’ve already converted!”
“Prove it!”
“M-Mother Goddess Heaven! Unbeliever Hell!”
“He’s one of us! Stop tying him up! Now find the one who worshiped the Fire God!”
A wave of conversions overflowed in every direction.

The oppressive force radiating from thousands—tens of thousands—of people was so great that even Jeok Cheongang, who had privately wondered whether he should try believing in the Fire God, fell silent.
The Beast Miao King desperately wanted to put an end to this madness.
“E-enough now...”
He had barely managed to speak when Jin Taekyung’s voice rang out.
“Everyone, quiet! The Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace—the priest chosen by the Earth Mother Goddess—is about to speak!”
“Enough... What?”
“Please speak, Priest.”
“What kind of boss?”
Priest? Me?
Before the Beast Miao King could make sense of the word, countless eyes turned toward him.
A suffocating silence settled over the crowd. He was a well-liked Palace Lord, but he had never seen his people look at him with so much love and trust.
He stood frozen as a statue. Then his lips parted.
“Mother Goddess Heaven. Unbeliever Hell.”
“Waaaaaaaaah!”
And so, under the care of the great Earth Mother Goddess, Nanman achieved true unity at last.

sentences.text: Even now, nearly ten days after that day, restoration work was still underway at the Nanman Beast Palace.
The Inner Palace, its very heart, had been completely devastated.
The Outer Palace had also suffered considerable damage in the aftermath of the battle.
Fortunately, by mobilizing all the warriors and beasts, they had managed to clear away most of the rubble in a short time.
But considering all the houses and pavilions that still had to be built for the tribespeople who had suddenly lost their homes, the road ahead seemed endless.
“Right, we lift together on three.
One, two.”
“Hngh!”
Grrrrind!
They combined their strength to lift a huge boulder, then hoisted thick timber onto bruised shoulders.
Despite the unending hard labor, no one complained.
This was work for everyone’s sake.
The Nanman Beast Palace was a symbol to all who lived in this land, a home of the heart passed down from their ancestors.
It no longer mattered which tribe the people beside them belonged to, what they wore or ate, or which local god they worshiped.
Everyone here had come for one purpose: to rebuild the Nanman Beast Palace.
That was why one middle-aged man had walked three hundred li to get here, too.
Whack!
The ax blade bounced off the thick timber, sending a sharp pain through his palm.
He groaned before he could stop himself, and a young man came over.
“That’s not how you swing it.
Let me see your hand.”
The middle-aged man held it out without thinking.
He had inherited his family’s business and spent his life as a merchant.
Now his palms were covered in blisters and blood.
“Ouch.
That must hurt.
You haven’t done much of this before, have you?”
“N-no, I haven’t.”
“You can’t do it with strength alone.
Put your weight behind the ax and follow the grain.
One clean whack.
Want me to show you?”
The middle-aged man stared blankly at the young man speaking to him so affably.
Something about him felt unfamiliar.
Not simply because they had never met.
It was his appearance, and the halting way he spoke, almost like a child.
Then a thought struck him.
“Could you be...?”
“Han Chinese?
Yes.”
“Ah, then you’re the one I’ve only heard about through rumors...”
“That’s right.
I’m the one.”
“Oh!
Ohhh!”
The young man gave him a warm smile.
“My name is Hyuk Mujin.”
“The Blazing Flame Divine Dragon, Jin Tae...
Wait.
Mujin who?”
“Hyuk Mujin.
The famous Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung’s right-hand man!
The pillar of the great Jin Family of Taiyuan!
The proud Vice Pavilion Master of the Murim Alliance’s Fire Dragon Pavilion!”
What the hell was wrong with this guy?
Hyuk...what?
Did Han Chinese people have names like that?
The middle-aged man stared at Hyuk Mujin with an uncertain expression, but just as he was about to pick up his ax again—
Tap.
Tap-tap.
Raindrops suddenly began to fall.
At the same time, sighs escaped from the people working nearby.
There was a mountain of work left to do, and rain would naturally slow them down.
“Damn it.
Now it’s raining out of a clear sky.”
“What can we do?
We’ll just have to think of it as a passing shower.”
“Come on!
Let’s keep at it a little longer!”
The middle-aged man glanced up.
There wasn’t a cloud in sight.
Even for Nanman’s unpredictable climate, this was unusual.
Still, a little shower won’t hurt.
Perhaps it was because he was already soaked in sweat, but the sudden rain didn’t feel entirely unpleasant.
The drops struck his palms and seemed to wash his wounds clean.
That feels good.
He closed his eyes without realizing it.
A hand clamped around his wrist.
Startled, he opened his eyes.
“What...is this?”
Hyuk Mujin’s face had gone rigid.
He was staring at the middle-aged man’s palm.
Slowly.
The wounds were disappearing.
No—healing.
The blisters that had filled both palms, the skin crushed and torn by swinging the ax...
The rain washed away the abundant blood, revealing new muscle and flesh beneath—paler and firmer than before.
They looked up at the sky at the same instant, eyes wide.
Boom.
Boom.
Booooom!
Through the sunlit rain came the sound of drums, announcing someone’s return.
A miracle.
Those two words explained everything.
There was no other way to describe it.
Tap.
Ssshhhh.
Rain had begun to fall.
Warm rain that soaked buildings and earth, coaxed flowers and sprouts into bloom, and fell on the heads of every living thing.
It washed away their wounds and fatigue.
“My wound!
It’s healed!”
“My body feels so light!”
“W-what in the world...?”
Grrr?
The people stood dazed until a lion’s roar rang out from somewhere.
“By order of the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, everyone outside!”
The shout, charged with powerful internal energy, reached every corner of the Outer Palace.
Drawn by the command, people came out to find a massive White Tiger and three men standing before them.
Jeok Cheongang.
The Beast Miao King.
And Jin Taekyung.
“I’ve called them all out, just as you asked,” Jeok Cheongang whispered.
“Now what?”
“Wouldn’t it be enough to tell them to come outside and get rained on?
They’ll understand once they experience it themselves.”
At the Beast Miao King and Jeok Cheongang’s whispers, Jin Taekyung shook his head without hesitation.
Unlike those two martial artists to the bone, he had been born and raised in the modern world.
He knew what marketing could do.
“We can’t just let them get wet and call it a day.
We have to dress this up and sell it first.”
“Dress it up?
Sell it?”
“What in the world are you talking about?”
“It’s complicated.
Think of it as a bit of political maneuvering.”
Martial artists could reach the end of their lives without learning a thing about politics.
Anyone born in twenty-first-century Korea knew better.
It was a ruthless world.
Being bad at a game was enough to make people wish you dead.
Jin Taekyung, who had been called an orphan dozens of times in games he had logged into just for fun, knew the importance of politics better than anyone.
Make the guy who did well look like he failed, and the guy who failed look like he did well.
And...
Make the guy who did well look even better.
That was politics.
Modern marketing.
He wasn’t about to waste this opportunity.
It’d be a shame if everyone just went, “Wow, a miracle!” and left it at that.
He muttered inwardly, then took a deep breath.
He shouted toward the people, filling his voice with internal energy.
“Listen, everyone!
This holy rain was bestowed by the Earth Mother Goddess!”
The Earth Mother Goddess?
People blinked at the unfamiliar name.
Beside him, the Beast Miao King frowned.
“What’s that?”
“A god.”
“We don’t have a god like that here.”
“We do now.”
What the hell is wrong with this bastard?
While the Beast Miao King stood speechless, Jin Taekyung went on.
“The Earth Mother Goddess is the mother of this land, and she is the One God!”
The One God.
The crowd gaped.
Nanman was home to thirty-two tribes and more than a hundred local gods—far more gods than tribes.
And Jin Taekyung was telling them there was only one?
Nanman might have suffered a disaster and the Nanman Beast Palace might have gone to shit, but the faith they had held all their lives remained.
“What nonsense!”
“I’ve never even heard of an Earth Mother Goddess!”
“I know you have worked hard for Nanman, but how dare you utter such blasphemy!
The Wood God I worship is the One God!”
“Don’t bring the Wood God into this!
The Fire God is the true god!”
“You little bastard!”
Yet Jin Taekyung looked pleased as he watched the believers grabbing one another by the collars and fighting.
Idiots.
Nanman’s religious landscape was as chaotic as the era of the Five Barbarians and Sixteen Kingdoms.
That would make things easier.
Unlike them, he had evidence to back his claim.
“You fools!
Can you stand in this holy rain and still not feel the Earth Mother Goddess’s grace?”
His stern reprimand rang across the courtyard, and the noise vanished as if it had been washed away.
One tribesman, his fist drawn back for an uppercut, looked at the sky in confusion.
Ssshhhhhh.
Rain fell from a cloudless sky.
It healed the sick and brought new shoots out of the earth.
The sight gave him pause.
“B-but the Wood God...”
“So what did your Wood God do ten days ago?
Even when I was setting fire to the mountain, it didn’t do much.”
“W-well...”
Jin Taekyung cut him off with another shout.
“Everyone gathered here must have seen it!
The dazzling radiance of that day!
The warmth!”
“The miracle then and the miracle today were both blessings from the Earth Mother Goddess, who took pity on you!”
Uncertainty flickered across the people’s faces.
They had seen and felt it all.
And the rain falling on them now was another miracle.
“The Earth Mother Goddess...”
Even the name sounded warm and familiar.
Saying it brought a mother’s embrace to mind.
And she was the One God, too.
The one and only One God.
“Th-then what are the other gods we’ve worshiped until now?”
Jin Taekyung answered without a moment’s hesitation.
“You can’t compare the great Earth Mother Goddess to a bunch of lesser gods.”
“L-lesser gods...!”
“The Earth Mother Goddess bestowed this miracle and gave me a divine message: ‘Useless gods.
The kind that aren’t worth knowing.’ She told me to protect you from them.”
“Oh!
Ohhh!”
“A miracle, and a divine message too!”
Excitement swept through the crowd.
They were all shouting together now.
Jin Taekyung seized the moment and threw both hands into the air.
“Shout together!
Earth Mother Goddess!”
“Earth Mother Goddess!
Earth Mother Goddess!”
“Louder!”
“Earth Mother Goddess!
Earth Mother Goddess!”
“Repeat after me.
Mother Goddess Heaven!
Unbeliever Hell!”
“Mother Goddess Heaven!
Unbeliever Hell!”
“Those in Nanman who believe in the Earth Mother Goddess will be saved even after death, while those who do not believe will fall into a pit of fire when they die!”
“Woooooah!
O Mother Goddess!”
“Save us!
Save this land!”
The tribespeople had become the Earth Mother Goddess’s sons and daughters before the Beast Miao King’s eyes.
He stared at Jin Taekyung, stunned.
What the hell are you doing, you lunatic?
He wanted to stop him.
He had to stop him.
He didn’t know what political maneuvering or dressing things up had to do with this, but the look in everyone’s eyes had already gone frighteningly wild.
They screamed to the Earth Mother Goddess as though their throats might tear, their voices shaking heaven and earth.
“Mother Goddess Heaven!
Unbeliever Hell!”
“Where’s that guy who said he believed in the Wood God?”
“There!
That’s him!
Throw him in the fire!”
“Gasp!
No!
I-I’ve already converted!”
“Prove it!”
“M-Mother Goddess Heaven!
Unbeliever Hell!”
“He’s one of us!
Stop tying him up!
Now find the one who worshiped the Fire God!”
A wave of conversions overflowed in every direction.

The oppressive force radiating from thousands—tens of thousands—of people was so great that even Jeok Cheongang, who had privately wondered whether he should try believing in the Fire God, fell silent.
The Beast Miao King desperately wanted to put an end to this madness.
“E-enough now...”
He had barely managed to speak when Jin Taekyung’s voice rang out.
“Everyone, quiet!
The Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace—the priest chosen by the Earth Mother Goddess—is about to speak!”
“Enough...
What?”
“Please speak, Priest.”
“What kind of boss?”
Priest?
Me?
Before the Beast Miao King could make sense of the word, countless eyes turned toward him.
A suffocating silence settled over the crowd.
He was a well-liked Palace Lord, but he had never seen his people look at him with so much love and trust.
He stood frozen as a statue.
Then his lips parted.
“Mother Goddess Heaven.
Unbeliever Hell.”
“Waaaaaaaaah!”
And so, under the care of the great Earth Mother Goddess, Nanman achieved true unity at last.

chapters.title: Chapter 722
paragraphs: The Earth Mother Goddess.
Warmth seemed to radiate from the name alone, and this One God turned all of Nanman upside down the moment she appeared.
It was a spectacular debut that swept away Nanman’s religious scene—once every bit as fiercely competitive as Korea’s idol market.
And then came the wave of faith.
No, the tide of fanaticism.
“Earth Mother Goddess! Earth Mother Goddess!”
“Mother Goddess Heaven! Unbeliever Hell!”
Those who believed in the Earth Mother Goddess would be saved even after death, while those who denied her would die and be thrown into a pit of fire.
Within half a day, her new sons and daughters were marching through the streets, shouting slogans. Before long, they began proselytizing.
“Hey, you. Wait a moment.”
“Why, why do you ask?”
“Do you believe in any god?”
“Well, um... Ah, yes! I believe in the Earth Mother Goddess!”
“Mother Goddess Heaven.”
“Pardon?”
“You don’t know the slogan? You’re a heretic! Unbeliever Heeell!”
“Eek! I’ll convert! I’ll convert!”
Jeok Cheongang watched the spectacle and summed up his thoughts in one short sentence.
“What a fucking shitshow.”
Jeok Cheongang was an outsider, so his reaction ended there. But the Beast Miao King, who had somehow become the Earth Mother Goddess’s priest, was half out of his mind.
“This... This isn’t right. Our traditions... Our native faith...”
It didn’t take him long, though, to realize what was happening.
“Wait. This...”
The Beast Miao King fell deep into thought, then murmured, “Not bad. No, this is actually great.”
“You get it now? Nothing brings people together like religion.”
Nanman was rebuilding, and for now everyone was pulling together. Even so, there was no denying that the Nanman Beast Palace was divided.
“You’ve been wondering what to do with the tribal chieftains we threw into the underground prison, haven’t you?”
“...Yes. No matter what crimes they committed, each of them led a tribe.”
He hadn’t spared them out of some misplaced sympathy.
At its core, the Nanman Beast Palace was an alliance of thirty-two tribes, and more than twenty of their chieftains had taken part in the betrayal.
If he executed them all as traitors, some people were bound to resent it. People took their own side.
“For now, the people want them executed. But given time, problems will arise. They simply haven’t surfaced yet.”
Memories had a way of becoming kinder with time.
Once the chaos settled, people would probably begin to whisper.
Our chieftain was a decent man, though.
That’s right. Baeksang tricked him. He couldn’t help it.
Come to think of it, isn’t it strange that so many chieftains were involved?
I could picture it all too easily.
Those cautious conversations would begin in small groups, spread throughout the Nanman Beast Palace, and eventually cause another rift.
“On top of that, the tribes whose chieftains were traitors involved in this affair will be subjected to the other tribes’ silent contempt. That will lead to resentment between the tribes.”
“But we can’t just let them all go.”
“They were blinded by wealth and glory and betrayed Nanman once already. Would a second betrayal be so difficult?”
No wonder the Beast Miao King had agonized over what to do with them. He needed a way to punish the traitors without tearing Nanman apart.
At least, that had been the case until the One God known as the Earth Mother Goddess appeared and performed an unprecedented miracle.
“Now is the perfect time. We can expose their crimes under the law, execute them, and root every weed out of this land!”
The law? Executions?
I clicked my tongue at the sight of his clenched fist.
He still doesn’t get it.
“What?”
“The law is fine, but this is judgment. Divine judgment.”
“Divine... judgment?”

“The men in the underground prison are traitors who joined forces with the Fiend known as Dark Heaven to corrupt this land. And you, Great Hero Yayul, are the one and only priest. You received a divine revelation from the Earth Mother Goddess: kill every last one of those bastards and purify Nanman.”
The Beast Miao King stared at me, wide-eyed. So did Jeok Cheongang, who had been listening beside us.
I could read the thoughts in their eyes.
Wait, he’s spinning it like that?
Wow. Is this guy seriously insane?
What a pair of naïve old men.
Ten Kings be damned. Maybe spending their entire lives focused on martial arts had left them ignorant of how the world worked.
Even after leading the Nanman Beast Palace for so long, the Beast Miao King wasn’t much more politically savvy than Jeok Cheongang.
No wonder Baeksang’s faction ran rampant.
But who was I?
A proud citizen of Korea.
I had spent my whole life in a country with more churches than fried-chicken restaurants, where you could spot twenty-first-century martyrs carrying crosses near any subway station.
I decided to show the Beast Miao King, who still didn’t understand what it meant to be a priest, the power he held.
“Now, repeat after me.”
The Beast Miao King stared blankly at me, then echoed my words.
“Now, repeat after me.”
“No, not that. We’re starting now.”
“Ah. Right.”
“I am a priest.”
“I am a priest.”
“The Earth Mother Goddess is a god.”
“The Earth Mother Goddess is a god.”
“Good job. Now continue.”
“I am a priest. The Earth Mother Goddess is a god.”
“Excellent. Repeat it.”
“I am a priest. The Earth Mother Goddess is a god. I am a priest. The Earth Mother Goddess is a god. I am... invincible!”
That last part wasn’t quite what I’d taught him.
Regardless, the Beast Miao King trembled with excitement, awakened to his role as the Earth Mother Goddess’s priest. Then he took the first great step toward reforming Nanman.
“In the name of the benevolent Earth Mother Goddess, I convene the Tribal Grand Council!”
He really was a priest now.
The Tribal Grand Council began in the blink of an eye.

Partly because so few tribal chieftains were able to attend, but sending messengers probably hadn’t been necessary anyway. The chieftains were already waiting for the Beast Miao King in a hastily prepared meeting room.
“Palace Lord!”
“It’s just a rumor, isn’t it? Tell us it’s a rumor!”
“What is this about an Earth Mother Goddess all of a sudden?”
“Fuck, the tribespeople have gone completely insane. They’re like Demonic Cultists during the Great Faction War!”
“This is absurd! Are you telling us to abandon the Wood God we’ve worshiped all our lives?”

They rushed at the Beast Miao King, their faces a mixture of disbelief and shock. But as soon as they heard what kind of effect launching the Earth Mother Goddess as a new brand could have on the market, they made their declarations in solemn tones.
“As tribal chieftain, I must set an example. I shall convert.”
“The Tribal Grand Council supports you, Palace Lord.”
“Wow, a united Nanman!”
“The Wood God? When it comes to gods, the Earth Mother Goddess is the one.”
They were in charge for a reason. They caught on fast.
Of course, some people weren’t so quick and came to confront the Beast Miao King.
“Palace Lord! How can this make any sense?”
“What exactly is the Earth Mother Goddess? And where did this nonsense about Mother Goddess Heaven and Unbeliever Hell come from?”
“It’s poison! The Palace Lord has spread poison throughout Nanman!”
“Do you think we priests will stand by and watch? We would rather die than let this pass!”
Dozens of priests, every one of them very old.
They had spent their lives serving the local gods, but they confronted the Beast Miao King with voices that rang out loud and clear despite their age.
Until Jeok Cheongang opened his mouth.
“If you won’t let it pass, what are you going to do about it?”
“What did you say?”
“Well, listen to the way this young bastard talks to his elders.”
“Palace Lord! Punish that insolent man at once! Some nobody we’ve never even heard of, running his mouth like—”
“Fire King.”
“That’s my sobriquet. Fire King Jeok Cheongang.”
“I’ll let anyone a hundred or older off. The rest of you, heads to the floor.”
The fame of the Fire King Jeok Cheongang—or rather, his temper—was well known not only in the Central Plains but also throughout Nanman.
“Um, Palace Lord?”
“Ah, what a lovely downpour.”

When even the Beast Miao King, their final lifeline, looked off toward a distant mountain, the priests immediately got down with their heads to the floor and swore that from then on, they would keep their mouths shut about the Earth Mother Goddess no matter what.
“Honestly, we call ourselves priests, but we’ve never even seen the gods we serve. Isn’t that right?”
“Hahaha. True, true. But the Earth Mother Goddess has shown us a miracle herself. How extraordinary!”
“Um, Palace Lord. Might there be any positions left on the Earth Mother Goddess’s side? You would remain the priest, of course, but perhaps another role...”
“Ahem. Since you mention it, the gods we serve are all closely tied to this land, aren’t they? Perhaps we could join forces...”
“Exactly! The Earth Mother Goddess is the mother of this land. In a sense, she gave birth to all the gods!”
A fantastic collaboration: priests who didn’t want to lose their livelihoods and the Beast Miao King, who wanted to unite Nanman completely.
After a serious discussion, the Earth Mother Goddess emerged as a god with dozens of lesser gods under her. I had no desire for a religious war, so I lent a little help too.
“This is getting complicated. Why don’t we just make one?”
“Make what?”
“Well... I guess we could call it a Bible for now?”
“A Bible?”
“What’s that?”
“The history of this land. The word of God. Think of it along those lines.”
“Oh! Ohhh!”
“Truly, a talent sent by the gods!”
After that, I tossed out a few hints and watched from the sidelines.
They started racking their brains for lore like webnovel authors with a deadline breathing down their necks.
Then the traitors who had spent the past ten days locked in the underground prison were finally dragged before everyone.
“P-please spare me!”
“Baeksang tricked me! I never joined forces with Dark Heaven!”
But there was no forgiveness. No mercy.
Ssshhhhhh.
The benevolent Earth Mother Goddess’s blessing fell upon the land.
Beneath the rain—by then known as the Sacred Rain—the people cried out for judgment, and the executioner’s blade flashed.
Slash!
That was the end of it. The bodies of the traitors who had once led this land were thrown to the beasts.
The rain fell without end, washing away the blood they had spilled.
And only then did the people suddenly realize.
They had finally become one.
They had overcome a catastrophe together, witnessed and experienced an unbelievable miracle, and at last become one family within the warm embrace of the Earth Mother Goddess.
That was the true miracle.
A miracle that had finally united the people of thirty-two tribes.
And the forest keeper who had cut down every diseased tree and weed in the forest shouted before them all.
“From this moment on, we are the people of Nanman—wholly united as one!”
“Waaaaaah!”
Their voices rose together, echoing in every direction.
It sounded like the roar of warriors heralding the Great War soon to come.

Partly because so few tribal chieftains were able to attend, but sending messengers probably hadn’t been necessary anyway.
The chieftains were already waiting for the Beast Miao King in a hastily prepared meeting room.
“Palace Lord!”
“It’s just a rumor, isn’t it?
Tell us it’s a rumor!”
“What is this about an Earth Mother Goddess all of a sudden?”
“Fuck, the tribespeople have gone completely insane.
They’re like Demonic Cultists during the Great Faction War!”
“This is absurd!
Are you telling us to abandon the Wood God we’ve worshiped all our lives?”
They rushed at the Beast Miao King, their faces a mixture of disbelief and shock.
But as soon as they heard what kind of effect launching the Earth Mother Goddess as a new brand could have on the market, they made their declarations in solemn tones.
“As tribal chieftain, I must set an example.
I shall convert.”
“The Tribal Grand Council supports you, Palace Lord.”
“Wow, a united Nanman!”
“The Wood God?
When it comes to gods, the Earth Mother Goddess is the one.”
They were in charge for a reason.
They caught on fast.
Of course, some people weren’t so quick and came to confront the Beast Miao King.
“Palace Lord!
How can this make any sense?”
“What exactly is the Earth Mother Goddess?
And where did this nonsense about Mother Goddess Heaven and Unbeliever Hell come from?”
“It’s poison!
The Palace Lord has spread poison throughout Nanman!”
“Do you think we priests will stand by and watch?
We would rather die than let this pass!”
Dozens of priests, every one of them very old.
They had spent their lives serving the local gods, but they confronted the Beast Miao King with voices that rang out loud and clear despite their age.
Until Jeok Cheongang opened his mouth.
“If you won’t let it pass, what are you going to do about it?”
“What did you say?”
“Well, listen to the way this young bastard talks to his elders.”
“Palace Lord!
Punish that insolent man at once!
Some nobody we’ve never even heard of, running his mouth like—”
“Fire King.”
“That’s my sobriquet.
Fire King Jeok Cheongang.”
“I’ll let anyone a hundred or older off.
The rest of you, heads to the floor.”
The fame of the Fire King Jeok Cheongang—or rather, his temper—was well known not only in the Central Plains but also throughout Nanman.
“Um, Palace Lord?”
“Ah, what a lovely downpour.”

When even the Beast Miao King, their final lifeline, looked off toward a distant mountain, the priests immediately got down with their heads to the floor and swore that from then on, they would keep their mouths shut about the Earth Mother Goddess no matter what.
“Honestly, we call ourselves priests, but we’ve never even seen the gods we serve.
Isn’t that right?”
“Hahaha.
True, true.
But the Earth Mother Goddess has shown us a miracle herself.
How extraordinary!”
“Um, Palace Lord.
Might there be any positions left on the Earth Mother Goddess’s side?
You would remain the priest, of course, but perhaps another role...”
“Ahem.
Since you mention it, the gods we serve are all closely tied to this land, aren’t they?
Perhaps we could join forces...”
“Exactly!
The Earth Mother Goddess is the mother of this land.
In a sense, she gave birth to all the gods!”
A fantastic collaboration: priests who didn’t want to lose their livelihoods and the Beast Miao King, who wanted to unite Nanman completely.
After a serious discussion, the Earth Mother Goddess emerged as a god with dozens of lesser gods under her.
I had no desire for a religious war, so I lent a little help too.
“This is getting complicated.
Why don’t we just make one?”
“Make what?”
“Well...
I guess we could call it a Bible for now?”
“A Bible?”
“What’s that?”
“The history of this land.
The word of God.
Think of it along those lines.”
“Oh!
Ohhh!”
“Truly, a talent sent by the gods!”
After that, I tossed out a few hints and watched from the sidelines.
They started racking their brains for lore like webnovel authors with a deadline breathing down their necks.
Then the traitors who had spent the past ten days locked in the underground prison were finally dragged before everyone.
“P-please spare me!”
“Baeksang tricked me!
I never joined forces with Dark Heaven!”
But there was no forgiveness.
No mercy.
Ssshhhhhh.
The benevolent Earth Mother Goddess’s blessing fell upon the land.
Beneath the rain—by then known as the Sacred Rain—the people cried out for judgment, and the executioner’s blade flashed.
Slash!
That was the end of it.
The bodies of the traitors who had once led this land were thrown to the beasts.
The rain fell without end, washing away the blood they had spilled.
And only then did the people suddenly realize.
They had finally become one.
They had overcome a catastrophe together, witnessed and experienced an unbelievable miracle, and at last become one family within the warm embrace of the Earth Mother Goddess.
That was the true miracle.
A miracle that had finally united the people of thirty-two tribes.
And the forest keeper who had cut down every diseased tree and weed in the forest shouted before them all.
“From this moment on, we are the people of Nanman—wholly united as one!”
“Waaaaaah!”
Their voices rose together, echoing in every direction.
It sounded like the roar of warriors heralding the Great War soon to come.

chapters.title: Chapter 723
paragraphs: One day. Two days. Then three.
The rain that had come to be called the Sacred Rain still fell across Nanman. Beneath the benevolent grace of the Earth Mother Goddess, nothing could stop its newly united people.
Thud! Craaack!
With a single swing of an ax from an older man, a massive tree snapped, while a thin woman casually hoisted a mountain of firewood.
Watching from the window, I muttered, “Wow. They got one hell of a buff.”
“A b-buff?”
The question came from behind me. I already knew I had a visitor, so I turned to answer.
“Nothing. What brings you here? Shouldn’t you be swamped right now?”
“I was passing by. Besides, I’m not as busy as I was. Everything is being put right in the blink of an eye.”
“Really?”
For an uninvited guest, Yayul Mok was a welcome sight. I looked at the Young Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace and went on.
“That’s good news. Who do they have to thank?”
Yayul Mok shrugged.
“Father says it’s thanks to some Han Chinese man. He must be mistaken.”
“I don’t think he is.”
“He must be. A despicable Han Chinese man would never help us.”
“True. You can’t trust anyone from the Central Plains.”
“Now you’re speaking sense.”
A brief silence passed. Then, as if on cue, we both let out a quiet laugh.
“It’s all thanks to you, Jin Taekyung.”
“We all worked hard, but that’s true. I did contribute quite a lot.”
The smile on Yayul Mok’s face deepened at my shameless reply.
“Are all Han Chinese as lacking in humility as you?”
“No. Just me.”
“That’s a relief.”
“Why?”
“Because I think I could grow to like Han Chinese more than I do now.”
I looked at him with fresh eyes.
I never thought I’d hear him say that. I’d noticed the change little by little, but the hostility toward the Central Plains that once filled him was gone.
“Don’t like them too much. Go there and you’ll find plenty of madmen.”
“You take me for a child. I know people are much the same wherever you go. In Nanman and the Central Plains alike.”
“Really? You didn’t seem to know that when we first met.”
“...That was because you turned the fields into a sea of fire.”
Looking a little embarrassed by the memory, Yayul Mok came over to the window. He gazed out through its half-open shutters, then spoke.
“It still doesn’t feel real. That all this could happen in the place where I was born and raised.”
“The disaster? Or the miracle?”
“Both.” After a moment, he added, “But this, too, must be a god’s will.”
“...You believe in the Earth Mother Goddess too?”
“I don’t know about that. But I believe a god exists. I’ve seen things I can’t explain any other way.”
Anyone who encounters something beyond understanding is bound to think of a god. You might not know who’s up there in that impossibly distant sky, but you’d figure they must be someone impressive.
I’m no different.
I kept that last thought to myself and changed the subject.
“So, how’s the cleanup going?”
“If you mean the restoration, we’re already in the final stages. We should see the finished results within a few days at the latest.”
Considering that the Inner Palace had been reduced to a wasteland and more than several hundred houses and pavilions in the Outer Palace had collapsed, it was a truly astonishing pace.
But instead of being surprised, I gave a small nod.
Well, that buff is incredible.
The rain falling even now carried the powers of life and purification. It was an area-wide buff that kept people full of energy and enhanced their physical abilities.
It’ll wear off when the rain stops, of course. But a few days is plenty.

They say even a sheet of paper is easier to lift when two people do it together. Here, tens of thousands of Nanman people were working day and night to rebuild their homes, to make a new start in the place where they belonged.
And their efforts were bearing fruit at an incredible pace.
“What about the other matter?”
Yayul Mok understood what I meant.
“We abolished the Great Chieftain system to remove the hierarchy and divisions that remained between the tribes. The Miao people and all four of the other major tribes agreed.”
“Good. Oh, what about Yohi?”
He nodded.
“She was the first to propose abolishing it.”
The tribal chieftains who had joined hands with Baeksang had been executed in front of countless witnesses, but Yohi alone had received a full pardon.
She had repented of her wrongdoing, however late. More importantly, she had led the beasts in helping the tribespeople escape the Outer Palace. No one had raised any real objection to her pardon.
“She said that she couldn’t leave behind the same precedent as Baeksang, Heugung, and herself.”
“She’s right. The Great Chieftains had too much power.”
“Father and the other tribal chieftains agreed. From now on, the Nanman Beast Palace will answer to the Palace Lord alone. The Tribal Grand Council will remain in case of an emergency. And...”
As I listened to the rest of Yayul Mok’s explanation, I realized once again that the Nanman Beast Palace had been reborn.

The Beast Miao King was now both Palace Lord and priest, with authority far greater than before. The appearance of the Earth Mother Goddess had calmed the people, and they had come together regardless of tribe or faith.
For hundreds of years, since the founding of the Nanman Beast Palace, this land had been divided into thirty-two pieces. At last, it was united.
You really could call it a small kingdom now.
Its tribespeople numbered in the tens of thousands, and its warriors nearly ten thousand. With the beasts they commanded as well, calling it a kingdom was no exaggeration.
Even allowing for the fact that the Nanman warriors were inferior to the martial arts of the Central Plains, they still represented an immense military force.
I looked at Yayul Mok with fresh interest.
“...Why are you looking at me like that?”
“Now that I think about it, you do look kind of noble. Turns out you’re a prince, or something.”
“...A prince?”
He repeated the word doubtfully, then let out a quiet laugh.
“What’s so funny? It’s not that far off.”
“I was just thinking what an honor it is.”
“What?”
“To be called a prince by the Apostle of the great Earth Mother Goddess. What else would you call it?”
What was he talking about?
While I blinked at him, Yayul Mok took something from inside his robe and held it out.
“Take it.”
This is...
“We decided to call it the Mother Goddess Scripture. Father asked me to give it to you.”
I took the bundle of bamboo strips, still bewildered.
Ding.

System — You have acquired Mother Goddess Scripture. — Mother Goddess Scripture is a scripture containing records of the Earth Mother Goddess. — A god can exist only when someone believes in it. — The Earth Mother Goddess has become known as the One God of Nanman! — Countless believers who follow the Earth Mother Goddess are ecstatic! — According to the records in Mother Goddess Scripture, your name has become known anew! — You have achieved Religious Reformation, an achievement that makes one wonder whether anyone would actually go this far! — You have acquired the Title Apostle of the Earth Mother Goddess!
Holographic windows filled the air along with the System notifications.
I stared at them for a moment, then hurriedly unrolled the bamboo strips. After reading the tiny writing on them, I burst out laughing in disbelief.
“What is this?”
Seeing my reaction, Yayul Mok shrugged.

“It says exactly what it means. The Earth Mother Goddess has been with this land since ancient times as its mother goddess, and whenever Nanman fell into crisis, she personally sent her apostle to save the people...”
“And that’s me?”
“Of course. Three hundred years ago, it was my ancestor, the first Palace Lord. And two hundred years ago, it was the Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan at the time—the clan you belong to.”
They’d managed to fit it all together.
Sure, I’d given them a few hints. I just hadn’t expected to find my name written out in full.
No, not just my name. Our names.
Rustle.
I skimmed the rest and found plenty I recognized. Jeok Cheongang, of course. The Fire Dragon Pavilion members. Even Namho.
This was supposed to be something like a Bible. Could they really put us all in it?
“I know it was thrown together in a hurry, but this is ridiculous. Who the hell came up with this setting?”
“My father.”
“No wonder it’s so impressive. How did he manage to make the setting this detailed?”
I avoided Yayul Mok’s gaze and tucked the bamboo strips into my robe.
The Apostle of the Earth Mother Goddess.
I’d somehow become an apostle of a god, a role that certainly hadn’t been written in my fate. But I didn’t feel bad about it. In fact, right now it was a major gain.
It should ease some of the resentment Nanman’s people hold toward the Central Plains.
Yayul Mok suddenly spoke, interrupting my thoughts.
“So, are you ready?”
“Hm?”
“To leave Nanman.”
After a moment’s silence, I smacked my lips.
“You’re sharp.”
“It would be strange if I hadn’t noticed.”
“How did you find out?”
“Even if I ignored everyone else, that huge fellow has been frantically gathering food since yesterday. As if he’s preparing for a long journey.”
There was no need to ask who he meant by “that huge fellow.” Guessing the culprit, I sighed.
“Taishan, you crazy bastard. I told you to move quietly.”
“Your master, Fire King Jeok Cheongang, made off with five jars of fruit wine.”
Oh, come on, Old Master.
I squeezed my eyes shut. Yayul Mok’s voice reached me anyway.
“You should at least say goodbye before you go. Everyone’s waiting.”
It wasn’t until we neared the North Gate that I realized Yayul Mok hadn’t been exaggerating when he said everyone.
This is...
Thousands of people. Maybe tens of thousands.
Among the countless people filling the field outside the North Gate, where fresh grass and flowers had spread thanks to the life-giving downpour, I saw several familiar faces.
Jeok Cheongang stood in front of a cart loaded with jars of fruit wine, pretending nothing was out of the ordinary.
Taishan held meat in both hands, looking solemn. Beside him were the Fire Dragon Pavilion members, each mounted on a beast.
And then...
“You’ve finally arrived.”
Yayul Cheok, the Beast Miao King and master of the Nanman Beast Palace, spoke with a stern face. He stood here on behalf of everyone in this land.
“Why were you going to leave without a word?”
I scratched the back of my head.
“I was going to tell you.”
“You were?”
“Well... in a letter.”
“Just a letter?”
“You looked so busy...”
“Do you think that makes sense?”
Was this what they called a question-mark murderer?
I couldn’t find an answer. The Beast Miao King, a full head taller than me, gazed down at me.
“Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”
It was a quiet summons. The Beast Miao King continued in a solemn voice.
“You came to our homeland for a reason. You had a purpose here, did you not?”

“And now you mean to leave without a word, though you have not achieved that purpose. You faced death countless times in an unfamiliar land and saved countless lives. Yet not once did you ask for the reward you were owed.”
His gaze and voice were fixed on me, but everyone gathered there could hear him. Everyone was watching.
“Why?”
I found myself answering.
“I was just one person trying to save other people.”
“I didn’t do it for a reward. And I couldn’t ask anyone to make another sacrifice. That’s why I was going to leave.”
Silence fell.

Tens of thousands of people stood together, yet I couldn’t hear a single breath. Against that silence, the rain falling on our heads sounded louder than ever. Beyond it, the Beast Miao King’s towering figure moved.
Rustle.
His back was as firm as a pillar—the back of the Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace, a man who should never have had to bow to anyone. Now it bent toward me.
Before all his people, he offered me a deeply respectful clasped-fist bow.
“I, Yayul Cheok, the Beast Miao King, on behalf of everyone who lives on this land, formally petition Great Hero Jin Taekyung, Fire Dragon Pavilion Master, for our admission into the Murim Alliance.”
It happened on a day when the rain was slowly easing.

chapters.title: Chapter 724
paragraphs: Some people left. Others stayed behind.
As the Beast Miao King watched the travelers disappear into the distance, he knew they would meet again before the ache of this farewell had faded.
And when they did, it would be on a battlefield, fighting back-to-back.
“In the end, we’re going to the Central Plains once again.”
The Beast Miao King gave a small nod at the voice beside him.
“Yes. So it has come to this.”
“A great deal of blood will be spilled.”
“Do you think your father made the wrong decision?”
“No.”
Yayul Mok continued calmly.
“If my father—no, if the Palace Lord hadn’t wanted to go to the Central Plains, I would have gone with them on my own.”
His gaze followed the figures receding in the distance.
Strangers from a foreign land. Yet it was because those strangers had come that they had been able to protect their homeland.
“Now it’s our turn to help them.”
There had been a time when Yayul Mok, too, had been hostile to the Central Plains and rejected the Han Chinese.

But things were different now. The still-unseasoned Young Palace Lord of the Nanman Beast Palace had learned what it meant to act with humanity from one stranger. He would never forget the conversation they had shared.
“What would you do if the pasture caught fire?”
“Put it out right away.”
“Why?”
“Because if we don’t, the flames will spread everywhere.”
“Good. There’s your answer.”
“Don’t overthink why we came. There’s a fire, so we’re trying to put it out. Just like the Nanman people who left this land for the Central Plains decades ago.”
At first, he hadn’t believed it. He couldn’t.
The Han Chinese he knew were despicable people who had betrayed Nanman’s trust and driven countless of its people to their deaths.
There was no way they had traveled more than ten thousand li to help without asking for anything in return.
That was what he had thought then.
But now I understand what you meant.
The pasture called the world was already on fire, and the vast inferno known as Dark Heaven would devour everything.
Where people were born and raised, how they dressed, what they looked like—none of it mattered now.
Just as Nanman had finally become one, everyone would have to join forces to put out the fire.
“We’ll fight with our lives on the line. For everyone who lives on this land. And for them.”
At the sight of his son’s resolve, the Beast Miao King smiled faintly.
When did he grow up so much?
Just as Nanman had finally become one, his only son had grown as well.
So why did the Beast Miao King’s heart feel as hollow as an empty jar?
You hopeless fool.
He swallowed the bitter thought and tilted a flask he had taken from his robes.
Fragrant fruit wine fell with the dwindling rain and soaked into the earth—the soil of the homeland where two sworn brothers had been born and raised together.
“Good wine, this. Wouldn’t you agree?”
The Beast Miao King had not tasted a drop, yet at his mumble the people around him looked puzzled. He merely laughed with relief.
This was enough.
One distant day, they would meet again and raise their cups together.
Yes. Someday, without fail.
The Beast Miao King lifted his head. Through the thinning rain, azure heaven spread above the countless people of Nanman.
Or perhaps it was the gaze of an unseen absolute being.
“Sound the war drums.”
His low voice broke the suffocating silence. He drew a deep breath, gathered his internal energy, and shouted.
“God wills it!”
His azure dragon’s roar rang in every direction. Somewhere high on a hill, the snow-white White Tiger that had been watching them let out a roar of its own.
Kraaaaaaang!
Clang-clang-clang!
“Waaaaaaah!”
Thousands—tens of thousands—of beasts and humans stamped their feet and cried out. Sunlight flashed from countless blades, scattering in every direction.
At long last, the prelude to the Great War had begun.
A melancholy look in his eyes, Hyuk Mujin waited until everyone was watching before slowly opening his mouth.
“I was just one person trying to save other people.”
“Stop.”
“I didn’t do it for a reward. And I couldn’t ask anyone to make another sacrifice. That’s why I was going to leave.”
“I said stop.”
“Come on, why are you like this? I never get tired of doing this, no matter how many times I repeat it. Honestly, you all agree, don’t you?”
Taishan, who was tearing into a wild boar’s hind leg atop a bear running at full speed, nodded vigorously.
“Taishan agrees!”
“See? Even he agrees. I was just one person trying to save—”
I quietly cut Hyuk Mujin off.
“Mujin.”
“Yes.”
“Do you want to become a eunuch?”
The grin vanished from his face.
“No.”
“Is your life too boring, then?”
“Not at all. I’m worried it’s already more exciting than I can handle.”
“Want me to make it peaceful?”
“You don’t mean that you’re going to kill me, do you?”
“What if I do?”
“Wow, look over there. Beautiful scenery.”
“Good. Let’s travel quietly.”
“...Yes, sir.”
Hyuk Mujin shut his mouth, but Taishan looked disappointed and called for an encore.
“Pavilion Master! Taishan wants to hear more!”
So I called in his designated bully.
“Old Man Nam, I think it’s time to shut that bastard’s mouth.”
“Oh, finally!”
Namho cheered like an independence fighter at liberation and pulled a muzzle from his robes as though he’d been waiting for the signal.
Made of sturdy black iron and leather straps, it looked bizarre—and strangely familiar.
“Wait. Where did you get that?”
“From a Nanman animal trainer. He said they mostly use it to tame wild bears.”
“Why are you looking at me like that? Is there a problem?”
“Well, not exactly.”
Something about it bothered me. I had the uneasy feeling that if Namho put it on him, I’d have to stop calling him Taishan and start calling him product number TAESAN-317.
I hesitated, then gave in and sighed.
“Don’t put it on him. Actually, just throw it away.”
“No! Why?”
Why? Because I felt like it would dirty my eyes.
I snatched the muzzle from the practically wailing Namho and hurled it into the distance. Jeok Cheongang, who had watched the whole thing, spoke with an uneasy look on his face.
“What on earth happened in Nanman?”
For a moment, I didn’t understand what he meant.
“Pardon?”
“I’m asking what happened to make every last one of you lose your mind.”
“A lot happened in Nanman, sure, but they were all like this to begin with.”
“What?”
“Surprising, but true.”
“You brat! Don’t talk nonsense. With things this much of a goddamn mess, how did none of you get killed?”
Yeah. Fuck.
Looking back on what had happened in Nanman, I had a reasonable suspicion that the Earth Mother Goddess really had blessed us.
I came close to death several times. Making it back in one piece is a miracle.

Of course, I was the only one who had come close to death that many times. The others had suffered injuries, major and minor, but the Sacred Rain had worked so well that every one of them had recovered completely.
And we somehow stopped Dark Heaven’s plot.
A great many people had died in the process. Still, stopping the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—practically the Fire Dragon Pavilion’s top priority, and mine—was more than half a success.
The Nanman Beast Palace officially joined the Murim Alliance, too.

Truthfully, that had been all but certain once we stopped the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. Even without the Earth Mother Goddess’s value as a new brand, the outcome probably wouldn’t have changed much.
Stamp out a fire halfheartedly and it only burns hotter. Anger can draw scattered people together.
All I had done was give them another point to rally around: a One God who could erase boundaries between tribes that had stood for centuries and help them become a more united, more powerful force.
And that made the Murim Alliance stronger, too.
On this, I had no doubts. The Nanman Beast Palace was firmly on our side now.
According to what the Beast Miao King had promised before we left, they would send more troops than they had during the Great Faction War and do everything in their power to hold back Dark Heaven.
So why?
Why do I still feel uneasy?
We’d accomplished a great deal, yet I couldn’t shake the feeling that something was wrong.
Perhaps it was because one question remained unanswered.

The new Murim Alliance has been formed. The forces of the Central Plains are gathering around the Nine Sects and One Gang and the Five Great Families. Yet Dark Heaven still hasn’t shown its full strength.

Their first intervention in Shanxi Province, the Shaolin Bloodshed that followed, and every incident since—none of them had been minor. But each had involved only a fragment of Dark Heaven, not the organization as a whole.
They should be past the point of testing the waters.
What the hell were they—or rather, what was the Lord of Heaven—trying to do?
And why did the Lord of Heaven...
“Why would the Lord of Heaven take this much interest in me, of all people?”
I hadn’t meant to say it aloud. Everyone looked at me at once, and before I could explain, Hyuk Mujin perked up like a meerkat.
“Gasp, Captain. Did someone confess to you? Oh my God. A Nanman?”
I wanted to gouge out his eyes, sparkling like the morning star. I fought the urge.
“It’s not like that, you crazy bastard.”
“Then she’s Han Chinese?”
“How many times do I have to tell you—wait. Come to think of it, that part’s right.”
“Wow. When did this happen? Who confessed?”
“The Lord of Heaven.”
“Now there’s an impressive name for a young lady. Sounds like a daughter from a respectable family...”
Hyuk Mujin stopped. He blinked, thought for a moment, then spoke again.
“Who?”
“The Lord of Heaven.”
“The one I know? I mean, the one everyone knows?”
“Who else?”
“Fuck. That respectable household was in Xinjiang...”
Beyond Qinghai, where the Kunlun Sect stood, lay Xinjiang. For a thousand years, Xinjiang had been the domain of the Demonic Path.
Once everyone realized that the supposed young lady interested in me belonged to Dark Heaven’s household, they stared at one another, momentarily lost for words. Then the questions came all at once.
“Why would the Lord of Heaven be interested in you?” Hyuk Mujin asked.
Namho cut in. “Isn’t it obvious? He keeps getting in the Lord of Heaven’s way.”
“Sure, but the Captain isn’t one of the Three Saints or the Ten Kings. He’s just a scrap who’s only just made a name for himself.”
“Now that you mention it, you’re not wrong.”
“Taishan can eat scraps.”
“You son of a bitch. I knew this might happen, so I brought another muzzle. Come here. Open your mouth.”
“Why are you all talking about him like that? Our Pavilion Master is a scrap? Song Escort, Sama Pyo! Say something!”
“Young Lady Ju, I’m sorry, but I think I have to leave. I managed to make it all the way to Nanman, but if the Lord of Heaven has taken an interest in that man...”
“Taishan! That’s not meat! Don’t bite it! Old Man Nam, put that muzzle down!”
Fuck. I had never seen such a complete mess.
I stared blankly at the disaster unfolding before me. Then a quiet Sound Transmission reached my ears.
—Let’s talk.
It was Jeok Cheongang.
