chapters.title: Chapter 725
paragraphs: “Let’s talk.”
I gave a small nod at the Sound Transmission in my ear and loosened my grip on the reins.
The beast understood and gradually slowed. Jeok Cheongang drew alongside me, then spoke.
“Is it true the Lord of Heaven has taken a particular interest in you?”
“Yes.”
“Huh. Strange. This old man is hearing about it for the first time.”
“I suppose so. It’s the first time I’ve mentioned it, too.”
“Why didn’t you tell me?”
“You never asked.”
Honestly, I expected to get hit for that. I even snapped into a defensive stance.
But Jeok Cheongang only stared at me for a moment before muttering, almost to himself, “You didn’t tell me because I didn’t ask... Well, I can’t say you’re wrong.”
What had gotten into him?
“Um, Old Master?”
“What.”
“Are you... sulking?”
“What? Sulking? Me?”
“Yes.”
Jeok Cheongang laughed as though I’d told him a marvelous joke.

“Why would I sulk? I’m not five years old. Of course, we had plenty of time to discuss it over the past three days, and I held back from asking out of consideration for you. But that doesn’t matter in the slightest, so don’t give it another thought. The fool is the one who didn’t ask, isn’t he? Hahaha.”

“People in the martial world say a master and disciple should keep no secrets from each other. But that hardly applies to us, so pay it no mind. If you think about it, I needed someone to carry on the Fire Gate Clan’s lineage, and you needed martial arts. We both got what we wanted. That’s enough. Talking about the bond between master and disciple in this day and age is laughable anyway.”

“I ran my balls off getting to Nanman because I was worried something might happen to you. Even plucked out every hair on my perfectly good head to hide my identity. But I’m fine. My balls didn’t fall off, and my hair will grow back soon enough. Of course it will.”

“Why would this old man sulk just because he didn’t hear some goddamn story? A thirsty man should dig his own well. If I waited for you to tell me when the time was right, wouldn’t I end up dried out and dead just like this old man? Hahahaha.”
Watching Jeok Cheongang laugh like an immortal, I thought, He’s really fucking sulking.
Could a person even sulk this much?
Forbes could name him the World’s Most Sulky Person, and no one would object.
“I remember the day I first met you. I wasn’t in my right mind then, what with the infirmities of old age. I suppose that’s why they say old people ought to die...”
The pressure was suffocating.
I finally managed to interrupt Jeok Cheongang’s runaway train of a speech.
“What I said earlier was a joke. I had too much on my mind to tell you. I needed time to sort through it myself.”
“Hm.”
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes. Sounding a little more like himself, he asked gruffly, “So was the part about the Lord of Heaven a joke too?”
“Unfortunately, that part’s true.”
“What proof do you have?”
I told him what had happened. He’d already heard a brief version while we were at the Nanman Beast Palace, but this time I went into far more detail.
By the time I finished, his brow was furrowed.
“Those bastards tried to capture you?”
“Yes. But when that didn’t work, they tried to kill me. The Great Snow Fiend and Black Hand Fist Demon at the Poisonblood Grounds, and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress too.”
“Did they try to capture you on the Lord of Heaven’s orders?”
“That...”
I thought back for a moment, then shook my head.
“I don’t think so.”
“Why not?”
“If the Lord of Heaven had ordered her to capture me, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress wouldn’t have tried to kill me. Not even if she had to face her own death alone.”
“Loyalty that outweighs her life... Hard to believe.”
“It wasn’t just loyalty.”
I answered quietly as I recalled everything about the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. The look in her eyes. Her expression. The rapture in her voice, and all she had said and done.
What I’d sensed from her that day couldn’t be described as mere loyalty.
It was...
“Fanaticism. To the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—no, to Dark Heaven—the Lord of Heaven is a living god.”
“Everyone in Dark Heaven fears and reveres him. If he ordered them to capture me at any cost, that would be a divine command no one could defy.”
The Blood Lord, for all his power. The Western Heaven Demon Lord. Even the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, who had now met her end.
All of them had bowed before the Lord of Heaven and called themselves his servants.
Each was a monster capable of tearing an ordinary Supreme Peak master apart with their bare hands. And the Lord of Heaven was the king—the god—those monsters worshiped.
“I can’t be certain, but I think the Southern Heaven Demon Empress tried to capture me simply because the Lord of Heaven had shown an interest in me.”
“To win his favor?”
I nodded. Jeok Cheongang let out a low groan.
“Fanatics...”
The word faded into the wind.
Seated on the tiger’s back, he watched the scenery rush past in silence. Then he spoke again.
“Have you ever seen a member of the Demonic Cult?”
“Do I look sixty to you?”
“Yes. At your age, it would be natural that you hadn’t seen one. You were born long after the Great Faction War ended.”
“Then why ask?”
“A thought occurred to me. We might be better off fighting the Demonic Cult of those days all over again.”

“They were fanatics too, of course. But their leader, the Heavenly Demon, was still a man. The hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path beneath him knew it. To them, he was the Cult Leader who led them. He was not a god.”
I understood what Jeok Cheongang meant.
To the Demonic Cult, the Heavenly Demon had been flesh and blood. To Dark Heaven, the Lord of Heaven was a god.
They would fight for that god without fear of death. They would die smiling, even with countless spears and blades buried in their bodies.
“This will be a more terrible war than any we’ve known.”
Jeok Cheongang fixed me with a grave look.
“Especially for you.”
“Because the Lord of Heaven is watching me?”
“Whether you wanted it or not, you’ve drawn more attention than you should have. Somewhere in the world, even now, people are speaking your name.”

“The Three Saints and Ten Kings are old names. But you are different. You possess a talent without precedent throughout history, and no one in the world can deny that you became a master despite having only just passed the age of twenty.”
His gaze held unmistakable pride—and worry.
“That is why the Lord of Heaven is watching you, too. And more importantly, he has already seen you once—your true nature and the infinite potential hidden within you.”
“...The Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison.”
“Yes. He used some unknown supernatural power to look at you through the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes.”
How could I forget?
Stone dust raining onto my head. Blood spattered across the stone wall.
And the words of the Western Heaven Demon Lord, standing there as he looked at me.
No. The words of the Lord of Heaven, who had borrowed his servant’s body for a moment.
Interesting. Very interesting.
He had been smiling then. Even as his entire body turned into a handful of ashes and scattered away, he had not forgotten to offer me one final greeting.
I’ll see you again.
The memory still made my heart sink.
Jeok Cheongang watched me draw a slow breath, then said, “Perhaps... the Lord of Heaven has some inkling of the secrets you’ve never told anyone.”
“That’s why I can no longer avoid asking.”

sentences.text: “Let’s talk.”
I gave a small nod at the Sound Transmission in my ear and loosened my grip on the reins.
The beast understood and gradually slowed.
Jeok Cheongang drew alongside me, then spoke.
“Is it true the Lord of Heaven has taken a particular interest in you?”
“Yes.”
“Huh.
Strange.
This old man is hearing about it for the first time.”
“I suppose so.
It’s the first time I’ve mentioned it, too.”
“Why didn’t you tell me?”
“You never asked.”
Honestly, I expected to get hit for that.
I even snapped into a defensive stance.
But Jeok Cheongang only stared at me for a moment before muttering, almost to himself, “You didn’t tell me because I didn’t ask...
Well, I can’t say you’re wrong.”
What had gotten into him?
“Um, Old Master?”
“What.”
“Are you... sulking?”
“What?
Sulking?
Me?”
“Yes.”
Jeok Cheongang laughed as though I’d told him a marvelous joke.
“Why would I sulk?
I’m not five years old.
Of course, we had plenty of time to discuss it over the past three days, and I held back from asking out of consideration for you.
But that doesn’t matter in the slightest, so don’t give it another thought.
The fool is the one who didn’t ask, isn’t he?
Hahaha.”
“People in the martial world say a master and disciple should keep no secrets from each other.
But that hardly applies to us, so pay it no mind.
If you think about it, I needed someone to carry on the Fire Gate Clan’s lineage, and you needed martial arts.
We both got what we wanted.
That’s enough.
Talking about the bond between master and disciple in this day and age is laughable anyway.”
“I ran my balls off getting to Nanman because I was worried something might happen to you.
Even plucked out every hair on my perfectly good head to hide my identity.
But I’m fine.
My balls didn’t fall off, and my hair will grow back soon enough.
Of course it will.”
“Why would this old man sulk just because he didn’t hear some goddamn story?
A thirsty man should dig his own well.
If I waited for you to tell me when the time was right, wouldn’t I end up dried out and dead just like this old man?
Hahahaha.”
Watching Jeok Cheongang laugh like an immortal, I thought, He’s really fucking sulking.
Could a person even sulk this much?
Forbes could name him the World’s Most Sulky Person, and no one would object.
“I remember the day I first met you.
I wasn’t in my right mind then, what with the infirmities of old age.
I suppose that’s why they say old people ought to die...”
The pressure was suffocating.
I finally managed to interrupt Jeok Cheongang’s runaway train of a speech.
“What I said earlier was a joke.
I had too much on my mind to tell you.
I needed time to sort through it myself.”
“Hm.”
Jeok Cheongang narrowed his eyes.
Sounding a little more like himself, he asked gruffly, “So was the part about the Lord of Heaven a joke too?”
“Unfortunately, that part’s true.”
“What proof do you have?”
I told him what had happened.
He’d already heard a brief version while we were at the Nanman Beast Palace, but this time I went into far more detail.
By the time I finished, his brow was furrowed.
“Those bastards tried to capture you?”
“Yes.
But when that didn’t work, they tried to kill me.
The Great Snow Fiend and Black Hand Fist Demon at the Poisonblood Grounds, and the Southern Heaven Demon Empress too.”
“Did they try to capture you on the Lord of Heaven’s orders?”
“That...”
I thought back for a moment, then shook my head.
“I don’t think so.”
“Why not?”
“If the Lord of Heaven had ordered her to capture me, the Southern Heaven Demon Empress wouldn’t have tried to kill me.
Not even if she had to face her own death alone.”
“Loyalty that outweighs her life...
Hard to believe.”
“It wasn’t just loyalty.”
I answered quietly as I recalled everything about the Southern Heaven Demon Empress.
The look in her eyes.
Her expression.
The rapture in her voice, and all she had said and done.
What I’d sensed from her that day couldn’t be described as mere loyalty.
It was...
“Fanaticism.
To the Southern Heaven Demon Empress—no, to Dark Heaven—the Lord of Heaven is a living god.”
“Everyone in Dark Heaven fears and reveres him.
If he ordered them to capture me at any cost, that would be a divine command no one could defy.”
The Blood Lord, for all his power.
The Western Heaven Demon Lord.
Even the Southern Heaven Demon Empress, who had now met her end.
All of them had bowed before the Lord of Heaven and called themselves his servants.
Each was a monster capable of tearing an ordinary Supreme Peak master apart with their bare hands.
And the Lord of Heaven was the king—the god—those monsters worshiped.
“I can’t be certain, but I think the Southern Heaven Demon Empress tried to capture me simply because the Lord of Heaven had shown an interest in me.”
“To win his favor?”
I nodded.
Jeok Cheongang let out a low groan.
“Fanatics...”
The word faded into the wind.
Seated on the tiger’s back, he watched the scenery rush past in silence.
Then he spoke again.
“Have you ever seen a member of the Demonic Cult?”
“Do I look sixty to you?”
“Yes.
At your age, it would be natural that you hadn’t seen one.
You were born long after the Great Faction War ended.”
“Then why ask?”
“A thought occurred to me.
We might be better off fighting the Demonic Cult of those days all over again.”
“They were fanatics too, of course.
But their leader, the Heavenly Demon, was still a man.
The hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path beneath him knew it.
To them, he was the Cult Leader who led them.
He was not a god.”
I understood what Jeok Cheongang meant.
To the Demonic Cult, the Heavenly Demon had been flesh and blood.
To Dark Heaven, the Lord of Heaven was a god.
They would fight for that god without fear of death.
They would die smiling, even with countless spears and blades buried in their bodies.
“This will be a more terrible war than any we’ve known.”
Jeok Cheongang fixed me with a grave look.
“Especially for you.”
“Because the Lord of Heaven is watching me?”
“Whether you wanted it or not, you’ve drawn more attention than you should have.
Somewhere in the world, even now, people are speaking your name.”
“The Three Saints and Ten Kings are old names.
But you are different.
You possess a talent without precedent throughout history, and no one in the world can deny that you became a master despite having only just passed the age of twenty.”
His gaze held unmistakable pride—and worry.
“That is why the Lord of Heaven is watching you, too.
And more importantly, he has already seen you once—your true nature and the infinite potential hidden within you.”
“...The Sichuan Tang Clan’s underground prison.”
“Yes.
He used some unknown supernatural power to look at you through the Western Heaven Demon Lord’s eyes.”
How could I forget?
Stone dust raining onto my head.
Blood spattered across the stone wall.
And the words of the Western Heaven Demon Lord, standing there as he looked at me.
No.
The words of the Lord of Heaven, who had borrowed his servant’s body for a moment.
Interesting.
Very interesting.
He had been smiling then.
Even as his entire body turned into a handful of ashes and scattered away, he had not forgotten to offer me one final greeting.
I’ll see you again.

paragraphs: System Synchronization begins. - 10, 9, 8, 7, 6... Logout complete.
I opened my eyes to a familiar chime. The first thing I saw was a ceiling impossibly far above me.
Not the wooden ceiling that smelled of old, dry grass, but a pristine white one made of solid alloy.
I still wasn’t used to the jarring shift between worlds. As I lay there, I recalled my last memory of the modern world.
The training room.

Right. This was the Peace Guild’s training room. Only a handful of people, myself included, were allowed inside. Protected by formidable security and surveillance systems, it was where I had left for Murim—right after finally taking care of an important matter I had put off for a long time.
That’s right.
I stared at the ceiling in silence.
My memories of my time in Murim had returned, along with all my senses, but I had no desire whatsoever to get up.
Murim to the modern world. The modern world to Murim.
A spell of listlessness after crossing between the two wasn’t unusual for me. This time, though, it hit especially hard.
...I really went and did it.
I’d imagined telling someone my secret dozens of times. Of course, I’d never actually done it. I couldn’t have.
It was too dangerous.
But... it was also true that, somewhere in the back of my mind, I had thought that a day like this would come eventually. I just hadn’t expected that day, which had seemed so far away, to be today.
What did you say?
I could still see Jeok Cheongang’s reaction when he first heard my confession. He hadn’t looked shocked or incredulous. No, he simply hadn’t understood what I was saying.
“What did you just say?”
“Exactly what I said. I came from farther away than you think, Old Master.”
“Shanxi Province is some distance from the Central Plains, yes. But what does that have to do with your secret...?”
“Farther than that. Farther than Nanman, even.”
“Farther than Nanman?”
“Yes. So far you couldn’t reach it if you walked your entire life.”
“You mean you have to take a boat?”
“No. That’s not it. I mean... it’s a completely different world.”
A completely different world.
Jeok Cheongang listened to what came next, then fell silent for a long time, trying to make sense of it in his own way.
“So you’re saying you came from the realm of immortals.”
“...Uh. I guess you could put it that way.”
“Are you a Little Immortal?”
“I’m an ordinary citizen.”

If Jeok Cheongang had been from the modern world, we might have understood each other a little better. In a world that already had monsters and magic, one man from Murim wouldn’t have been impossible to comprehend.
Whether that man wound up in a psychiatric hospital or got dragged off to a laboratory afterward was another question.
But Jeok Cheongang had spent over a hundred years in Murim, a world without even the internet. Everything I told him was bound to sound bewildering.
“When you fall asleep here, you go to the realm of immortals?”
“Not every time, but unless something unusual happens, yes.”
“And when you wish to leave the realm of immortals and return here...”
“It works the same way. Each time, time in the other world moves very slowly.”
“...Goddamn it.”
After a desperate struggle to hold on to his common sense and reason, Jeok Cheongang finally reached a conclusion.
“Damn it. I don’t understand.”
“What?”
“I’m telling you, I still don’t understand.”
Some truths couldn’t be understood even if you saw them with your own eyes and heard them with your own ears. Everything I’d told Jeok Cheongang was like that for him.
Yet amid all his confusion, one thing remained unchanged.
“But the idiot standing before this old man is named Jin Taekyung. Not a Little Immortal descended from the realm of immortals. Blazing Flame Divine Dragon Jin Taekyung.”
“That alone is enough.”
I hadn’t understood then why those words left me speechless. Why I had to clench my teeth against the heat rising in my chest.
But... yes. As Jeok Cheongang had said, that alone was enough for me, too.
And now I thought I understood why.
I’d been afraid. Afraid that the other world, now such a large part of my life, might deny that I belonged there.
What am I, a little kid?
A rueful laugh slipped out. At the same time, the weight pressing on my heart lifted, and I felt relieved.
Right. This is enough. For now, at least.
Since when had I ever lived with my eyes fixed on the future? I’d chosen where to go one day, one moment at a time, and that had brought me here.
The path I’d chosen today was as wide and warm as a beach in summer.
I’d seen on TV that athletes all had their own routines.
One soccer player always stepped onto the field with his left foot first. A star Major League batter spat out a sunflower seed every time he swung his bat.
To an ordinary person, that might seem like an awful lot of fuss over nothing. But everyone had little superstitions for peace of mind and good luck.
No profession took them more seriously than Hunters.
Lose a soccer game, and the sky doesn’t fall. Strike out on three pitches with the bases loaded and a chance to take the lead, and the ground doesn’t open beneath you.
A Hunter, though, could be dead the moment luck turned bad.
There was no next game. No next at-bat. Just their life and their family’s faces flashing through their mind as they drew their final breath, and one sudden thought:
Fuck, I should’ve worn my blue underwear today.
It sounded like a joke, but it was true. Those had been the last words of an A-rank Hunter who’d died in a Gate a few years ago, at the height of his popularity.
Or was it red underwear?
I’d been working nonstop back then, so the details were hazy. Anyway.
The point was, I had a routine of my own. I’d followed it without fail until now, and it had just been broken.
Bang!
The door flew open as if something had exploded.
The lock I had installed as a precaution was destroyed. Fortunately, I had finished all my preparations one step ahead of time, so I did my best to remain calm as I welcomed the unwelcome guest.
“Well, well. You don’t even knock anymore before barging in.”
“Huff. Hah.”
He was breathing hard, sweat beading on his forehead, his suit in disarray. I looked at him and added, “Team Leader Choi.”
Normally, I’d have been glad to see him. Right now, I wanted to punch that handsome face.
But Team Leader Choi—who, by all rights, should now be called the Guild Master—didn’t notice my mood. Or rather, he had no attention to spare for it.
“Huff. Hoo.”
What, was the Demon King chasing him?

These days, Team Leader Choi could hold his own against any Peak Master in the Central Plains. He finally caught his breath, thrust out what he was holding, and shouted, “What is this? What on earth is this?”
“If you don’t have anything important to say, come back a little later... Ah. That?”
“That? Is this something you can dismiss with ‘that’?”
Rage button: ON.

The way he nearly lost his mind over my casual answer told me two things. First, I was going to have to break the essential routine I’d followed every day since finishing Hunter training. Second, there was no getting out of explaining that thing right now.
“Calm down. Calm down. I’ll tell you everything, so put that down first. Oh, and what would you like to drink?”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung. What you drink isn’t important right n—”
“I’ll just make you coffee. What was it again? That tiger-poop coffee you gave me last time to celebrate the opening of the office.”
“Hah.”
“That okay?”
Team Leader Choi stared at me, shock and disbelief mingling in his eyes, then sank onto the sofa.
In his trembling hand was a sheaf of papers covered in my own handwriting.
[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]
Looking at it again, my penmanship was a work of art.
Team Leader Choi really was a rich kid.
A moment ago, he’d been snorting like a Minotaur with its horns ripped out. One whiff of rich coffee, though, and he had his composure back. I couldn’t help sniffing the air myself.
“Does tiger-poop coffee calm you down or something? Or is this one of your routines?”
Team Leader Choi answered coolly. “It isn’t a tiger. It’s a cat. A civet cat.”
“Tiger, cat. Whatever.”
“And rather than poop, please say feces. The word ‘secretion’ is also available.”
“Poop.”
“Feces. Or secretion.”
“Right. So, poop.”
“Unless you’ve forgotten, it will be dinnertime soon. If you keep saying ‘poop’ to someone’s face like that...”
“Poop.”
As the atmosphere grew increasingly shitty, Team Leader Choi was the first to back down.
“Fine. That isn’t what matters right now.”
“Mm.”
On second thought, I was being an idiot. I took a breath and let go of my irritation. Team Leader Choi had broken a routine I absolutely needed to keep, but I was the one who’d given him the reason.
[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]
Anyone who saw this would have come running. Even the President of the United States.
“Given what’s at stake, I’ll ask you directly.”
His voice trembled slightly. He looked me in the eye and went on.
“This... no, this mana cultivation method. Where did it come from?”
I answered without hesitation.
“Who do you think? The person sitting across from you.”
“I made it myself. From beginning to end.”
A suffocating silence fell. Team Leader Choi stared at me, eyes wavering, before letting out the breath he’d been holding.
“Hoo.”
“Why are you so surprised? Didn’t the errand boy I sent explain?”
Of course, he wasn’t just an errand boy. The Skeleton King might be a little unhinged, but he was a powerful Named Monster—and secretly operated as an S-rank Hunter for the Peace Guild.
More importantly, I could trust him.
Team Leader Choi knew that better than anyone. He gave a quiet laugh.
“That was quite an errand boy.”
“That’s why I entrusted it to him. I was originally going to give it to you myself, but you happened not to be there.”
“...I had somewhere to stop by.”
He left it at that, and I didn’t ask where he’d been.
The person who had suddenly left us all two months ago had left a space that still held a lingering warmth, like the coffee cup before us that Team Leader Choi had not taken a single sip from.
“I heard what you told Skeleton King. No—Mr. King. But I’m sorry...”
“You had to check for yourself. I get it.”

“Yes. But the moment I saw what was inside, even before hearing an explanation, I knew. Jin Taekyung is the only person in the entire world who could have created a mana cultivation method like this.”
At his praise, I scratched the back of my head.
“Come on, it’s not that impressive. I did put a lot of thought and effort into making it something even beginners could learn, but...”
“There can’t be many S-rank Hunters with handwriting this bad. Or people with a sense for names like yours.”
“What?”
“And someone who has both? I didn’t need to think twice.”
“That’s how I knew this mana cultivation method could only have come from one person: Jin Taekyung.”
I looked from Team Leader Choi’s utterly certain face to [The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method] on the table, then back again.
What the fuck.
Mana cultivation method or not, maybe I should just tear the whole thing to shreds.

I’d chosen where to go one day, one moment at a time, and that had brought me here.
The path I’d chosen today was as wide and warm as a beach in summer.
I’d seen on TV that athletes all had their own routines.
One soccer player always stepped onto the field with his left foot first.
A star Major League batter spat out a sunflower seed every time he swung his bat.
To an ordinary person, that might seem like an awful lot of fuss over nothing.
But everyone had little superstitions for peace of mind and good luck.
No profession took them more seriously than Hunters.
Lose a soccer game, and the sky doesn’t fall.
Strike out on three pitches with the bases loaded and a chance to take the lead, and the ground doesn’t open beneath you.
A Hunter, though, could be dead the moment luck turned bad.
There was no next game.
No next at-bat.
Just their life and their family’s faces flashing through their mind as they drew their final breath, and one sudden thought:
Fuck, I should’ve worn my blue underwear today.
It sounded like a joke, but it was true.
Those had been the last words of an A-rank Hunter who’d died in a Gate a few years ago, at the height of his popularity.
Or was it red underwear?
I’d been working nonstop back then, so the details were hazy.
Anyway.
The point was, I had a routine of my own.
I’d followed it without fail until now, and it had just been broken.
Bang!
The door flew open as if something had exploded.
The lock I had installed as a precaution was destroyed.
Fortunately, I had finished all my preparations one step ahead of time, so I did my best to remain calm as I welcomed the unwelcome guest.
“Well, well.
You don’t even knock anymore before barging in.”
“Huff.
Hah.”
He was breathing hard, sweat beading on his forehead, his suit in disarray.
I looked at him and added, “Team Leader Choi.”
Normally, I’d have been glad to see him.
Right now, I wanted to punch that handsome face.
But Team Leader Choi—who, by all rights, should now be called the Guild Master—didn’t notice my mood.
Or rather, he had no attention to spare for it.
“Huff.
Hoo.”
What, was the Demon King chasing him?
These days, Team Leader Choi could hold his own against any Peak Master in the Central Plains.
He finally caught his breath, thrust out what he was holding, and shouted, “What is this?
What on earth is this?”
“If you don’t have anything important to say, come back a little later...
Ah.
That?”
“That?
Is this something you can dismiss with ‘that’?”
Rage button: ON.
The way he nearly lost his mind over my casual answer told me two things.
First, I was going to have to break the essential routine I’d followed every day since finishing Hunter training.
Second, there was no getting out of explaining that thing right now.
“Calm down.
Calm down.
I’ll tell you everything, so put that down first.
Oh, and what would you like to drink?”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung.
What you drink isn’t important right n—”
“I’ll just make you coffee.
What was it again?
That tiger-poop coffee you gave me last time to celebrate the opening of the office.”
“Hah.”
“That okay?”
Team Leader Choi stared at me, shock and disbelief mingling in his eyes, then sank onto the sofa.
In his trembling hand was a sheaf of papers covered in my own handwriting.
[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]
Looking at it again, my penmanship was a work of art.
Team Leader Choi really was a rich kid.
A moment ago, he’d been snorting like a Minotaur with its horns ripped out.
One whiff of rich coffee, though, and he had his composure back.
I couldn’t help sniffing the air myself.
“Does tiger-poop coffee calm you down or something?
Or is this one of your routines?”
Team Leader Choi answered coolly.
“It isn’t a tiger.
It’s a cat.
A civet cat.”
“Tiger, cat.
Whatever.”
“And rather than poop, please say feces.
The word ‘secretion’ is also available.”
“Poop.”
“Feces.
Or secretion.”
“Right.
So, poop.”
“Unless you’ve forgotten, it will be dinnertime soon.
If you keep saying ‘poop’ to someone’s face like that...”
“Poop.”
As the atmosphere grew increasingly shitty, Team Leader Choi was the first to back down.
“Fine.
That isn’t what matters right now.”
“Mm.”
On second thought, I was being an idiot.
I took a breath and let go of my irritation.
Team Leader Choi had broken a routine I absolutely needed to keep, but I was the one who’d given him the reason.
[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]
Anyone who saw this would have come running.
Even the President of the United States.
“Given what’s at stake, I’ll ask you directly.”
His voice trembled slightly.
He looked me in the eye and went on.
“This... no, this mana cultivation method.
Where did it come from?”
I answered without hesitation.
“Who do you think?
The person sitting across from you.”
“I made it myself.
From beginning to end.”
A suffocating silence fell.
Team Leader Choi stared at me, eyes wavering, before letting out the breath he’d been holding.
“Hoo.”
“Why are you so surprised?
Didn’t the errand boy I sent explain?”
Of course, he wasn’t just an errand boy.
The Skeleton King might be a little unhinged, but he was a powerful Named Monster—and secretly operated as an S-rank Hunter for the Peace Guild.
More importantly, I could trust him.
Team Leader Choi knew that better than anyone.
He gave a quiet laugh.
“That was quite an errand boy.”
“That’s why I entrusted it to him.
I was originally going to give it to you myself, but you happened not to be there.”
“...I had somewhere to stop by.”
He left it at that, and I didn’t ask where he’d been.
The person who had suddenly left us all two months ago had left a space that still held a lingering warmth, like the coffee cup before us that Team Leader Choi had not taken a single sip from.
“I heard what you told Skeleton King.
No—Mr.
King.
But I’m sorry...”
“You had to check for yourself.
I get it.”
“Yes.
But the moment I saw what was inside, even before hearing an explanation, I knew.
Jin Taekyung is the only person in the entire world who could have created a mana cultivation method like this.”
At his praise, I scratched the back of my head.
“Come on, it’s not that impressive.
I did put a lot of thought and effort into making it something even beginners could learn, but...”
“There can’t be many S-rank Hunters with handwriting this bad.
Or people with a sense for names like yours.”
“What?”
“And someone who has both?
I didn’t need to think twice.”
“That’s how I knew this mana cultivation method could only have come from one person: Jin Taekyung.”
I looked from Team Leader Choi’s utterly certain face to [The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method] on the table, then back again.
What the fuck.
Mana cultivation method or not, maybe I should just tear the whole thing to shreds.

chapters.title: Chapter 727
paragraphs: Should I tear it up or not?
Looking at Jin Taekyung, whose thoughts were written plainly across his face, Choi Minwoo let out a faint, incredulous laugh inwardly.
I really can’t figure him out.
Most of the time, his words, actions, and thoughts were as simple as could be. But every so often, Jin Taekyung showed a side of himself that went beyond surprising.
You’d think I’d be used to it by now. But this...
Choi Minwoo looked down at the table.
[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]
The crooked handwriting looked like a child’s, and the title was ridiculous. But there was nothing ridiculous about what filled those ten or so sheets of A4 paper.
He created an entirely new Mana Cultivation Method.
There was a reason Choi Minwoo had gone so far as to criticize Jin Taekyung’s handwriting earlier. It was a small act of revenge for suddenly handing over something this absurd without saying a word.
The shock he had felt a few hours ago had been that great.
How is this possible?
He had never seen explanations or instructions so simple and clear. The method was exceptionally stable, with a firm grounding in the fundamentals.

Choi Minwoo had grown skilled enough to hold his own against a Peak Master of Murim. He had recognized the value of this new method immediately. He had also understood what the recent events that had drawn the world’s attention meant to Jin Taekyung.
“The Week of Judgment.”
Choi Minwoo broke the brief silence and looked at Jin Taekyung.

“Just as God created heaven and earth over the course of a week, terrorists around the world endured a Week of Judgment. President Doramp Jr. said that at a White House press conference a few days ago.”
The President of the United States had said it in public. Naturally, his provocative remarks had spread around the world in less than an hour. By now, everyone in Korea had heard about them.
Everyone but one person, perhaps.
“He said that?”
Jin Taekyung had been holed up in the training room the whole time. Choi Minwoo nodded.
“It was a fairly aggressive thing for any president to say, especially the American president. Some people criticized him for deliberately provoking the terrorists.”
“Hm. Why bring up something as grand as creating heaven and earth? What about retaliatory terrorism?”
“None. Not a single one.”
“Not one?”
“Yes. If anything, they’ve even been keeping their mouths shut.”
The sullen look on Jin Taekyung’s face eased a little.
“Guess beating the crap out of them paid off.”
It was at that exact moment that Choi Minwoo, who had been gazing pensively at Jin Taekyung, suddenly spoke.
“So that was why.”
“Why what?”
“I thought about two things. Why you suddenly suppressed the terrorists. And what it meant that you gave me this new Mana Cultivation Method.”
Now he had his answer.
[The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method]
Choi Minwoo lifted the papers, held together with a single careless staple.
“You’re planning to make this Mana Cultivation Method available to everyone.”
Jin Taekyung grinned.
“Our Team Leader Choi really is sharp.”
The look Team Leader Choi gave me was hard to read. Part of it seemed like admiration. The rest looked like he had a lot to think about.
“Why? Is there a problem?”
“Well...”
He ran a hand through his disheveled hair.
“There are so many problems, I don’t know where to start.”
“There’s nothing wrong with the Mana Cultivation Method itself, so you mean practical problems.”
“...Yes. Unfortunately.”
“What’s the biggest one?”
He thought for a moment.
“For starters, making the method public is a problem in its own right.”
“Go on.”

“You know that only a tiny fraction of high-ranking Hunters possess Mana Cultivation Methods. They’re closely guarded knowledge—secret arts, essentially. You also know how closed-off those Hunters are, and how different their world is from the one other Hunters live in.”
“I know. I’ve been in this business for years. Though back when I was an F-rank Hunter, I’d never even heard of a Mana Cultivation Method.”
No profession divided its members more sharply than the Hunter business.
Ordinary people judged one another by education, family background, and looks. Hunters were sorted into high and low by Grade alone.
How much mana you’d been granted. How agile you were. How strong. Those crude measures determined your place, and you were graded like cattle headed for slaughter.
There’s a reason they call F-rank Hunters slaves.

High-ranking Hunters, meanwhile, practically lived above the clouds. They earned more from a single raid than most Hunters could make in a lifetime and spent their days under spotlights and envious stares.

Maybe that was why they’d built walls around themselves, like nobles of old living inside their castles. No one but another high-ranking Hunter could cross those walls. Even if someone was lucky enough to receive a high Grade, the gate opened only with their permission.
Those high-ranking Hunters were connected by invisible ties across the world, each protected by the giant Guild they belonged to.
“This isn’t limited to Korea,” Team Leader Choi said. “If you make this method public, the backlash will be greater than you expect.”
“Because they’ll think releasing a Mana Cultivation Method makes what they have less valuable?”
“That’s part of it. There’s another reason.”
“What?”
“The problem is that it’s us.”
It was a short answer, but I immediately understood what he meant.
Have we stood out too much?
I suddenly remembered my conversation with Jeok Cheongang just before I logged out. Whether I had wanted it or not, he’d said, I had already drawn far more attention than necessary.
The spotlight was bright. But everything around it was dark.
I’d read that line in a novel I liked back in school. It was true. The brighter I became, the deeper the darkness around me grew.
In Murim and in the modern world.
“Team Leader Choi, by any chance...?”
He understood the question and shook his head.
“There’s been no major problem yet, but we’re facing pressure behind the scenes. We’ve put plans for more overseas branches on hold for now.”
“It’s that serious?”
“Every major Guild in the world is watching us. They don’t need to make a show of force to cause us trouble. If they decide to act, things won’t be easy for us.”
“Why didn’t you tell me?”
He gave me a flat look.
“Did you give me a chance?”
“...Fair.”
Still, this place was a complete mess too.
People with plenty to lose didn’t like the world changing. The handful of Hunters with Mana Cultivation Methods of their own were no exception.
At this point, calling them power brokers would be more accurate than calling them Hunters.

Some of them might have enough influence to bend an entire country to their will. With their wealth, fame, and overwhelming strength, they could turn common sense on its head. They didn’t want change, and they certainly didn’t want anyone new rising to their level.
Anyone like me or Team Leader Choi.
Even so, these bastards might be worse than Murim sects.

Leak a sect’s unique martial arts in Murim, and they’d hunt you down with murder in their eyes and smash your skull. But at least they wouldn’t throw a fit over a merchant selling the Three Calamities Sword Technique at a market.
These guys already had more than enough, and they were ready to raise hell because we wanted to share one little Mana Cultivation Method?
Huh. Now I’m pissed.
“If we release it, they’ll go nuts, right?”
“Yes. And we’ll have a mess on our hands.”
“What if I go after them?”
“What?”
“Now that I think about it, this is fucking ridiculous. We release the method without overthinking it, then I go after whichever assholes start trouble. That ought to shut them—”
“No! Don’t! Absolutely not!”
For Team Leader Choi’s normally low, composed voice to reach that volume, he might as well have said, Over my dead body, you lunatic.
This time, though, I couldn’t just give in.
“I know what you’re saying, Team Leader Choi, but we have to make it public. I didn’t create it to keep it to myself like a diary.”
Magical power had already increased throughout the world. No—it was still increasing, even now. Mutated Gates were appearing one after another, and Monster Waves had begun.
“Monsters are growing stronger as magical power increases. You know that too, Team Leader. But if people learn about this Mana Cultivation Method under the current circumstances...”
“Hunters’ abilities will improve across the board. It’s stable enough for even the lowest-ranked Hunters to learn without difficulty.”
Team Leader Choi’s expression hardened.

“I understand what you’re thinking, Mr. Jin. Wasn’t that why you suppressed the various rebel groups and terrorists in the first place—to reduce the possibility of the Mana Cultivation Method being misused as much as possible?”
“Yes. Before I worried about how sharp the weapon I’d made was, I had to think about whose hands it might end up in.”
About two weeks ago in modern-world time, an incident in Texas had driven that point home: an attempted terrorist attack using a Magic Gem.
Fortunately, the terrorist’s attempt had ended in failure, and there had been no casualties. But that incident had made me realize something for certain.
“When I said I wanted to share it with everyone, that included every kind of criminal and lunatic.”

Afterward, I followed Magic Johnson to the Pentagon and obtained information about them with the tacit approval of the President of the United States. Alongside the people who had come with me, I dyed the desert red with blood and cut away every element that might become a threat.
Rebel groups that trained kidnapped children to shoot. Fanatical terrorists willing to carry out suicide attacks...
I killed anyone who stood in the way, and the dead were bound to the Skeleton King’s undead army, which chased after those who fled.
For the ones farther away, we used captured leaders to send false orders: rebel groups were told to attack terrorist organizations, and terrorist organizations were told to attack rebel groups.
It was a war between bastards and motherfuckers. Tricked into launching all-out attacks on one another, both sides suffered massive losses.

“As you know, we couldn’t wipe them out completely, and we won’t be able to in the future. But we’ve achieved what we needed to for now. Even if those bastards learn this method, they won’t be as dangerous as they were before.”
They wouldn’t be the only ones growing stronger from it. Hunters everywhere would improve enough to fight monsters strengthened by the rise in magical power. That should help keep the balance.
And if things get much worse...
Then I’d release the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique, too. So far, I’d taught it to only a handful of people, including Team Leader Choi.

The low-ranking Hunters who knew absolutely nothing about Mana Cultivation Methods would not be able to apply the Jin Family’s Cultivation Technique even if I handed it to them right now. But once they had learned the method, they would be able to cultivate it on their own.
I met Team Leader Choi’s eyes.
“We have to make it public. One way or another.”
“Luckily, it isn’t too late. The public still thinks pretty highly of both of us.”
“Pretty highly” was an understatement. People were going wild over us.

I was being hailed as a young hero of a new age. After Butler Kim’s death, Team Leader Choi had become Guild Master of the Peace Guild—and before the paint on his new nameplate had dried, he’d taken over the Ares Guild too.

Then there was the glow of his family name. His maternal grandfather was Cheon Taemin, the savior who had saved humanity from the Demon King Asmodeus. Team Leader Choi was his only blood relative and heir.
I grabbed his hand.
“Team Leader Choi.”
I gripped it tight. When he met my fervent gaze, he flinched as though he’d been burned.
“W-Why are you doing this all of a sudden?”
He looked as though he’d run into Magic Johnson in a dark alley at night. I held on and pressed ahead.
“If you’re that worried, let’s try another way. Hm?”
“What way...?”
“Put your maternal grandfather’s name to work for us just this once.”
“What?”
“Come on. Let’s cash in on the savior’s name.”

Team Leader Choi was his only blood relative and heir.
I grabbed his hand.
“Team Leader Choi.”
I gripped it tight.
When he met my fervent gaze, he flinched as though he’d been burned.
“W-Why are you doing this all of a sudden?”
He looked as though he’d run into Magic Johnson in a dark alley at night.
I held on and pressed ahead.
“If you’re that worried, let’s try another way.
Hm?”
“What way...?”
“Put your maternal grandfather’s name to work for us just this once.”
“What?”
“Come on.
Let’s cash in on the savior’s name.”

chapters.title: Chapter 728
paragraphs: People are all the same.
Success after success makes them more confident, and before long, they start closing the eyes and ears they once kept wide open.
But Team Leader Choi was a decent person before he was an excellent Hunter or manager. Even though the decision was his to make, he always sought everyone’s understanding.
“...So I’d like to hear what you all think.”
When Team Leader Choi finished speaking in a low voice, the people sitting on the sofa fell silent for a moment.
No, people wasn’t quite right. At some point, a monster had made himself at home among them.
And that monster looked more serious than ever.
“This body objects.”
Every gaze turned toward him at the firm refusal, delivered without a hint of hesitation.
But the Skeleton King continued without a care.
“You all know why. Expand your influence too far, and people grow wary. Human envy and jealousy invite danger. Am I wrong?”
I’d thought this before, but the bastard really had become almost human.
When I awkwardly shook my head, the Skeleton King’s voice gained even more force.
“This body would prefer to avoid any more attention, too. If other humans discover my true identity, it will cause trouble for all of you. So put an end to this foolish talk.”
He ended his speech with a stern rebuke. The rest of us looked at one another as though we’d rehearsed it.
He had a point.
He definitely had a point, but...
“If you’re so desperate to avoid attention, why’d you make an SNS account the second you got a phone?”
Team Leader Choi, Im Kkeokjeong, and Song Song nodded in turn.
“I agree with Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“Come to think of it, yeah. I don’t use that stuff, so I hadn’t realized, but he seems pretty famous.”
“More than pretty famous. He hasn’t even had the account long, and he’s already got over a hundred thousand followers.”
The Skeleton King, who had faltered after being struck in the heart of the matter, thrust out his chest at Song Song’s words.
“As of today, a hundred and twenty thousand.”
“Really?”
“Of course. Advertising offers are pouring in from all sides.”
I watched him preen and let out a dry laugh.
“Look at this fucking bastard. Want me to split you into a hundred and twenty thousand bone fragments?”
“Delete the account. Now. That’s your last warning.”
After hesitating for a moment at my threat, the Skeleton King answered in a depressed voice.
“...Understood.”
“At least you’re obedient. But you didn’t post any strange nonsense on SNS, did you?”
The internet’s reach was staggering. In Murim, people sent messenger pigeons. Here, a few taps of a finger could send something around the world.
If that bastard posted some shit, we’re in trouble.
Song Song broke in, sounding unconcerned.
“Fortunately, there’s nothing much. I looked through everything just in case, and he’s only posted a ton of pictures of his own face.”
“Really?”
“Yeah. Most of his followers are overseas, too. And the overwhelming majority are men.”
“That’s a relief, but why would so many men... Ah.”
It hit me.
I remembered whose hands had created the Skeleton King’s handsome face.
Magic Johnson.
The Grand Mage of the century. And the century’s gayest man.

Magic Johnson—the man said to work unbelievable magic with two staffs—had put plenty of his own taste into the Skeleton King’s current appearance. The guy was handsome by any standard, but his face and build were perfectly suited to the tastes of a certain crowd.
A crowd of a hundred and twenty thousand.
That was enough people to kick the asses of a hundred thousand followers of the Demonic Path if they came swarming back. Whether they’d stop at kicking was another question.
This guy’s kind of impressive.
He’d gathered that many followers in no time without a name anyone knew or a face anyone recognized. Even the Murim Alliance Leader couldn’t pull that off.
Oblivious to my newfound regard, the Skeleton King fiddled with his phone and spoke with a stricken look.
“I cannot bring myself to delete it. You are the most wicked, cruel human in the world.”
“What crime did I commit in my previous life to deserve being called cruel by a monster bastard?”
“Ah, to part so suddenly. Somewhere, an unknown woman who can no longer gaze upon this body’s dazzling face will weep without end.”
“Why are you looking at me like that?”
“Nothing. You’re better off not knowing.”
Some truths were better left hidden.
I exchanged a glance with Song Song. With our silent agreement settled, I looked around.
“Anyway. Everyone’s on board?”
Im Kkeokjeong nodded as if the answer were obvious.
“Well, if you and Team Leader Choi have decided, I’m with you.”
“Song-i, what about you?”
“Hmm.”
Song Song crossed her legs at an angle and continued.
“From what I’ve heard, we’re doing this for everyone. If I say no, I’ll be the only bitch here, won’t I?”
“No.”
“Really?”
“Yeah. You weren’t all that nice to begin with.”
“Oh, listen to this bastard.”
Song Song smiled sweetly and raised her middle finger before suddenly sighing.
“What a ride. When Team Leader Choi offered me a transfer and I left the Ares Guild, I never imagined we’d end up here.”
“You should’ve just stayed there.”
“Hey, I couldn’t. That Branch Leader was too much of a pervert. I figured I’d be better off working for someone young, handsome, and rich. But I got a bad feeling on the very first day.”
“The first day?”

“Yeah. I’d come to get away from one pervert, and there was some other weird bastard waiting for me. I was starving, and he burned all the meat. Then, out of nowhere, he told me his star sign was Taurus. What kind of lunatic does that?”
“Ah-ha.”
I gave a quiet laugh and looked at her without another word.
Truthfully, I felt bad for Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong. Ever since the Peace Guild was founded, they’d been dragged through one crisis after another. None of it was what they’d signed up for.
“Hmm.”
“What’s that look for?”
“Nothing. I just wanted to tell you that it isn’t too late yet.”
“What?”
“This could be a lot more dangerous than you or Uncle Kkeokjeong realize.”
There was no laughter in my voice this time. Song Song’s gaze turned serious.
“How dangerous are we talking?”
“We’re past the point where this is just a domestic matter.”
“You seem to have a tendency to underestimate yourself. You and Team Leader Choi left Korea behind a long time ago.”
She wasn’t exaggerating.

Ever since I took down the Arch Lich in China, my name had become known throughout the world. Meanwhile, Team Leader Choi had appeared in the media as the new City Lord of the Ares Guild and the successor to the living Savior.
But this was different. If anything, everything we’d achieved was what had created the problem.
I shrugged.
“Someone once said that the bigger you get, the more there is to take a bite out of.”
“So how much are you planning to let them take?”
“I’m not. And I don’t intend to start.”
Song Song stared at me for a moment before suddenly speaking.
“You know something?”
“What?”
“It’s way too late for us to back out. Both Uncle Kkeokjeong and me.”
Im Kkeokjeong quietly added to her words.
“I wasn’t planning to back out anyway.”
“Uncle.”
“Whether it’s too late or not doesn’t matter. Once you start something, you have to see it through to the end. At least for the sake of the one who left us first.”
“Right, Team Leader Choi?”
At Im Kkeokjeong’s quiet question, everyone’s gazes turned in one direction.
Team Leader Choi had gone quiet at some point. He was looking at the empty place someone had left behind. Until recently, it had still held that person’s warmth. Now nothing could fill it.
He spoke.
“I visited the grave today. Someone had carved words beside the gravestone. ‘Thank you for coming. I love you. Please come again.’”
No one said anything. Team Leader Choi continued calmly.
“So next time, I’d like all of us to go visit that person together. Next year, the year after that...and even decades from now.”
It was the resolve of a man who had been forced to send someone precious on ahead.
The words all of us together carried his determination not to let the same thing happen again.
Decades from now.
Yeah. That was enough.
I didn’t know what we’d look like then. For now, knowing we’d go forward together was enough.
“Team Leader Choi.”
At my quiet call, he gave a heavy nod.
“Understood. Let’s begin.”
We’d already discussed the broad strokes. Team Leader Choi took out his phone and called the first person.
Beep. Beep. Click.
The call connected before it could ring a third time. A deep voice, practiced by a hectic life in politics, came from the other end.
“Speaking. Baek Hanseong here.”
There were plenty of people named Baek Hanseong in Korea. But only one Team Leader Choi would call first in a situation like this.
“Yes, Mr. President. I’m calling about something important.”
“Ha-ha. Well, putting it that way already makes me feel a little strange. I’m looking forward to it, but at the same time, I’m starting to feel uneasy.”
At the appearance of a major figure who moved an entire country, Im Kkeokjeong and Song Song fell silent. The Skeleton King’s eyes widened as he whispered to me.
“President Baek Hanseong? Is he—”
“That’s right. Our country’s pres—”
“I know. Isn’t he the popular celebrity with more than ten million followers?”
“Damn it. A human has a hundred times this body’s following.”
As I watched the Skeleton King vent his frustration, I thought:
Please just fucking die already...
Come to think of it, he already had.
The corridor was dazzlingly bright. An A-rank Magic Gem filled with immense energy supplied power throughout the building, and every floor was crowded with people busy at work.
Until darkness fell without warning.
Crackle. Whoooosh.
The lights faded. Every machine stopped.
Confused shouts erupted from all around, shattering the momentary silence.
“What the hell?”
“Uh, looks like a power outage.”

“You call that an answer? Fuck... I told them to replace the Magic Gem before this happened. They’ve had a straw stuck in it for over twenty years, sucking it dry. It’s probably begging us to put it out of its misery.”
“Right? Though the experts said an A-rank Magic Gem would last at least thirty years.”
“So what, does it matter why the Magic Gem ran out ten years early? Are you so curious you’re about to go insane?”
“N-No, sir.”

“Enough. Everyone, focus! The Security Team and Technical Team will be here within two minutes, so don’t move a finger—stay exactly where you are! Anyone with spare mana lanterns, go get them right now.”
But despite the department head’s shout, the entire building lit up again before even a minute had passed. The power had returned.
“Damn it. Running around for nothing...”
The department head grumbled before waving away the Security Team, who had arrived a step too late.
“As you can see, everything’s fine. Any idea why the power went out?”
“I asked our team leader, too, and apparently it happens once every few years, although it’s rare. The Technical Team will have to investigate to find the exact cause.”
“Right. That’s their job.”
The Security Team Hunter gave an awkward smile and went through the checks. Had anything gone missing during the blackout? Was anyone hurt? Had anyone noticed anything suspicious?
But it was little more than a simple procedure, and there were mountains of work waiting to be handled. No one had the time or energy to devote to a blackout that had lasted barely a minute.
“Sorry, but could you come back if you have any more questions? We’re a little busy right now.”
The Security Team employee nodded at the department head’s words.
“Of course. You do look a lot busier than usual. Something going on?”
“A notice came down from above. Apparently, something big is going to happen sometime today.”
“Something big?”
“Yeah. We don’t know the details, but it looks like it came from the Blue House. Everyone’s on edge. At this rate, we can forget leaving on time.”
“Sorry. I’ve taken up your time.”
“Don’t worry about it. We’re all working for the country. Take care. See you later.”
“You too.”
But as they returned to their respective positions, none of them knew.
During that short span of less than a minute, some ghostlike entity had moved through every part of the building, riding the thick darkness.
And that one item had disappeared from the evidence storage room deep underground.

The hundreds of employees going about their work, the highly skilled Hunters of the Security Team, and even the alarm magic had failed to notice. The entity that had completed everything with ease leisurely slipped out of the building.
Step. Step.
Along with someone’s footsteps.
“Sehwan, did you check the third floor?”
“Yes, Team Leader. Nothing out of the ordinary. Any word from Technical?”
“It hasn’t even been ten minutes. You think they’ve found the cause already?”
“Fair point. By the way, isn’t the weather great today?”
Sssrk.
Behind the Security Team employee as he chatted with his superior, a dark shadow stirred faintly.

chapters.title: Chapter 729
paragraphs: I’d never gone fishing in my life, and I didn’t know how.
But I did know how to catch more fish.
Bait.
That was what we needed. Scatter hints about a major announcement far and wide, then draw as much attention as possible from as many fish—or rather, people—as we could.
Of course, we’d need to do a little persuading along the way.

Team Leader Choi and I weren’t trying to fill a bucket. We wanted a boat so full the catch spilled over the sides. And for that, we needed a good crew. The first person Team Leader Choi called was President Baek Hanseong.
“Pardon?”

He had gone through every kind of hardship before entering the Blue House at the age of just over forty. His eyes widened at the words Mana Cultivation Method, and when the name of one particular person followed, he spilled his coffee.
“I-Is that true? Did he really...?”
“Yes. My maternal grandfather created it himself. He wanted to share this Mana Cultivation Method with everyone.”
“I-I can’t believe it.”
Who was Cheon Taemin?
A living savior. A hero who had accomplished something no one else in human history ever had.
He was the Slayer who had defeated the Demon King Asmodeus and brought the Great Cataclysm to an end. Everyone respected his name.
“But why is the Mana Cultivation Method called Smiling...?”
“...I took out the wrong one. Please forget what you just saw.”
Honestly, if people knew I’d created it, I wouldn’t care whether it was called The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method or As-Salamu Alaykum.
But with Cheon Taemin’s name attached, Team Leader Choi and I agreed that The Smiling Mana Cultivation Method was a problem.
“This is the Mana Cultivation Method my maternal grandfather created.”
Team Leader Choi placed a neatly bound booklet on the table. A new name was printed on the cover.
“Heaven and Earth Cultivation Technique...”

“The Heaven and Earth Cultivation Technique is versatile enough for even the lowest-ranking Hunter to learn, and exceptionally safe. It won’t produce tremendous results the moment someone learns it, but it will undoubtedly be a great help to Hunters.”
Of course it would. That was what I’d made it for.
The name had changed for grown-up reasons, but I’d come up with the new one too. Feeling a little proud, I added, “In short, it’s a fucking incredible Mana Cultivation Method.”
Team Leader Choi gave me a pointed cough, but President Baek Hanseong didn’t pay any attention. He didn’t seem to have any attention to spare.
He stared as though possessed at the booklet containing the principles of the Heaven and Earth Cultivation Technique. Only after a long while did he finally come to his senses.
“But why bring something this important to me...?”
“We need an ally.”
President Baek hadn’t bought the presidential chair secondhand on Oi Market. He understood at once why Team Leader Choi and I had come.
“You want a breakwater.”
“We hope we can support each other.”
“But no matter how large a Guild steps forward, it will be difficult as long as he is still here.”
A sound assessment.
If it were true.
Unfortunately, it isn’t.

We needed to avoid outside opposition as much as possible. chapters.title: Chapter 730
paragraphs: Knock. Knock.
Every eye turned toward the door.

Even the janitors at Ares Guild knew the entire leadership was in the conference room discussing important business. For someone to knock now, there were only two possibilities: the matter was just as important, or they’d already written their resignation letter.
Go Jun would have started swearing. Their new City Lord, though, didn’t so much as twitch an eyebrow, even with the meeting finally going his way.
“Come in.”
Click.
A middle-aged man appeared in the half-open doorway. The Chief Secretary approached Choi Minwoo and bowed.
“I’m sorry to interrupt the meeting, Vice Guild Master.”
“That’s all right,” Choi said calmly. “If you have a good reason.”

The Chief Secretary swallowed. He hadn’t worked for Choi long, but he already knew his employer was quick to reward good work and punish mistakes. He also knew the report sent up from the lobby’s Security Team a minute ago was beyond his authority to handle.
“An important guest has arrived.”
He held out a trembling hand.
Choi’s expression grew grave as he looked at what the secretary had brought him.
This is...
Recognition brought a rush of thoughts, but he didn’t hesitate for long.
“Where is the guest?”
“Still in the lobby...”
“Show them to my private office. I’ll be there shortly.”
“Yes, sir.”
The Chief Secretary answered as if he’d been waiting for exactly that instruction, then left. Choi turned back to the seated executives.
“I think we’ve covered the urgent matters. What do you all think?”
“Pardon?”
“Vice Guild Master, are you saying...?”
“If you’ll excuse me, I think we should end today’s meeting here.”
Several executives stared at him in disbelief.
This was too much. However important the guest might be, how could he end a meeting attended by every overseas Branch Leader just like that?
Scrape.
“Vice Guild Master!”
One executive found the courage to leap to his feet.
Bang!
The sudden crash swallowed his voice.
Jin Taekyung lifted his hand from the alloy table, leaving a palm print in it.
“What, did they lay eggs? Why do these damn bugs keep flying around? Do we need to gut this conference room again?”
“Oh, sorry. Go on with what you were saying. Vice Guild Master, where were you?”
The lone standing executive looked at Choi, his face stiff.
“Since things have turned out this way, I’d like to say something.”
His voice carried the determination not to back down this time. Several executives’ eyes gleamed, and Choi Minwoo calmly nodded.
“Yes, go ahead.”
“Then may I leave early?”
“It’s my wedding anniversary today...”
The others gave their colleague flat looks.
He’d been divorced for three years.
The Team Leader Choi I knew was a reasonable man.
Even when he had the power to crush someone, he knew when to ease off. He preferred to settle things as calmly and amicably as possible.
Which meant he wouldn’t dismiss dozens of executives with a few words over just anything.
That made me even more curious about the guest who had shown up so suddenly.
Ding.
“It was because of them, right? This important guest?”
I asked as soon as the private elevator doors closed.
“Half and half. I called the executives together to reassure them. There was never any room for trouble to begin with.”
“True. Most of the ones still around are on your side.”
“Even if someone had complaints, there was no reason for the Guild to oppose the publicization plan.”
“Because it also suggests that Cheon Tae... no, that your maternal grandfather is still going strong, Team Leader Choi. Right?”
“Yes. The reason Ares Guild hasn’t enjoyed its former standing is my maternal grandfather’s absence. In that sense, Mr. Jin’s proposal to use his fame was the best option for all of us.”
Cheon Taemin’s very existence was practically a cheat code in this world.
His name alone could command the attention of the entire world and send the hyenas lurking in the shadows, waiting for an opening, backing away.
Just like...
Yeah. Like the Martial God.
The thought came to me and hovered on the tip of my tongue, then faded. Team Leader Choi spoke again, his voice low.
“But unlike the Ares Guild executives, someone else can’t have been pleased by the news.”
“Someone else?”
He handed me something.
“The owner of this business card.”
Ding.
The elevator doors opened. We kept talking as we crossed a corridor that had been cleared on his orders.
“A business card? This?”
I frowned at the thing in my hand.
It was the size and shape of a business card, but could you really call it one? The platinum-colored surface gleamed, yet it bore no name, no title—not even a phone number.
The only thing I could guess was that its owner was an unimaginably wealthy magnate.
“This is heavier than I expected. Feels like it might actually be platinum. Are we meeting Middle Eastern royalty?”
“If that were the case, I would have finished the meeting and come.”
“Then who?”
“Look closely at the edge.”
I examined the card again. Only then did I notice the two birds engraved into it, one on each side.
This is...
“Do you know what kind of birds they are?”
“No idea.”
“Ravens.”
“Ravens?”
“Huginn and Muninn, to be precise.”
“What, the ravens have names? Aren’t they just ravens?”
“Someone without an interest in the subject might not know. They’re creatures from mythology.”
“Mythology?”
“Ancient Norse mythology.”
Step. Step.
Our footsteps sounded unusually loud. As the office door drew nearer, Team Leader Choi continued.
“Huginn and Muninn are the two ravens associated with a god from those myths.”
“Which god?”
“Odin.”
“You’ve heard that name plenty of times, haven’t you?”
After a moment, I nodded.
Huginn and Muninn were new to me. Odin was another matter.
Oh, yeah. Another matter entirely.
Not just because he was a god everyone had heard of, or a character from the superhero movies I’d enjoyed as a kid.
Odin was a name known the world over.
Because Odin was the Guild everyone recognized as the best in the world.
Step.
We came to a stop. Beyond the door, I sensed a vast, carefully contained qi.
Team Leader Choi’s calm voice crossed the quiet corridor.
“Let’s go.”
Click.
The door opened at last.
Someone standing before the fireplace slowly turned to face us.
At first, everyone thought it was a minor mishap.
They were busy and preoccupied with problems that needed immediate attention. And it had begun and ended in the blink of an eye.
But it was no minor mishap. The first to realize that was the youngest employee assigned to the evidence storage room.
“Um, Manager? I think we’re missing a piece of evidence.”
“What? What are you talking about?”
“I just checked the inventory, and we seem to be one item short...”
“Quit talking nonsense and check again, you idiot. Nothing’s been taken out of storage in over a week.”
The manager frowned, crossed his legs, and went back to watching his stocks.
Thirty minutes later, the youngest employee returned, scratching the back of his head.
“Manager, I really think it’s missing. One of the items connected to Go Jun is gone.”
“Hey, I told you. The storage room’s been locked for a week. My stock’s already hit its daily limit down, so stop pissing me off with this non—”
The manager broke off.
“What did you just say?”
“I told you. It really is gone,” the employee said, shrinking back.
“No, not that. What did you say right before that?”
“Huh? Oh—the items connected to Go Jun?”
At the name that once again slipped from the youngest employee’s mouth, the manager felt a chill run down his spine.
Go Jun. Of all the things to go missing, it had to be evidence from the Go Jun case.
“Hey, the door. The door! Open the storage room right now! Get the others too—no, wait. Don’t call them yet!”
He jumped up and hurried to the evidence storage room. After he and the youngest employee spent hours searching every corner, he finally had to admit it.
Fuck...
It was gone. It really was gone.
The clueless junior hadn’t been talking nonsense. And the stock he’d bought the day before yesterday hitting its daily limit down was the least of his worries.
If word got out, his whole life would hit limit down.
What the hell is this?
Half dazed, he stared around the storage room. It made no sense.
They’d last checked the inventory only a week ago. Since then, no one had entered the room, yet an item had vanished without a trace.
Neither the anti-theft Magic placed on each piece of evidence nor the alarm Magic covering the entire room had gone off.
And it had to be evidence connected to Go Jun.

The mere disappearance of evidence was already enough to require him to write an incident report, but if evidence related to Go Jun had disappeared, this would not end with ordinary disciplinary action. The higher-ups had already collected the important pieces, but it had been an enormous case.
“...Seriously, this is driving me crazy.”
The manager felt the future go dark before his eyes. A civil servant’s lifeline might be long, but it wasn’t a steel cable. It could still be cut.
He pictured his tiger-like wife and rabbit-like children waiting at home. He couldn’t bring himself to report it.
Right. Bury it. Just for now, and see what happens.
If he could talk the clueless junior around, he might find a way out later.
Decision made, he called to the youngest employee somewhere in the vast storage room, using the kindest voice he could muster.
“Are you there?”
“Ah, yes. I just got here.”
“You went somewhere. Come over here for a moment. I have something important to discuss with you...”
He turned around and saw the youngest employee, eyes shining brightly.
Behind him stood the Security Team Leader, as imposing as an iron tower.
“What’s going on?” the Security Team Leader asked. “I heard there was a problem.”
“Manager Kim?”
Fuck. I’m screwed.
The manager barely held back the curse. He opened his mouth, despair in his voice.
“It’s gone.”
“Pardon?”
“The necklace that came in among Go Jun’s personal effects. It’s gone.”

“Oh, sorry.
Go on with what you were saying.
Vice Guild Master, where were you?”
The lone standing executive looked at Choi, his face stiff.
“Since things have turned out this way, I’d like to say something.”
His voice carried the determination not to back down this time.
Several executives’ eyes gleamed, and Choi Minwoo calmly nodded.
“Yes, go ahead.”
“Then may I leave early?”
“It’s my wedding anniversary today...”
The others gave their colleague flat looks.
He’d been divorced for three years.
The Team Leader Choi I knew was a reasonable man.
Even when he had the power to crush someone, he knew when to ease off.
He preferred to settle things as calmly and amicably as possible.
Which meant he wouldn’t dismiss dozens of executives with a few words over just anything.
That made me even more curious about the guest who had shown up so suddenly.
Ding.
“It was because of them, right?
This important guest?”
I asked as soon as the private elevator doors closed.
“Half and half.
I called the executives together to reassure them.
There was never any room for trouble to begin with.”
“True.
Most of the ones still around are on your side.”
“Even if someone had complaints, there was no reason for the Guild to oppose the publicization plan.”
“Because it also suggests that Cheon Tae... no, that your maternal grandfather is still going strong, Team Leader Choi.
Right?”
“Yes.
The reason Ares Guild hasn’t enjoyed its former standing is my maternal grandfather’s absence.
In that sense, Mr.
Jin’s proposal to use his fame was the best option for all of us.”
Cheon Taemin’s very existence was practically a cheat code in this world.
His name alone could command the attention of the entire world and send the hyenas lurking in the shadows, waiting for an opening, backing away.
Just like...
Yeah.
Like the Martial God.
The thought came to me and hovered on the tip of my tongue, then faded.
Team Leader Choi spoke again, his voice low.
“But unlike the Ares Guild executives, someone else can’t have been pleased by the news.”
“Someone else?”
He handed me something.
“The owner of this business card.”
Ding.
The elevator doors opened.
We kept talking as we crossed a corridor that had been cleared on his orders.
“A business card?
This?”
I frowned at the thing in my hand.
It was the size and shape of a business card, but could you really call it one?
The platinum-colored surface gleamed, yet it bore no name, no title—not even a phone number.
The only thing I could guess was that its owner was an unimaginably wealthy magnate.
“This is heavier than I expected.
Feels like it might actually be platinum.
Are we meeting Middle Eastern royalty?”
“If that were the case, I would have finished the meeting and come.”
“Then who?”
“Look closely at the edge.”
I examined the card again.
Only then did I notice the two birds engraved into it, one on each side.
This is...
“Do you know what kind of birds they are?”
“No idea.”
“Ravens.”
“Ravens?”
“Huginn and Muninn, to be precise.”
“What, the ravens have names?
Aren’t they just ravens?”
“Someone without an interest in the subject might not know.
They’re creatures from mythology.”
“Mythology?”
“Ancient Norse mythology.”
Step.
Step.
Our footsteps sounded unusually loud.
As the office door drew nearer, Team Leader Choi continued.
“Huginn and Muninn are the two ravens associated with a god from those myths.”
“Which god?”
“Odin.”
“You’ve heard that name plenty of times, haven’t you?”
After a moment, I nodded.
Huginn and Muninn were new to me.
Odin was another matter.
Oh, yeah.
Another matter entirely.
Not just because he was a god everyone had heard of, or a character from the superhero movies I’d enjoyed as a kid.
Odin was a name known the world over.
Because Odin was the Guild everyone recognized as the best in the world.
Step.
We came to a stop.
Beyond the door, I sensed a vast, carefully contained qi.
Team Leader Choi’s calm voice crossed the quiet corridor.
“Let’s go.”
Click.
The door opened at last.
Someone standing before the fireplace slowly turned to face us.
At first, everyone thought it was a minor mishap.
They were busy and preoccupied with problems that needed immediate attention.
And it had begun and ended in the blink of an eye.
But it was no minor mishap.
The first to realize that was the youngest employee assigned to the evidence storage room.
“Um, Manager?
I think we’re missing a piece of evidence.”
“What?
What are you talking about?”
“I just checked the inventory, and we seem to be one item short...”
“Quit talking nonsense and check again, you idiot.
Nothing’s been taken out of storage in over a week.”
The manager frowned, crossed his legs, and went back to watching his stocks.
Thirty minutes later, the youngest employee returned, scratching the back of his head.
“Manager, I really think it’s missing.
One of the items connected to Go Jun is gone.”
“Hey, I told you.
The storage room’s been locked for a week.
My stock’s already hit its daily limit down, so stop pissing me off with this non—”
The manager broke off.
“What did you just say?”
“I told you.
It really is gone,” the employee said, shrinking back.
“No, not that.
What did you say right before that?”
“Huh?
Oh—the items connected to Go Jun?”
At the name that once again slipped from the youngest employee’s mouth, the manager felt a chill run down his spine.
Go Jun.
Of all the things to go missing, it had to be evidence from the Go Jun case.
“Hey, the door.
The door!
Open the storage room right now!
Get the others too—no, wait.
Don’t call them yet!”
He jumped up and hurried to the evidence storage room.
After he and the youngest employee spent hours searching every corner, he finally had to admit it.
Fuck...
It was gone.
It really was gone.
The clueless junior hadn’t been talking nonsense.
And the stock he’d bought the day before yesterday hitting its daily limit down was the least of his worries.
If word got out, his whole life would hit limit down.
What the hell is this?
Half dazed, he stared around the storage room.
It made no sense.
They’d last checked the inventory only a week ago.
Since then, no one had entered the room, yet an item had vanished without a trace.
Neither the anti-theft Magic placed on each piece of evidence nor the alarm Magic covering the entire room had gone off.
And it had to be evidence connected to Go Jun.

The mere disappearance of evidence was already enough to require him to write an incident report, but if evidence related to Go Jun had disappeared, this would not end with ordinary disciplinary action.
The higher-ups had already collected the important pieces, but it had been an enormous case.
“...Seriously, this is driving me crazy.”
The manager felt the future go dark before his eyes.
A civil servant’s lifeline might be long, but it wasn’t a steel cable.
It could still be cut.
He pictured his tiger-like wife and rabbit-like children waiting at home.
He couldn’t bring himself to report it.
Right.
Bury it.
Just for now, and see what happens.
If he could talk the clueless junior around, he might find a way out later.
Decision made, he called to the youngest employee somewhere in the vast storage room, using the kindest voice he could muster.
“Are you there?”
“Ah, yes.
I just got here.”
“You went somewhere.
Come over here for a moment.
I have something important to discuss with you...”
He turned around and saw the youngest employee, eyes shining brightly.
Behind him stood the Security Team Leader, as imposing as an iron tower.
“What’s going on?” the Security Team Leader asked.
“I heard there was a problem.”
“Manager Kim?”
Fuck.
I’m screwed.
The manager barely held back the curse.
He opened his mouth, despair in his voice.
“It’s gone.”
“Pardon?”
“The necklace that came in among Go Jun’s personal effects.
It’s gone.”
