paragraphs: Step.
A glossy dress shoe pressed into the carpet.
The man had finally turned to face us, and one thought came to mind.
He looks like a crow.

Dressed in black from head to toe, he looked like a European gentleman who had wandered in from the nineteenth century. His suit didn’t have a wrinkle in it, his coat collar stood high, and he wore a silk hat that had gone out of fashion a hundred years ago.
He was unmistakably Black, but his eyes, visible through a clear monocle, were a mysterious gold.
He studied us for a moment, then touched the brim of his hat in greeting.
“Pleased to meet you both.”
His Korean came through smoothly, courtesy of translation Magic.
He was an uninvited guest who had appeared without an appointment, but we couldn’t openly snub a messenger from Odin Guild. Besides, anyone carrying this much mana...
He’s no ordinary messenger.
I gave the stranger a small nod, and Team Leader Choi offered him a seat.
“Please, sit down.”
The three of us sat facing one another across a solid wood table. An odd silence settled over us before our guest broke it.
“I should introduce myself. I am Huginn of Odin Guild.”
“The crow?”
I hadn’t meant to say it aloud. Huginn gave a faint smile.
“Ah. I do have a real name, of course, but I have been called Huginn since I entered the Guild Master’s service. You may call me that as well.”
Once a Hunter made a name for himself, people often used an epithet based on his abilities more than his actual name. But no matter how hard I searched my memory, I couldn’t place Huginn.
One of Odin’s Guild Master’s hidden right-hand men, maybe?
Even Korea’s major Guilds kept plenty of secrets. I worked on the front lines; I could hardly expect to know the inner workings of a foreign Guild.
Especially Odin Guild.
There had been a time when Ares Guild was considered the best in the world. But a little over twenty years ago, Cheon Taemin vanished from the public eye without a trace.
People wondered what had happened. Lee Jungryong became Ares Guild’s new captain, but no amount of skill could fill the void Cheon Taemin had left.
One year passed. Then five. Then ten.
Countless devoted followers of Cheon Taemin still called Ares Guild the best. Those who knew the reality—Hunters in particular—saw things differently.
To put it bluntly, Ares Guild had been a setting sun for the past ten years.
Odin Guild, meanwhile, was the rising sun.

Based in Europe, they had rapidly expanded their influence while Ares Guild was faltering. Along the way, they acquired and merged with several major Guilds, rising into a giant that no one could deny.
A giant powerful enough to send a mere messenger to Ares Guild’s new master.
“I’ve come today to convey the Guild Master’s congratulations.”
At Huginn’s words, Team Leader Choi calmly opened his mouth.
“Is that so?”
“Yes. He is delighted to see a capable young man with all the right qualifications take charge of Ares Guild.”
It sounded like praise. It wasn’t.
I ran my tongue over my lips.
Well, look at these bastards...
Some things showed through no matter how much wrapping you piled on. Huginn’s courteous tone and manner couldn’t hide what lay beneath them.
Looking down on us from the start.
I felt as if we were receiving an envoy from an overlord state. Team Leader Choi wasn’t too stupid to notice, or rash enough to show his displeasure openly.
“That is rather high praise while my maternal grandfather is still with us, but I’m grateful nonetheless. Grateful enough to want to thank him in person.”
Huginn kept smiling despite the barb.
“Ah, he was very sorry he could not come himself.”
“The Guild Master must be busy. I’d heard he had withdrawn from public life several years ago... but it seems you can’t trust rumors.”
The higher someone rose, the harder it became to get them out of their seat. That was an eternal truth. Cheon Taemin, who had reportedly vanished altogether, was simply an extreme case.
Most major Guild Masters limited their contact with the outside world. Odin’s Guild Master was no different.
“Even so, he is someone I have always respected, so I would like to visit him and pay my respects. What do you think?”
“Haha. Well...”
Huginn laughed aloud and laced his fingers together.
“I’m sorry, but he has been so busy lately that I doubt it would be possible.”
“It sounds as though something has happened.”
“Yes. A minor matter, though quite troublesome in its way. He seems to be giving a great deal of thought to how he should handle it. The others are, too.”
“The others?”
“Acquaintances he has known for many years. The person he is meeting today is from Kronos... Ah, my apologies. I shouldn’t have said that.”
The name of another major Guild—one of the world’s Ten Great Guilds alongside Ares—had slipped out.
Team Leader Choi spoke quietly. “Kronos Guild.”
“I would appreciate it if you could forget you heard that. I make mistakes like this from time to time, and the Guild Master calls me in for a reprimand.”
The troubled look on Huginn’s face made me let out a short laugh.
“What mistake?”
“Pardon?”
“Mr. Crow, drop the half-assed acting. Let’s talk honestly.”
Hmm. Maybe I should have just kept watching.
But listening to him felt like choking down a hundred sweet potatoes without a drop of dongchimi broth to wash them down. I couldn’t take it anymore.
I leaned back into the plush sofa.

“To put it bluntly, you came because of the Mana Cultivation Method that’s about to be released, right? Stop at a reasonable point. If you go any further, this won’t be fun. We can join hands with another major Guild like Kronos and bury you, so don’t get cocky. That’s what you wanted to say, isn’t it?”
“Fuck’s sake. We all know what this is about, so why give ourselves headaches talking in circles? We’re not recording you. Say what you came to say and go. Right?”
Huginn listened to the whole torrent without a word, then turned to Team Leader Choi.
“I hesitated to mention this for fear of being discourteous, but must Mr. Jin be present?”
“Of course.”
Team Leader Choi’s reply was calm.
“Mr. Jin is that important. And if you wanted to speak with me alone, you should have said so at the outset.”
“Then may I ask to speak with you alone now?”
“I refuse.”
There wasn’t a moment’s hesitation in Team Leader Choi’s answer. Huginn blinked his golden eyes.
“Well... this is awkward.”
“We feel the same. Had you made an appointment, we could have arranged any number of things beforehand.”
“Hm.”
Huginn adjusted his monocle.
“Since I was the first to be rude, I owe you both a formal apology.”
Would you look at him.
I’d thought the crow getup was just a gimmick, but apparently he hadn’t dressed like a gentleman for nothing. Since Huginn was being so courteous, I answered like a gentleman myself.
“You were rude first, so I’m not apologizing.”
“I already understand how you feel, so don’t stare at me like that. As I said earlier, let’s just have an honest conversation. Okay?”
Huginn sighed and nodded.
“Very well. Since you insist, I shall be direct.”
“Keep it short. Get to the point.”
Huginn’s monocle flashed beneath the office’s lighting Magic. The brief silence ended as he looked from me to Team Leader Choi and spoke.
“Stop the release of the Mana Cultivation Method. If you refuse, there will be consequences.”
It was a single sentence that fulfilled my request to get straight to the point one hundred percent—and made us feel even worse than I had expected.
“Well, I figured that was coming, but... fuck, it’s unpleasant to hear. Don’t you think?”
Team Leader Choi shrugged.
“Isn’t it better than listening to him talk in circles again?”
“That’s true. If he’d done that one more time, I really would’ve...”
“You must control yourself.”
“I was going to, even without you telling me. I don’t want to make this a bigger problem. Though I probably would’ve told him to take off the monocle first.”
Team Leader Choi let out a short laugh. Huginn’s eyes narrowed.
“You are every bit as rude as I was told.”
“You’re being pretty damn unpleasant too. I’d never heard of you, much less seen you.”
“Do you intend to make a show of force here?”
“If I have to. Once you take off that monocle.”
“Listen, Mr. Jin.”
“Yes, hello? Go ahead.”
“Do not lose your temper. This is merely a proposal.”
“Your mouth may be crooked, but you should still speak straight. To my ears, that sounds like a threat, not a proposal.”
“If you choose to hear it as a threat, it may well become one. But your opinion is not what matters to me.”
Huginn answered firmly, then turned toward Team Leader Choi.
“What will you do, Mr. Choi?”
His golden eyes gleamed coldly. A voice filled with force slipped between Huginn’s lips.
“Make the choice yourself.”
Huginn was certain.
He can’t refuse this.
It was an ultimatum in all but name. Anyone with the slightest sense would back down.
Jin Taekyung was unpredictable to the point of being half-mad. But the young Asian man before Huginn, Choi Minwoo, would make a different choice.
Besides...
The Slayer won’t intervene. Master said so. That makes it a fact.
The assurance had come from the one man to whom Huginn gave his absolute loyalty. His Master had never been wrong. Choi Minwoo’s answer was as good as decided.
Perhaps that was why his response, when it came, sounded only natural.
“Since things have come to this, I suppose I have no choice. All right.”
“As expected. You are a wise man, Mr. Choi.”
Huginn felt his composure returning after his exchange with Jin Taekyung. He recovered his smile.
“Then I may take it that tomorrow evening’s release of the Mana Cultivation Method has been canceled entirely?”
“Of course. I’ve changed my mind.”
“Excellent. He will be pleased to hear it.”
Huginn rose and added, “As will the others.”
“I hope so,” Choi Minwoo said.
“They are reasonable people. From now on, we should be able to establish a good relationship in a more amicable atmosphere.”
With that pointed remark, Huginn looked at Jin Taekyung.
Only moments ago, Jin had been spouting vulgarities to his face. Now he was practically lying back on the sofa, fiddling with his smartphone.
Rude to the very end.
But satisfaction outweighed Huginn’s annoyance. He had won.
Before leaving, he adjusted his silk hat like the cultured gentleman he was and offered Jin his hand.
“Mr. Jin, I was discourteous today, though I did not intend to be. I hope we can meet with smiles next time.”
Only a winner had the privilege of mocking the loser with kind words. When Jin refused his hand and gave a curt reply instead, Huginn felt better still.
“You’re in a hurry. It hasn’t even finished uploading.”
“I have an urgent matter to attend to. Good day.”
His business here was done. Huginn gave Choi Minwoo a polite nod, turned, and headed for the door.
Step. Step.
His light footsteps crossed the carpet. But Huginn was forced to stop in front of the door.
He couldn’t ignore what Jin had just said.
“Did you say...?”
Huginn turned back, his words trailing off. He stared at Jin as if he couldn’t believe it.
Jin blinked.
“Hm? Oh, uploading?”
“Uploading...?”
“Yeah. It’s nothing important. You should get going—you look busy.”
Uploading. Uploading. Uploading.
The word throbbed in Huginn’s ears in time with his heartbeat.
“What. Exactly. Did you. Upload?”
And the answer to his clipped question came not from Jin Taekyung, but from Choi Minwoo.
“Didn’t I tell you? I changed my mind.”
“Surely not.”
“The Mana Cultivation Method. We’ve decided to release it today.”

From now on, we should be able to establish a good relationship in a more amicable atmosphere.”
With that pointed remark, Huginn looked at Jin Taekyung.
Only moments ago, Jin had been spouting vulgarities to his face.
Now he was practically lying back on the sofa, fiddling with his smartphone.
Rude to the very end.
But satisfaction outweighed Huginn’s annoyance.
He had won.
Before leaving, he adjusted his silk hat like the cultured gentleman he was and offered Jin his hand.
“Mr.
Jin, I was discourteous today, though I did not intend to be.
I hope we can meet with smiles next time.”
Only a winner had the privilege of mocking the loser with kind words.
When Jin refused his hand and gave a curt reply instead, Huginn felt better still.
“You’re in a hurry.
It hasn’t even finished uploading.”
“I have an urgent matter to attend to.
Good day.”
His business here was done.
Huginn gave Choi Minwoo a polite nod, turned, and headed for the door.
Step.
Step.
His light footsteps crossed the carpet.
But Huginn was forced to stop in front of the door.
He couldn’t ignore what Jin had just said.
“Did you say...?”
Huginn turned back, his words trailing off.
He stared at Jin as if he couldn’t believe it.
Jin blinked.
“Hm?
Oh, uploading?”
“Uploading...?”
“Yeah.
It’s nothing important.
You should get going—you look busy.”
Uploading.
Uploading.
Uploading.
The word throbbed in Huginn’s ears in time with his heartbeat.
“What.
Exactly.
Did you.
Upload?”
And the answer to his clipped question came not from Jin Taekyung, but from Choi Minwoo.
“Didn’t I tell you?
I changed my mind.”
“Surely not.”
“The Mana Cultivation Method.
We’ve decided to release it today.”

chapters.title: Chapter 732
paragraphs: Civilization sure is convenient.
You can store enormous amounts of data on a smartphone smaller than your palm, then share whatever you want with everyone else by moving a finger a few times.
Granted, all that technology had restricted what I could do until now. This time, though, it worked in my favor.
Mr. Jin Taekyung. Do you have the file with you?
Remembering the Sound Transmission Team Leader Choi had sent me just a few minutes ago, I let out a quiet laugh.
I waved my smartphone at Huginn, who stood frozen like a statue.
“See this?”
The screen’s light flickered in Huginn’s golden eyes.
At Team Leader Choi’s request, I had uploaded the file to a personal social media account I’d created months ago and never used. The words Post published were displayed on the screen.
“Guess that’s what you get in the Vice Guild Master’s office. Even the Wi-Fi’s on another level. The file’s pretty big, too, though it might not look like much.”
“...Mr. Jin.”
His voice sounded ready to boil over. I blinked my deer-like eyes at him.
“Hm? What?”
“What, exactly, have you done?”
“A good deed.”
Huginn’s skin flushed dark red. He took a deep breath before speaking again, his voice controlled.
“Delete it now. It is not too late.”
I put on a serious face.
“Should I? Honestly, I’m a little scared too.”
“A poor decision can still be corrected.”
“Easier said than done. You know how scary the world is these days. It’s probably spreading everywhere already.”
Buzz. Buzz. Bzzzz.
Before I’d finished speaking, my phone began vibrating nonstop.
Huginn realized the vibrations were notifications that people were sharing the post, and anxiety settled over his face.
“It has only been a few dozen seconds. We can still contain this.”
“Oh? Really?”
“You have my word.”

“But people are going to curse me out. They’ll say I baited everyone and then deleted the post and ran. I already scattered so much bait everywhere that this won’t end with just a moderate amount of abuse.”
“For now, you could announce that the Mana Cultivation Method needs further improvement... No. Rather than waste time discussing it, why not delete the post immediately?”
At Huginn’s urging, I let out a soft sigh.
“I’d like to, but there’s one thing I can’t stop thinking about.”
“Tell me. I will take care of it.”
“What should I have for dinner tonight?”
“Dinner. What could I eat that would make people say I’d had a great meal? What do you think, Team Leader Choi?”
Beside the motionless Huginn, Team Leader Choi answered thoughtfully.
“Kimchi stew.”
“Kimchi stew?”
“Yes. Kimchi stew boiled with plenty of pork. And white rice.”
“Oh, you know your food.”
The moment I exclaimed in admiration—
Crack.
Bones shifted inside someone’s tightly clenched fist. Huginn trembled for several seconds, then spoke in a low voice.
“So you insist... on making a foolish choice.”
I shrugged.
“Why? Not a fan of Korean food?”
“I promise you, you will regret this.”
“If you feel that strongly, I guess I have no choice. We’ll have soybean paste stew instead of kimchi stew tonight. What do you think, Team Leader Choi?”
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“Either is fine with me. I’m hungry, as it happens.”
“That’s because we’ve been listening to bullshit since early evening. A dog barking once or twice can be cute, but it gets tiring when it won’t stop.”
I looked at Huginn and added, “Especially when it isn’t my dog, but a mutt raised in the neighborhood next door.”
“Don’t know who owns it, but what’s the world coming to? Who lets a dog run loose without a leash or a muzzle these days?”
Muttering as if to myself, I glanced at my phone.
Five in the afternoon.
Dinner wouldn’t be too early, but oddly enough, I wasn’t hungry today.
The reason was probably...
Buzz. Buzz. Bzzzz.
The share notifications still coming in without a break.
“Team Leader Choi, how many followers did my account have? I made it and hardly ever checked.”
“More than five hundred million, as far as I know.”
“Five hundred million? That many?”
“It’s a popular social media platform worldwide, across countries and races. Of course, nearly half your followers are Chinese.”
“Wow. I should thank the Arch Lich.”
Huginn had been listening to us. Now he spoke coldly.
“I once heard a Korean proverb. ‘After losing the cow, repair the pasture.’”
“Guess you didn’t hear it from a Korean. It’s a barn, not a pasture.”
“Pasture, stable—what does it matter? What matters is that the two of you have made the worst possible choice today.”
“We’ll see about that.”
“I assure you, before long you will lose everything. And then you will have nothing left to repair.”
At Huginn’s vicious words, I snorted quietly.
“The longer I look at you, the harder it is to tell whether you’re a crow or a bastard dog.”
“...Mr. Jin.”
“You’re a servant sent to deliver a message. You talk too much. If you’ve got more to say, bring your master here. Tell him to stop acting so important, like he really is a god.”
The moment I finished speaking, wind gusted from somewhere.
The vast mana pouring from Huginn’s body writhed. His aura was easily powerful enough for an S-rank Hunter—everything I’d expected, and more.
But the power that seemed ready to overflow in every direction stopped dead at Team Leader Choi’s quiet words.
“I cannot take responsibility for what happens next.”
“If you are prepared for that, do as you wish, Mr. Huginn.”
A brief silence passed.
The surging mana slowly subsided. The icy chill faded from Huginn’s golden eyes, and the hand that had twitched toward something inside his clothes returned to its place.
Pat. Pat.
He straightened his clothes, which had briefly fallen out of order, and spoke with a stiff expression.
“I have been discourteous. I apologize.”
I clicked my tongue at how readily he admitted it.
Too bad I wouldn’t get to smash that neat monocle. But it couldn’t be helped. The trouble we’d stirred up here today was enough for now.
No need to provoke him any further.
Odin Guild was undeniably a giant, and it cast a shadow to match.
Huginn himself was unknown to the outside world. There was no telling how many other S-rank Hunters Odin Guild had hidden away.
And the other major Guilds will probably side with Odin.
Half-crushing Huginn’s face now would cost us more than we’d gain. Team Leader Choi knew it, and so did Huginn, despite his momentary loss of composure.
“I should be going. I expect we will meet again soon.”
Still playing the gentleman, Huginn headed for the door with that pointed farewell. Team Leader Choi made sure to give him one last reply.
Or rather, one last bluff.
“I will remember Odin Guild’s intentions. So will Mr. Jin Taekyung. And so will my maternal grandfather.”
“...I understand.”
Something appeared in Huginn’s eyes as he answered—surprise, perhaps, or doubt. Then he was gone.
Click.
Team Leader Choi stared silently at the firmly closed door and muttered:
“So it begins.”
“Well, we knew they’d try to stop us. With the release announced for tomorrow, they had no reason to hold back.”
“They were more blatant than I expected. And...”
His voice trailed off. Team Leader Choi glanced briefly at the empty space Huginn had left behind before continuing.
“I doubt they sent a messenger only because of the Mana Cultivation Method.”
“You mean?”
“I had the feeling he came to confirm someone’s absence. Someone as important to them as the Mana Cultivation Method the world will see tomorrow. Perhaps more important.”
I closed my mouth and quietly repeated one person’s name.
Cheon Taemin.
The living savior. A Hunter unlike any who had come before, or would ever come again.
The whole world revered him, and his strength was said to be beyond anyone’s reach. If the enemies hiding in the shadows learned he could not step forward, they would not hesitate to attack.
“But his condition is our most closely guarded secret.”
Only six people knew that Cheon Taemin was in a vegetative state.
Team Leader Choi and me. Song Song and Im Kkeokjeong. The Skeleton King and Magic Johnson.
Everyone who had known the truth before them was already dead.
Lee Jungryong. Song Cheonwoo. And finally, Go Jun.

In the past and even now, the truth about Cheon Taemin was something that could never be revealed to the outside world. And Magic Johnson, whom we had been forced to ask for help, was someone Team Leader Choi had more than enough reason to trust.
He was the one who had moved Cheon Taemin out of the secret area and cast several protective spells over him.
Wait. Magic?
My expression stiffened as a thought struck me. Team Leader Choi nodded.
“Do you remember what Mr. Johnson said in Ares Guild’s Area A?”
“...A mage.”
“Yes. Lee Jungryong had help. Mr. Johnson said Area A had been constructed by a mage on the level of a Grand Mage.”
“Then, could it be...”
“The secret could have been leaked from the very beginning.”
“And if they already know...”
Team Leader Choi took a breath.
“This could be a difficult fight. Far more difficult than we expected.”
So why did he look so calm? Despite the gravity of his words, both his voice and his expression were composed.
“Why are you looking at me like that?” he asked.
I scratched my chin. “Maybe it’s just me, but you seem pretty relaxed for someone saying all that.”
“Pardon?”

“No, it feels like your words and actions don’t match. You’ve always been the kind of person who put safety first, but just now, you didn’t even blink before using your grandfather’s name to make a bluff.”
Team Leader Choi blinked, then gave a quiet laugh.
“Isn’t it obvious?”
“What is?”
“You’re here, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“No matter how powerful a card our enemies play, I have a Joker card named Jin Taekyung. Naturally, that makes me bolder.”
For a moment, I couldn’t think of a reply. I stood there stammering like Mute Samryong, and Team Leader Choi’s smile deepened.
“Oh, and...”
“And? What else?”
“I’m hungry. Let’s have kimchi stew tonight, as we first decided.”
Pat, pat.
Team Leader Choi tapped me on the shoulder, picked up his coat, and left the office. I stood there dazed for a moment, watching his back with an incredulous expression.
Team Leader Choi had changed. He hadn’t used to be like this.
But, well...
I don’t mind it.
I muttered inwardly and followed him.
Even now, the smartphone in my pocket continued to buzz without end.

chapters.title: Chapter 733
paragraphs: At some point, I’d become the kind of person who could go three days and nights without sleep and still be fine. Even so, getting a good night’s rest was a wonderful thing.
Especially when I woke up refreshed in a place where I was staying with my precious family.
“Home really is the best.”
I sat down at the enormous dining table, and Team Leader Choi gave me a sour look from across it.
“This is my home, technically.”
“Is that important right now?”
“I would say so. It is a matter of legal ownership.”
“I’m starting to wonder if homeless people can even bear to live.”
“Anyone listening would think you really had no house and no money.”
As if.
I had a house in my own name now, and more money than I knew what to do with.
But even with trillions of won sitting in my bank account, I’d be hard-pressed to find a safer place for my family and me to stay.
No. At least not anywhere in Korea.
From the outside, it looked like an enormous mansion. In reality, it was an impregnable fortress wrapped in layer upon layer of protective Magic.
And since the public still knew it as Cheon Taemin’s mansion, it would not be an exaggeration to say that it carried more symbolic weight than even the Blue House.
With everyone watching, breaking in is practically impossible. Even if an S-rank Hunter attacked, we could buy more than enough time.
For someone like me, who put my family’s safety above all else in every situation, it was the perfect place.
Of course, Team Leader Choi might feel differently about suddenly having us as housemates.
“Now that I think about it, I’m being pretty shameless. Should I start paying rent this month?”
“If you offer, I will accept it. At ten million won per person, forty million a month should do.”
I gazed out the window at the sunlight pouring down and muttered:
“Ah, nice weather.”
“Anyway, why’s the rent so high? You even got the math wrong.”
“My calculations are always accurate.”
“What are you talking about? Ten million each makes thirty million, not forty. My father died ages ago.”
“There is one more person.”
No sooner had Team Leader Choi said it than a blond foreigner came ambling down the hall and dropped into a chair.
“Feed me.”
Speak of the fucking devil.
Putting everything else aside, the very first thing he said after getting up and seeing our faces made it clear he was a first-rate lout.
“You gonna get your own damn food, or eat after I smack you?”
The Skeleton King considered his options carefully.
“I shall get my own food.”
“Good choice. Bring mine while you’re at it.”
“Oh, and don’t forget the soup. Forget it and you’re dead.”
One of the mansion’s best features was the artificial intelligence in the kitchen, which always had hot food ready.
A little later, the Skeleton King brought me a meal, grumbling all the while. Team Leader Choi watched as I polished off my yukgaejang.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, you always eat well.”
“People aren’t machines. You have to eat to live.”
“Did you sleep well?”
“Yes. It’s been a while. I probably collapsed almost the moment I lay down.”
Team Leader Choi nodded as if he had expected that answer.
“So that is why you could not answer your phone.”
“My phone?”
“You received calls from several places during the night. Have you still not checked?”
“Huh?”
Only then did I check my smartphone. It had vibrated so much that I had switched it to silent, but there were now more than a hundred missed calls and messages that had piled up since last night.
What the hell?
The names scattered through the list were too familiar—and too illustrious—to write off as ads or spam.
Prince Felix of the United Kingdom, whom I had met during the operation to suppress the Arch Lich. Faye Chen, an S-rank Hunter.
Chuck Hagel of the United States, with whom I had destroyed a terrorist organization only two weeks ago by modern reckoning, and Magic Johnson, a name that had become impossible to leave out.
That wasn’t all.
President Baek Hanseong was on the list, of course. So were President Doramp Jr. of the United States, whom I had met during my visit to the Pentagon, and Chairman Xiao Yang of China.
“It was a long night,” Team Leader Choi said, raising his coffee cup with a tired look. “Longer than I expected. Though I did hear quite a bit of news.”
“News?”
“Yes. Chairman Xiao Yang, in particular, passed along something interesting.”
Tap, tap.
Team Leader Choi tapped the tablet PC in front of him with one long finger. A hologram rose above the screen and projected dozens of images.
Flash.
“...What is this?”
Once the images had formed, I frowned and put down my spoon.
I had a strong stomach and was used to gruesome sights, but I couldn’t keep eating while I looked at these.
“Why are there so many corpses?”
“They were prisoners who were alive and well and incarcerated at Beijing Special Detention Center as recently as last night. And among them are some faces you know, Mr. Jin Taekyung.”
“I do?”
Swish.
Team Leader Choi waved a hand instead of answering. The images scattered and vanished, all but one, which expanded before me.
“Do you recognize him now?”
I studied it in silence.
The middle-aged man lay there peacefully, as though deep in sleep. His face was familiar, but the Skeleton King recalled his name before I did.
“That human. His name was, ah... Wu Xueming? Some peculiar name like that.”
He smiled smugly when Team Leader Choi and I looked at him.
“Ha-ha. You underestimate the information-gathering abilities of this body. Unlike lazy creatures such as yourselves, I devoted myself to my smartphone even at the expense of my sleeping hours.”
“You just couldn’t sleep. You’re dead, after all.”
The Skeleton King grew dejected and began picking at his yukgaejang. Team Leader Choi nodded before speaking.
“Former Premier of the State Council of the People’s Republic of China, and a member of the Politburo Standing Committee. And...”
I finally remembered everything about Wu Xueming and cut in.
“Wu Heixing’s father. His son was the bastard who teamed up with Lee Jungryong to kill me.”
“Correct. Wu Xueming was effectively China’s second most powerful man, and the leader of the Crown Prince Party—Chairman Xiao Yang’s strongest political rival.”
I knew all that. After the operation against the Arch Lich, Wu Xueming had raised questions about his son’s death, and I’d learned plenty about him.
One of the main reasons Wu Heixing had been able to cause so much trouble and get away with it was his father’s family. The Wu clan was among China’s most distinguished.
But...
“Didn’t all that corruption come out and knock Wu Xueming out of power? Last I heard, he was waiting for trial.”
“That is correct. Chairman Xiao Yang seized the opportunity, and most of the Crown Prince Party, including Wu Xueming, was imprisoned.”
“And now Wu Xueming is suddenly dead?”

“Wu Xueming was still middle-aged, and he had spent decades drinking potions like water for the sake of his health. His cause of death was sudden cardiac arrest, but there is no way he and some fifty of his relatives could all die the same way at the exact same time.”
“Relatives? Then those pictures...”
“According to Chairman Xiao Yang, every one of them belonged to the Wu family. Some were children.”
The annihilation of an entire household.
Those words sounded like something out of Murim. A chill ran down my spine, and an almost unbelievable thought struck me.
“Team Leader Choi. You don’t think...”
But before I could finish, Team Leader Choi shook his head.
“Chairman Xiao Yang did not do this. If anything, he wanted to win Wu Xueming over more than anyone.”
Win him over.
Wu Xueming had been Xiao Yang’s greatest political rival. Now that he had no hope of a comeback, Xiao Yang had no particular need to kill him. Then again, he had no reason to keep him alive, either.
So what did he hope to gain by winning him over? What did Wu Xueming have?
The Crown Prince Party’s collapsed influence? His vast fortune, which was all but certain to be seized?
I silently rolled the word persuade around in my mind. Before long, I realized the answer.
“...The Mana Cultivation Method.”
At the single word that escaped like a groan, the Skeleton King blinked, and Team Leader Choi answered in a low voice.
“Yes. Chairman Xiao Yang was trying to win Wu Xueming over in order to obtain the very Mana Cultivation Method that had turned Wu Heixing into an S-rank Hunter.”
An S-rank Hunter with that level of power would naturally discover a unique training method of his own at some point.

But Wu Heixing had been different. He had already learned a Mana Cultivation Method passed down through his family, and after his death and Wu Xueming’s downfall, I had stopped paying much attention to the matter.
But the fact that Wu Xueming and all his relatives suddenly died last night means...
I didn’t care what Xiao Yang planned to do with the method. What mattered was that the destruction of the Wu family had ended his attempt to get it—and who had done that.
I already knew the answer.
“Odin Guild.”
A dry voice, unfamiliar even to me, slipped between my lips. Team Leader Choi ran his fingers over his coffee cup, which had gone cold.
“That seems most likely.”

“According to Chairman Xiao Yang, Wu Xueming appeared willing to cooperate. He had little choice. If he refused to hand over the Mana Cultivation Method, he faced life imprisonment at the least, and possibly execution. But...”
Team Leader Choi trailed off and bit his lip.
“Someone else would not have wanted that.”
It felt as though the blood throughout my body had frozen.
They had made their move. Faster than I’d expected, and with far more cruelty.
But even so, to wipe out an entire household...
I looked at the hologram, still hovering above the table. Women, children, old people. All of them lay in a sleep from which they would never wake.
Simply because they had been born into the Wu family.
Did they go this far to stop the Mana Cultivation Method from getting out? Or...
Was this a reply to what happened last night?
The thoughts hovered on the tip of my tongue, then scattered. I stared at the faces of the dead for a while before speaking.
“Team Leader Choi.”
“Yes. Please, go ahead.”
“If you’ve got time, want to go out for coffee?”
“I do not mind. But where would we go all of a sudden?”
“Let’s see. Was it Paris?”
“What?”
Team Leader Choi looked at me, puzzled. I went on calmly.
“Odin Guild. I feel like going to see the boss’s ugly mug.”

sentences.text: At some point, I’d become the kind of person who could go three days and nights without sleep and still be fine.
Even so, getting a good night’s rest was a wonderful thing.
Especially when I woke up refreshed in a place where I was staying with my precious family.
“Home really is the best.”
I sat down at the enormous dining table, and Team Leader Choi gave me a sour look from across it.
“This is my home, technically.”
“Is that important right now?”
“I would say so.
It is a matter of legal ownership.”
“I’m starting to wonder if homeless people can even bear to live.”
“Anyone listening would think you really had no house and no money.”
As if.
I had a house in my own name now, and more money than I knew what to do with.
But even with trillions of won sitting in my bank account, I’d be hard-pressed to find a safer place for my family and me to stay.
No.
At least not anywhere in Korea.
From the outside, it looked like an enormous mansion.
In reality, it was an impregnable fortress wrapped in layer upon layer of protective Magic.
And since the public still knew it as Cheon Taemin’s mansion, it would not be an exaggeration to say that it carried more symbolic weight than even the Blue House.
With everyone watching, breaking in is practically impossible.
Even if an S-rank Hunter attacked, we could buy more than enough time.
For someone like me, who put my family’s safety above all else in every situation, it was the perfect place.
Of course, Team Leader Choi might feel differently about suddenly having us as housemates.
“Now that I think about it, I’m being pretty shameless.
Should I start paying rent this month?”
“If you offer, I will accept it.
At ten million won per person, forty million a month should do.”
I gazed out the window at the sunlight pouring down and muttered:
“Ah, nice weather.”
“Anyway, why’s the rent so high?
You even got the math wrong.”
“My calculations are always accurate.”
“What are you talking about?
Ten million each makes thirty million, not forty.
My father died ages ago.”
“There is one more person.”
No sooner had Team Leader Choi said it than a blond foreigner came ambling down the hall and dropped into a chair.
“Feed me.”
Speak of the fucking devil.
Putting everything else aside, the very first thing he said after getting up and seeing our faces made it clear he was a first-rate lout.
“You gonna get your own damn food, or eat after I smack you?”
The Skeleton King considered his options carefully.
“I shall get my own food.”
“Good choice.
Bring mine while you’re at it.”
“Oh, and don’t forget the soup.
Forget it and you’re dead.”
One of the mansion’s best features was the artificial intelligence in the kitchen, which always had hot food ready.
A little later, the Skeleton King brought me a meal, grumbling all the while.
Team Leader Choi watched as I polished off my yukgaejang.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung, you always eat well.”
“People aren’t machines.
You have to eat to live.”
“Did you sleep well?”
“Yes.
It’s been a while.
I probably collapsed almost the moment I lay down.”
Team Leader Choi nodded as if he had expected that answer.
“So that is why you could not answer your phone.”
“My phone?”
“You received calls from several places during the night.
Have you still not checked?”
“Huh?”
Only then did I check my smartphone.
It had vibrated so much that I had switched it to silent, but there were now more than a hundred missed calls and messages that had piled up since last night.
What the hell?
The names scattered through the list were too familiar—and too illustrious—to write off as ads or spam.
Prince Felix of the United Kingdom, whom I had met during the operation to suppress the Arch Lich.
Faye Chen, an S-rank Hunter.
Chuck Hagel of the United States, with whom I had destroyed a terrorist organization only two weeks ago by modern reckoning, and Magic Johnson, a name that had become impossible to leave out.
That wasn’t all.
President Baek Hanseong was on the list, of course.
So were President Doramp Jr. of the United States, whom I had met during my visit to the Pentagon, and Chairman Xiao Yang of China.
“It was a long night,” Team Leader Choi said, raising his coffee cup with a tired look.
“Longer than I expected.
Though I did hear quite a bit of news.”
“News?”
“Yes.
Chairman Xiao Yang, in particular, passed along something interesting.”
Tap, tap.
Team Leader Choi tapped the tablet PC in front of him with one long finger.
A hologram rose above the screen and projected dozens of images.
Flash.
“...What is this?”
Once the images had formed, I frowned and put down my spoon.
I had a strong stomach and was used to gruesome sights, but I couldn’t keep eating while I looked at these.
“Why are there so many corpses?”
“They were prisoners who were alive and well and incarcerated at Beijing Special Detention Center as recently as last night.
And among them are some faces you know, Mr.
Jin Taekyung.”
“I do?”
Swish.
Team Leader Choi waved a hand instead of answering.
The images scattered and vanished, all but one, which expanded before me.
“Do you recognize him now?”
I studied it in silence.
The middle-aged man lay there peacefully, as though deep in sleep.
His face was familiar, but the Skeleton King recalled his name before I did.
“That human.
His name was, ah...
Wu Xueming?
Some peculiar name like that.”
He smiled smugly when Team Leader Choi and I looked at him.
“Ha-ha.
You underestimate the information-gathering abilities of this body.
Unlike lazy creatures such as yourselves, I devoted myself to my smartphone even at the expense of my sleeping hours.”
“You just couldn’t sleep.
You’re dead, after all.”
The Skeleton King grew dejected and began picking at his yukgaejang.

And...”

chapters.title: Chapter 734
paragraphs: Team Leader Choi rarely showed a change in expression.

He kept his feelings to himself, and in interviews he stuck to the essentials. Even veteran reporters—the kind who claimed they’d grabbed a microphone at their first-birthday celebration—struggled to get a word out of him.
But Team Leader Choi was flesh and blood. Sometimes he showed plenty of emotion, especially when he was talking to me. Then he let out everything he usually kept hidden.
Like now.
“Odin Guild. I feel like going to see the boss’s ugly mug.”
The instant I finished speaking, his mouth fell open in a daze. Beneath his trembling eyelids, his pupils were already shaking like an earthquake.
This bastard’s planning to cause trouble again.
Team Leader Choi stared at me with exactly that look in his eyes. After a long silence, he finally managed to force out his voice.
“Are you serious?”
“Hm.”
I thought for a moment.
“Maybe fifty-fifty?”
“So you’re half-insane.”
“Is that how it works?”
“I am genuinely curious. Where did this insane idea of going to see the Odin Guild Master right now come from? Your heart or your head?”
“My heart.”
Team Leader Choi sighed.
“That is a relief, at least. You have not gone completely insane.”

“You’re calling a perfectly sane person crazy? I’m just planning to look the man in the face and have a cup of coffee with him. Ares Guild has branches in France anyway, so I can use that as an excuse and kill two birds with one stone...”
“It is a Guild branch, not a chain store. And you expect me to believe that? Are you joking?”
At Team Leader Choi’s utterly serious question, I smacked my lips.
“Well, if the conversation doesn’t go smoothly, there might be a little trouble.”
“I will take that to mean an enormous amount of trouble.”
I almost asked what he was making such a big deal about, but stopped myself.
I couldn’t honestly say his concern was exaggerated. It had only been a few weeks in the modern world since I’d stormed into Ares Guild alone and cracked Go Jun’s skull.
Can’t exactly argue after pulling a stunt like that.
Besides, I wasn’t an idiot. I knew perfectly well that following my heart right now would probably end badly.
“All right.”
“The Eiffel Tower collapses, the Guild collapses, public opinion turns into a wasteland... What?”
“I said all right.”
Team Leader Choi, already a step ahead of me in his hallucinations, blinked.
“Really?”
I gave a small nod.
“We don’t have a pretext.”

Even in Murim, where human lives were worth no more than livestock, you needed at least some justification. If I flew to Paris and picked a fight with Odin Guild now, all I’d get was an Interpol wanted notice.
At least I had public support when I dealt with Go Jun.

That incident had caused an international stir, but it had happened in Korea. Unlike this time, there had been clear testimony and evidence. The public had also been furious over Go Jun’s many crimes against humanity.
Those were the reasons I’d been able to step outside the law without becoming a criminal.
Paris would be different.
My heart was screaming at me to storm into Paris and raise hell, but the part of my reason that was still alive was facing reality.
Team Leader Choi’s eyes widened at my decision. The Skeleton King, who had been staring at his smartphone while shoveling down yukgaejang, dropped his spoon.
“This cannot be. Did you just say ‘pretext’?”
“Impossible. You bastard, you’re a monster! What have you done with the treacherous human?”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, this is a simple verification procedure. Please do not take offense. Where did we first meet?”
“Doppelganger! Get out of the treacherous human’s body!”
These two were acting like fucking idiots.
Instead of answering, I picked up the spoon on the table and smacked the Skeleton King on top of his head.
Crack!
“My skull! My beautiful skull!”
Team Leader Choi watched the Skeleton King howl and nodded.
“What a relief. You are Jin Taekyung.”
After completing that strangely unpleasant verification procedure, Team Leader Choi let out a sigh of relief.
“In any case, I am glad you changed your mind.”
“If this were something I could settle that way, I’d have bought a ticket to Paris already. To hell with international crime.”
“That is true. If Odin Guild disappeared, another Odin Guild would take its place.”
It was the same as when Ares Guild had been our enemy.

The world was vast, and another enemy would fill the space left by the one we defeated. We’d taken Ares Guild by siege; others could do the same to us. Now the City Lord’s duty was to defend the castle from the competitors swarming around it and expand his territory as far as he could.
And Odin Guild wasn’t some stray wolf that had wandered in from who knew where.
It was a beast with a massive body and sharp claws.
A greedy one, too, judging by what was written on the tablet Team Leader Choi had just put in front of me.
“What is this...?”
“The proposal the Chinese government sent Odin Guild during the Monster Wave in Sichuan Province, inviting them to participate. It was unofficial, of course, and had no legal force.”
An unofficial proposal.
I wondered how Team Leader Choi had obtained something that should have been nearly impossible to leak. Then the answer came to me.
“Grandpa Jongseok gave it to you?”
“Not Grandpa Jongseok. Chairman Xiao Yang.”
“Right. Grandpa Jongseok.”
“What? It sounds friendly. Besides, the old guy likes me a lot.”
Team Leader Choi looked at me as though he’d half given up.

“As you know, Mr. Jin Taekyung, during the early stages of the crisis, China’s State Council and Politburo Standing Committee were reluctant to request help from abroad. They were especially vehemently opposed to support from the West.”
The Skeleton King, still tenderly stroking his skull, interrupted with a puzzled look.
“They opposed it? Why?”
Well, why indeed?
There were any number of reasons, but they all came down to one answer. I kindly gave it to him.
“Because it’s China.”
“What does that mean? Humans are dying either way!”
“Because it’s China.”
“No, treacherous human. You seem not to have understood my question...”
“Yeah. China.”
“That’s just how it is. You might not get it yet.”
I left the Skeleton King looking thoroughly confused and turned back to Team Leader Choi.
“But China did ask the West for help eventually, didn’t it? Prince Felix of the United Kingdom and Magic Johnson came, too.”

“Yes. Once the damage from the Arch Lich reached astronomical proportions, China’s leaders had no choice but to accept Chairman Xiao Yang’s argument. They would have to pay a suitable diplomatic and material price when it was over, though, so they had to consider that when assembling their forces.”
That was how four S-rank Hunters had gathered, not counting me.
An incredible force in its own right. But what mattered now was that Odin Guild had backed out when it should have been a central part of that force alongside Lee Jungryong’s Ares Guild.
“Then why did Odin Guild turn down the offer? That looks like enough money to make them accept. More than enough.”
The fee listed on the tablet was staggering—nearly twice what I’d heard Ares Guild had been paid, with several other perks attached. China had offered top-tier treatment befitting the name Odin.
Team Leader Choi’s next words answered my question.
“The Chinese government was the one that ultimately turned it down.”
“What?”
“Odin Guild added a condition when the negotiations were almost complete.”
“What condition...?”
Team Leader Choi took a sip of lukewarm coffee, then spoke quietly.

“They wanted China to lease ten cities—including Chengdu, Meishan, Ziyang, and Suining, the representative administrative districts of Sichuan Province—to Odin Guild for the next ninety-nine years, as well as authorize the establishment of an official branch in Beijing.”
“They were effectively asking China to cede Sichuan Province. Permission to set up an official branch, which the Chinese government prohibits, was an added bonus.”
Good God. What did I just hear?
I stared at him and muttered, “Wow. Those bastards are insane. They’re worse than Chinks.”
“According to Chairman Xiao Yang, Odin Guild had contacted the French government shortly before the negotiations.”
“Even so, how could they make an offer that crazy?”
“It is France.”
“No, there’s such a thing as common sense.”
“France.”
“...Team Leader Choi?”
“France.”
Why did this feel oddly familiar? Was it just me?
As I stared at him with a sour expression, Team Leader Choi spoke to me in a gentle voice.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung, did you know Koreans have another name for the French?”
“Oh.”
With a sudden flash of insight, I let out an exclamation.
“European Chinks...!”
Team Leader Choi nodded.

“Their skin color and culture are different, but they are the same sort. The President can have an affair or do whatever else he likes, and the French do not care. Odin Guild did not put its headquarters in Paris by accident. Scandals there cause little commotion.”
“But wasn’t that just an internet meme?”
“I remember my school days in Paris. When a photograph of my maternal grandfather appeared in our history textbook, everyone in the classroom looked at me and pulled their eyes into slits.”
“Oh.”
“The teacher did it, too.”
“Ah! Ah...”
“It is all right. It was a long time ago.”
Team Leader Choi set aside the painful childhood memory that had surfaced and continued.

“What matters most is that even with the French government behind it, Odin Guild cannot move against us openly. As with their assassination of Wu Xueming’s family, they can only send a warning rather than threaten us directly.”
He was right.

Cheon Taemin’s flag flew over the walls of Ares Guild, and the world couldn’t simply ignore what it had seen me do. That held true even for Odin Guild, the greatest Guild in the world, or any other major Guild.
And above all...
“People around the world are cheering us on. The media may not be able to openly criticize the major Guilds, but plenty of people are condemning them.”
Public sentiment.
The strongest weapon—and shield—we had gained by releasing the Mana Cultivation Method.
We needed to make full use of it. Make sure even Odin Guild couldn’t come near us...
“Um, sorry to ruin the mood.”
The Skeleton King suddenly held out his smartphone.
“Is this the cheering you mean?”
On the screen of the smartphone he offered me was a breaking-news alert that had been posted only a few dozen seconds earlier.

Odin Guild Announces Support for Ares Odin Guild Unveils New Mana Cultivation Method Senior Official: “A Project We’ve Been Preparing for Years” “Though We’re a Step Behind, We Want to Change the World with Them.” The World’s Greatest Guild Shows Its Class
Fuck. What the hell is this now?

Jin Taekyung, during the early stages of the crisis, China’s State Council and Politburo Standing Committee were reluctant to request help from abroad.
They were especially vehemently opposed to support from the West.”
The Skeleton King, still tenderly stroking his skull, interrupted with a puzzled look.
“They opposed it?
Why?”
Well, why indeed?
There were any number of reasons, but they all came down to one answer.
I kindly gave it to him.
“Because it’s China.”
“What does that mean?
Humans are dying either way!”
“Because it’s China.”
“No, treacherous human.
You seem not to have understood my question...”
“Yeah.
China.”
“That’s just how it is.
You might not get it yet.”
I left the Skeleton King looking thoroughly confused and turned back to Team Leader Choi.
“But China did ask the West for help eventually, didn’t it?
Prince Felix of the United Kingdom and Magic Johnson came, too.”
“Yes.
Once the damage from the Arch Lich reached astronomical proportions, China’s leaders had no choice but to accept Chairman Xiao Yang’s argument.
They would have to pay a suitable diplomatic and material price when it was over, though, so they had to consider that when assembling their forces.”
That was how four S-rank Hunters had gathered, not counting me.
An incredible force in its own right.
But what mattered now was that Odin Guild had backed out when it should have been a central part of that force alongside Lee Jungryong’s Ares Guild.
“Then why did Odin Guild turn down the offer?
That looks like enough money to make them accept.
More than enough.”
The fee listed on the tablet was staggering—nearly twice what I’d heard Ares Guild had been paid, with several other perks attached.
China had offered top-tier treatment befitting the name Odin.
Team Leader Choi’s next words answered my question.
“The Chinese government was the one that ultimately turned it down.”
“What?”
“Odin Guild added a condition when the negotiations were almost complete.”
“What condition...?”
Team Leader Choi took a sip of lukewarm coffee, then spoke quietly.

“They wanted China to lease ten cities—including Chengdu, Meishan, Ziyang, and Suining, the representative administrative districts of Sichuan Province—to Odin Guild for the next ninety-nine years, as well as authorize the establishment of an official branch in Beijing.”
“They were effectively asking China to cede Sichuan Province.
Permission to set up an official branch, which the Chinese government prohibits, was an added bonus.”
Good God.
What did I just hear?
I stared at him and muttered, “Wow.
Those bastards are insane.
They’re worse than Chinks.”
“According to Chairman Xiao Yang, Odin Guild had contacted the French government shortly before the negotiations.”
“Even so, how could they make an offer that crazy?”
“It is France.”
“No, there’s such a thing as common sense.”
“France.”
“...Team Leader Choi?”
“France.”
Why did this feel oddly familiar?
Was it just me?
As I stared at him with a sour expression, Team Leader Choi spoke to me in a gentle voice.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung, did you know Koreans have another name for the French?”
“Oh.”
With a sudden flash of insight, I let out an exclamation.
“European Chinks...!”
Team Leader Choi nodded.
“Their skin color and culture are different, but they are the same sort.
The President can have an affair or do whatever else he likes, and the French do not care.
Odin Guild did not put its headquarters in Paris by accident.
Scandals there cause little commotion.”
“But wasn’t that just an internet meme?”
“I remember my school days in Paris.
When a photograph of my maternal grandfather appeared in our history textbook, everyone in the classroom looked at me and pulled their eyes into slits.”
“Oh.”
“The teacher did it, too.”
“Ah!
“It is all right.
It was a long time ago.”
Team Leader Choi set aside the painful childhood memory that had surfaced and continued.
“What matters most is that even with the French government behind it, Odin Guild cannot move against us openly.
As with their assassination of Wu Xueming’s family, they can only send a warning rather than threaten us directly.”
He was right.
Cheon Taemin’s flag flew over the walls of Ares Guild, and the world couldn’t simply ignore what it had seen me do.
That held true even for Odin Guild, the greatest Guild in the world, or any other major Guild.
And above all...
“People around the world are cheering us on.
The media may not be able to openly criticize the major Guilds, but plenty of people are condemning them.”
Public sentiment.
The strongest weapon—and shield—we had gained by releasing the Mana Cultivation Method.
We needed to make full use of it.
Make sure even Odin Guild couldn’t come near us...
“Um, sorry to ruin the mood.”
The Skeleton King suddenly held out his smartphone.
“Is this the cheering you mean?”
On the screen of the smartphone he offered me was a breaking-news alert that had been posted only a few dozen seconds earlier.

Odin Guild Announces Support for Ares Odin Guild Unveils New Mana Cultivation Method Senior Official: “A Project We’ve Been Preparing for Years” “Though We’re a Step Behind, We Want to Change the World with Them.” The World’s Greatest Guild Shows Its Class
Fuck.
What the hell is this now?

chapters.title: Chapter 735
paragraphs: A middle-aged man in a thin silk robe gazed out the window.
Clouds carrying January’s chill swept past, so close he could almost touch them. Far below, he could make out buildings and plazas laid out in separate districts.
A great city steeped in history. Countless people moved through it, reduced to tiny dots.
The gloomy gray sky and mist-shrouded streets hardly suited Paris’s name, the City of Light. But the middle-aged man didn’t care.
He loved everything about this city—about Paris.
From a skyscraper too high for even the mist to reach, the world was always beautiful.
Especially on a day like today.
Ding. Deeeeng—
Bells rang out across the plaza, announcing seven in the morning. The middle-aged man turned slowly from the wall of windows.
Behind him lay a vast study.
At the round table in its center, over ten figures waited for him, appearing amid the green glow unique to holograms.
“It’s been a long time since we all gathered like this. Our last meeting was, what... three years ago?”
The corners of the people’s mouths, visible beneath their masks, curled slightly at the joke the middle-aged man made as soon as he took the seat of honor.
Three years?
They had held a secret meeting just two nights ago.
“If I remember correctly, it was ten years ago.”
“Ten years? Already?”
“Wasn’t it closer to thirty?”
“Damn it. Thirty years ago was the Great Cataclysm. I don’t even want to remember the hell we went through, so drop it.”
Quiet laughter mingled with their conversation.
The middle-aged man watched them with a gentle smile.
“You all seem to be in good spirits. Yes, it’s nice to indulge in idle chatter now and then.”
Silence fell at his quiet words.
They all closed their mouths at once, as though on cue. Still smiling, the middle-aged man went on.
“I did not call this meeting to listen to pointless nonsense or trashy small talk like this... What does everyone think?”
Their eyes wavered at each breath he took, each slight movement of his fingertips.
Even through a hologram, his overwhelming presence—and his aura—reached them.
Everyone at the meeting was a major figure. None could hope to rival him.
The reason was simple.
The man before them was the master of Odin Guild, known as the greatest Guild in the world, and one of the absolute beings capable of controlling the world.
“I-I apologize, Michael. I was pleased that everything was proceeding without a hitch, and...”
“I wasn’t asking for excuses.”
Michael cut him off.
“I simply found it pathetic to see you all relaxing as though everything were over.”
“Our opponent is more daring than we expected. How else could they have done something so insane?”
No one at the table needed to ask what he meant. By now, the whole world knew.
The public release of the Mana Cultivation Method.
To a tiny number of people, it was an act of madness that threatened to overturn the established order. Their opponent had made it happen anyway.
“I sent Huginn, and they still didn’t get the message. Reckless beyond belief... but I suppose that means they’re confident.”
One of them spoke cautiously.
“If, hypothetically, they’re counting on Sky...”
“I believe I already told you not to concern yourselves with him.”
“...Understood.”
The reply lacked conviction.
Until now, Michael’s word had been law to all of them.
Once he had spoken with such certainty, they had no choice but to dig a hole for any lingering doubts deep in their hearts and bury them there.
But this time, none of them could stop turning the question over.
Because the person in question was none other than Cheon Taemin.
Even so, how can he tell us not to worry about something this serious?
What happens if Sky gets involved?
Where did he get his information...?
The questions kept circling through their minds.

Michael’s information had always been reliable. No one knew who provided it or what methods he used to obtain it, but as long as they trusted and acted on the information he brought them, they profited.
Immense wealth and fame. Lofty social status.
Yet even the highest, strongest wall could fall in an instant.
And the name Cheon Taemin was not something they could simply bury through faith. The sense of crisis they felt was conveyed in its entirety to one person.
Tap. Tap.
A finger drummed slowly on the round table. Waves of powerful mana rolled over them, pulling them from their thoughts.
“You seem uneasy.”
They hurried to answer his gentle voice.
“Not at all.”
“How could we be?”
“Our alliance is powerful. We won’t lose to brats like them.”
They kept the qualification to themselves: As long as Cheon Taemin stays out of it.
For now, they could only trust Michael. Judging by the power and ability he had shown them all this time, those mere fledglings would not be opponents at all, just as one of them had said.
“Choi, that young man, is resourceful, but his limitations are equally clear.”
“The same goes for Jin Taekyung. However strong he is, he can’t get past the walls we’ve built.”
There had certainly been a time when such a thing was possible.
A time so cruel and chaotic that it could only be called the Great Cataclysm.
Humans slaughtered monsters. Monsters slaughtered humans. And humans slaughtered other humans like livestock.
It was a turbulent period when nothing seemed strange, no matter what happened.
But the Great Cataclysm was over.
On a sea lashed by storms, nothing that happened would seem strange. But in a peaceful world like this one, a mere ripple could not bring about change.
The Mana Cultivation Method they had released was no different.
“Their decision to make the Mana Cultivation Method public has cost us dearly. But we’ve dealt with the immediate crisis. There’s no reason to worry.”
“Exactly. The media didn’t dare criticize us, and above all, you acted quickly, Guild Master.”
Michael nodded without a word.
News of the Mana Cultivation Method Odin Guild had unveiled at sunrise was even now spreading across the world through every kind of media.
Public criticism of the established major Guilds would gradually die down. And the fledglings who had ignored his generous offer would soon regret it.
This time, he would not settle for words. He would show them directly through his actions.
How foolish.
Michael muttered inwardly.

In today’s world, a Mana Cultivation Method was a treasure beyond price. A Guild’s standing and a nation’s influence depended on the strength of their Hunters, yet those fools had given one away to the entire world.
They should have asked themselves why no one had ever done it before.

Others had stepped forward in the past, armed with nothing but morality and a sense of justice. Powerful people recognized around the world, they had wanted to share their special abilities with everyone.
That was why they had died.
And this time will end the same way.
History repeated itself.
Although the Mana Cultivation Method had been made public because of their opponent’s unexpected and impulsive act, they would have to pay the price for their foolishness.
That was how the world worked.
There was only one thing that continued to bother him: the young man who had caused the greatest change in recent times.
Jin Taekyung.
Unlike Choi Minwoo, whom Michael still considered a fledgling, that bastard was a powerful figure no one could deny.

In less than a year, he had amassed countless achievements and considerable fame. Recently, he had brought down Ares Guild’s headquarters single-handedly, despite the hundreds of Hunters waiting there, Go Jun among them.
And that was not all.
The world didn’t know it yet, but Michael knew Jin Taekyung had recently wiped out terrorist organizations and rebel groups.
Power that ranks among the best even among S-rank Hunters. And daring.
Not one of the people chattering before him could match that.
An S-rank Hunter who led a major Guild known around the world. A politician who could sway a powerful nation. A tycoon who owned hundreds of Gates and oil fields...
Every one of them deserved to be called a major figure. To Michael, they were all greedy idiots.
Of course, they’re the reason I was able to make Odin Guild the greatest in the world.
Michael muttered inwardly and clicked his tongue softly.
Tsk.
The chatter stopped. Every eye turned to him.
He looked over them one by one. Then he sensed someone approaching from a distance.
“It seems we have a guest.”
“Ah, then...”
“I will notify you separately about the next meeting.”
Bzzzt.
That was all.
The instant Michael spoke, the holograms melted away and disappeared. At the same time, the study’s tightly closed doors swung wide open at a gesture from him.
“So, did you enjoy your trip?”
The man in old-fashioned clothes answered Michael’s waiting question.
“I was merely following orders.”
“You’re always so stiff. Come in, Huginn.”
“Thank you.”
Thud.
Huginn took off his hat, gave it a few taps, and stepped into the study.
Michael saw grains of sand scattered near the door and smiled calmly.
“You’ve been getting around.”
“The schedule was rather tight.”
“You went a long way. It must have been difficult. Did you encounter any problems?”
“There were some, but I took care of them.”
His answer was curt, but the heat in Huginn’s eyes still held traces of battle.
Michael nodded without showing any particular reaction.
He had personally selected and trained Huginn. As a fixer, the man was without equal, and he carried out every assignment perfectly.
This one included.
“Did you bring your friends?”
“Yes. When they heard why I’d come, they volunteered to help. Unlike the reception I got in Korea, everyone treated me kindly.”
“How good of them to come all that way. Where are they now?”
“They should all be on their way to their destinations.”
“And the gifts?”
“I made certain they were handed over.”
Huginn drew a pocket watch from his coat and checked it.
“There is about an hour left until the first gift is delivered.”
“An hour. Good. Coffee while we wait?”
“If possible, I would prefer black tea.”
Michael smiled and made them a cup of each.
Exactly one hour later, he confirmed with his own eyes that his orders had been carried out without fail.
BOOOOM!
Beneath the pale clouds, red flames surged upward with a deafening roar. And then...
Whooosh!
The air slowly began to warp. Michael watched it and murmured lightly,
“As expected, it is a beautiful city.”
A building was engulfed in flames.
With Ares Guild’s Paris branch at its center, space began to tear apart.

chapters.title: Chapter 736
paragraphs: It started with barely a tremor. Nothing more, nothing less.
But that was only the first sign.
Rumble...
The ground shook.

Visitors lined up outside the Louvre ducked instinctively. In Paris’s 10th arrondissement, people who had been fighting with fistfuls of each other’s collars broke apart and scattered, swearing as they ran.
And in the 6th arrondissement...
People forgot to scream. They could only stare, dazed, at the sight before them.
Gooooom.
Crimson-black darkness coiled around a skyscraper that rose to a dizzying height, then surged upward.
Everyone held their breath at the vast, ominous energy, unlike anything they had ever felt.
BOOOOOM!
The skyscraper that had housed Ares Guild’s Paris branch exploded.
The layers of defensive Magic around its exterior. The sturdy frame built to withstand a missile strike. All of it shattered and burst outward.
Fragments large and small, once part of a building some fifty stories tall, rained down in flames.
Fwoosh. Whoooooosh!
It was impossible to believe. Impossible to deny.
As countless fragments blotted out the sky, a thought came to the people below.
Maybe today is the day of the apocalypse described in the Bible.
Then they saw the air twisting out of shape, and suspicion hardened into despairing certainty.
Fwoooooosh!
None of them had ever seen it happen. But as people living amid the brightest civilization in history, they knew what the phenomenon was called.
“Monster Wave...”
The words escaped someone like a groan.
Yet even with debris falling toward them and monsters emerging from the warped space, no one ran.
Not the Sorbonne students cycling to class. Not the young couple walking through the Luxembourg Gardens with a stroller. Not the police rushing to calm the public.
Everyone who had been going about their morning—the entire 6th arrondissement—froze where they stood, gripped by fear and a chill that sank into their bones.
And then—
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
A rain of fire engulfed everything within a radius of over a hundred meters, and the gates of hell opened.
Thud. Thud.
Huge monsters with arms and legs as thick as temple pillars, each with two heads on a single body, beat their chests and roared.
—Gwooooooar!
Crash!
Glass shattered all around them, unable to withstand the force of their roars.
Fear, which only powerful monsters could emit, shot out like invisible ropes and bound thousands of people in place.
—Grrrr.
A growl rich with satisfaction.
The hunt was about to begin.
Or so it should have been.
Whoooooosh! Boom!
A flash struck the monster at the front, sending it staggering. Everything above its shoulders was gone.
Thud!
The ground shook. The hundred or so monsters raised their heads as one.
Among the thousands of people rooted to the spot, predators hidden in the flock of sheep were revealing themselves.
They came with dazzling flashes too fast for the eye to follow.
Whoooooosh! Crack!
Rattle, rattle.
Flesh and bone crumpled. Blue blood sprayed in every direction.
A Twin Head Ogre that had survived at the cost of one of its heads stepped backward without realizing it.
It had no idea what waited behind it.
Crunch!
A gigantic fist burst its remaining head like a watermelon.
The giant possessed strength and a physique far beyond those of the other ogres. It licked its subordinate’s brain matter from its fist, and a golden-eyed human was reflected in its enormous pupils.
—Karsh. Marto.
The words were in the Demon Realm language. They sounded almost like a curse.
Huginn paid them no attention. He turned and bowed politely to someone behind him.
“It is a Named Monster—a Giant Ogre. What would you like to do?”
A calm voice answered.
“Not bad. This should do for a demonstration.”
“Then...?”
“I’ll take it. Clear out the rest.”
That was all.
At the order, Huginn and a hundred Hunters swept forward as one, like the storm and lightning painted on their armor.
Like the ancient god whose name they bore: Odin.
Whooooooosh! Slash!
A clash. Then a slaughter.
Limbs as thick as logs flew through the air, and dazzling aura cut through the magical power surging around the monsters.
It was a scene out of myth.
And even in a myth crowded with figures, there was always one hero who shone above the rest.
—Gwooooooar!
Crack!
One Strike.
The roar that had seemed ready to swallow the city fell silent.
Ruuuuumble!
The Giant Ogre, dozens of meters tall, dropped to its knees before a human who looked tiny beside its mountain of a body.
But to the people who had seen it all, that human was anything but small.
A hero had protected them. A true giant stood before them.
Brought back from the brink of death, the crowd cried out the hero’s name—or the heroes’ names—as one.
“Michael! Michael!”
“Odin Guild!”

—Local witnesses say Odin Guild, based nearby, was the first to head to the scene...

Why did they have to die?

Otherwise, I wouldn’t be able to face the owner of the immense energy approaching behind me in my right mind.
Michael Silbert.

sentences.text: It started with barely a tremor.
Nothing more, nothing less.
But that was only the first sign.
Rumble...
The ground shook.
Visitors lined up outside the Louvre ducked instinctively.
In Paris’s 10th arrondissement, people who had been fighting with fistfuls of each other’s collars broke apart and scattered, swearing as they ran.
And in the 6th arrondissement...
People forgot to scream.
They could only stare, dazed, at the sight before them.
Gooooom.
Crimson-black darkness coiled around a skyscraper that rose to a dizzying height, then surged upward.
Everyone held their breath at the vast, ominous energy, unlike anything they had ever felt.
BOOOOOM!
The skyscraper that had housed Ares Guild’s Paris branch exploded.
The layers of defensive Magic around its exterior.
The sturdy frame built to withstand a missile strike.
All of it shattered and burst outward.
Fragments large and small, once part of a building some fifty stories tall, rained down in flames.
Fwoosh.
Whoooooosh!
It was impossible to believe.
Impossible to deny.
As countless fragments blotted out the sky, a thought came to the people below.
Maybe today is the day of the apocalypse described in the Bible.
Then they saw the air twisting out of shape, and suspicion hardened into despairing certainty.
Fwoooooosh!
None of them had ever seen it happen.
But as people living amid the brightest civilization in history, they knew what the phenomenon was called.
“Monster Wave...”
The words escaped someone like a groan.
Yet even with debris falling toward them and monsters emerging from the warped space, no one ran.
Not the Sorbonne students cycling to class.
Not the young couple walking through the Luxembourg Gardens with a stroller.
Not the police rushing to calm the public.
Everyone who had been going about their morning—the entire 6th arrondissement—froze where they stood, gripped by fear and a chill that sank into their bones.
And then—
BOOM!
BOOM!
BOOM!
A rain of fire engulfed everything within a radius of over a hundred meters, and the gates of hell opened.
Thud.
Thud.
Huge monsters with arms and legs as thick as temple pillars, each with two heads on a single body, beat their chests and roared.
—Gwooooooar!
Crash!
Glass shattered all around them, unable to withstand the force of their roars.
Fear, which only powerful monsters could emit, shot out like invisible ropes and bound thousands of people in place.
—Grrrr.
A growl rich with satisfaction.
The hunt was about to begin.
Or so it should have been.
Whoooooosh!
Boom!
A flash struck the monster at the front, sending it staggering.
Everything above its shoulders was gone.
Thud!
The ground shook.
The hundred or so monsters raised their heads as one.
Among the thousands of people rooted to the spot, predators hidden in the flock of sheep were revealing themselves.
They came with dazzling flashes too fast for the eye to follow.
Whoooooosh!
Crack!
Rattle, rattle.
Flesh and bone crumpled.
Blue blood sprayed in every direction.
A Twin Head Ogre that had survived at the cost of one of its heads stepped backward without realizing it.
It had no idea what waited behind it.
Crunch!
A gigantic fist burst its remaining head like a watermelon.
The giant possessed strength and a physique far beyond those of the other ogres.
It licked its subordinate’s brain matter from its fist, and a golden-eyed human was reflected in its enormous pupils.
—Karsh.
Marto.
The words were in the Demon Realm language.
They sounded almost like a curse.
Huginn paid them no attention.
He turned and bowed politely to someone behind him.
“It is a Named Monster—a Giant Ogre.
What would you like to do?”
A calm voice answered.
“Not bad.
This should do for a demonstration.”
“Then...?”
“I’ll take it.
Clear out the rest.”
That was all.
At the order, Huginn and a hundred Hunters swept forward as one, like the storm and lightning painted on their armor.
Like the ancient god whose name they bore: Odin.
Whooooooosh!
Slash!
A clash.
Then a slaughter.
Limbs as thick as logs flew through the air, and dazzling aura cut through the magical power surging around the monsters.
It was a scene out of myth.
And even in a myth crowded with figures, there was always one hero who shone above the rest.
—Gwooooooar!
Crack!
One Strike.
The roar that had seemed ready to swallow the city fell silent.
Ruuuuumble!
The Giant Ogre, dozens of meters tall, dropped to its knees before a human who looked tiny beside its mountain of a body.
But to the people who had seen it all, that human was anything but small.
A hero had protected them.
A true giant stood before them.
Brought back from the brink of death, the crowd cried out the hero’s name—or the heroes’ names—as one.
“Michael!
Michael!”
“Odin Guild!”
As the cheers spread like wildfire, Michael declared in a ringing voice, “Rest assured.
As long as Odin Guild and I are here to protect you, no danger will come to you.”
Then he looked toward the ruins beneath the heaps of concrete and added, too quietly for anyone to hear, “At least not today.”
With a faint smile, he stepped toward the remaining monsters, trampling the fallen name Ares beneath his foot.
The letters had lost their shine when they tore free of the building and fell among the rubble.
