chapters.title: Chapter 737
paragraphs: Michael Silbert.
Anyone living in the modern world knew his name.
He was the Guild Master of Odin Guild, called the greatest in the world, and an extraordinary figure even among the countless heroes born from the Great Cataclysm.
People loved Michael Silbert for risking his life to save them. I had admired him too.
No. I used to admire him.
Step.
Footsteps stopped behind me.
I turned slowly. A man stood amid the heat-soaked ash and ruins, gazing at me.
“So, it’s you.”
A few words broke the silence, but they were enough. We had recognized each other. Even without the photographs of him plastered across every kind of media, we would have known.
This is...
I could feel it: the immense power compressed inside that neither-large-nor-small body. It was more powerful than Lee Jungryong’s—or rather, more powerful than any S-rank Hunter I had ever faced.
And that was not all I realized.
“...So it was you?”
Michael Silbert.
The moment I met his gray eyes, I knew whose work the ruins beneath my feet were. I knew who had started this terrible disaster.
My question echoed his first words, but it meant something very different. Michael answered calmly.
“What a pointless question. If it wasn’t me, who else could it be?”
“What?”
“It’s an obvious and trite story anyway. There’s no point in asking or answering anything more.”
What was this?
What the hell was this bastard talking about?
For a moment, I forgot my anger and stood frozen. Michael blinked at me, looking genuinely puzzled.
“I don’t understand why you look so surprised. We already understand each other’s intentions, and now that negotiations have broken down, this is merely the inevitable next step.”
“You son of a—”
“Didn’t I warn you through Huginn? Refuse my proposal, and there would be a price to pay.”
He cut me off as though none of this mattered. Then Michael Silbert—the hero of the Great Cataclysm, beloved the world over—reached out and caught a handful of ash drifting through the air.
“I hear you’ve been rather busy these past few weeks. Were you wandering that vast desert looking for an oasis?”
“A word of advice. There’s no such thing as a perfect secret. Not even at the Pentagon.”
He opened his fist. Ash mixed with monster blood lay in his palm, calling up a sight I had witnessed countless times a few weeks ago.
Fanatics dying in droves all around me. Their screams. Grains of desert sand made sticky with blood flowing like a river...
Through those memories, his low voice reached me.
“If you wanted a peaceful, better world, you should have uprooted them completely from the start.”
“...You don’t mean—”
“Considering they were deranged fanatics, it was a perfectly reasonable deal. I wanted a price paid for ignoring my warning. They wanted weapons for revenge.”
Now I understood.
The real cause of this sudden Monster Wave. Why the madman in front of me could admit to it so openly.
Borrow another’s knife to kill.
The instant it all fell into place—
Fwoosh.
My vision burned hot. Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi surged from my dantian, transformed into lava, and flowed through my limbs and bones.
I was ready. From the moment I had first faced him, my mind had been searching without pause for the best way to move.
One step.
That was all it would take. The instant I planted my foot, the distance between us would vanish. Then I could shut that bullshit-spouting mouth with my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
No. I had to.
For the innocent people killed by another human being, not a monster. And to remove the cause of an even greater disaster before it struck.
But—
Grab.
Two hands seized my shoulders, and a familiar voice struck my ears.
“Mr. Jin Taekyung!”
“People are watching. Not now.”
Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King.
They had to be holding back their own anger. As I thought of them, the fury boiling inside me began to settle.
I knew they were right. Attacking the bastard in front of me would be easy. Dealing with what came afterward would be difficult, even for me.
I have no evidence. Nothing that would convince the public I’m justified.

To the rest of the world, Michael Silbert was a hero of the Great Cataclysm who had defeated a terrorist bent on revenge. Whether or not I could kill him, attacking him here would get me branded a public enemy—even if this were Murim rather than the modern world.
And that was probably...
Exactly what he wants.
Cheon Taemin, the beginning and end of Ares Guild, had been unconscious for some time. What would happen if I fell now?
Even if I killed him here, I couldn’t take responsibility for what followed.
Our greatest enemy stood before me, but there were others who had yet to show themselves.
By the time I reached that thought, both my head and my heart had gone cold.
Hssss.
The aura I had built up, ready to burst, subsided. Michael Silbert sighed softly.
“What a shame. You looked much better when you were full of youthful fire.”
“Shut up before I tear your mouth apart.”
“If it were that easy to tear my mouth apart, someone would have done it hundreds of times by now. But do you know something?”
A faint smile touched his lips.
“One day, I noticed that everyone who had said something like that to me had vanished without a trace. I know a more certain way of dealing with them than tearing their mouths apart.”
“So be grateful you have good friends today. You’re lucky they’re so capable, too. Wouldn’t you agree?”
He was speaking to me, but he was looking past my shoulder.
That strange look brought my dulled sense of danger snapping back.
The Skeleton King.
Magic Johnson had given him a clean new identity, and he was working as a Hunter with Peace Guild. Even so, it would be a problem if he drew the wrong kind of attention.
Michael Silbert was that difficult an opponent. The moment a weakness appeared, he would pounce without mercy and tear into it.
Should I have left him behind?
The thought had barely crossed my mind when Michael’s attention shifted.
“So you’re the young Vice Guild Master of Ares Guild I’ve heard about. How is your maternal grandfather?”
Team Leader Choi answered in an icy voice.
“He’s well. I can’t say how he’ll react when I tell him what happened to the Paris branch.”
“I regret how things turned out myself. I have great respect for your grandfather. I hope you’ll put in a good word for me.”
“I certainly intend to tell him exactly what I saw and heard.”
There was not a trace of hesitation in his answer. Michael Silbert was gazing at Team Leader Choi when—
Whoosh! Whoosh!
A group raced across the ruins, cutting through the air. At their head was Huginn, the messenger who had visited Ares Guild not long ago.
He spared us a glance, then hurried to Michael and bowed.
“Guild Master, everything is ready.”
“The casualty count first.”
“Approximately three hundred. We’ve rescued forty-five survivors.”
“That’s enough for now. Have people gathered?”
“Not only the nearby citizens. Every reporter in Paris is waiting for you.”
“Faster than I expected.”
“We were fortunate. The foreign press was already on alert because of the release of the new Mana Cultivation Method.”
“And the CCTV footage?”

“We secured it immediately. It captured everything from beginning to end: the terrorist carrying out a suicide attack with bombs and unrefined Magic Gems, and Odin Guild suppressing the Monster Wave.”
At first, I hadn’t understood what Huginn meant by ready. As I listened, my mind went cold.
This is...
Meticulous.

The unveiling of a new Mana Cultivation Method. The attack on the Paris branch and the Monster Wave, carried out by a Middle Eastern terrorist seeking revenge. Now a press conference with the world’s attention on it.
Dozens of gears, large and small, meshing without a fraction of an inch out of place. Every part of their plan was moving as intended.
That was why they could discuss it openly in front of us. They knew we had no way to stop the gears once they were turning.
Even if we shouted the truth for three days and three nights in front of the countless cameras camped out in the distance, no one would believe us anyway.
The worst part was that those madmen were right. Force alone could not change that reality.
“I’m sorry, but I must be going. A great many people are waiting for me.”
Michael Silbert acknowledged me, Team Leader Choi, and finally the Skeleton King with a glance before slowly turning away.
Then he stopped and added, “You’ll be busy from now on. Far busier than you expect.”
Grind.
I watched him walk away, clenching my fist with all my strength. But I could not bring myself to strike.
Not long afterward, I understood what he meant.
Ding.
System A sudden Quest, Chain of Terror Attacks, has been generated! You cannot choose whether to accept this Quest. The System will force it to proceed!
It was January. The joy of the New Year had not yet faded.
Winter turned red.
“It has begun.”
At Huginn’s low voice beside his ear, Michael Silbert calmly asked:
“Where this time?”
“London.”
“The old king will be furious.”
“Buckingham Palace should be fine. London Bridge will collapse instead.”
Michael gave a soft laugh at his subordinate’s dry joke.
“Once London is done... eight to go.”
“Yes.”
Huginn had brought ten people back from the desert. Every one of them was a deranged fanatic and a seasoned Hunter. They would carry out their missions without a hitch.
Their bombs would bring down buildings. Their unrefined Magic Gems would be enough to shatter people’s hopes.
And our Odin Guild will piece that shattered hope back together.
Everything was ready.
He had reached this position through countless sacrifices and effort.
He could tolerate neither a single mistake nor failure.
As the reporters drew closer and the citizens’ cheers reached him, Michael hid his smile behind a grief-stricken expression.

“If you wanted a peaceful, better world, you should have uprooted them completely from the start.”
“...You don’t mean—”
“Considering they were deranged fanatics, it was a perfectly reasonable deal.
I wanted a price paid for ignoring my warning.
They wanted weapons for revenge.”
Now I understood.
The real cause of this sudden Monster Wave.
Why the madman in front of me could admit to it so openly.
Borrow another’s knife to kill.
The instant it all fell into place—
Fwoosh.
My vision burned hot.
Three jiazi of Scorching Yang Qi surged from my dantian, transformed into lava, and flowed through my limbs and bones.
I was ready.
From the moment I had first faced him, my mind had been searching without pause for the best way to move.
One step.
That was all it would take.
The instant I planted my foot, the distance between us would vanish.
Then I could shut that bullshit-spouting mouth with my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist.
No.
I had to.
For the innocent people killed by another human being, not a monster.
And to remove the cause of an even greater disaster before it struck.
But—
Grab.
Two hands seized my shoulders, and a familiar voice struck my ears.
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung!”
“People are watching.
Not now.”
Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King.
They had to be holding back their own anger.
As I thought of them, the fury boiling inside me began to settle.
I knew they were right.
Attacking the bastard in front of me would be easy.
Dealing with what came afterward would be difficult, even for me.
I have no evidence.
Nothing that would convince the public I’m justified.
To the rest of the world, Michael Silbert was a hero of the Great Cataclysm who had defeated a terrorist bent on revenge.
Whether or not I could kill him, attacking him here would get me branded a public enemy—even if this were Murim rather than the modern world.
And that was probably...
Exactly what he wants.
Cheon Taemin, the beginning and end of Ares Guild, had been unconscious for some time.
What would happen if I fell now?
Even if I killed him here, I couldn’t take responsibility for what followed.
Our greatest enemy stood before me, but there were others who had yet to show themselves.
By the time I reached that thought, both my head and my heart had gone cold.
Hssss.
The aura I had built up, ready to burst, subsided.
Michael Silbert sighed softly.
“What a shame.
You looked much better when you were full of youthful fire.”
“Shut up before I tear your mouth apart.”
“If it were that easy to tear my mouth apart, someone would have done it hundreds of times by now.
But do you know something?”
A faint smile touched his lips.
“One day, I noticed that everyone who had said something like that to me had vanished without a trace.
I know a more certain way of dealing with them than tearing their mouths apart.”
“So be grateful you have good friends today.
You’re lucky they’re so capable, too.
Wouldn’t you agree?”
He was speaking to me, but he was looking past my shoulder.
That strange look brought my dulled sense of danger snapping back.
The Skeleton King.
Magic Johnson had given him a clean new identity, and he was working as a Hunter with Peace Guild.
Even so, it would be a problem if he drew the wrong kind of attention.
Michael Silbert was that difficult an opponent.
The moment a weakness appeared, he would pounce without mercy and tear into it.
Should I have left him behind?
The thought had barely crossed my mind when Michael’s attention shifted.
“So you’re the young Vice Guild Master of Ares Guild I’ve heard about.
How is your maternal grandfather?”
Team Leader Choi answered in an icy voice.
“He’s well.
I can’t say how he’ll react when I tell him what happened to the Paris branch.”
“I regret how things turned out myself.
I have great respect for your grandfather.
I hope you’ll put in a good word for me.”
“I certainly intend to tell him exactly what I saw and heard.”
There was not a trace of hesitation in his answer.
Michael Silbert was gazing at Team Leader Choi when—
Whoosh!
Whoosh!
A group raced across the ruins, cutting through the air.
At their head was Huginn, the messenger who had visited Ares Guild not long ago.
He spared us a glance, then hurried to Michael and bowed.
“Guild Master, everything is ready.”
“The casualty count first.”
“Approximately three hundred.
We’ve rescued forty-five survivors.”
“That’s enough for now.
Have people gathered?”
“Not only the nearby citizens.
Every reporter in Paris is waiting for you.”
“Faster than I expected.”
“We were fortunate.
The foreign press was already on alert because of the release of the new Mana Cultivation Method.”
“And the CCTV footage?”
“We secured it immediately.
It captured everything from beginning to end: the terrorist carrying out a suicide attack with bombs and unrefined Magic Gems, and Odin Guild suppressing the Monster Wave.”
At first, I hadn’t understood what Huginn meant by ready.
As I listened, my mind went cold.
This is...
Meticulous.
The unveiling of a new Mana Cultivation Method.
The attack on the Paris branch and the Monster Wave, carried out by a Middle Eastern terrorist seeking revenge.
Now a press conference with the world’s attention on it.
Dozens of gears, large and small, meshing without a fraction of an inch out of place.
Every part of their plan was moving as intended.
That was why they could discuss it openly in front of us.
They knew we had no way to stop the gears once they were turning.
Even if we shouted the truth for three days and three nights in front of the countless cameras camped out in the distance, no one would believe us anyway.
The worst part was that those madmen were right.
Force alone could not change that reality.
“I’m sorry, but I must be going.
A great many people are waiting for me.”
Michael Silbert acknowledged me, Team Leader Choi, and finally the Skeleton King with a glance before slowly turning away.
Then he stopped and added, “You’ll be busy from now on.
Far busier than you expect.”
Grind.
I watched him walk away, clenching my fist with all my strength.
But I could not bring myself to strike.
Not long afterward, I understood what he meant.
Ding.
System A sudden Quest, Chain of Terror Attacks, has been generated!
You cannot choose whether to accept this Quest.
The System will force it to proceed!
It was January.
The joy of the New Year had not yet faded.
Winter turned red.
“It has begun.”
At Huginn’s low voice beside his ear, Michael Silbert calmly asked:
“Where this time?”
“London.”
“The old king will be furious.”
“Buckingham Palace should be fine.
London Bridge will collapse instead.”
Michael gave a soft laugh at his subordinate’s dry joke.
“Once London is done... eight to go.”
“Yes.”
Huginn had brought ten people back from the desert.
Every one of them was a deranged fanatic and a seasoned Hunter.
They would carry out their missions without a hitch.
Their bombs would bring down buildings.
Their unrefined Magic Gems would be enough to shatter people’s hopes.
And our Odin Guild will piece that shattered hope back together.
Everything was ready.
He had reached this position through countless sacrifices and effort.
He could tolerate neither a single mistake nor failure.
As the reporters drew closer and the citizens’ cheers reached him, Michael hid his smile behind a grief-stricken expression.

chapters.title: Chapter 738
paragraphs: There was a strange magic in the words New Year.
The excitement of beginning another year. The vague hope that things would be better than they had been the year before.
But one day in January, before people had even turned the first page of their new calendars, that excitement and hope collapsed in an instant.
“Breaking news. Just one hour after our report from Paris, a second Monster Wave has struck London, United Kingdom. Central London is in chaos, and King Philip II of the United Kingdom has...”
“More breaking news! Another Monster Wave has struck Mumbai, India! This is the third Monster Wave in a single day, something unprecedented since the Great Cataclysm...”
“Oh my God. Can you see this? Rio de Janeiro’s landmark, Christ the Redeemer—Cristo Redentor—is falling!”
It was the beginning of a catastrophe.

First, France’s Luxembourg Gardens were stained with blood. Then London Bridge, which had stood through a long and storied history, collapsed. And Brazil’s colossal statue of Jesus, weighing over six hundred tons, toppled over, crushing buildings and people beneath it.
Rumble, rumble, rumble!
The ground shook with a deafening roar.
Beyond the flames that surged up from the explosion, those who could barely keep their feet heard something growl.
—Grrr...
Monster Waves.
The name had become synonymous with disaster. Legions of monsters tore through space and swept in every direction like a wave.
—Kraaaargh!
“M-Monsters!”
“Get away!”
“Aaaah!”
Screams filled the forest of skyscrapers that civilization had raised.
Some people fled. Some were seized by monsters, torn apart, and killed. Others raised shining weapons and fought against creatures that did not belong to this world.
“Formation! Don’t retreat!”
“Ranged units, fire!”
Boom! Boom! KABOOM!
Humans and monsters. Monsters and humans.
The two species, incapable of coexisting from the start, charged at one another. The flames that had begun in Paris spread across the world.
[Red Square in Moscow stained with blood by monsters]
[Disaster strikes China once again—the Forbidden City engulfed in flames]
[Five Monster Waves in a single day. Upon hearing the news, Pope Urban VIII says, “O God.”]
[The sixth Monster Wave strikes New York. Wall Street in shock.]
[Tokyo Tower seized by flying monsters. Crashed Air Self-Defense Force aircraft cause secondary damage.]

[Odin Guild Master Michael Silbert, who swiftly suppressed the first Monster Wave, releases CCTV footage obtained in Paris: “This is not merely a disaster. It is clearly a terrorist attack with a purpose.”]
Major cities home to millions—some to more than ten million—were thrown into chaos.
People watched one shocking report after another on their televisions and smartphones, too stunned to speak.
Disaster.
It was the only word for what was happening.
At the same time, the fear spreading like a plague paralyzed people’s reason.
“Hello? You saw the news, right? I’m coming to pick you up from school right now, so...”
“Hey, what are you doing?”
“Can’t you see? Packing my things.”
“What are you talking about? You’ve still got hours before you can leave work.”
“Fuck, does that matter right now? I’m going to make sure my family’s safe.”
“Hey, hey! Manager Kim!”
No one could predict a Monster Wave any more than they could predict a natural disaster. People dropped what they were doing and moved as if in a daze.
Toward the homes where their families waited. Or toward emergency shelters where they might have a slightly better chance of surviving.
Offices emptied, most work and road traffic ground to a halt, and people crowding onto the subways could not put down their phones.
What weighed them down now was an extreme fear and anxiety they could not see.
A Monster Wave might strike right where they stood. They—or someone they loved—might die because of it.
Wheeeeeeeen.
“Temporary state of emergency. This is a temporary state of emergency. Residents living nearby are advised to prepare for any eventuality and proceed to an emergency shelter...”
Countries around the world declared states of emergency at the same time.
Sirens sounded without pause in the streets. Soldiers armed with heavy weapons and Hunters called up on short notice waited tensely for instructions from their governments.
They waited until the sun—or the moon—disappeared from the sky above them, according to each country’s time zone.
At last, their governments made another announcement.
“The temporary state of emergency has been lifted.”
Only twenty-four hours had passed since the first Monster Wave struck Paris. The disaster that had seemed as if it might last until the end of the world finally ended in Cairo, Egypt.
It left behind a horrifying, unprecedented record: ten Monster Waves in a single day.
Then the hero who had successfully stopped five of them stepped before countless cameras.
“Odin Guild will continue to do its duty as your sword and shield.”
Michael Silbert.
As people watched him shed hot tears while mourning the souls of the fallen, they cried along with him.
They cheered for the hero who had saved so many lives, and for Odin Guild.
No—not everyone.
Bang!
More than a dozen holographic televisions crumbled to dust with a deafening crash.
I stared at the empty air where a man’s face had appeared only moments ago. Then I suddenly opened my mouth.
“Should I apologize?”
Team Leader Choi shook his head from the nearby sofa.
“It’s fine. If you hadn’t stepped in, I would have smashed them myself.”
He wasn’t exaggerating or being polite.
I looked at his clenched fist, white with the force of his grip. Drops of blood fell from it, along with the green monster blood he had not yet wiped away.
Drip. Drip.
The white wool carpet was gradually becoming stained red and green, but no one in the room cared.
Everything around me felt cold and empty.
They got us. Completely.
Ten.
Ten Monster Waves, and we hadn’t stopped a single one. No—perhaps it was more accurate to say we couldn’t have stopped them.
They planned it that way from the start.
It was impossible to stop Monster Waves in major cities thousands, even tens of thousands, of kilometers apart.
Even if Magic Johnson had been with us, it would have made no difference.
The Monster Waves that occurred today had been planned terrorist attacks from beginning to end—bombs detonating without regard for either time or place.
By the time we heard the news and arrived, all that awaited us were more ruins and more bodies.
There was one slight difference between the Monster Wave in Paris and those that followed: where they struck.
They weren’t targeting Ares Guild’s overseas branches.
The terrorists working with Michael Silbert had gone to all kinds of places. Tourist attractions packed with crowds. The headquarters of major corporations everyone knew by name.
But more often than anything else, they had targeted branches of major Guilds like Ares.
“Why?”
Team Leader Choi looked up at my abrupt question. I added one word.
“The targets.”
That was explanation enough. Team Leader Choi stared into empty space with hollow eyes, then suddenly opened his mouth.
“Isolation.”
“Isolation?”
“Yes. Isolating Ares Guild. That must be what Michael Silbert wants.”
“But why do it like the Paris branch...?”
I stopped.
Thoughts raced through my tangled mind. Somewhere among them was an answer I had missed.
The Middle Eastern terrorist group.
The men working with Michael Silbert had not finished their mission.
The final strike that would bring this horrific day to a close—the keen, ice-cold blade that would isolate Ares Guild from the entire world—was rushing toward us.
Perhaps even now.
Step. Step.
Footsteps echoed unusually loudly through the darkness.
Perhaps it was because there were several dozen people. Perhaps it was because they were crossing a dark cave. One thing, at least, was certain.
No one knew this place existed, and no one could find their way here.
Step.
The footsteps, which had seemed as though they would go on forever, stopped together.
Something stirred in the pitch-black darkness.
“Inshallah.”
The word sounded as though it had been whispered into their ears. Several dozen people dropped to their knees and prostrated themselves.
Then they opened their mouths and answered in unison.
“Inshallah.”
God willing.
It was an invocation that bound them together and a prayer that reminded them of God’s greatness. The figure stirring beyond the darkness finally emerged.
Swish.
A long robe brushed the ground. The people bowed their heads lower and murmured as one.
“This lowly servant of Allah humbly greets the great Prophet.”
The Prophet.
To them, even the title of a being whose face they dared not look upon was sacred and untouchable.
“Raise your heads.”
The voice gave no hint of age or gender. The people trembled.
Then they pressed their faces to the ground and answered.
“How could these lowly servants dare look upon the great Prophet?”
“Please withdraw your command.”
Whoosh.
A gust of wind came from somewhere and enveloped them.
Then the Prophet’s voice, mingled with the wind, reached their ears.
“What became of them?”
Everyone knew whom the Prophet meant.
The old man prostrated at the very front opened his mouth.
“They completed the missions entrusted to them and returned to God’s embrace.”
The Prophet gave a slight nod.
“Inshallah. As was only right.”
“Inshallah.”
Ten warriors had crossed the desert and scattered across the five oceans and six continents. As warriors of God, they had completed their missions and returned to the embrace of God.
Now it was time to claim the blood price.
The Prophet spoke in a mysterious voice.
“Let the whole world know what brought about all this disaster.”

chapters.title: Chapter 739
paragraphs: Ten Monster Waves in a single day were enough to plunge the world into shock and terror.

Worse, they had struck capitals and major cities whose names were known around the world. Several major Guilds, led by Odin Guild, had swiftly suppressed the Monster Waves, but the damage was immense. The confirmed death toll alone had reached several thousand.
People kept their senses on high alert in their homes or emergency shelters, and Michael Silbert did not miss the opportunity to seize the attention of the entire world.
“This is footage Odin Guild obtained during the first Monster Wave in Paris.”
When the CCTV footage was released, it sent another shock through the world.
Odin Guild Master Michael Silbert: “Before it became a Monster Wave, this was a meticulously planned terrorist attack.”
Not a natural disaster, but a man-made one
A calamity born of malice
Ten killers armed with bombs and Magic Gems. Who are the suicide terrorists in the released CCTV footage?
Experts analyzing the CCTV footage: “Each carried several unrefined A-grade Magic Gems and targeted areas near Gates with high concentrations of magical power.”
The world shudders at a horrifying déjà vu: “Remember what happened in South Korea.”
Bringing in bombs and unrefined A-grade Magic Gems: a clear violation of international law
Bombs and Magic Gems traced to Africa and the Middle East
News reports poured in from every direction.

Once it became clear that the Monster Waves had not been unstoppable natural disasters but tragedies caused by terrorism, people were consumed by anger and emptiness, and the internet reached saturation point.
└ I’ve got no words. These people are seriously insane. └ Are they out of their fucking minds?
└ The truth must be brought to light. Every last one of them must be hanged.

└ I saw a foreign article mentioning South Korea. Is that about the Go Jun incident a little while ago? └ Yeah. And now the people who hate Korea are foaming at the mouth, saying Korea’s the root of all evil. └ What the fuck? They wouldn’t even be alive if it weren’t for Cheon Taemin. └ What countries are these people from? └ Jjajang. Wasabi. └ Oh. └ Japan’s always been like that, but what’s with those Chinese bastards? Have they already forgotten Lord Fuck helped them? └ “China.” └ That one word says it all. └ To be fair, maybe because he helped them before, it’s nowhere near as bad in China as it is in Japan. Some people are even tracing the IQs of commenters insulting Lord Fuck so they can teach them a lesson. └ My IQ’s 110. Can they track my location from that? └ I’ve seen people bashing Korea on foreign forums too. Cheon Taemin and Jin Taekyung worked hard to raise Korea’s standing, and that bastard Go Jun went and ruined it all. └ Jin Taekyung raised Korea’s standing? You sure? Funny, I haven’t seen him once today wwwwwww. └ Haven’t seen your Air Self-Defense Force since a Wyvern beat the shit out of it, either. I did get a good look at Tokyo Tower collapsing, though. └ Welcome, wasabi. └ Does Lord Fuck have ten bodies, you Japanese bastard? Watch some TV. Taekyung ran himself ragged today. He was a step late, but seeing him try to save even one person somehow really moved me. └ So criticizing Korea automatically makes someone Japanese now, lol? Unfortunately, I’m Korean. └ If you want to keep pretending you’re Korean, take the W key off your keyboard.

└ There was no point paying attention to trolls. The most important thing now was finding out who the terrorists belonged to and why they had committed such acts. └ The terrorists are all from the Arab world, so it’s obvious. It has to be either Al-Qaeda or IS. └ If it’s so obvious, why haven’t the countries that were hit issued a joint statement or an official announcement? They need to verify it first. Al-Qaeda and IS have both taken serious losses lately. └ I agree with the comment above. A few weeks ago, their main bases were completely wrecked and their leader was killed and replaced.
Everyone knew about the bloodbath that had swept through the Middle East and Africa.

A mysterious group of vigilantes had appeared. No one knew their faces, their names, or even their genders. They had beheaded the leaders of the terrorist and rebel groups. With their leadership gone in an instant, the two factions had torn themselves apart in fierce internal struggles, suffered enormous losses, and finally raised the white flag.

└ Doesn’t that make it even more obvious? A little while ago, they practically surrendered and begged people to stop, saying they wouldn’t commit any more terrorist attacks. The world shudders at a horrifying déjà vu: “Remember what happened in South Korea.”

chapters.title: Chapter 740
paragraphs: Circulating qi did more than increase internal energy.
It cleared away the waste that naturally built up in the body and calmed the mind. And in a state of such deep concentration, all five senses were heightened to their limits.
What’s that...?
Step. Step.
Someone’s footsteps sounded like thunder.
Before long, I realized who the uninvited guest pacing outside the door was and brought my internal energy under control.
Chime.
The System notification announcing the end of my qi circulation had barely sounded when the doorknob turned behind me.
Click.
A rich scent drifted through the gap as the door eased open. I let out a long breath, bringing everything to a close, and spoke.
“I thought I told everyone to stay out until I came out on my own... Is it because you’re a monster that you can’t understand human speech? Or do you just not want to?”
The uninvited guest hesitated, then cleared his throat. It was the Skeleton King.
“Ahem. How did you know it was this body?”
“Your presence.”
“My presence?”
“Yeah. You don’t breathe. Probably because you’re already dead.”
“...That makes a strange amount of sense, but I don’t like it.”
“I’m not trying to make you happy.”
I pulled on the tracksuit I had tossed aside nearby and turned around. The Skeleton King stood there like a butler, holding a gleaming silver tray.
“So why are you here?”
Normally, he would have been sulking by now, his lips sticking out a good five feet.
But today was different. He kept stealing glances at me as he lowered the tray to the floor.
“Eat. This body brought it here personally for you.”
“I told you not to bring me food.”
“But you haven’t eaten in over three days.”
Over three days?

I looked around. The room was sealed on all sides, without so much as a window. I had come in without my smartphone, and whether it was that or the fact that I’d had no mind to care, I’d lost track of time.
Has it been that long already?
Humans were strange. The moment I realized how many days had passed, hunger caught up with me.
But...
Did I even have the right to feel hungry?
Thousands had died. Tens of thousands had been injured. I didn’t know what kind of lives they’d led, but most of them must have done nothing wrong.
Those people had suffered because of what I’d done. They’d died, been hurt, lost family and friends they loved.
People who had hailed me as a hero only a short while ago had begun turning against me, one by one. Their condemnation had reached the people around me, too.
All because they were close to me.
What went wrong? Where did it start?
I’d shut myself in this room to answer the question that wouldn’t leave my mind. I’d spent each day without food or sleep, circulating qi and turning it over in my thoughts.
At last, I’d found an answer.
Not one that would put everything right. Just an insight that let me forget for a little while.
“Smells good.”
“Huh?”
“Not you. The food.”
The Skeleton King seemed to buffer for a moment before answering.
“Uh, yeah. It’s doenjang jjigae and braised short ribs.”
I could tell who had made it just from the smell. Picturing my mother anxiously preparing meals for me these past few days, I lifted the lid from the tray.
Click.
I stared blankly at the food as steam rose from it. Then I scooped up a spoonful of doenjang jjigae, something I had not seen in a long time.
The moment I put it in my mouth, I spat it right back out.
Ptooey.
“Wh—what? Why?”
What the hell was this?
I looked back and forth between the flustered Skeleton King and the doenjang jjigae before opening my mouth hesitantly.
“Who made this?”
“Your younger sister.”
“...Ah. Right.”
“Is something wrong?”
Was something wrong? Yes. Seriously wrong.
But instead of answering, I let out a quiet laugh. I didn’t know why. I just did.
“I’ll eat before I go.”
“What?”
“I said I’ll eat this, then go. I need a shower, too.”
The Skeleton King blinked at me for a while, as if he hadn’t understood. Then he nodded hurriedly.
“Oh? Oh, all right. Then this body will...”
“Yeah. See you later.”
He eased the door shut and slipped away like a thief. Another inexplicable laugh escaped me.
I set down my spoon, picked up a piece of braised short rib, and took a big bite.
Thankfully, my mother had made the ribs.
“There were vicious dogs going around biting people, so I beat them senseless. Now two mad dogs have shown up.”
Those were my first words to Team Leader Choi in days. His lips moved as though he had been about to say something, but he nodded instead.
“That’s right. And those two mad dogs bit even more people.”
“Do you think it’s my fault too, Team Leader Choi?”
“Mad dogs are mad dogs. The timing and the excuse may change, but they would have bared their teeth at people sooner or later.”
“But I’m the one who gave them the opportunity.”
“If you insist on blaming yourself, say we. You didn’t do it alone.”
“That’s right. This body also achieved a great feat in the desert.”
At the Skeleton King’s sudden interruption, Team Leader Choi shrugged.
“So he says.”
“I’m not blaming myself. I just think I need to be clear about that much.”
Every incident had a cause and an effect. With so many people dead or injured, I couldn’t pretend I had no part in the cause.
I had no intention of trying.
“I understand why people condemn me. And I’m grateful to the ones who support me.”
“Is that all?”
“No. The most important part is still left.”
I went on calmly.
“No matter what the world says, I’m going to catch those mad dogs.”
The Skeleton King’s eyes gleamed. A faint smile appeared on Team Leader Choi’s face.
“You found your own answer.”
“It’s not a complete answer. But it’s enough of a reason to keep going, isn’t it?”
“It is. Then I can give you a few pieces of news with a lighter heart.”
“A few pieces of news...?”
“I’d been gathering information on Michael Silbert and Odin Guild since before this happened. I received the results recently.”
Team Leader Choi had been watching the other major Guilds since before the Mana Cultivation Method was released. Given how thorough he was, of course he had.
“What did you find? Good news, I hope.”
“Unfortunately, some of it is bad. Which would you like first?”
“How much worse could things get? Give me the bad news.”
Team Leader Choi gave a short laugh and took a thick stack of documents from a drawer.
“I did my best to organize it, but there’s still an enormous amount.”
“What’s this?”
“Information on Odin Guild’s assets and businesses. Much of it isn’t publicly known.”
“They’re held under other names?”

“Yes. On paper, they have no connection to Odin Guild. In practice, they’re run much like its subsidiaries. Other major Guilds and corporations do the same thing, but Odin’s scale is in another league.”
I knew next to nothing about this sort of thing, but the thickness of the stack told me plenty. I skimmed pages full of words and sentences I could barely understand, searching for a comparison.
“Bigger than Ares Guild?”
“You would have to combine Ares Guild and Peace Guild, then add three or four major Guilds on top of that.”
“Holy shit.”

“Count just the Gates Odin Guild controls this way, and there are more than two hundred worldwide. They hold permanent leases, so they effectively own them. Those Gates produce an enormous quantity of Magic Gems.”
Even if a considerable number of those holdings were controlled through unofficial channels, having control of around two hundred Gates put Odin Guild on the level of a small country.
No. Given the strength of its Hunters, it might be more powerful than one.
I wish he were just a mad dog.
Michael Silbert wasn’t merely a mad dog. He was a Tosa mastiff among fighting dogs, and he was clever to boot.
But he was also a bastard I absolutely had to beat to death.
That thought brought another to mind.
“Then is it possible that the Magic Gems from those Gates were used in this terrorist attack without being refined?”
“No. At least, not according to the documents.”
“According to the documents?”

“As you know, Michael Silbert is an extremely thorough person. He had no reason to take the risk of smuggling Magic Gems, and even if he had, he would not have left any gaps in the records. The Magic Gems used in the terrorist attacks most likely came out of the Middle East or Africa.”
That made sense.
The Middle East and Africa had been hotbeds of terrorism and civil war since before the Great Cataclysm. Even now, there were people somewhere in those regions fighting bloody battles.
No one knew exactly how many Magic Gems came out of Gates held by terrorists and rebels, or how many of those Gems remained unrefined.
Besides, Michael Silbert wasn’t alone. He had a reliable accomplice who was every bit as much a mad dog.
“The Prophet.”
At the name that slipped from my mouth, Team Leader Choi nodded with a grim expression.
“I searched thoroughly for information on the Prophet as well.”
“What kind of bastard is the Prophet?”
I genuinely wanted to know who this madman was—the one who had beheaded the leaders of two major terrorist organizations, united their scattered followers, and shaken the world.
Team Leader Choi’s answer was nothing like what I’d hoped to hear.
“We don’t know.”
“You don’t know?”
“No. Even allowing for the circumstances, there’s no information about the Prophet at all. He vanished completely after that declaration.”
“Wait. Even the United States doesn’t know?”
“Not just the United States. Even with the entire world searching, the situation is still the same.”
I blinked and thought.
How is that possible?
The madman calling himself the Prophet had thrown the United States and the rest of the world into turmoil. How could he vanish right under everyone’s noses?
“You’re not hiding what you know to protect classified information, are you?”
“I spoke with Chuck Hagel recently. He swore to God he didn’t know where the Prophet was.”
Chuck Hagel had been with us in the desert. He was also the United States Secretary of Defense, not just an S-rank Hunter.
Unless he was lying, if even the Secretary of Defense did not know, then the Prophet really must have shot straight up into the sky.
Who the hell is he?
I frowned. Team Leader Choi went on.

“And there’s one more thing. Mr. Johnson contacted us. He said he had found someone among the other Grand Mages who was likely to have been in contact with Michael Silbert. He said we would probably be able to learn more vital information through that person.”
This, at least, was good news.
I hadn’t heard the Grand Mage’s name yet, but he must know something about Michael Silbert’s true nature. He had personally created Ares Guild’s Area A and knew about Cheon Taemin’s condition.
One of only three Grand Mages in the world. He would give us a new lead.
Or so I thought.
Then, not long afterward, Team Leader Choi’s phone rang. I heard Magic Johnson’s voice.
“Damn it. He’s dead.”

At last, I’d found an answer.
Not one that would put everything right.
Just an insight that let me forget for a little while.
“Smells good.”
“Huh?”
“Not you.
The food.”
The Skeleton King seemed to buffer for a moment before answering.
“Uh, yeah.
It’s doenjang jjigae and braised short ribs.”
I could tell who had made it just from the smell.
Picturing my mother anxiously preparing meals for me these past few days, I lifted the lid from the tray.
Click.
I stared blankly at the food as steam rose from it.
Then I scooped up a spoonful of doenjang jjigae, something I had not seen in a long time.
The moment I put it in my mouth, I spat it right back out.
Ptooey.
“Wh—what?
Why?”
What the hell was this?
I looked back and forth between the flustered Skeleton King and the doenjang jjigae before opening my mouth hesitantly.
“Who made this?”
“Your younger sister.”
Right.”
“Is something wrong?”
Was something wrong?
Yes.
Seriously wrong.
But instead of answering, I let out a quiet laugh.
I didn’t know why.
I just did.
“I’ll eat before I go.”
“What?”
“I said I’ll eat this, then go.
I need a shower, too.”
The Skeleton King blinked at me for a while, as if he hadn’t understood.
Then he nodded hurriedly.
“Oh?
Oh, all right.
Then this body will...”
“Yeah.
See you later.”
He eased the door shut and slipped away like a thief.
Another inexplicable laugh escaped me.
I set down my spoon, picked up a piece of braised short rib, and took a big bite.
Thankfully, my mother had made the ribs.
“There were vicious dogs going around biting people, so I beat them senseless.
Now two mad dogs have shown up.”
Those were my first words to Team Leader Choi in days.
His lips moved as though he had been about to say something, but he nodded instead.
“That’s right.
And those two mad dogs bit even more people.”
“Do you think it’s my fault too, Team Leader Choi?”
“Mad dogs are mad dogs.
The timing and the excuse may change, but they would have bared their teeth at people sooner or later.”
“But I’m the one who gave them the opportunity.”
“If you insist on blaming yourself, say we.
You didn’t do it alone.”
“That’s right.
This body also achieved a great feat in the desert.”
At the Skeleton King’s sudden interruption, Team Leader Choi shrugged.
“So he says.”
“I’m not blaming myself.
I just think I need to be clear about that much.”
Every incident had a cause and an effect.
With so many people dead or injured, I couldn’t pretend I had no part in the cause.
I had no intention of trying.
“I understand why people condemn me.
And I’m grateful to the ones who support me.”
“Is that all?”
“No.
The most important part is still left.”
I went on calmly.
“No matter what the world says, I’m going to catch those mad dogs.”
The Skeleton King’s eyes gleamed.
A faint smile appeared on Team Leader Choi’s face.
“You found your own answer.”
“It’s not a complete answer.
But it’s enough of a reason to keep going, isn’t it?”
“It is.
Then I can give you a few pieces of news with a lighter heart.”
“A few pieces of news...?”
“I’d been gathering information on Michael Silbert and Odin Guild since before this happened.
I received the results recently.”
Team Leader Choi had been watching the other major Guilds since before the Mana Cultivation Method was released.
Given how thorough he was, of course he had.
“What did you find?
Good news, I hope.”
“Unfortunately, some of it is bad.
Which would you like first?”
“How much worse could things get?
Give me the bad news.”
Team Leader Choi gave a short laugh and took a thick stack of documents from a drawer.
“I did my best to organize it, but there’s still an enormous amount.”
“What’s this?”
“Information on Odin Guild’s assets and businesses.
Much of it isn’t publicly known.”
“They’re held under other names?”
“Yes.
On paper, they have no connection to Odin Guild.
In practice, they’re run much like its subsidiaries.
Other major Guilds and corporations do the same thing, but Odin’s scale is in another league.”
I knew next to nothing about this sort of thing, but the thickness of the stack told me plenty.
I skimmed pages full of words and sentences I could barely understand, searching for a comparison.
“Bigger than Ares Guild?”
“You would have to combine Ares Guild and Peace Guild, then add three or four major Guilds on top of that.”
“Holy shit.”
“Count just the Gates Odin Guild controls this way, and there are more than two hundred worldwide.
They hold permanent leases, so they effectively own them.
Those Gates produce an enormous quantity of Magic Gems.”
Even if a considerable number of those holdings were controlled through unofficial channels, having control of around two hundred Gates put Odin Guild on the level of a small country.
No.
Given the strength of its Hunters, it might be more powerful than one.
I wish he were just a mad dog.
Michael Silbert wasn’t merely a mad dog.
He was a Tosa mastiff among fighting dogs, and he was clever to boot.
But he was also a bastard I absolutely had to beat to death.
That thought brought another to mind.
“Then is it possible that the Magic Gems from those Gates were used in this terrorist attack without being refined?”
“No.
At least, not according to the documents.”
“According to the documents?”
“As you know, Michael Silbert is an extremely thorough person.
He had no reason to take the risk of smuggling Magic Gems, and even if he had, he would not have left any gaps in the records.
The Magic Gems used in the terrorist attacks most likely came out of the Middle East or Africa.”
That made sense.
The Middle East and Africa had been hotbeds of terrorism and civil war since before the Great Cataclysm.
Even now, there were people somewhere in those regions fighting bloody battles.
No one knew exactly how many Magic Gems came out of Gates held by terrorists and rebels, or how many of those Gems remained unrefined.
Besides, Michael Silbert wasn’t alone.
He had a reliable accomplice who was every bit as much a mad dog.
“The Prophet.”
At the name that slipped from my mouth, Team Leader Choi nodded with a grim expression.
“I searched thoroughly for information on the Prophet as well.”
“What kind of bastard is the Prophet?”
I genuinely wanted to know who this madman was—the one who had beheaded the leaders of two major terrorist organizations, united their scattered followers, and shaken the world.
Team Leader Choi’s answer was nothing like what I’d hoped to hear.
“We don’t know.”
“You don’t know?”
“No.
Even allowing for the circumstances, there’s no information about the Prophet at all.
He vanished completely after that declaration.”
“Wait.
Even the United States doesn’t know?”
“Not just the United States.
Even with the entire world searching, the situation is still the same.”
I blinked and thought.
How is that possible?
The madman calling himself the Prophet had thrown the United States and the rest of the world into turmoil.
How could he vanish right under everyone’s noses?
“You’re not hiding what you know to protect classified information, are you?”
“I spoke with Chuck Hagel recently.
He swore to God he didn’t know where the Prophet was.”
Chuck Hagel had been with us in the desert.
He was also the United States Secretary of Defense, not just an S-rank Hunter.
Unless he was lying, if even the Secretary of Defense did not know, then the Prophet really must have shot straight up into the sky.
Who the hell is he?
I frowned.
Team Leader Choi went on.
“And there’s one more thing.
Mr.
Johnson contacted us.
He said he had found someone among the other Grand Mages who was likely to have been in contact with Michael Silbert.
He said we would probably be able to learn more vital information through that person.”
This, at least, was good news.
I hadn’t heard the Grand Mage’s name yet, but he must know something about Michael Silbert’s true nature.
He had personally created Ares Guild’s Area A and knew about Cheon Taemin’s condition.
One of only three Grand Mages in the world.
He would give us a new lead.
Or so I thought.
Then, not long afterward, Team Leader Choi’s phone rang.
I heard Magic Johnson’s voice.
“Damn it.
He’s dead.”

chapters.title: Chapter 741
paragraphs: “Damn it. He’s dead.”
I’d hoped I was wrong.
But the unease I’d felt at those few words over the phone had been right on the mark.
“Sorry, but you need to come right away. We have to find as many clues as we can before this case slips out of our hands...”
“Where are you?”
There was no time to hesitate.
We headed for the coordinates Magic Johnson had given us as fast as we could. After several long-distance Teleports in succession, we arrived on a mountain blanketed in white.
Crunch.
The snow that had lain there for ages crumbled beneath my feet.
The breathtaking scenery of the Alps, something I had only ever seen on the internet, unfolded before my eyes. But I had no time to admire the view.
And neither did—
“Intruders spotted!”
—the group guarding the area nearby.
“Stop! Stop!”
“Shooters, ready!”
Chk-chk-chk!
At the urgent shouts, gun barrels and blades were pointed at us.
The soldiers and Hunters were heavily armed. I stopped, and a familiar voice came from among them.
“If you insist on attacking, I won’t stop you. But it would be in your best interest to check the intruders’ faces first.”
“One more step and we shoot... Mr. Johnson?”
“Don’t act rashly, Colonel. They’re my guests.”
A huge Black man walked past the middle-aged commander in a beret and stopped before us.
Fatigue and sorrow weighed on his face.
Magic Johnson, whom I had not seen for several weeks—no, several months—gave us a faint smile and greeted us.
“Long time no see, friends. How have you been?”
I smacked my lips bitterly and firmly grasped the hand he held out.
“Not well at all.”
“Who are the people outside? It looked like an even split between soldiers and Hunters.”
“Swiss Federal Police. This area’s under their jurisdiction, and I didn’t want to become a murder suspect just because I found the body first. Come on.”
Team Leader Choi, the Skeleton King, and I followed Magic Johnson.
We passed between the soldiers and Hunters watching us with equal parts wariness and curiosity, then entered a forest deep in snow. A faint sense of déjà vu stirred.
This is...
I closed my eyes and focused. As I slowly reached out, I felt an invisible ripple through the fierce snowstorm.
“Mana?”
Magic Johnson nodded.
“A barrier. Concealed well enough that even most S-rank Hunters wouldn’t notice it, and just as flawless as it is discreet.”
He wasn’t exaggerating.
Even the Skeleton King had barely noticed the barrier until Johnson pointed it out.
“Impressive work for a human. But not enough to fool this body’s keen gaze. After all, I am no ordinary S-rank Hunter. I am an exceptionally gifted—”
“Monster.”
The Skeleton King fell silent, crestfallen.
Having shut him up with one word, I studied the barrier and recalled something from not long ago.
It’s similar.
Just as a particular martial art left behind a specific trace, magic worked the same way.
The flow of mana was as distinctive as a fingerprint. I was sure of it.
No doubt about it. It feels like Area A.
Magic Johnson met my eyes, as if he’d read my mind.
“I’d been looking for people connected to Area A at your request, even before all this happened. But of everyone I know, only one person came to mind.”
I now knew who the Grand Mage who designed Area A was. I also knew he’d announced his retirement more than a decade ago and disappeared from public view.
“I didn’t expect him to be staying in a place like this. But had you been in contact with that person separately?”
“Not at all. He was quite eccentric and reclusive.”
“But we were friends. We were close enough that he could at least give me a hint about the hideout where he planned to stay someday.”
Whoosh.
Mana mingled with mana, and the snowstorm came to a stop amid a flash of pure white light.
No—the scenery had changed.
The vast snowfield was gone. We stood inside an enormous cave, its long passages winding like a maze.
“Follow me. Magic, including spatial movement, can’t be cast inside.”
We talked as we followed him through the cave.
Unsurprisingly, things hadn’t been going smoothly for Magic Johnson either.
“You’ve seen the news, so you know our L.A. branch was hit. It’s on the outskirts of the city, but there’s so much foot traffic around it that we couldn’t prevent casualties.”
Magic Johnson was a Grand Mage and the owner of the vast Wizard Guild.
Although it had been pushed out of the rankings several years ago, the Wizard Guild had once been one of the world’s top ten Guilds, even if only in last place.
Yet neither the Wizard Guild, with its many mages, nor Magic Johnson had been able to stop the planned terrorist attacks that unfolded with lightning speed.
“By the time I got there, it was too late. Afterward, I was swamped dealing with everything else.”
I didn’t ask what had kept him so busy. Everyone here knew.
The so-called “vigilante incident”—our campaign against the Middle Eastern terrorists and African rebel groups.

That campaign had become both the justification for these attacks and the means of carrying them out. Much of the public now blamed us for it. Magic Johnson had been one of the vigilantes, and he couldn’t escape the criticism.
None of us could. I’d simply taken the hardest hit from the media.
“I’m sorry.”
“What?”
“I felt I owed you an apology. If I hadn’t proposed it, the whole world wouldn’t be cursing us out right now...”
“Damn it. Is that what you’re talking about?”
Johnson stopped and shook his head.
“Listen, Jin. This isn’t your fault. You don’t need to apologize to me, either. Understand?”
“Of course, but—”
“Let me ask you something. If you could go back, what would you do? Leave those bastards alone?”
I didn’t need long to think. I’d turned that question over and over in a room where no light could reach me.
“No.”
“What about you two?”
Team Leader Choi and the Skeleton King looked at each other, then answered almost at the same time.
“Nothing would change. If anything, I’d make even more certain they were dealt with.”
“This body will kill that bastard called the Prophet without fail.”
“Good. Clear answers.”
Johnson shrugged at their different answers, which amounted to the same thing.
“And I’m saying this just in case, but no matter what people say about that incident, I don’t regret it in the slightest. Chuck Hagel feels the same way, even though he isn’t here right now.”
Chuck Hagel.
I could still picture him beating down terrorists while suffering through cigar withdrawal.
Team Leader Choi had mentioned on the way here that Chuck was facing plenty of trouble himself.
“How’s Chuck doing?”
“Not well.”
“That was quick.”

“Because it’s true. The external and internal pressure coming down on him is tremendous. At this rate, it wouldn’t be strange if he were dismissed from his position as Secretary of Defense before long.”
Team Leader Choi joined in, his voice calm.
“The pressure must be too much for even the President to shield him.”

“Chuck’s situation is different from yours. He’s a high-ranking official—the United States Secretary of Defense. The President may have tacitly approved what we did, but that only protected him while it stayed secret.”
“But the entire world found out. And it was revealed directly by a terrorist of historic proportions called the Prophet.”
“...Yeah. Thanks to some damn traitor.”
The operation had gone ahead with the President’s tacit approval. Our mission as “vigilantes” was never supposed to become public.
That was why I’d dared to act so boldly in the modern world, with all its restrictions. I’d trusted that the satellite surveillance system would be disrupted and every related record destroyed.
But information about us had leaked out in plain sight, and I vividly remembered what Michael Silbert had said amid the ruins of Paris.
I’ll give you one piece of advice. There are no perfect secrets in this world. Not even in the Pentagon.
The United States was still the world’s most powerful nation, and the Pentagon was its Department of Defense headquarters, reputed to have the tightest security in the country.
Yet information that should have been kept secret even within the Pentagon had made its way out.
So easily.
But...
With him involved, it’s no surprise.
I was taking it with a calm that surprised even me.
Because the opponent was Michael Silbert. He was stronger than any Hunter I had ever encountered—and even more insane than he was strong.
And then there was the unidentified madman called the Prophet.
No ordinary person could do this. No person could even try.
Even evil had its degrees.
In that sense, the path those bastards had taken had already crossed the line by an absurd distance.
Thousands were already dead, and more than ten times that number injured.

Not every crime committed throughout the world over the course of the week—including the day the Paris branch collapsed—could have been their doing, but it was obvious that they had exerted a considerable influence.
Fear paralyzed reason and gave rise to another kind of madness.

Along with the ten terrorist attacks accompanied by Monster Waves, the distribution of magical power continued to rise at an even steeper rate, and Mutated Gate phenomena were now occurring dozens of times a day.

Some terrified people were already speaking of the end of the world. With crosses hanging at their waists and microphones in their hands, they shouted about God’s mercy at the top of their lungs in the streets.
Just as their parents had done long ago.
But I wasn’t looking for God.
Those bastards were only human, not devils, and I was ready to bring them down.
There was only one problem...
The thread leading to one of them had been severed just like that.
As I muttered inwardly, I stopped walking. At some point, the long, winding passage of the cave had come to an end.
And waiting for us at the end was a corpse.
Every bone and scrap of skin on its body had dried up and shriveled tight, like a mummy.
“...What is this?”
Team Leader Choi’s voice came out like a groan.
At that moment—
Chime.
System A new Quest has been generated!
The clear chime rang out more ominously than ever.

chapters.title: Chapter 742
paragraphs: System A new Quest has been generated! An Unexpected Quest, Unknown Death, has been forcibly accepted! Quest Unknown Death The reclusive Grand Mage Siegfried Bassmann has died for an unknown reason. Yet everything has a cause. Discover how he died and who killed him. Grade: Supreme Peak Restriction: Jin Taekyung Mission: Reveal the truth behind his death (Incomplete) Reward: ??? Failure: ???
I stared at the Quest window floating in midair.
The name of the deceased in the first line of the description told me that this corpse, which had met such a gruesome end, belonged to one of only three Grand Mages in the entire world.
Siegfried Bassmann.
Siegfried, also known as the “Hero.” The greatest Hunter ever produced by Switzerland, a permanently neutral country, and a Grand Mage with exceptional talent for summoning and barrier magic.
If Magic Johnson was a War Mage who specialized in combat and killing, Siegfried was one of the few scholars who had devoted himself to the study of magic itself.
At least until today, when he was found dead in his own hideout.
“Was he like this when you arrived?”
Magic Johnson nodded, his expression grim.
“Yes. I could hardly believe it myself. I checked several times before I accepted that the body was Siegfried’s.”
“How often did you keep in touch?”

“Once or twice a year after he went into hiding. Even then, I’d have to contact him ten times or so before he answered, and it took him ages. This is my first time here. He was intensely private and hated visits like this.”
“Then the last time you heard from him was...”
“Hmm. About three years ago, I think.”
“Three years. I heard he went into hiding nearly ten years ago.”
“The last time we met, just before he retired, he gave me a communication artifact he’d made himself. Told me to use it if anything was truly urgent.”

I took the artifact Magic Johnson pulled from inside his clothes. It was a crystal ball about the size of an adult’s fist, and it held a considerable amount of mana—as if to prove a Grand Mage had made it.
Of course. Normal radio signals and communications would have been impossible inside a space surrounded by layers upon layers of barriers. He probably intended it that way.

I’d never met Siegfried Bassmann, but by all accounts he was a shut-in. He avoided attention of any kind, and once a subject caught his interest, he’d dig into it until he’d dissected every last part of it.

“I contacted him every Thanksgiving and Christmas, but he stopped answering three years ago. I knew what he was like, so I let it go. Being called a hero made him uncomfortable, and he hated attention from the press. Even after the Great Cataclysm ended, he’d sometimes disappear into his research for long stretches.”
I couldn’t make sense of it.
A Grand Mage who had gone into hiding to escape the public eye had died like this in his own refuge.
One thing, though, was certain.
“This wasn’t an ordinary natural death. Whatever killed him, a body couldn’t end up like this in just three years.”
Maybe not even in three hundred.
Would a shut-in Grand Mage whose hobby was magic research and whose specialty was staying home run his hideout on gas and electricity?
This enormous cavern, which could only be entered by breaking through its barriers, was filled with all kinds of magic. Everything, from the temperature to the humidity, was controlled perfectly.
And Siegfried’s body showed none of the rot or stench of ordinary decay.
It’s just... dried out. As if something sucked every bit of life from it.
I’d never seen a death this strange, even in Murim.
Which left me with more questions. How had he died in his own hideout? And how deeply was his death connected to my enemies?
“Michael Silbert. And The Prophet.”
The two likeliest suspects.
Magic Johnson understood what I meant. “If I had to choose one of them, I’d pick the first without hesitation.”
“Why?”

“Because we know there’s a connection between Michael and Siegfried. From everything we’ve seen, Michael Silbert must know Sky is unconscious. Otherwise, he’d never have joined forces with terrorists to pull off something this insane.”
It was a plausible theory. Siegfried had built Area A inside Ares Guild’s headquarters, and he could well have learned the truth about Cheon Taemin’s condition while doing it.
But...
“I’m asking because I don’t know, but was Siegfried close to Michael Silbert when he was alive?”
“That...”

“Unlikely. No, you might as well call it impossible. Very few people had any relationship with Siegfried, myself included. And there was only one person he ever said he truly respected.”

“Cheon Taemin.”

I’d heard the interview caused a stir at the time: it was unusual enough for him to speak to the press, let alone express such strong feelings about anyone.
“Perhaps... that’s why Lee Jungryong commissioned Siegfried to build Area A.”
Team Leader Choi spoke up suddenly, then continued slowly.
“Siegfried Bassmann was a master in that field, and he had very few personal relationships. On top of that, he deeply respected my maternal grandfather. He would have kept the secret.”
Magic Johnson gave a small nod.
“That’s true. Even I knew nothing about Area A, and I was one of the people closest to him. Hell, I never thought he’d accept a commission from anyone.”
“At least when it came to maintaining secrecy, Lee Jungryong’s judgment was accurate. But if the information wasn’t leaked, the question that remains is...”
“How did Michael Silbert find out?”
I muttered the question as I examined the body again, searching every inch for signs of torture. Even with every sense sharpened, I found nothing new.
If this wasn’t simply a lizard shedding its tail, then there had to be a reason he needed to be killed.
I couldn’t prove it yet, but Michael Silbert was still our likeliest suspect. Finding out what had happened here could be the first step toward bringing him down.
There’s something. There has to be...
I kept searching the body, repeating those words to myself. At last, frustrated, I looked up and saw someone standing nearby.
Or rather, a monster shaped like a person.
“Why are you standing there trying to look cool? You’ve been quiet this whole time.”
The Skeleton King stood with his arms crossed, deep in thought. He frowned.
“Silence, foolish human. This body was engaged in profound contemplation.”
“What kind of bullshit were you contemplating now?”
“Can you not feel it?”
I stopped. “Feel what?”
“This space. The concentration of magical power is higher here than elsewhere.”
If he’d said mana, I would have argued immediately. My Qi Sense was better than anyone else’s here, and I hadn’t noticed anything unusual.
But magical power was another matter. The Skeleton King was an S-rank monster. When it came to sensing magical power, even I couldn’t match him.
“Large human. Did you not feel it?”
Magic Johnson scratched the back of his head.
“I did, though not as clearly as you. I just didn’t think it was strange.”
“You are infinitely more foolish than this body. Why?”
“This isn’t just a house. It’s also a laboratory equipped with everything Siegfried could want. You could rummage through a single storage room and find mountains of monster corpses and Magic Gems.”
Oh. He had a point.
Just as filtering shit water wouldn’t make it perfectly clear, the same was true of Magic Gems and monster corpses. No matter how thoroughly they were purified, some magical power would remain.
Siegfried’s hideout was full of things that held magical power. No wonder the concentration was high.

“I see what you’re thinking,” Johnson went on, “but even if monsters are the reason there’s so much magical power here, that doesn’t tell us anything. If a monster killed Siegfried, there should at least be signs of a fight.”
I was an idiot for getting my hopes up.
The Skeleton King could only blink at Johnson’s perfectly reasonable objection. I muttered, “Fucking moron.”
“How dare this treacherous human insult whom!”
“Shut up before I pull your jawbone off. I’ll let it slide since you actually tried thinking for once.”
“Don’t go confusing the investigation. My head’s about to explode as it is.”
The Demon Realm was far away. My fist was close.
The Skeleton King closed his mouth, looking thoroughly displeased. Team Leader Choi, who had continued examining the body, clicked his tongue.
“If this was an assassination, there should be at least a small wound. But there isn’t one. The body is clean.”
“Then...”
“Magic is the only explanation I can think of.”
Yet even Magic Johnson, a Grand Mage himself, looked troubled.
“I specialize in offensive magic, but I’ve never seen or heard of anything like this. It’s far more complex and sinister than the magic we use. Closer to that fellow’s work, if anything.”
“That fellow,” who had been keeping his mouth firmly shut, frowned.
“This body merely places vengeful spirits into dead flesh. This body knows nothing of such wicked magic.”
Isn’t that already fucking wicked magic?
But since he said he did not know, what could I say? Besides, he was quite unlike an ordinary monster, so he had no reason to lie.
Damn it. It has to be him.
Michael Silbert.
That name alone kept circling through my mind.

chapters.title: Chapter 743
paragraphs: A space reserved for one person alone.
In the light that faintly illuminated the darkness, an eerie sound of flesh tearing echoed through the air.
Crack. Crack-crack.
Bones and muscles twisted. A tremendous force surged in time with the beating of a heart, bringing about a transformation.
What was weak grew strong.
What was strong grew stronger still.
The man’s veins stood out across his body, and cold sweat had soaked him through. A thin line of blood slipped between his tightly pressed lips and ran down his chin.
Drip.
Drops of blood fell one by one.
Yet despite the agony wringing every part of his body, there was no trace of fear or pain in his gray eyes.
To some, it would have been worse than death. To him, it was familiar.
And the reward for enduring it was always sweet.
Just like now.
Hssssss.

The sickening cracks fell silent. At the same time, the energy that had been thrashing inside him rapidly settled. The veins bulging so grotesquely across his body slowly receded, and his muscles stopped convulsing.
Once again, the man received his “Reward.”
Whoosh—boom!
In an instant, a tremendous wave of qi burst from him and swept in every direction. The light that had faintly illuminated the space vanished, and everything within some ten meters crumbled to dust.
It was power.
Overwhelming power.
Michael Silbert felt the change within himself and smiled.
Vrrrrr.
A faint vibration reached him from somewhere.
Michael knew exactly what it meant. He rose without hesitation and silently extended a hand. A hidden door opened, spilling light from the other side.
Step. Step.
His footsteps were strong and steady, as though the ordeal moments earlier had never happened. He crossed his study—vast was a better word for it—and stopped before a large mirror.
The full-length mirror glowed and faintly vibrated. Michael studied his reflection in its flawless surface, then laid a hand against the glass.
Tap.
In the next moment—
Flash!
A brief flare of light transformed the view in the mirror. Michael and his study vanished, replaced by an endless horizon, buildings moving slowly past, and a lone figure.
Dark skin, golden eyes, a silk top hat, and a monocle—the last two rarely seen these days.
Michael greeted the loyal retainer who had served him for years.
“You’ve been working hard, Huginn.”
Huginn tipped his hat to his superior.
“Not at all, Guild Master.”
That was greeting enough. As though by agreement, they went straight to business.
“The Swiss Federal Police recovered Siegfried Bassmann’s body an hour ago.”
“And those bastards?”
The question was brief. Huginn needed no clarification.
“They were questioned briefly as witnesses and released. If we push as hard as we can, we might drag them before the International Court of Justice, but I doubt we can take it any further.”
“I assume that isn’t just your own assessment. Who’s your source?”
“In Switzerland, Minister Berse.”
“Berse?”
Michael nodded calmly at the name of the Minister of the Interior, whose election as Switzerland’s president next year was considered all but certain.
“Then I’ve heard enough. We should let the matter end there.”
“I agree, Guild Master. Still, given what’s at stake, pursuing them to the end might be worth considering.”
“You want to throw them into a pit of filth, one way or another?”

“Shouldn’t we drag them in by the collar if we have to? The whole world will be watching as soon as this gets out. Siegfried Bassmann’s cause of death is unknown, and people will have questions. Then...”
“Conspiracy theories will spread. And those bastards will be their first targets.”
“Yes. Under the circumstances, wouldn’t that be effective?”
Michael shook his head without hesitation.
“Conspiracy theories are nonsense. Only fools obsessed with gossip and their own fantasies would suspect them.”

Siegfried Bassmann had been a figure of tremendous stature, not just in Switzerland but around the world. Michael could easily use his death to spread theories about his enemies. It would just as easily backfire.
If he forcibly dragged his enemies into a pit of filth, some of that filth would splash onto him as well.

“Most people won’t give those theories a second thought. Worse, some will start wondering whether everything that’s happened around those bastards was staged. People who curse them today will take their side tomorrow.”

As far as Michael knew, that was human nature. They were quick to condemn someone after being deceived by one tiny false aspect, then quickly changed their attitude once the whole truth came to light, gently embracing the person they had cursed.
As though nothing had happened.
As though the rest of the world had cursed him, but they never had.
Michael had no desire to see that happen. The plan’s uncertain outcome was reason enough, but more importantly, its central figure was missing.
Jin Taekyung.
The name hovered on the tip of his tongue.

At most, Siegfried Bassmann’s death might put pressure on Magic Johnson. Even that was unlikely. Unless Michael brought down Jin Taekyung—the man at the center of it all—he would only be wasting his strength.
“Leave the Swiss matter alone. There’s nothing to gain from it.”
Huginn answered the calm, firm order at once.
“Understood. I’ll relay that to Minister Berse as well.”
“Good. How are things with the media outlets?”
“Going well. We fed them firewood, and the flames took off. There is one matter I need to raise, though...”
“Money?”
“Yes. They’ve demanded much more than we expected.”
“Greedy, aren’t they? What they’ve already received should be more than enough.”
“That’s why I consider it fortunate. We only need to give them what they want.”
Michael let out a quiet laugh. Huginn was right. Satisfy a person’s greed at the right moment—better yet, give them more than they had imagined wanting—and they would never betray you.
“I’ll give you access to some of my secret accounts. Take whatever you need.”
“Should I take that to mean I can give them enough to astonish them?”
“Exactly. You’ve become quite the villain.”
“I learned from a certain someone.”
“There’s an interesting saying among Easterners: ‘When three people gather, they can make a tiger.’ Keep the media under our control until this is over. Just as you have been.”
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
Michael knew the power of the media. He knew, too, how shallow and frightening a crowd’s judgment could be.
Part of him found it ridiculous that he had to go this far.
I was certain no one alive could stop me now, apart from Cheon Taemin.
Not the Ares Guild, once called the best in the world. Not Lee Jungryong, who had filled the void Cheon Taemin left behind. Not even the heroes of the Great Cataclysm, Magic Johnson among them.
None of them had been his match.
Then Jin Taekyung appeared.
How is that possible?
Michael could hardly believe it. He had been a young man from the slums with nothing but poverty to his name. Reaching his current position had taken years upon years of patience.
Jin Taekyung was different.
He had appeared out of nowhere and, in barely more than a year, amassed extraordinary achievements and Fame. The whole world had come to love him.
Just as it had loved someone from Michael’s past, still vivid in his memory.
Sky.
One week ago, Michael had sensed a trace of Cheon Taemin in the young Asian man he met for the first time in the ruins.
He looked different. He felt different. But Michael’s instincts had warned him.
He’s dangerous.
He’ll be the greatest obstacle in my way.
Those instincts had been right. Even with countless media outlets pouring out malicious stories, people had not stopped voicing their support for Jin Taekyung.
Those swept up in the terror of the attacks and the crowd mentality the media had cultivated were simply louder. Jin Taekyung still stood firm.
But if my guess is right... it’s only a matter of time before he falls.
Michael thought to himself as he recalled Jin Taekyung’s eyes, blazing with rage.
And someone who had stood beside him.
One step. Only one step remained between Michael and the summit he had longed to reach. He already held the flag that would proclaim his conquest.
“Huginn.”
Huginn had waited in silence while his superior was lost in thought.
“Yes, Guild Master.”
“There must be no mistakes or unexpected complications with this mission.”
“Don’t worry. I handled everything exactly as you ordered. Nothing was overlooked.”
Michael smiled at the ready answer from the loyal retainer who had shared so many years—and so many secrets—with him.
“Good. That’s all I need to hear.”
“I won’t disappoint you.”
The man who had given the order and the man who had carried it out both knew what their actions would bring. They knew countless people would die or be injured.
To Michael, that was a minor detail.

It was an unavoidable sacrifice on the way to the goal he had long sought. If he could obtain what he wanted, then the sacrifice of those who would die somewhere in this vast world was an absurdly cheap price.
Crash!
The magically treated glass shattered at once. A moment ago, it had been a communications crystal ball. Now a wave swept its countless fragments away.
Whooosh.
Wind swept over Huginn as he stood at the stern, gazing at the rolling sea.
Three days at the latest. It’ll probably begin before then.
The crystal ball’s fragments were not the only things he had cast into the deep. Before long, the whole world would see the result.
The calculations were perfect. The mission was a success.
He felt no guilt. Only the satisfaction of having carried out his orders perfectly, and one small question he had yet to answer.
Will this be enough to bring Jin Taekyung down completely?
Huginn shook his head. The superior he served was always thorough, and the path he chose had always been the right one.
“We’re heading back. Get ready.”
At his brief command, the ship turned.
Behind it, growing slowly more distant, Tokyo’s forest of buildings rose against the sky.
