Worse, some will start wondering whether everything that’s happened around those bastards was staged.
People who curse them today will take their side tomorrow.”
As far as Michael knew, that was human nature.
They were quick to condemn someone after being deceived by one tiny false aspect, then quickly changed their attitude once the whole truth came to light, gently embracing the person they had cursed.
As though nothing had happened.
As though the rest of the world had cursed him, but they never had.
Michael had no desire to see that happen.
The plan’s uncertain outcome was reason enough, but more importantly, its central figure was missing.
Jin Taekyung.
The name hovered on the tip of his tongue.
At most, Siegfried Bassmann’s death might put pressure on Magic Johnson.
Even that was unlikely.
Unless Michael brought down Jin Taekyung—the man at the center of it all—he would only be wasting his strength.
“Leave the Swiss matter alone.
There’s nothing to gain from it.”
Huginn answered the calm, firm order at once.
“Understood.
I’ll relay that to Minister Berse as well.”
“Good.
How are things with the media outlets?”
“Going well.
We fed them firewood, and the flames took off.
There is one matter I need to raise, though...”
“Money?”
“Yes.
They’ve demanded much more than we expected.”
“Greedy, aren’t they?
What they’ve already received should be more than enough.”
“That’s why I consider it fortunate.
We only need to give them what they want.”
Michael let out a quiet laugh.
Huginn was right.
Satisfy a person’s greed at the right moment—better yet, give them more than they had imagined wanting—and they would never betray you.
“I’ll give you access to some of my secret accounts.
Take whatever you need.”
“Should I take that to mean I can give them enough to astonish them?”
“Exactly.
You’ve become quite the villain.”
“I learned from a certain someone.”
“There’s an interesting saying among Easterners: ‘When three people gather, they can make a tiger.’ Keep the media under our control until this is over.
Just as you have been.”
“I’ll keep that in mind.”
Michael knew the power of the media.
He knew, too, how shallow and frightening a crowd’s judgment could be.
Part of him found it ridiculous that he had to go this far.
I was certain no one alive could stop me now, apart from Cheon Taemin.
Not the Ares Guild, once called the best in the world.
Not Lee Jungryong, who had filled the void Cheon Taemin left behind.
Not even the heroes of the Great Cataclysm, Magic Johnson among them.
None of them had been his match.
Then Jin Taekyung appeared.
How is that possible?
Michael could hardly believe it.
He had been a young man from the slums with nothing but poverty to his name.
Reaching his current position had taken years upon years of patience.
Jin Taekyung was different.
He had appeared out of nowhere and, in barely more than a year, amassed extraordinary achievements and Fame.
The whole world had come to love him.
Just as it had loved someone from Michael’s past, still vivid in his memory.
Sky.
One week ago, Michael had sensed a trace of Cheon Taemin in the young Asian man he met for the first time in the ruins.
He looked different.
He felt different.
But Michael’s instincts had warned him.
He’s dangerous.
He’ll be the greatest obstacle in my way.
Those instincts had been right.
Even with countless media outlets pouring out malicious stories, people had not stopped voicing their support for Jin Taekyung.
Those swept up in the terror of the attacks and the crowd mentality the media had cultivated were simply louder.
Jin Taekyung still stood firm.
But if my guess is right... it’s only a matter of time before he falls.
Michael thought to himself as he recalled Jin Taekyung’s eyes, blazing with rage.
And someone who had stood beside him.
One step.
Only one step remained between Michael and the summit he had longed to reach.
He already held the flag that would proclaim his conquest.
“Huginn.”
Huginn had waited in silence while his superior was lost in thought.
“Yes, Guild Master.”
“There must be no mistakes or unexpected complications with this mission.”
“Don’t worry.
I handled everything exactly as you ordered.
Nothing was overlooked.”
Michael smiled at the ready answer from the loyal retainer who had shared so many years—and so many secrets—with him.
“Good.
That’s all I need to hear.”
“I won’t disappoint you.”
The man who had given the order and the man who had carried it out both knew what their actions would bring.
They knew countless people would die or be injured.
To Michael, that was a minor detail.
It was an unavoidable sacrifice on the way to the goal he had long sought.
If he could obtain what he wanted, then the sacrifice of those who would die somewhere in this vast world was an absurdly cheap price.
Crash!
The magically treated glass shattered at once.
A moment ago, it had been a communications crystal ball.
Now a wave swept its countless fragments away.
Whooosh.
Wind swept over Huginn as he stood at the stern, gazing at the rolling sea.
Three days at the latest.
It’ll probably begin before then.
The crystal ball’s fragments were not the only things he had cast into the deep.
Before long, the whole world would see the result.
The calculations were perfect.
The mission was a success.
He felt no guilt.
Only the satisfaction of having carried out his orders perfectly, and one small question he had yet to answer.
Will this be enough to bring Jin Taekyung down completely?
Huginn shook his head.
The superior he served was always thorough, and the path he chose had always been the right one.
“We’re heading back.
Get ready.”
At his brief command, the ship turned.
Behind it, growing slowly more distant, Tokyo’s forest of buildings rose against the sky.

chapters.title: Chapter 744
paragraphs: A thought occurred to me.
I wished that everything tormenting me right now was merely a scene from some movie or novel. Something like that.
Then at least some evidence would pop up somewhere.
Of course, contrary to the hope I had secretly been holding on to, nothing of the sort happened.
Everyone, myself included, searched every inch of Siegfried Bassmann’s hideout, but what popped out wasn’t evidence concerning his death. It was a person.
More precisely, over a hundred Hunters from the Swiss Federal Police, who had followed us and arrived late.
“Everyone, please stop.”
“We’re taking control of the scene under legal procedure. Put down whatever you’re holding immediately and...”
Well, what else could we do?

If they had abruptly pointed swords at us, I would have answered with my spear. But they were carrying out official duties, and instead of swords, they had thrust forward the invincible cheat code known as legal procedure.
Even unorthodox swordsmen who drew their weapons at the slightest provocation hesitated in front of government soldiers.
And as a twenty-first-century modern man with a logical mindset, my answer had been decided from the start.
“Are you going to put us in handcuffs too?”
“...Excuse me?”
“Yeah, that’d be a bit much. So what do we do now?”
With countless media outlets wishing me a long and healthy life while cursing me to hell, causing another incident would’ve been insane.
My companions and I cooperated so obediently that even the Swiss Hunters were surprised. After undergoing a thorough body search and brief questioning, we were released.
The high-ranking official who introduced himself as the lead investigator had just one thing to say.
“Additional investigations related to this case will be conducted, so we ask for your continued cooperation in the future.”
That was all.
We hadn’t given them anything to hold against us, but their matter-of-fact response still surprised me.
According to Team Leader Choi, Michael Silbert’s influence reached the leaders of countries across the world. Switzerland, in particular, was where he sheltered his astronomical wealth from taxes.
I was sure that bastard would use Switzerland to pressure us somehow.
Team Leader Choi had a straightforward answer.

“They deliberately let us go. Since it was clear that neither the evidence nor the circumstances had anything to do with us, they must have judged that pursuing the matter any further would be difficult.”
“That bastard Michael let us go on purpose? Just getting dragged into this case would already hurt us.”

“The public is fickle. Right now, quite a few people are cursing us because they’re being controlled by the media and mob psychology. But that’s because The Prophet and terrorism provide a plausible justification at first glance.”
“And if the reason doesn’t hold up, people won’t buy it?”
“People have acted on what they consider justified for thousands of years. If that justification falls apart, a good number of those condemning us will change sides.”
“Oh.”
Come to think of it, that was a pattern people displayed often—no, quite frequently.
You only had to look at the entertainment news on any online portal. The moment a celebrity got caught up in a scandal, netizens swarmed like bees to the honey the media had put out.
There were the genius prophets who claimed they had known it would happen ever since the celebrity’s debut, and even twenty-first-century physiognomists insisting that face-reading was a science.

And around the time the winner of that world’s greatest malicious-comment contest was crowned by upvotes, a new fact would emerge and turn the situation around, and the swarm would change its tune in an instant.
Why?
Simple.
They had no excuse to keep cursing them.
Siegfried Bassmann’s mysterious death was that kind of case. Michael Silbert understood how people worked, and he knew exactly when to press on and when to stop.
“Michael is, in a word, a madman.”
Magic Johnson broke the silence, his voice subdued.
“But the biggest reason we need to be wary of him is that this mad bastard is more meticulous and stronger than anyone.”
Even the Skeleton King wore an uncharacteristically grave expression.
“I agree. When I first saw that bastard in Paris, I felt something so eerie that it was difficult to believe he was human.”
Most madmen ended up in prison or a psychiatric hospital.
But when a madman like Michael had everything, the world had another name for him.
One of the powerful.
Of the people I’d met in the modern world, Lee Jungryong qualified. So did Go Jun, though he fell short of his Master in plenty of ways.
But that bastard...
He had already gone beyond that category.
You’d have to add those two together, then multiply the result, to get a madman like him.
Michael Silbert was a monster who’d given up being human.
Why? What could he possibly want to go this far?
I looked up. The sky was clear as hell, and the surrounding landscape had kept its northern European beauty. It couldn’t have been more at odds with what was happening.
Fuck.
I muttered a quiet curse inwardly, then pulled a small pouch from inside my clothes and handed it to Magic Johnson.
“Here.”
“This is... a subspace pocket.”
“Don’t open it yet. Take it with you and look through it properly. Team Leader Choi and I are hopeless when it comes to magic. We wouldn’t know what we were looking at.”
“Magic? Jin, what are you suddenly talking about?”
He looked bewildered. Then his eyes widened.
“Don’t tell me...”
“Yeah. I swiped it earlier. I’m sure the deceased would understand.”
All three stood there with their mouths open. Well, two people and one monster. I made a show of sighing.
“Not the reaction I was hoping for. Should I return it?”
Magic Johnson snatched the pocket.
“N-no, that’s not what I meant. But how did you...?”
“The Hunters assigned to me were pretty lax with their body search.”
Team Leader Choi blinked at me. “Lax?”
“Yeah.”
A blatant lie, of course.
A Grand Mage’s magical research materials were an immense treasure in their own right.
The Swiss Hunters had thoroughly searched the subspace pockets we carried, worried that even one of the materials might be smuggled out.
They hadn’t searched my Inventory.
More precisely, they couldn’t have.
As soon as I gave up looking for evidence on the body, I’d started scooping up materials. Anything that looked even remotely promising. Whatever I could lay my hands on.
The result of that theft was now in Magic Johnson’s hands.
“We didn’t notice a thing,” he said. “When did you manage all this?”
“I told you. They weren’t watching closely, so I slipped it out.”
“You secretly slipped it out?”
He opened the pocket and looked inside.
“...Jin. You didn’t steal the entire laboratory, did you?”
Well. I had picked up this and that, so I had brought quite a lot.
Everyone had been distracted, though, and there were mountains of documents left behind. It probably wasn’t that obvious.
Probably.
“Anyway, is it enough to work with?”
“Enough? Are you serious? There’s more than enough.”
“Then please investigate it based on those materials for the time being.”
“But with everything happening, I can’t focus entirely on—no. I’ll do my best. If I find even the smallest clue in here, Michael won’t be able to carry on like this.”
I nodded.
“Please do.”

The distribution of magical power had intensified again, and the damage was mounting. Magic Johnson would be a tremendous help with the aftermath, but we needed to deal with the root of the problem first.
“We’ll gather information from other angles,” Team Leader Choi said. “If we can locate one person, we may be able to prevent the worst.”
Magic Johnson answered with something like a sigh.
“The Prophet.”
“Yes. If either of the two heads is removed, things should improve considerably.”
“If we could eliminate The Prophet, all the better. We have Jin. Find out where the man is, and he’s dead. The problem is...”
“I know. Even the Pentagon hasn’t located him yet. But we have to try.”
Michael Silbert and The Prophet.
The Prophet and Michael Silbert.
The two madmen moved as though they were one, but The Prophet was by far the easier one for me to eliminate.
Kill the master of the world’s greatest Guild, and I’d be a fucking bastard on par with Demon King Asmodeus. Bring back the head of a fanatical terrorist, and the whole world would cheer.
“We’ll find him,” I said, calm despite the anger in my voice. “Even if we have to turn over the entire desert.”
The civilization humanity had built was magnificent.
The sight of people cheering after discovering fire for the first time in the distant past could no longer be found anywhere.
Those wandering groups had become farming societies. Factories rose where fields and rice paddies had once stood, and humanity forged the modern world from steel and blood.
Humanity, once the weakest of all, had thus become the master of this blue planet.
They flew across the sky faster than light, ventured into space, and used weapons born of that progress to kill one another.
Humanity was the ruler of this land, its people, and an explorer forever moving forward.
But even humanity could not do everything.
Some unknown realms remained beyond its reach after hundreds of millions of years, impossible to explore even with magic.
One was the infinite expanse of space. The other lay deep beneath the sea, where light could not reach.
The deep sea.

Even adventurers who had discovered the five oceans and six continents and reached into the domain of outer space had never set foot there. It was still filled with countless speculations and secrets.
No—perhaps it was a secret that should never have been pried into.
Shhrrk.
Something enormous moved. Hundreds of deep-sea fish had mistaken it for part of the terrain and strayed close. They could not withstand the power within it and were torn in half.
Crunch.
The lightless depths swallowed their red blood.
Hssss.
A faint light spread beyond the darkness.
Each time the scales covering something enormous, several meters in radius, shifted, the surrounding space alternately brightened and darkened.
At last, the center of the glow shone clearly.
It was no luminous organ like those found on some deep-sea fish. The power it held was beyond comparison.
It was an eye.
The eye of a creature so enormous that it was difficult to believe.
A monster everyone thought had vanished long ago had awakened after an unfathomable span of time.

chapters.title: Chapter 745
paragraphs: The desert night was bitterly cold.
The scorching sun and heat haze were gone. In their place remained subzero temperatures and an unusually large moon.
A temperature swing of sixty degrees in a single day.
But even the bitter cold could not stop the figure climbing a crescent-shaped dune.
Sssrrk.
Despite the steep slope, the figure moved as though gliding across the sand. The hem of a thin silk robe brushed the grains, then came to a stop.
“This is the place.”
The moment that flat voice sounded, the empty air rippled.
Ffft.
With a faint sound, a dozen or so figures descended onto the dune. Their faces hidden behind black masks and turbans, they each dropped respectfully to one knee and whispered,
“Inshallah. We pay our respects to the great Prophet who has returned to this land.”
Standing alone before them, the Prophet’s robe fluttered lightly.
“Inshallah. I wondered when you would reveal yourselves.”
Those words made it clear that the Prophet had seen through everything from the beginning. The dozen pairs of eyes visible above the masks trembled.
“Prophet...”
“I know. You followed me because you care for me, even though it meant defying my orders.”
“If you would punish us for our disobedience, we would gladly pay for it with our lives. But we, the Hasasin, will never leave your side, no matter the circumstances.”
The Hasasin. Or the Assassins.

Their stronghold had fallen to their enemies around the thirteenth century. For centuries afterward, the ancient order of assassins had survived as little more than a religious sect, until the Great Cataclysm brought it back to life.
Its members would not be dissuaded.
“The Western heretics are cunning, and they wield great power. If they were to discover you...”
“Al-Nizar. Loyal beyond any other, yet foolish and full of worry.”
“Look at me.”
The leader of the Hasasin flinched and cautiously raised his head.
His great Prophet gazed down at him, silhouetted against a sky strewn with stars. Within the strangely dark folds of the robe, a pair of eyes shone with a mysterious light.
“Do you still not understand?”
The Prophet raised both arms toward the sky.
Vwoooom.
An immense force swelled beneath the robe, pushing its folds outward. The wind died. The air vibrated.
The Hasasin swallowed without realizing it. Their eyes followed the Prophet’s hands, and in the next moment—
Shhhhhhhk.
They saw it: a transparent membrane that began in the sky and curved around them, enclosing an area several hundred meters in radius.
It was both a protective barrier that no product of science—not even Magic—could detect and a screen that concealed them from their enemies’ eyes.
“As long as I protect you, they will not find so much as our shadows.”
Even the Hasasin, who had endured extreme training, could not hide their surging emotions at that moment.
Their Prophet possessed such astonishing power. And the Prophet had called lowly servants like them us.
“Inshallah...!”
“Prophet!”
Their cries of joy and emotion echoed through the quiet desert.
But the Prophet had another miracle to show them.
Sssrrk.
The long, loose sleeve of the robe fluttered. The crescent-shaped dune beneath their feet shook.
No—it split apart.
Crk-crk-crk!
It was a wondrous sight.
In the distant past, Moses had parted the Red Sea and led the Hebrews across it. Now, more than a thousand years later, a new Prophet had divided part of a vast sea of sand in two.
What lay hidden beneath those countless grains glittered in the moonlight like a gift from God.
“My God...”
“Prophet, what are those?”
Instead of answering, the Prophet silently extended a hand.
Clank. Clank. Clank!
Locks burst apart under an invisible force. The leader of the Hasasin stared wide-eyed at the contents of the dozens of iron chests.
“T-this is...”
Even the darkness could not hide their brilliance.
Gold and silver bars in quantities he had never seen, and weapons imbued with various kinds of Magic, dazzled him. But something else shocked him most of all.
“Magic Gems...!”
The cry that escaped him like a groan was the truth.
Magic Gems.
Hundreds of them, unmistakably high-grade to top-grade. Some were exceptionally large and radiated immense power.
Fwoooosh.
Even he, a leader of the Hasasin who had reached the realm of an S-rank Hunter, could not easily approach that powerful energy.
“Hk.”
He drew a sharp breath before he could stop himself. The Prophet’s familiar, toneless voice reached him.
“S-rank Magic Gems. Their original power remains intact.”
“P-Prophet...”
“Stand back. That power is beyond you.”
With that quiet warning, the unrefined S-rank Magic Gems floated into the air. They moved like living things and disappeared into the Prophet’s robe.
Ten of them.
The leader of the Hasasin watched, his gaze trembling.
How did the Prophet get hold of those...?
He already knew the Prophet’s abilities defied common sense.
But from the Great Cataclysm until now, only a little over a hundred S-rank monsters had officially appeared in human history.

On extremely rare occasions, a tiny number of A-rank monsters had possessed S-rank Magic Gems. But those instances were exactly what they were—exceptional cases. Even in the Middle East, where countless Gates existed, S-rank Magic Gems had appeared only once or twice.
Yet here were ten of them, their original magical power intact.
That’s an incredible amount. It’s impossible to believe.
His faith in the Prophet was boundless, but this time he could not help wanting to ask.
He turned his head—and met the faintly glowing eyes within the robe.
“Tell me. Who do you think stands before you?”
The gaze seemed to see through him. Shock struck the leader of the Hasasin like lightning, and he dropped to his knees.
How dare someone like him question the Prophet’s actions?
It was something that could not happen—and must never happen.
“Great Prophet, please forgive this sinful servant!”
The air froze.
The other Hasasin touched their weapons and waited for the Prophet to speak. If the order came, they were ready to kill their own leader without a moment’s hesitation.
The Prophet spoke God’s word and led them all.
Since the death of the Prophet Muhammad, the Islamic world had spent more than a thousand years feuding and fighting. Blood had stained the desert sands.
Over time, a tiny few had gained immense wealth and power. But in the great cities built on oil, the word of Allah had given way to the capitalism of apostates.
It was time to bring Allah’s children, who had turned their blades on one another, back to a single root—and to save their fellow believers persecuted even in the Western world.
In the name of the great God.
In the name of the Prophet who had come to them decades ago in God’s stead.
And just as an invisible blade slowly cut through the silence, one tightly closed mouth finally opened.
“Al-Nizar.”
The voice revealed neither age nor even gender.
The leader of the Hasasin swallowed. Cold sweat had soaked him from head to toe.
“Prophet.”
“One last piece of advice, my son of God. You are still immature—and that is precisely why I care for you all the more.”
“Inshallah. All of this is the result of the long patience and providence God has granted me. You must never doubt it. Do you understand?”
“I’ll remember. I’ll remember.”
Drip.
Cold sweat and tears fell together onto the sand.
The Prophet gazed kindly at the leader as he trembled with relief and emotion, then continued.
“The time has come again. Tell your brothers who have been preparing.”
Everyone’s eyes widened.
Nearly ten days had passed since the day they called “Allah’s Judgment.” All who followed the Prophet had been waiting impatiently for the next day of judgment.
“Prophet. Do you mean...?”
“God wills it. Bring down His hammer upon the apostates eating away at us from within and the Western heretics.”
The eyes visible above the masks gleamed with fanaticism and exultation.
The Prophet looked up at the star-strewn sky and murmured,
“There is not much time left until the end.”
Some wanted catastrophe. Some struggled to prevent it. Still others wanted something beyond it.
Even now, each was racing toward a different goal.
Sugihara Gyoiku was a laborer who had worked in cargo shipping for a long time.
He was a lifelong Tokyo native and, at the same time, a seasoned laborer who had entered the maritime transport industry when he was young.
People sometimes looked down on him for doing manual labor, but he did not care much. Not everyone could be a Hunter, lawyer, or doctor, and the world needed people like him, too.
Lately, though, he had been in a foul mood.
How could he not be?
Chikushō. Damn monsters.
Just ten days earlier, a Monster Wave in Tokyo had killed and injured many people.
Tokyo Tower, which he had secretly been proud of as a Tokyo native, had collapsed horribly. The chicken restaurant he had frequented for thirty years had also vanished in the aftermath.
I didn’t like that the owner was a Chosenjin, but the chicken was incredible.
Gyoiku was sad that he could no longer stop in for Korean-style chicken and beer after work. Still, he went to work today as usual.
“Gyoiku-san. You’re here?”
“Yo.”
He exchanged brief greetings with the other dockworkers and headed straight to the work site. Cargo ships already crowded Tokyo Bay.
“Where should we start?”
“We’ve already started. Come on.”

As Gyoiku loaded cargo onto a ship, he chatted with his coworkers. Tokyo’s magical-power levels had been rising particularly fast lately. The prime minister, scion of a prominent political family, had said something insane again.
Then someone mentioned a tsunami.
“A tsunami?”
“Yeah. Apparently it’s getting closer to Tokyo. They say it’s huge.”
“Hmm.”
“Don’t worry. The government said it would die down soon.”
“Guess it will.”

Gyoiku felt a little uneasy, but only a little. Even if there was a tsunami, it would never make it all the way to Tokyo. Tokyo Bay was sheltered by the land around it, and its magical defense systems were firmly in place.
Maybe I’ll look for a new Korean chicken place after work.
Gyoiku straightened his back, thinking about something pointless—and froze like a statue.
“Huh?”
What is that?
The question flashed through his mind. A moment later, he remembered what he had just heard.
The tsunami.
Gyoiku stared blankly, mouth open, toward the sea beyond the harbor.
A wave larger than any he had ever seen was racing toward him. It rose so high it looked ready to blot out the sun.
Goooooong.
Along with the cry of some unknown thing—a sound that froze him merely by hearing it.

sentences.text: The desert night was bitterly cold.
The scorching sun and heat haze were gone.
In their place remained subzero temperatures and an unusually large moon.
A temperature swing of sixty degrees in a single day.
But even the bitter cold could not stop the figure climbing a crescent-shaped dune.
Sssrrk.
Despite the steep slope, the figure moved as though gliding across the sand.
The hem of a thin silk robe brushed the grains, then came to a stop.
“This is the place.”
The moment that flat voice sounded, the empty air rippled.
Ffft.
With a faint sound, a dozen or so figures descended onto the dune.
Their faces hidden behind black masks and turbans, they each dropped respectfully to one knee and whispered,
“Inshallah.
We pay our respects to the great Prophet who has returned to this land.”
Standing alone before them, the Prophet’s robe fluttered lightly.
“Inshallah.
I wondered when you would reveal yourselves.”
Those words made it clear that the Prophet had seen through everything from the beginning.
The dozen pairs of eyes visible above the masks trembled.
“Prophet...”
“I know.
You followed me because you care for me, even though it meant defying my orders.”
“If you would punish us for our disobedience, we would gladly pay for it with our lives.
But we, the Hasasin, will never leave your side, no matter the circumstances.”
The Hasasin.
Or the Assassins.
Their stronghold had fallen to their enemies around the thirteenth century.
For centuries afterward, the ancient order of assassins had survived as little more than a religious sect, until the Great Cataclysm brought it back to life.
Its members would not be dissuaded.
“The Western heretics are cunning, and they wield great power.
If they were to discover you...”
“Al-Nizar.
Loyal beyond any other, yet foolish and full of worry.”
“Look at me.”
The leader of the Hasasin flinched and cautiously raised his head.
His great Prophet gazed down at him, silhouetted against a sky strewn with stars.
Within the strangely dark folds of the robe, a pair of eyes shone with a mysterious light.
“Do you still not understand?”
The Prophet raised both arms toward the sky.
Vwoooom.
An immense force swelled beneath the robe, pushing its folds outward.
The wind died.
The air vibrated.
The Hasasin swallowed without realizing it.
Their eyes followed the Prophet’s hands, and in the next moment—
Shhhhhhhk.
They saw it: a transparent membrane that began in the sky and curved around them, enclosing an area several hundred meters in radius.
It was both a protective barrier that no product of science—not even Magic—could detect and a screen that concealed them from their enemies’ eyes.
“As long as I protect you, they will not find so much as our shadows.”
Even the Hasasin, who had endured extreme training, could not hide their surging emotions at that moment.
Their Prophet possessed such astonishing power.
And the Prophet had called lowly servants like them us.
“Inshallah...!”
“Prophet!”
Their cries of joy and emotion echoed through the quiet desert.
But the Prophet had another miracle to show them.
Sssrrk.
The long, loose sleeve of the robe fluttered.
The crescent-shaped dune beneath their feet shook.
No—it split apart.
Crk-crk-crk!
It was a wondrous sight.
In the distant past, Moses had parted the Red Sea and led the Hebrews across it.
Now, more than a thousand years later, a new Prophet had divided part of a vast sea of sand in two.
What lay hidden beneath those countless grains glittered in the moonlight like a gift from God.
“My God...”
“Prophet, what are those?”
Instead of answering, the Prophet silently extended a hand.
Clank.
Clank.
Clank!
Locks burst apart under an invisible force.
The leader of the Hasasin stared wide-eyed at the contents of the dozens of iron chests.
“T-this is...”
Even the darkness could not hide their brilliance.
Gold and silver bars in quantities he had never seen, and weapons imbued with various kinds of Magic, dazzled him.
But something else shocked him most of all.
“Magic Gems...!”
The cry that escaped him like a groan was the truth.
Magic Gems.
Hundreds of them, unmistakably high-grade to top-grade.
Some were exceptionally large and radiated immense power.
Fwoooosh.
Even he, a leader of the Hasasin who had reached the realm of an S-rank Hunter, could not easily approach that powerful energy.
“Hk.”
He drew a sharp breath before he could stop himself.
The Prophet’s familiar, toneless voice reached him.
“S-rank Magic Gems.
Their original power remains intact.”
“P-Prophet...”

That power is beyond you.”

They moved like living things and disappeared into the Prophet’s robe.

chapters.title: Chapter 746
paragraphs: Returning to everyday life usually means things have settled down.
But immediately after the mysterious death of Siegfried Bassmann, we returned to our respective positions only to face a frantic stretch of time.
“The magical-power reading at the C-rank Gate in Sokcho, Gangwon Province, is rising rapidly. It’s at Stage Two... entering Stage Three! We have a mutation Gate!”
“How many people can we deploy?”
“Four teams are on standby at the Gangwon Province branch. The Teleport Magic Formation linked to Sokcho City Hall can get them to the site within five minutes.”
“Send them now. This could turn into a monster wave. Make rescuing survivors and containing the situation your top priorities.”
The situation after our return was about as bad as it could get.
Until a few years ago, mutation Gates had appeared no more than once a month. Now we were seeing three or four a day—and that was just in Korea.
While stock prices rose and fell, magical-power readings climbed every single day.
Broadcasters cut back on entertainment shows. On newly launched disaster-news channels, experts from every field argued fiercely.

“Many people overlook the fact that magical-power readings have risen steadily every year. Compared to the period immediately after the Great Cataclysm, today’s readings are actually quite low. Once this situation is resolved, things will settle down quickly, so the public needn’t worry—”

“Settle down quickly? What kind of nonsense is that? And how can you compare today with the period right after the Great Cataclysm? After we killed the Demon King on the ‘Day of Victory,’ did humanity put down its weapons and dance Ganggangsullae together? Back then, you could go to Han River Park and find Lizardmen. It took nearly a year just to finish off the monster armies that were still out there. Have you forgotten?”
“I live in Ilsan, and I never saw any Lizardmen in Han River Park. I’m right.”
“What a fucking idiot...”
“Now, now. You’re a year younger than me. No need to swear.”
“A year younger, my ass, you fucking bastard. My parents registered my birth late. Happy?”
“Mr. Host, are you going to let him talk to me like that?”
The sight of white-haired academic authorities turning red in the face on TV and fighting over whose argument would win was no longer particularly surprising.
While they grabbed each other by the collars, the next channel was reporting breaking news of a mutation Gate or monster wave somewhere in the world.
And at those horrific scenes, I fought as hard as I could.
Shhk!
White Flame’s spearhead sliced cleanly through hide and bone harder than armor.
The enormous monster—I had no idea how many I’d killed by then—stopped dead in its tracks. Then it slowly turned around and split in two from top to bottom.
Shff. Thud!
As its three-meter body fell in two equal halves, I met the eyes of a man sprawled a few steps away.
He had escaped death by a hair. In his hand was a plastic protest sign painted with red letters.
ARREST INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL JIN TAEKYUNG!!!
Hmm.
I wondered how I was supposed to react, then gave him a rueful smile.
Even if he hated me, three exclamation marks seemed a bit much.
“Are you okay?”
“You look all right apart from a few scratches, but stay seated just in case. It’s over now. The rescue team will be here soon.”
I left the man moving his lips without a word and turned away.
In barely thirty minutes, the street had been devastated. Monster carcasses lay among human bodies.
I sharpened my senses and searched the area, but felt no other signs of life.
The damage never should have been this bad.
It was tragic enough that a monster wave had struck this peaceful little city.
And that the hundreds of protesters gathered to condemn me had chosen this street for their rally.
Splash. Splash.
I crossed the street through puddles of mingled red and blue blood.
The hyenas had already caught the scent. They rushed me with cameras and microphones.
“What do you think of this monster wave?”
“You arrived before anyone else and stopped the monster wave! First, as a fellow human being, I’d like to express my deepest gratitude—”
“These people were here to condemn you. Could someone who supports you have caused this monster wave deliberately—”
“Why hasn’t Mr. Sky appeared yet? What connection do you have to the recent death of Siegfried Bassmann?”
“Jin, give us a statement!”
It felt as though filth were raining down on me from every direction.
A few defended me, but far more reporters were desperate for sensational headlines.
And I suspected many of them were being paid handsomely to ask those questions.
By someone like...
Odin Guild.
I’d already suspected as much. I hadn’t been particularly surprised when Team Leader Choi first told me.
Turn the media against us, and public opinion would follow.
Dragging me and Ares Guild through the mud so openly, when we had overwhelming public support, wasn’t something just anyone could attempt.
Michael Silbert had both the power and the justification to try.
The problem was that, in the media at least, it was working far better than I’d imagined.
“The Prophet still hasn’t shown himself. What would you say to him, knowing he’s watching you from somewhere?”
“Statistics show that Ares Guild handles an average of 3.6 incidents a day, while Odin Guild handles 6.5. Any comment?”
“Mr. Jin Taekyung! Mr. Jin Taekyung!”
“Hey, you! What kind of question is that? You call yourselves reporters?”
“Everyone, step back. Now!”
It was chaos.
Reporters pushed forward for more stories and more payoffs. Police officers and Hunters struggled to hold them back.
I slipped between them, my stomach churning, while a voice seemed to echo inside my head.
You humans... really are a shitshow.
I never thought I’d hear that from a monster.
But I had no answer.
Maybe seeing that sign had taken the fight out of me.
“Shut up. You’re loud.”
I hadn’t used much internal energy, but I was mentally exhausted. After giving the Skeleton King a curt reply inside my Inventory, I pulled out the Magic Scroll I’d brought and tore it.
Riiip. Fwoosh!
The familiar sensation of Teleport Magic swept through me.
The scenery changed in an instant. As my vision cleared, I saw a familiar face.
“You’re back early. I only just heard you were on your way.”
Exhaustion weighed on Song Song’s voice, and she had dark circles under her eyes that hadn’t been there before. She promptly held out a handkerchief.
“Wipe your face. You’ve got blood on it.”
I looked from the handkerchief to her and smacked my lips.
“Just curious. Are you saving your Clean Magic to make soup with?”

“Do you think Magic works by putting coins into it? You can chug potions to replenish mana, but you can’t replenish mental energy that’s already been spent. I’m already not getting enough sleep these days, so shut up and use the handkerchief.”
I knew who was chiefly responsible for her lack of sleep, so I couldn’t argue.
I wiped off the blood and handed it back. Song Song took the dirty handkerchief and quietly cast a spell.
“Clean.”
Whoosh.
Dust and blood vanished, leaving the handkerchief spotless.
I stared at her. She blinked innocently.
“What? It’s designer.”
At that shameless answer—and the realization that she’d set me up for it—I couldn’t help snorting.
“Ha.”
“There. You’re smiling. You looked miserable on TV.”
“You were watching?”
“I saw it live. Heard those fucking reporters talking bullshit, too.”
“...Well, I guess I have to take it. When you get down to it, I bear some responsibility for this mess.”
Song Song frowned.
“Are you going to start talking bullshit too?”
“I thought you were getting back to normal. What’s with you? If you want to blame yourself that badly, kill those bastards first. Then you can beat yourself up all you like.”
That was exactly what I wanted to do.
But it wasn’t that easy. Three days had passed since our trip to Switzerland, and little had changed.
Magic Johnson’s investigation had produced no results. Neither magic nor satellite surveillance could find a trace of The Prophet. And Michael Silbert’s Odin Guild kept rising higher by the day.

“Don’t blame yourself so much, and don’t worry so much. You’re not the only one working hard. Uncle Kkeokjeong was raising hell yesterday, saying he’d go straight to Paris and cut Michael’s head off.”
“That... It’s reassuring to have an entire army on our side, but if he did that, Uncle Kkeokjeong would be the one losing his head.”
“Yeah. That’s exactly what I told him.”
“You told him that?”
“Of course. It’s true. He was a bit dejected, but he came around pretty quickly.”
Well, I was grateful for that much.
Song Song and I talked as we walked. By the time she’d finished telling me about my mother and Hayeon, who were staying at the mansion under tight security, we had reached Team Leader Choi’s office.
“You’re here.”
He looked even more exhausted than Song Song. His usually immaculate office was a mess, and empty coffee cups covered the desk.
“Thank you for making the long trip. But...”
Team Leader Choi looked back and forth between Song Song and me, then lowered his voice.
“Where’s the other one?”
“Don’t worry. He came with me.”
I’m here.
Had I kept him shut away too long? He sounded furious.
I took the Skeleton King out of my Inventory, pretending to rummage through the subspace pouch at my waist as I recited the command.
Inventory open. Summon.
A sturdy young white man popped into view. Song Song muttered, “Wow. Easy birth.”
“Shut your mouth, beautiful but ill-mannered human female. How dare you compare this body to such a thing...”
“Thanks. I feel so much better now.”
“Damn it.”
The Skeleton King’s face was full of displeasure as he muttered a curse, but there was nothing we could do about it.
Even if his identity is partly out in the open, we need to keep him hidden as much as we can.
We’d given him a new past and identity, but nothing in this world was perfect. Even the Pentagon, supposedly the most secure place on earth, had been breached the same way.
Given the circumstances, we had no choice but to limit his exposure as much as possible.
But Team Leader Choi’s next words made me realize we would have to play the Skeleton King card.
“Three minutes ago, Tokyo Bay collapsed.”

And I suspected many of them were being paid handsomely to ask those questions.
By someone like...
Odin Guild.
I’d already suspected as much.
I hadn’t been particularly surprised when Team Leader Choi first told me.
Turn the media against us, and public opinion would follow.
Dragging me and Ares Guild through the mud so openly, when we had overwhelming public support, wasn’t something just anyone could attempt.
Michael Silbert had both the power and the justification to try.
The problem was that, in the media at least, it was working far better than I’d imagined.
“The Prophet still hasn’t shown himself.
What would you say to him, knowing he’s watching you from somewhere?”
“Statistics show that Ares Guild handles an average of 3.6 incidents a day, while Odin Guild handles 6.5.
Any comment?”
“Mr.
Jin Taekyung!
Mr.
Jin Taekyung!”
“Hey, you!
What kind of question is that?
You call yourselves reporters?”
“Everyone, step back.
Now!”
It was chaos.
Reporters pushed forward for more stories and more payoffs.
Police officers and Hunters struggled to hold them back.
I slipped between them, my stomach churning, while a voice seemed to echo inside my head.
You humans... really are a shitshow.
I never thought I’d hear that from a monster.
But I had no answer.
Maybe seeing that sign had taken the fight out of me.
“Shut up.
You’re loud.”
I hadn’t used much internal energy, but I was mentally exhausted.
After giving the Skeleton King a curt reply inside my Inventory, I pulled out the Magic Scroll I’d brought and tore it.
Riiip.
Fwoosh!
The familiar sensation of Teleport Magic swept through me.
The scenery changed in an instant.
As my vision cleared, I saw a familiar face.
“You’re back early.
I only just heard you were on your way.”
Exhaustion weighed on Song Song’s voice, and she had dark circles under her eyes that hadn’t been there before.
She promptly held out a handkerchief.
“Wipe your face.
You’ve got blood on it.”
I looked from the handkerchief to her and smacked my lips.
“Just curious.
Are you saving your Clean Magic to make soup with?”
“Do you think Magic works by putting coins into it?
You can chug potions to replenish mana, but you can’t replenish mental energy that’s already been spent.
I’m already not getting enough sleep these days, so shut up and use the handkerchief.”
I knew who was chiefly responsible for her lack of sleep, so I couldn’t argue.
I wiped off the blood and handed it back.
Song Song took the dirty handkerchief and quietly cast a spell.
“Clean.”
Whoosh.
Dust and blood vanished, leaving the handkerchief spotless.
I stared at her.
She blinked innocently.
“What?
It’s designer.”
At that shameless answer—and the realization that she’d set me up for it—I couldn’t help snorting.
“Ha.”
“There.
You’re smiling.
You looked miserable on TV.”
“You were watching?”
“I saw it live.
Heard those fucking reporters talking bullshit, too.”
“...Well, I guess I have to take it.
When you get down to it, I bear some responsibility for this mess.”
Song Song frowned.
“Are you going to start talking bullshit too?”
“I thought you were getting back to normal.
What’s with you?
If you want to blame yourself that badly, kill those bastards first.
Then you can beat yourself up all you like.”
That was exactly what I wanted to do.
But it wasn’t that easy.
Three days had passed since our trip to Switzerland, and little had changed.
Magic Johnson’s investigation had produced no results.
Neither magic nor satellite surveillance could find a trace of The Prophet.
And Michael Silbert’s Odin Guild kept rising higher by the day.
“Don’t blame yourself so much, and don’t worry so much.
You’re not the only one working hard.
Uncle Kkeokjeong was raising hell yesterday, saying he’d go straight to Paris and cut Michael’s head off.”
“That...
It’s reassuring to have an entire army on our side, but if he did that, Uncle Kkeokjeong would be the one losing his head.”
“Yeah.
That’s exactly what I told him.”
“You told him that?”
“Of course.
It’s true.
He was a bit dejected, but he came around pretty quickly.”
Well, I was grateful for that much.
Song Song and I talked as we walked.
By the time she’d finished telling me about my mother and Hayeon, who were staying at the mansion under tight security, we had reached Team Leader Choi’s office.
“You’re here.”
He looked even more exhausted than Song Song.
His usually immaculate office was a mess, and empty coffee cups covered the desk.
“Thank you for making the long trip.
But...”
Team Leader Choi looked back and forth between Song Song and me, then lowered his voice.
“Where’s the other one?”
“Don’t worry.
He came with me.”
I’m here.
Had I kept him shut away too long?
He sounded furious.
I took the Skeleton King out of my Inventory, pretending to rummage through the subspace pouch at my waist as I recited the command.
Inventory open.
Summon.
A sturdy young white man popped into view.
Song Song muttered, “Wow.
Easy birth.”
“Shut your mouth, beautiful but ill-mannered human female.
How dare you compare this body to such a thing...”
“Thanks.
I feel so much better now.”
“Damn it.”
The Skeleton King’s face was full of displeasure as he muttered a curse, but there was nothing we could do about it.
Even if his identity is partly out in the open, we need to keep him hidden as much as we can.
We’d given him a new past and identity, but nothing in this world was perfect.
Even the Pentagon, supposedly the most secure place on earth, had been breached the same way.
Given the circumstances, we had no choice but to limit his exposure as much as possible.
But Team Leader Choi’s next words made me realize we would have to play the Skeleton King card.
“Three minutes ago, Tokyo Bay collapsed.”

chapters.title: Chapter 747
paragraphs: Beneath a sky shrouded in dark clouds, Sugihara Gyoiku stared blankly ahead.
What the hell just happened?
He was an ordinary civilian. His mind could not make sense of what had happened to him.
His arms and legs shook beyond his control. His stomach, full of salty seawater, could not bear the rescue helicopter’s rough movements.
No—perhaps what Gyoiku truly could not endure was the horrifying reality that had suddenly come crashing down on him.
“Ugh—bwaaaargh!”
Vomit sprayed everywhere.
Some of it hit the other people in the rescue net with him, but no one complained. No one even seemed to notice.
They only stared at the scene below with vacant eyes.
Craaaack!
Things broke, collapsed, and were swept away.
A wave dozens of meters high. Perhaps even hundreds of meters.
Even as they watched it happen, they could scarcely believe the disaster swallowing everything in its path.

The port of Tokyo Bay, where hundreds of ships came and went every day, had vanished without a trace. Cargo ships weighing tens of thousands of metric tons apiece broke apart like Styrofoam and rode the waves into a nearby industrial complex.
Rumble—BOOM!
Flames surged upward with a deafening roar, swallowing people’s screams.
Alarms wailed without pause. Far below, cars and crowds that looked as small as swarms of ants scattered in every direction.
Fleeing the disaster.
Unable to accept the fate that had befallen them.
And behind those struggling desperately to survive, an enormous shadow fell across the ground.
Whoooooosh!
“Ah... Ahhh...”
The survivors watching from above let out hollow moans.
The land they had painstakingly rebuilt through decades of sweat and blood after the Great Cataclysm was collapsing. A magnificent civilization was falling apart.
The white foam that had always scattered against the breakwaters and the blue seawater had both turned red.
Nothing could stop that enormous wave as it smashed through and swept away everything in its path.
No. Even if the wave subsided, it would make no difference.
This was not merely a natural disaster.
Something worse lurked beneath the deep waters that had swallowed the port and industrial complex.

The survivors who had miraculously lived through it knew the truth. That was why, upon spotting dozens of fighter jets flying toward them from the opposite direction, they could only scream as though coughing up blood.
“N-No!”
“Don’t come!”
But their desperate cries reached no one.
Not the squadron of fighter jets streaking across the sky with sonic booms. Not the elite Japanese Hunters aboard them, sent to deal with the disaster.
And not the deep-sea monster awakened from its long sleep.
Goooooong.
A low, immense call raised the waves just as they had begun to subside.
The strengthening wind whipped into a storm. Thunder rumbled among the countless dark clouds that now covered the sky.
Rumble, rumble...
Every living thing nearby froze like a statue and stared blankly upward.
It was fear engraved deep in their bones, an instinct they felt simply because they were alive.
Power.
The power of nature—and yet something beyond nature.
“What the hell is that...?”
The pilot was about to order the waiting Hunters to descend when the words escaped him in a groan.
At that moment—
Fwoosh!
Hundreds—thousands—of bolts of lightning plunged from the sky, turning the whole world white.
The Japanese Ministry of Defense’s operations control room, hastily called into session, was silent.
Suffocating silence. Throats working soundlessly. Unfocused eyes.
Dozens of high-ranking officials and generals were present, but no one spoke. They could only stare at the holographic screen with vacant eyes.
What... What just happened?
The same thought occupied every mind.

The flash had filled the screen with light so fierce that they had closed their eyes without realizing it. When they opened them again, all they saw were dozens of aircraft falling toward the ground—and the waves swallowing them.
“Th-They’ve all been wiped out.”
Someone’s thoughtless report broke the silence. It confirmed the truth none of them wanted to face.
Everything was gone. No—everyone was dead.
The hundreds, thousands of lightning bolts had turned everything within their range to ash.
The rescue helicopters carrying the miraculous survivors. The Air Self-Defense Force’s prized fighter squadron. The hundreds of Hunters mobilized for the emergency.
All gone.
But it was not only the tsunami—already engulfing ten cities and threatening the capital—that had plunged the control room into deathly silence.
The monster.
They had seen a monster that had vanished decades ago, one they had believed would never return.
“...Susanoo.”
The nickname came from its supposed command of the sea and storms.
The general who muttered it hurriedly shut his mouth when he felt the Defense Minister’s glare.
“Th-That was...”
“Shut your trap, Yoshimura.”
The Japanese Defense Minister cut off the general’s attempted excuse and looked around.
Half the people who should have been devising a response were still floundering in shock. The rest waited for him to speak again.
Like baby birds waiting to be fed.
Or people looking for the one scapegoat willing to take responsibility in their place.
Grind.
The elderly Defense Minister clenched his teeth.
For all the generals and officials in this room, he could not find a single suitable person.
The foolish, cowardly Prime Minister had retreated to a bunker long ago. The few capable, responsible commanders lacked the powerful backers needed to get into the Ministry of Defense’s control room.
That left only one person to shoulder the burden.
Incompetent bastards!
He cursed them inwardly, forgetting that he owed his own rise to an ancestor who had been a daimyo. But he was not so foolish that he could deny the reality before him.
“Stop that thing with everything we have! Self-Defense Forces, Hunters—I don’t care. Use every means at our disposal!”
“Y-Yes, sir!”
Bang!
The Defense Minister slammed his wrinkled hand on the table, then squeezed his eyes shut. He could not bring himself to finish.
Do we really... do we really have to go this far?
The hesitation lasted only a moment.
The situation had already spiraled out of control. If anyone could keep it from becoming an even greater disaster, it was that man.
“Ask the world for help. And that man in particular—we must bring him here, no matter what diplomatic price we have to pay.”
“What?”
“If it’s him...”
His lips trembled like a child faced with a plate of broccoli.
Then, facing the people staring back at him with no idea what he meant, the Defense Minister shouted until it seemed as though he were coughing up blood.
“That man! I said call that Chōsenjin! Jin Taekyuuung!”
His pride as a subject of the Great Japanese Empire rebelled at the thought, but he had no choice.
That monster—Leviathan—was a demon sent down from heaven.
We can’t let that nightmare happen again!
Before long, news reports playing on holographic televisions throughout the control room confirmed that he had been right to choose Jin Taekyung.

—The world has once again been engulfed in flames. In a video, the figure known as “The Prophet,” who carried out an unprecedented series of terrorist attacks ten days ago, has announced a second series of attacks...
—Breaking news. A Monster Wave has occurred in Manhattan, United States. The United States and countries around the world are entering a state of emergency...

—Entry and exit bans are now in effect for countries experiencing Monster Waves. As a result, part of the emergency mobilization of Hunters to assist Tokyo has fallen through. Among nearby Asian countries, Korea is believed to be the only one able to provide support...
“Japan’s Ministry of Defense has officially requested emergency assistance through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.”
The news President Baek Hanseong passed on to us was the starting gun. Everything had begun.
“Ares Guild and Peace Guild are heading out as the advance team. Five teams are already standing by, all volunteers of B-rank or higher.”
Team Leader Choi had acted faster than anyone.

The moment he first heard what had happened in Tokyo, he had already issued the mobilization order. President Baek Hanseong had prepared the Air Force so that we could reach our destination as quickly and safely as possible.
“What about a Teleport Magic Formation?” I asked as I gathered the equipment we needed.
Team Leader Choi shook his head.

“We could try it, but the probability of failure is far too high right now. The magical-power distribution around Tokyo rose sharply because of the Monster Wave ten days ago, and it’s already measuring more than three times the previous level.”
“Damn it. Reminds me of China.”
“Yes. It’s the same situation.”
Mana and magical power were opposed to each other.
Attempt spatial travel while magical-power levels were climbing this fast and fluctuating this wildly, and even a body made of solid iron could come apart like a thousand-piece puzzle.
“Then how long will it take?”
“Allowing for the worsening weather nearby, about thirty minutes.”
“Thirty minutes...”
Of course, we would not be landing safely on a wide airport runway.
There was at least a ninety-percent chance that Tokyo International Airport, once the pride of Japan, had already been blown to absolute shit.
And the other ten percent is the chance it’ll be blown to shit before we get there.
I took a deep breath.
The footage Japan’s Ministry of Defense had sent us replayed in my mind.
The Maritime Self-Defense Force swept away by a gigantic triangular wave. Land disappearing beneath the water.

It had broken through the extensive defensive Magic along Japan’s coastline as though it were nothing, swallowed tens of thousands of people, and reduced what little hope remained to ash beneath countless bolts of lightning.
As though proving the power attributed to it in myths passed down from time immemorial.
Leviathan.
The devil of the sea that had ruled the waters during the Great Cataclysm.
One of the most powerful S-rank monsters under the Demon King Asmodeus. A calamity that had vanished when Asmodeus died.
Some said Leviathan had died with the Demon King. Others insisted it had survived and was merely biding its time. With no evidence either way, the years had passed.
And today, more than thirty years later, the nightmare called Leviathan had returned.
Was its appearance a coincidence, or...
Had someone intended it?
Muttering the unresolved question inwardly, I finished my preparations and began walking toward the Hunters and aircraft waiting for me.
The wind blowing from far away seemed to carry a faint smell of blood.

chapters.title: Chapter 748
paragraphs: “Jin Taekyung has accepted Japan’s request for assistance.”
Michael Silbert listened to Huginn’s report and answered calmly.
“And?”

“Ares Guild and Peace Guild have assembled five teams of handpicked Hunters, and the Korean government has mobilized the Air Force to take them to Tokyo. I’ve prepared the Hunters’ profiles, just in case.”
Huginn handed him a tablet containing detailed information on every Hunter in the relief force. Michael glanced at it, and a faint smile crossed his lips.
“Well done. Any assistance from outside Korea?”
“None at present. China would be a great help if it joined in, but it lost its core forces in the war against the Arch Lich, and its relations with Japan are poor. It won’t answer the request.”
China had already suffered enormous losses fighting the Arch Lich and in the terrorist attack on Beijing ten days earlier.

Even with its vast number of Hunters, taking on a top-tier monster capable of causing a disaster by itself would be a heavy burden. All the more so when the request came from Japan, a country with which China had appalling diplomatic relations.
“There’s no need to worry about China. Even if the old Chairman wants to help Jin Taekyung, circumstances at home won’t allow it.”
Huginn realized there was something he had not yet been told.
“Are you planning to strike China again?”
“Someone might get the wrong idea if they heard you say that. A terrorist attack is an unfortunate event no one can predict before it happens. Don’t you agree?”
Michael held his gaze. Huginn lowered his head.
“My apologies. I misspoke.”
“Don’t worry about it. Everyone makes mistakes.”
“And this is only my personal opinion, but I suspect Shanghai may be the next target.”
His tone was casual, but Huginn could smell the thick blood embedded in those words.
Shanghai was China’s most populous metropolis. After Beijing, which had been struck ten days ago, another staggering loss of life was all but certain.
China is paying dearly for siding with Jin Taekyung.
And China was hardly alone.
Most people saw the series of attacks as indiscriminate terrorism. But the countries and Guilds that had shown Jin Taekyung a friendly face were being punished.
And it’ll end one of two ways.
Huginn muttered inwardly as he looked at his superior.
There stood a conqueror with greater ambitions than anyone else in the world, pressing toward his grand objective.
So why did Huginn feel this way?
I have a bad feeling about this.

The situation was perfect. Leviathan was a monster as powerful as the Arch Lich. And unlike the battle against the Arch Lich, in which no fewer than six S-rank Hunters had taken part, Jin Taekyung could expect no outside help this time beyond the forces already at his disposal, including Japan’s.
But...
If Jin Taekyung manages to overcome even this...
The thought came to him ominously.
What if, just this once, his superior had made the wrong choice? What if this trap became the sturdy rope that pulled Jin Taekyung out of the mire?
A vibration soon buried Huginn’s doubts.
Rrrrrumble.
“Entry into the operation area complete. Preparing to descend in ten seconds.”
The pilot’s report came through the speakers as the aircraft shook. Then Huginn heard his superior’s quiet voice.
“It’s begun.”
Michael, now clad in dazzling silver armor, was looking out the window.
A city engulfed in the cries of monsters and towering flames. The battlefield where the name Michael Silbert would once again be etched into the minds of the world.
“Prepare yourself, Huginn.”
He pressed a crown-engraved helmet onto his head. Looking like a god of old, he spoke to his crow once more.
“Prepare to become the best—beyond anyone’s doubt.”
The wait had been long. The pain had been deep.
Now he wanted to paint his name across this many-colored world. Not Cheon Taemin’s. Not Jin Taekyung’s.
Michael Silbert’s.
Humanity ruled five oceans and six continents. It had named every living thing it knew, past and present.
Rabbits. Dogs. Cats. Horses. Dinosaurs...
But there were exceptions.
Some beings passed down from the distant past possessed forms beyond humanity’s ability to comprehend and overwhelming power. It was difficult to explain them as anything else.
One such being was now bringing disaster upon humanity.
Goooooong.
A low cry reverberated in every direction.
Beneath deep waters filled with countless pieces of wreckage and mixed with blood, a gigantic mythical beast advanced with the waves, smashing and sweeping away everything that stood in its path.
Craaaack!
Some called it a crocodile. Others compared it to a whale.
In the end, humanity could find no way to define it. It was too enormous to be treated as a mere animal, and it possessed a mysterious power no one could explain.
So they called it a monster beyond explanation. Over the centuries, it acquired a name that meant this creature and no other.
Far away, amid human screams, that name rang out.
“Le—Leviathan!”
“This is an order! All B-rank Hunters and below, leave the battlefield immedia—”
WHOOOOOOM!
The shouts and screams vanished. A wave of overwhelming force swallowed and shattered everything in its path.
People. Buildings. Even the pitiful defensive Magic.
Grrrrr.
Leviathan let out a satisfied growl as waves dozens of meters high swept through the surrounding area.
It had been so long since it had awakened from that tiresome sleep. So long since it had rampaged to its heart’s content.
Yes. That was the last time.
Leviathan remembered its master.
The Demon King Asmodeus.
The absolute ruler who had united the chaotic Demon Realm and brought every monster to heel.
Yet even Asmodeus had fallen to human hands. Leviathan had retreated into the deep sea and gone to sleep.
With its master gone, it could no longer obtain the vast quantities of magical power and food it once had. To survive until the day he returned, it had needed to conserve its strength.
And the wait had not been in vain.
It’s changed. Nothing like it was when the Demon King was here, but it has changed.

Leviathan had still been uncertain when it awoke and crossed the ocean. The closer it came to this place, though, the more clearly it sensed the abundant magical power permeating the water, the land, the air.
And what, exactly, had awakened it.
Leviathan’s enormous eyes flashed.
In the deep waters that had become part of the sea, a powerful energy reached it from among countless pieces of wreckage and human corpses.
That’s...
There was no mistaking it. The appetizing scent of a Magic Gem—the source of a monster’s power.
One untouched by human hands, still holding all its original energy. A mass of pure magical power.
An excellent source of food, more than enough to replenish the strength it had expended, had been waiting for Leviathan in the human settlement.
So that’s why.
Leviathan understood what had awakened it. The magical power now permeating the world, combined with something containing energy of that magnitude, had been enough.
Leviathan was the calamity and ruler of the sea. Starved by its long sleep, its body had responded to the pulse of power carried through the seawater.
If I can make that magical power mine...
Greed filled Leviathan’s eyes. A feast lay before it. Why refuse?
Whoooooosh.
Leviathan surged forward.
The water grew shallower as it advanced toward its prey, exposing part of its back. The beast did not hesitate.
It had already assessed the situation. The humans in its path were weak, and all around it surged seawater that obeyed its will.
“It’s coming!”
“Lightning mages, prepare!”
“Ranged units, fire!”
Fwish-fwish-fwish! Crackle!
Countless arrows and lightning spells streaked through the air. The hastily assembled Hunters poured every ounce of strength into their volley.
The result was dismal.
BOOM-BOOM-BOOM!
The explosions cleared. The Hunters stared.
“What the...?”
A little scorching. Dozens of wounds.
No. Scratches.
That was the full extent of the damage they had inflicted on the monster before them. And the price that returned moments later was harsh.
Whoooosh—BOOM!
An enormous tail broke the surface and struck the water.
The tanks at the front clenched their teeth as a wave rose with a thunderous roar. They planted their half-submerged legs and layered their Tower Shields into a wall.
Clack-clack-clack!
Their movements were vigorous and as fast as lightning.
Fewer than a hundred Hunters remained, but every one of them was at least B-rank. They were seasoned fighters. They knew their duty.
“Formaaaaation!”
“Don’t fall back! Hold!”
“Protect us from the enemy, Great Shield!”
The tanks’ desperate shouts mingled with the mages’ incantations.
Then Leviathan spoke in a Demon Realm language none of them understood.
“Get lost.”
The enormous wave rising around it surged forward and split.
Splaash!
One wave became dozens. Dozens became hundreds of streams. Charged with powerful magical power, they took the shape of spears and fell upon the Hunters.
KABOOOOOM!
A shock wave arrived with a thunderous roar and shook everything around them.
Hundreds of spears made of water and magical power tore through the layered defensive Magic and crushed the Tower Shields standing before them like an iron wall.
Crack! Thunk-thunk-thunk!
“Urgh...!”
The water spears swallowed even the screams as they smashed armor and cut through flesh and bone.
The streams ran red with blood. As Hunters crumpled beneath them, a fierce wind swept overhead.
Tat-tat-tat-tat-tat!
Propellers churned.
Dozens of unmanned fighter jets broke through the storm and immediately opened fire with their guns and missiles.
Destroy Leviathan?
No one dreamed of it.
Their only goal was to hold the monster up, however briefly, until the main force capable of fighting it arrived.
But contrary to the hopes of those watching the scene from the operations control room, Leviathan’s power and authority were simply too overwhelming.
Goooooong.
The ancient beast that commanded tidal waves and storms roared. Lightning fell from the cloud-choked sky and swept through the unmanned jets.
Rrrrrumble—BOOM!
They crashed. Exploded. Sank.
At the center of the calamity, Leviathan drove its enormous body onward.
Its long sleep and the considerable magical power it had spent had left it slightly tired. None of that mattered.
That mass of magical power was drawing closer by the moment. Its scent was so appetizing it nearly overwhelmed Leviathan’s reason.
With it, Leviathan could regain its former strength. Cover this land with a tidal wave and claim it for its own.
Grrrrraaaah.
At last, with its prey before it, Leviathan opened its jaws wide.
Its crocodile-like maw swept toward the corpses and wreckage submerged in the deep water—and the mass of magical power hidden somewhere among them—to swallow everything in one bite.
It would have.
If not for a streak of light that descended onto the rippling surface of the water.
Fwoooooosh! Craaaack!
Blue-white light-flames, burning with tremendous heat, consumed the wave.

sentences.text: “Jin Taekyung has accepted Japan’s request for assistance.”
Michael Silbert listened to Huginn’s report and answered calmly.
“And?”
“Ares Guild and Peace Guild have assembled five teams of handpicked Hunters, and the Korean government has mobilized the Air Force to take them to Tokyo.
I’ve prepared the Hunters’ profiles, just in case.”
Huginn handed him a tablet containing detailed information on every Hunter in the relief force.
Michael glanced at it, and a faint smile crossed his lips.
“Well done.
Any assistance from outside Korea?”
“None at present.
China would be a great help if it joined in, but it lost its core forces in the war against the Arch Lich, and its relations with Japan are poor.
It won’t answer the request.”
China had already suffered enormous losses fighting the Arch Lich and in the terrorist attack on Beijing ten days earlier.
Even with its vast number of Hunters, taking on a top-tier monster capable of causing a disaster by itself would be a heavy burden.
All the more so when the request came from Japan, a country with which China had appalling diplomatic relations.
“There’s no need to worry about China.
Even if the old Chairman wants to help Jin Taekyung, circumstances at home won’t allow it.”
Huginn realized there was something he had not yet been told.
“Are you planning to strike China again?”
“Someone might get the wrong idea if they heard you say that.
A terrorist attack is an unfortunate event no one can predict before it happens.
Don’t you agree?”
Michael held his gaze.
Huginn lowered his head.
“My apologies.
I misspoke.”
“Don’t worry about it.
Everyone makes mistakes.”
“And this is only my personal opinion, but I suspect Shanghai may be the next target.”
His tone was casual, but Huginn could smell the thick blood embedded in those words.
Shanghai was China’s most populous metropolis.
After Beijing, which had been struck ten days ago, another staggering loss of life was all but certain.
China is paying dearly for siding with Jin Taekyung.
And China was hardly alone.
Most people saw the series of attacks as indiscriminate terrorism.
But the countries and Guilds that had shown Jin Taekyung a friendly face were being punished.
And it’ll end one of two ways.
Huginn muttered inwardly as he looked at his superior.
There stood a conqueror with greater ambitions than anyone else in the world, pressing toward his grand objective.
So why did Huginn feel this way?
I have a bad feeling about this.
The situation was perfect.
Leviathan was a monster as powerful as the Arch Lich.

And unlike the battle against the Arch Lich, in which no fewer than six S-rank Hunters had taken part, Jin Taekyung could expect no outside help this time beyond the forces already at his disposal, including Japan’s.
But...
If Jin Taekyung manages to overcome even this...
The thought came to him ominously.
What if, just this once, his superior had made the wrong choice?
What if this trap became the sturdy rope that pulled Jin Taekyung out of the mire?
A vibration soon buried Huginn’s doubts.
Rrrrrumble.
“Entry into the operation area complete.
Preparing to descend in ten seconds.”
The pilot’s report came through the speakers as the aircraft shook.
Then Huginn heard his superior’s quiet voice.
“It’s begun.”
Michael, now clad in dazzling silver armor, was looking out the window.
A city engulfed in the cries of monsters and towering flames.
The battlefield where the name Michael Silbert would once again be etched into the minds of the world.
“Prepare yourself, Huginn.”
He pressed a crown-engraved helmet onto his head.
Looking like a god of old, he spoke to his crow once more.
“Prepare to become the best—beyond anyone’s doubt.”
The wait had been long.
The pain had been deep.
Now he wanted to paint his name across this many-colored world.
Not Cheon Taemin’s.
Not Jin Taekyung’s.
Michael Silbert’s.

It had named every living thing it knew, past and present.
Rabbits.
Dogs.
Cats.
Horses.
Dinosaurs...
