chapters.title: Chapter 749
paragraphs: Leviathan was both the calamity and the king of the sea.
That was true in the Demon Realm and on Earth alike.
The sea was Leviathan’s birthplace, a battlefield where it had never known defeat. Within that vast territory, granted to it at birth, nothing could escape the king’s watch.
Or so it should have been.
Fwoooooosh!
In an instant, the monster stopped, its prey before it and greed filling its thoughts. At the same time, Leviathan’s senses, numbed by its long starvation, awakened.
What is this?
When had it begun?
As realization struck, the world seemed to slow. Leviathan could see and feel it clearly now.
A mighty force, swift as lightning and carrying the heat of the sun.
The flames plunging down and swallowing the blue surface were headed straight for it.
Splaaash!
There was no time to hesitate.
The enormous maw it had opened to swallow its prey turned sharply underwater. An instant later, Leviathan bit down on the flames with hundreds of teeth imbued with magical power.
It had no doubt it would crush them.
Krrrk!
Then flame met teeth, and an impact strong enough to rattle its skull struck.
Krrrrrrk!
What?
Leviathan’s enormous eyes widened in pain and shock.
The teeth that had sunk dozens of aircraft carriers during the Great Cataclysm—those sharp, destructive weapons—had shattered in a single blow.
How? How is this possible?
Leviathan froze, unable to make sense of it.
Then the countless bubbles stirred up by the collision scattered, revealing the cause.
A spear.
Gooooong.
The silver spear trembled, wreathed in flames that refused to go out even amid the water and waves.
As though it were alive. As though it liked the touch of the hand holding it.
And through the owner of that spear flowed the blood of a species Leviathan had killed countless times.
“How can a mere human...!”
At the cry of the mythical beast, filled with undisguised astonishment, the small and insignificant human answered by merely moving his lips.
One Annihilation.
A distant flash of light dyed the sea.
People often say that life comes down to one big shot.
I agree. Especially since going for that one shot can be exactly how you throw your life away.
Rrrrrumble!
A thunderous roar, as if the sky—or rather, the sea—were splitting apart.
A tremendous shock wave sent my spent body flying. Swept up in a swirling current, I heard warnings sound again and again as my vision faded.
Beep. Beep-beep!

System You have exhausted all your internal energy and stamina! - Your body cannot withstand the recoil of One Annihilation! - Status abnormality, Internal Energy Depletion, has been applied! - Status abnormality, Exhaustion, has been applied! - Status abnormality, Anemia, has been applied! - Status abnormality, Muscle Tear, has been applied! - Status abnormality, Internal Injury, has been applied! - Warning! Warning! Remember that every action comes with a price! - Excessive use of power may turn into a blade against you. - Special debuff, Broken Body, has been applied! - All combat-related attributes decrease by 50 until recovery! Depending on how recovery goes, you may permanently lose some attributes! Strength temporarily decreases by 50! Agility...
High risk, high return.
That was exactly it.

As I grew stronger, the power of One Annihilation had risen exponentially—until even this nearly perfect body, one that people in Murim might mistake for a Heavenly Martial Physique, could no longer withstand it.
Damn it.
I was dizzy. My breathing was ragged.
My body had gone beyond exhaustion and was screaming in agony. My dantian, dry as a desert, begged me to stop.
The backlash was so severe I could not move a finger.
But if I had not anticipated a situation like this, I would never have attempted something as insane as firing One Annihilation in the first place.
Open Inventory. Summon.
The System responded to my thought. A silhouette appeared in my blurred vision, and someone’s curt voice rang inside my head.
“You look awful. It suits you perfectly.”
I never thought I would be so glad to hear that rude tone.
Seeing me grin despite the pain, the Skeleton King clicked his tongue and shoved a small crystal bottle into my mouth.
A solution available only in this world.
A treasure known as a Top-Grade Potion.
Gulp.
The moment I managed to swallow it, a refreshing energy spread through every part of my body.
Ding!
System You have used Top-Grade Potion! - All status abnormalities have been removed!
My empty dantian filled to the brim. My torn muscles knitted back together, and my hazy vision became clear and sharp.
Healing power on par with a Level Up.
But the warning that followed caught even me off guard.
Beep!
System The special debuff, Broken Body, rejects the effect! - This debuff cannot be removed by artificial means! - The effects of Broken Body remain active!
...What the hell?
For a moment, I was thrown by something I had never experienced before. But I had no time to work out what the warning meant.
The fight was not over.
Grrrrrrrrrrr!
A roar rang out, clear even underwater.
Leviathan’s enormous body writhed in pain. Not even the countless wrecks and corpses sunk deep beneath the sea could conceal it.
KABOOOOOM!
It was some distance away, but I could see how badly it had been hurt.

The maw said to have once torn an aircraft carrier apart in a single bite had been ripped halfway off, along with one eye. Green blood poured from its flank, where hide and bone had been stripped away, staining the water for hundreds of meters around it.
Even so, the monster had been incredibly lucky.
If it had not instinctively turned its head at the last moment—and if this had been land instead of underwater—it would have met its end long ago.
I should have finished it with one strike.
A shame, but there was nothing I could do about it.
My opponent was Leviathan, the calamity of the sea.
They say even a mutt has the advantage in its own yard. Fighting a creature born in the sea, one that had ruled it ever since, was several times harder underwater than fighting the Arch Lich.
But...
I’ll kill it. I have to.
Splaaaaash!
The Skeleton King and I shot forward together. The powerful current in our path did nothing to slow us.
I tightened my webbed hand around the spear shaft. The transparent webbing was an effect of the Water Rescue Worker Title I had earned by completing a Quest at Dongting Lake a few months ago.
It lasted only twenty-four hours each time I activated it. Worse, its clash with the Scorching Yang Qi I had learned reduced all my power by a full twenty percent. But the effect was worth the cost.
Fwoooooosh!
I moved as quickly as though I were using a movement technique on land.
Still howling in pain, Leviathan spotted us closing in and roared.
“GRAAAAAAAH!”
The instant it opened its half-torn maw as wide as it could—
Krrrk. Krrrrrk!
The flow of the water changed. Though there was not a breath of wind underwater, everything around us was sucked toward its maw as if caught in a tornado.
It was a scene worthy of a disaster.
But I did not stop. I planted a foot on a nearby piece of wreckage and kicked off, picking up speed.
Toward the mythical monster. Toward the immense magical power stirring within it.
Then—
Gooooong.
The water and wreckage gathering around Leviathan burst outward in a massive wave.
KRAAAAAAAASH!
Was this what the Breath of the Dragons that once existed felt like?
The wave, charged with tremendous magical power, shot forward and erased everything in its path.
“You treacherous human!”
The Skeleton King shouted urgently behind me.
I did not answer. Instead, I drew on the internal energy filling my lower dantian and set an undying flame in the blade of White Flame.
Sssssss!
Heat spread in every direction. The raging current and pressure seemed to melt away. An energy like molten lava took the place of the sea’s chill.
For this moment, at least, this space belonged to me alone.
Nothing else could intrude.
Cut.
With that single thought, I brought the spearhead down.
Blue-white flames stretched out like a snake and struck the enormous wave just before it hit me.
No. They cut it.
Shhk!
The wave split cleanly in half and scattered to either side.
In that instant, I saw Leviathan’s eye widen in shock.
Then I saw its enormous body swimming at unbelievable speed toward something in the distance—something giving off a chilling energy.
The Magic Gem!
Now I understood why the monster had suddenly reappeared after decades in hiding. What had drawn it to these islands.
“Stop it!”
The Skeleton King reached out a hand with a shout that sounded almost like a scream. Bones rose upward like a growing tree and forcefully pushed against the tips of my feet.
Bang!
A dull boom sounded as I shot forward, cutting through the current toward Leviathan.
GRAAAAAH! KRRRUNCH!

Its crocodile-like maw swallowed a massive tangle of wreckage: steel beams from what had once been a cargo ship, concrete from a collapsed building, and something tiny by comparison that held an energy more dangerous than any of it.
Crunch.
Leviathan chewed and swallowed everything in one bite, then turned its head.
Fear and mockery mingled in its eye as it watched me approach. Then it swam away faster than I had ever seen it move.
Not toward me or the Skeleton King. Toward the open sea it had come from.
“It’ll take time to absorb the energy! Kill it before then!”
I heard the Skeleton King’s shout and gripped White Flame in reverse.
Barely a hundred meters separated us. But no matter how effective the Water Rescue Worker Title was, I could not match Leviathan’s speed.
Once. Just once.
I gathered every bit of internal energy I had left and poured it into the spearhead.
This time... I’ll finish it.
I focused. I felt the flow of the water and steadied my breathing. Every nerve and muscle seemed to come alive, the force of them gathering in my fingertips and shoulder.
Krrrrrk.
The veins across my body stood out.
Then, like releasing a bowstring drawn taut, I hurled the spear with all my strength.
KRAAAAAAAASH!
A single line of flame streaked through the deep water.
But no scream from the monster followed.

A silhouette appeared in my blurred vision, and someone’s curt voice rang inside my head.
“You look awful.
It suits you perfectly.”
I never thought I would be so glad to hear that rude tone.
Seeing me grin despite the pain, the Skeleton King clicked his tongue and shoved a small crystal bottle into my mouth.
A solution available only in this world.
A treasure known as a Top-Grade Potion.
Gulp.
The moment I managed to swallow it, a refreshing energy spread through every part of my body.
Ding!
System You have used Top-Grade Potion! - All status abnormalities have been removed!
My empty dantian filled to the brim.
My torn muscles knitted back together, and my hazy vision became clear and sharp.
Healing power on par with a Level Up.
But the warning that followed caught even me off guard.
Beep!
System The special debuff, Broken Body, rejects the effect! - This debuff cannot be removed by artificial means! - The effects of Broken Body remain active!
...What the hell?
For a moment, I was thrown by something I had never experienced before.
But I had no time to work out what the warning meant.
The fight was not over.
Grrrrrrrrrrr!
A roar rang out, clear even underwater.
Leviathan’s enormous body writhed in pain.
Not even the countless wrecks and corpses sunk deep beneath the sea could conceal it.
KABOOOOOM!
It was some distance away, but I could see how badly it had been hurt.
The maw said to have once torn an aircraft carrier apart in a single bite had been ripped halfway off, along with one eye.
Green blood poured from its flank, where hide and bone had been stripped away, staining the water for hundreds of meters around it.
Even so, the monster had been incredibly lucky.
If it had not instinctively turned its head at the last moment—and if this had been land instead of underwater—it would have met its end long ago.
I should have finished it with one strike.
A shame, but there was nothing I could do about it.
My opponent was Leviathan, the calamity of the sea.
They say even a mutt has the advantage in its own yard.
Fighting a creature born in the sea, one that had ruled it ever since, was several times harder underwater than fighting the Arch Lich.
But...
I’ll kill it.
I have to.
Splaaaaash!
The Skeleton King and I shot forward together.
The powerful current in our path did nothing to slow us.
I tightened my webbed hand around the spear shaft.
The transparent webbing was an effect of the Water Rescue Worker Title I had earned by completing a Quest at Dongting Lake a few months ago.
It lasted only twenty-four hours each time I activated it.
Worse, its clash with the Scorching Yang Qi I had learned reduced all my power by a full twenty percent.
But the effect was worth the cost.
Fwoooooosh!
I moved as quickly as though I were using a movement technique on land.
Still howling in pain, Leviathan spotted us closing in and roared.
“GRAAAAAAAH!”
The instant it opened its half-torn maw as wide as it could—
Krrrk.
Krrrrrk!
The flow of the water changed.
Though there was not a breath of wind underwater, everything around us was sucked toward its maw as if caught in a tornado.
It was a scene worthy of a disaster.
But I did not stop.
I planted a foot on a nearby piece of wreckage and kicked off, picking up speed.
Toward the mythical monster.
Toward the immense magical power stirring within it.
Then—
Gooooong.
The water and wreckage gathering around Leviathan burst outward in a massive wave.
KRAAAAAAAASH!
Was this what the Breath of the Dragons that once existed felt like?
The wave, charged with tremendous magical power, shot forward and erased everything in its path.
“You treacherous human!”
The Skeleton King shouted urgently behind me.
I did not answer.
Instead, I drew on the internal energy filling my lower dantian and set an undying flame in the blade of White Flame.
Sssssss!
Heat spread in every direction.
The raging current and pressure seemed to melt away.
An energy like molten lava took the place of the sea’s chill.
For this moment, at least, this space belonged to me alone.
Nothing else could intrude.
Cut.
With that single thought, I brought the spearhead down.
Blue-white flames stretched out like a snake and struck the enormous wave just before it hit me.
No.
They cut it.
Shhk!
The wave split cleanly in half and scattered to either side.
In that instant, I saw Leviathan’s eye widen in shock.
Then I saw its enormous body swimming at unbelievable speed toward something in the distance—something giving off a chilling energy.
The Magic Gem!
Now I understood why the monster had suddenly reappeared after decades in hiding.
What had drawn it to these islands.
“Stop it!”
The Skeleton King reached out a hand with a shout that sounded almost like a scream.
Bones rose upward like a growing tree and forcefully pushed against the tips of my feet.
Bang!
A dull boom sounded as I shot forward, cutting through the current toward Leviathan.
GRAAAAAH!
KRRRUNCH!

Its crocodile-like maw swallowed a massive tangle of wreckage: steel beams from what had once been a cargo ship, concrete from a collapsed building, and something tiny by comparison that held an energy more dangerous than any of it.
Crunch.
Leviathan chewed and swallowed everything in one bite, then turned its head.
Fear and mockery mingled in its eye as it watched me approach.
Then it swam away faster than I had ever seen it move.
Not toward me or the Skeleton King.
Toward the open sea it had come from.
“It’ll take time to absorb the energy!
Kill it before then!”
I heard the Skeleton King’s shout and gripped White Flame in reverse.
Barely a hundred meters separated us.
But no matter how effective the Water Rescue Worker Title was, I could not match Leviathan’s speed.
Once.
Just once.
I gathered every bit of internal energy I had left and poured it into the spearhead.
This time...
I’ll finish it.
I focused.
I felt the flow of the water and steadied my breathing.
Every nerve and muscle seemed to come alive, the force of them gathering in my fingertips and shoulder.
Krrrrrk.
The veins across my body stood out.
Then, like releasing a bowstring drawn taut, I hurled the spear with all my strength.
KRAAAAAAAASH!
A single line of flame streaked through the deep water.
But no scream from the monster followed.

chapters.title: Chapter 750
paragraphs: Deep beneath the sea.
Countless wrecks and corpses darkened the water until it was impossible to see an inch ahead. Then blue-white flames erupted.
Fwoosh! KRAAAAAASH!
The current split, and the water vaporized.
The flames carried an energy that defied the laws of nature. No—a spear shot forward like a ray of light.
Toward the enormous shadow moving at an unbelievable speed.
Toward a calamity that could never be allowed to live.
But the mythical monster defied the laws of nature just as surely as the energy in the spear did.
KRRRRRUMBLE!
The sea shook.
At the same time, large and small whirlpools of water surged up from the depths and blocked the spearhead as it raced forward.
KOOOOONG!
The collision sent waves of force spreading outward, one after another.
By the time the shock and thunderous roar that had shaken the world had subsided, the flames that had pulverized every obstacle in their path were also fading away, having exhausted their strength.
The spear had failed to reach the monster before its body vanished into the darkness far ahead.
Swish. Clack.
The sea had already grown quiet.
Someone caught the spear as it drifted helplessly with the current.
The man stood with his back to me, staring silently in the direction the monster had gone. He seemed ready to erupt like an active volcano.
No. Let me correct that.
He didn’t merely seem ready to erupt. One touch, and he would explode.
He’d been that way when the monster he could never allow to live had escaped.
And he was that way now.
“Enough.”
The instant the sharp voice slipped from my lips without my realizing it—
Flash.
A vivid green light spread through the water, and everything around me melted away.
The sea, dark as night. The enormous wreckage of high-rise buildings. Even the nameless corpses that had died with their eyes wide open.
In place of the vanished hologram, several dozen unfamiliar faces came into view.
Men in military uniforms and expensive-looking tailored suits.
The old man seated opposite me, at the head of the table, spoke with a grave expression.
“Good heavens. To think Leviathan got away.”
It was the first time I had seen his face, but according to Team Leader Choi, that old man was one of the three most powerful people in Japan.
No—if you counted the authority he actually wielded, he might be number one.
The position of Defense Minister was an immensely powerful one even in peacetime. In a situation like this, with the country at war, he possessed more power than anyone.
But looking at the old Defense Minister put me in a foul mood.
To be honest, I wanted to deal with that damned old man before Leviathan, who wasn’t even here.
Why? Simple.
An hour ago, he’d eliminated our last chance to catch it.
Now that I knew what had happened, I wasn’t about to be polite.
“Yeah. Shame it got away. If someone had helped at the end, we might have caught it.”
The conference room went still. While the other Japanese men glanced nervously at one another, the Defense Minister fixed me with an offended stare.
“That sounds as though you’re blaming Japan. Or have my old ears misheard you?”
“I heard you were over eighty, but you’re still in good shape. Your hearing’s pretty sharp for an old man.”
“What?”
“Have your ears actually gotten worse? You already heard me, so why do you keep asking?”
“How dare—!”
Bang!
The Defense Minister slammed the table and turned to Team Leader Choi.
“Are you going to stand there and allow this insolence?”
Normally, Team Leader Choi would have given me a warning look by now.
Normally.
“By ‘insolence,’ Defense Minister, do you mean striking the table during a meeting like this?”
“What?”
“Japan formally requested assistance through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. We answered that request and risked our lives to come here. And yet...”
Team Leader Choi’s words cut off, and his gaze turned cold.
“Why did you not deploy additional forces?”
“As I understand it, at the exact moment Jin Taekyung attacked Leviathan, at least two thousand Hunters had been mobilized. The Ground and Air Self-Defense Forces were also standing by.”
“That was...”
“I know most of them would not have been much help in a fight. But if you had deployed Japan’s Hunters, even then, they could have slowed Leviathan’s escape for a little while.”
Team Leader Choi’s words were clear and precise. They were also entirely true.
That little while was exactly what I’d needed.
A bit of support—and sacrifice—to distract the wounded monster and delay it as it dragged itself away.
Instead, after risking my life to go down into that deep water, I’d had to watch its back grow smaller in the distance.
Team Leader Choi and the roughly two hundred Hunters who’d disembarked from the aircraft and were preparing to enter had been forced to watch it escape, too.
“I could no longer stand by, so I tried to lead the Hunters in myself. Your side stopped us. You even invoked your authority over field operations.”
“If you wanted to keep your own losses down and claim the credit, you should have done the job properly. Then we wouldn’t be in this situation.”
The Defense Minister clenched his lips tightly before speaking.
“The encirclement... The encirclement was perfect.”
The Skeleton King looked at me with genuine curiosity.
“If it was perfect, shouldn’t Leviathan have failed to break through?”
“Yeah. It should have.”
“But it broke through?”
“Yep.”
“And you lost track of it because of the magical power it released?”
“Yep.”
Having listened to all my helpful answers, the Skeleton King muttered, “What? Are they fucking idiots...?”
With that single statement striking the truth with perfect accuracy, the temperature inside the conference room dropped below freezing.
But watching everyone fall silent and glance nervously around gave me no satisfaction at all.
Fucking lunatics.
Those bugs were worse than monsters, and they were sitting there calling themselves the operation’s command staff. I couldn’t even laugh.
It’s not like I can say “fuck this” and quit.
The number of casualties confirmed so far was roughly one hundred thousand.
It was only that low because, by some stroke of luck, the tsunami Leviathan had caused had stopped around the outskirts of Tokyo.
If it returned after I left, Tokyo would be renamed Atlantis.
And if it gives up on Japan and goes after somewhere else...
That would be a problem too.
Of course, the idiots here—including that old monkey chief—would probably dance for joy because they’d survived.
The worst part was, they really would.
After letting out a hundred-percent pure, deep sigh, I spoke to the Defense Minister, who had become completely silent.
“Enough. Get me someone else in charge.”
“S-someone else?”
“The Prime Minister. Or the King of Japan. Whoever it is, they’ll be better than you.”
“The King of Japan? How dare you speak of His Majesty the Emperor of the Great Japanese Empire—”
“Oh, give me a break. How long are you going to keep up the empire crap? Your empire got flattened by two atomic bombs. You should’ve given up the title of Emperor while you were at it.”
“That was a savage and barbaric act of destruction by those American Yankees!”
I plugged my ears as the Defense Minister shrieked.
“I think I’m going to get radiation poisoning. I think I’m going to get radiation poisoning. I think I’m going to get radiation poisoning. I think I’m going to get radiation poisoning.”
“Chikshō!”
Maybe he’d lived long enough not to care. Or maybe radiation contamination had robbed him of all fear.
Just as the Defense Minister was rampaging and charging at me with his old body, the Skeleton King reached out and seized him by the back of the neck.
“Stop, you old and insignificant hu—no, Yellow Monkey.”
“You wretch! Release me at once! How dare a fur-covered Yankee lay a hand on the Defense Minister of the Great Japanese Empire!”
“You dare insult the great United States in front of me?”
“I have not forgotten the terrible things you bastards did to this land and its innocent subjects of the Imperial State!”
Vengeful spirits of Pearl Harbor, descend upon me!
These fucking lunatics...
A Japanese imperialist from the ’70s-and-’80s generation arguing with an American monster from the Demon Realm.
Watching those horrifying hybrids with my own two eyes made my chest swell with emotion despite itself, but it was not over yet.
Fwoooooosh.
What the hell?
A chill ran through me, and the fluorescent lights began to dim.
Even the people struggling to separate the Defense Minister and the Skeleton King shuddered in the cold.
What the hell is happening all of a sudden?
I turned my head. My eyes met Team Leader Choi’s across the room.
That was when I realized it. My mouth fell open.
A shout from moments earlier rang through my ears again.
Vengeful spirits of Pearl Harbor, descend upon me!
No. Fuck. Don’t tell me...
Whoooooosh! KRAAASH!
The eerie energy became a gale, shattering the fluorescent lights overhead.
I was already running through the sudden darkness toward someone.
“Look closely, and feel their resentment—!”
“Hey, you crazy bastard!”
Crack!
Thank goodness.

Thanks to a time-honored promotion system that still valued family and connections over ability in the twenty-first century, most of the high-ranking officials and generals in the conference room were ordinary people. They were too frightened even to hear the Skeleton King’s shout.
And apparently my demand for someone in charge had gotten through. Before long, the manager—no, the Prime Minister—arrived.
“You came all this way to help our country! I am most grateful, Jinsang!”
“Ah, yes. Nice to meet you, Prime Minister Koizumi.”
I had never imagined I would live to see the day I met this man in person.
I’d only ever seen collections of his quotes online. Seeing him now gave me a brief jolt of excitement, like I’d met a celebrity.
Of course, this wasn’t the time to show it. We needed to deal with Leviathan.
At least, that was what I wanted to do.
I did.
“I’ll get straight to the point. To track Leviathan—”
“I hear the Defense Minister was rude to you, Jinsang. Once this is over, I shall reprimand him severely, if only to ease your hurt feelings!”
“Uh. Thanks. I appreciate it.”
“Why the look, Jinsang?”
“No, it’s just... We also need to discuss Leviathan. And the way you keep addressing me is a little...”
“The way I address you, Jinsang?”
“Ah, I see. It must sound like something else in Korean. Then shall I call you Gyeongsang, using the last syllable of your name?”
There was no way that would work.
I’d dodged a pile of shit only to get pissed on.
Is he wishing me a minor injury next time I fight Leviathan...?
I weighed Jinsang against Gyeongsang, then sighed.
Well, at least it isn’t Severe Injury.
